\lvert v\rvert e^{-\gamma(d(a,e)+d(b,e))}$, and, depending bilinearly on
$(v,v')$, \emph{concentrated at $(e,e')$} if $\lVert M_{ab}\rVert\le C
\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert e^{-\gamma(d(a,e)+d(a,e')+d(b,e)+d(b,e'))}$;
a vector is concentrated if it is so as a column. If $\lVert Y\rVert_{\beta
_0}\le C$, then $YM$ and $MY$ are concentrated where $M$ is, because
$e^{-\gamma(d(c,e)+d(c,e'))}\le e^{\beta_0d(a,c)}e^{-\gamma(d(a,e)+d(a,
e'))}$. For
$M$ concentrated at $e$ and $M'$ at $e'$, using $d(a,e)+d(a,e')\ge d(e,e')$
in both indices,
\[
\lvert\Tr(MM')\rvert\le C\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert N(\gamma/2)^2
e^{-\gamma d(e,e')},
\]
and if $M$ is concentrated at $(e,e')$, then
\[
\lvert\Tr M\rvert\le C\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert N(\gamma)e^{-\gamma
d(e,e')}.
\]

Now $x_v=\partial_vX=\bar Pv$ has $\lVert(x_v)_a\rVert\le Ce^{-\beta_0
d(a,e)}\lvert v\rvert$, so it is concentrated at $e$. The vector
$D^2c(X)[x_v,x_{v'}]$ has components at most $c_3N_k(x_v)N_k(x_{v'})\le
C\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert e^{-\beta_0(d(k,e)+d(k,e'))}$, so $x_{vv'}=
\partial_v\partial_{v'}X=-B^*(AB^*)^{-1}D^2c(X)[x_v,x_{v'}]$ is concentrated
at $(e,e')$. In the same way $A_v=\partial_vA=D^2c(X)[x_v,\cdot\,]$ is
concentrated at $e$, $A_{vv'}=D^3c(X)[x_v,x_{v'},\cdot\,]+D^2c(X)[x_{vv'},
\cdot\,]$ is concentrated at $(e,e')$, $\partial_vP=-B^*(AB^*)^{-1}A_vP$ is
concentrated at $e$, and $\partial_v\partial_{v'}P$ is a sum of products of
operators bounded in $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\beta_0}$ with either one factor
concentrated at $(e,e')$ or one factor concentrated at $e$ and one at $e'$.
The same holds for the derivatives of $\mathcal G_1=AA^*$ and $\mathcal G_2
=\bar P^*\bar P$. Then
\[
\begin{split}
\partial_v\partial_{v'}\bar H={}&\lambda\bigl(D^2Q[x_v,x_{v'}]+DQ[x_{vv'}]
\bigr)-\sum_e\partial_v\partial_{v'}\log j(X_e)\\
&+\sum_{i=1,2}\pm\tfrac12\bigl(\Tr(\mathcal G_i^{-1}\partial_v\partial
_{v'}\mathcal G_i)\\
&\qquad-\Tr(\mathcal G_i^{-1}\partial_v\mathcal G_i\,\mathcal G_i^{-1}
\partial_{v'}\mathcal G_i)\bigr),
\end{split}
\]
where $D^2Q$ and $DQ$ are the derivatives of $Q(Ue^X)$ in $X$. By the
bounds above every term is at most
\[
C(\lambda+1)\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert e^{-\gamma d(e,e')/2};
\]
for instance
\[
\lvert D^2Q[x_v,x_{v'}]\rvert\le C\sum_ae^{-\beta_0(d(a,e)+d(a,e')-2)}
\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert.
\]
Hence, using $\lambda\ge60c_6\ge60$, every block of the Hessian of $\bar H$
satisfies
\[
\lVert(\operatorname{Hess}\bar H)_{ee'}\rVert\le C\lambda e^{-\beta_0
d(e,e')/4},
\]
and $\lVert\operatorname{Hess}\bar H\rVert_\beta\le c_8\lambda$ with $\beta
=\beta_0/8$.

\emph{Approximation.} Let $\rho$ be smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with $0\le\rho'
\le1$, $\rho(t)=t$ for $t\le\frac32r$, $\rho\le\frac74r$ and $\rho$
constant on $[2r,\infty)$, and let
$\tau(\xi)_e=\rho(\lVert\xi_e\rVert)\xi_e/\lVert\xi_e\rVert$, which maps
$\g^{L'}$ into $\mathrm{Box}_{7r/4}$. Let $v$ be smooth and convex on
$[0,\infty)$, zero on $[0,r]$, with $0<v''\le1$ on $(r,\infty)$ and
$v''=1$ on $[\frac54r,\infty)$, and $V(\xi)=\sum_ev(\lVert\xi_e\rVert)$.
For $t\ge\frac32r$, $v''(t)=1$ and $v'(t)/t\ge1-\frac54r/t\ge\frac16$, so
$\operatorname{Hess}V\ge\frac16$ in the links with $\lVert\xi_e\rVert\ge
\frac32r$. Let $H_n=\bar H\circ\tau+nV$. Then
\[
\operatorname{Hess}H_n=D\tau^*\bigl(\operatorname{Hess}\bar H\circ\tau
\bigr)D\tau+\Delta_n,
\]
where $D\tau$ and $\Delta_n$ are block diagonal, $D\tau$ is the identity in
the links with $\lVert\xi_e\rVert\le\frac32r$, $\lVert D\tau\rVert\le1$, and
$\Delta_n\ge n\frac16-C_1$ in the other links, $C_1$ bounding $\nabla\bar H$
times the second derivative of $\tau$. So $\operatorname{Hess}H_n\ge m$ on
$\g^{L'}$ for $n\ge6(m+C_1)$, and all derivatives of $H_n$ of order at least
two are bounded. For $\varphi$ as in (ii) and $\alpha\le\alpha_G=\beta/(120
c_8)$, the block-scalar matrix $e^{\alpha\varphi}$ commutes with $D\tau$
and $\Delta_n$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:kernels}(ii)
\[
\bigl\lVert e^{\alpha\varphi}\operatorname{Hess}H_ne^{-\alpha\varphi}-
\operatorname{Hess}H_n\bigr\rVert\le\frac\alpha\beta c_8\lambda\le\frac m2 .
\]

\emph{Weighted Helffer--Sj\"ostrand.} Let $\mu_n$ have density proportional
to $e^{-H_n}$ on $\g^{L'}$ and $\mathcal L_n=-\Delta+\nabla H_n\cdot\nabla$
on $L^2(\mu_n)$. For $H_n$ smooth with $\operatorname{Hess}H_n\ge m>0$ and
bounded derivatives of order at least two, and $F,G$ smooth with bounded
derivatives, the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand representation~\cite{HS94,NS97} reads
$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_n}(F,G)=\langle\nabla F,\mathcal A^{-1}\nabla G
\rangle_{L^2(\mu_n)}$ with $\mathcal A=\mathcal L_n\otimes1+\operatorname{Hess}
H_n$ acting on $L^2(\mu_n;\g^{L'})$. With $w=e^{\alpha\varphi}$, constant in
$\xi$, $\mathcal A_w=w\mathcal Aw^{-1}=\mathcal L_n\otimes1+w\operatorname
{Hess}H_nw^{-1}$, and $\operatorname{Re}\langle u,\mathcal A_wu\rangle\ge
\frac m2\lVert u\rVert^2$ because $\mathcal L_n\ge0$; the adjoint satisfies
the same bound, so $\lVert\mathcal A_w^{-1}\rVert\le\frac2m=\frac{120}
\lambda$; this is the weighted form of the representation used
in~\cite{BJS00,Hel98}. Since $\mathcal A^{-1}=w^{-1}\mathcal A_w^{-1}w$,
\[
\begin{split}
\lvert\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu_n}(F,G)\rvert&=\bigl\lvert\langle w^{-1}\nabla
F,\mathcal A_w^{-1}w\nabla G\rangle\bigr\rvert\\
&\le\frac{120}\lambda\lVert w^{-1}\nabla F\rVert_{L^2(\mu_n)}\lVert w\nabla
G\rVert_{L^2(\mu_n)}.
\end{split}
\]
As $n\to\infty$, $e^{-H_n}$ decreases to $e^{-\bar H}\mathbf 1_{\mathrm{Box}
_r}$ off the boundary of $\mathrm{Box}_r$, since $\tau$ is the identity
there and $V>0$ off it, so $\mu_n\to\mu$ in total variation. For $F,G$
smooth on $T_U$, apply the bound to $(F\circ S)\chi$ and $(G\circ S)\chi$
with $\chi$ smooth, compactly supported and equal to $1$ near $\mathrm{Box}
_r$, and let $n\to\infty$; this proves (ii).

(iii) The left-invariant derivative of $U_ae^{X_a}$ along $\delta X_a$ is
$\Psi(\operatorname{ad}_{X_a})\delta X_a$, of norm at most $2\lVert\delta
X_a\rVert$, so $\lVert\partial_{\xi_f}F\rVert\le2\sum_{a\in X_1}\lVert\bar
P_{af}\rVert$, and similarly for $G$. Take $\varphi=d(\cdot,X_2)$ and $\alpha
=\alpha_G\le\beta_0$. Then $e^{-\alpha d(f,X_2)}\le e^{\beta_0d(a,f)}e^{-
\alpha d(a,X_2)}$, so $\lvert e^{-\alpha\varphi}\nabla'F\rvert\le2\lvert
X_1\rvert\lVert\bar P\rVert_{\beta_0}e^{-\alpha d(X_1,X_2)}$, and $e^{\alpha
d(f,X_2)}\le e^{\beta_0d(b,f)}$ for $b\in X_2$ gives $\lvert e^{\alpha
\varphi}\nabla'G\rvert\le2\lvert X_2\rvert\lVert\bar P\rVert_{\beta_0}$.
Insert these in (ii); with $C$ a bound for $\lVert\bar P\rVert_{\beta_0}$
on $\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$, $c_9=480C^2$.
\end{proof}

The rate $\alpha_G$ and the amplitude $c_9$ can be computed, and they turn
out not to depend on $G$. The proof above passes through the norms
$\lVert\cdot\rVert_\beta$, whose Schur sums bring in the large factors
$N(\beta)$; the computation below replaces them by weighted operator norms,
in which inverses and products cost nothing beyond their operator norms. For
a block matrix $M$ indexed by links and pairs and for $\vartheta\ge0$ let
\[
\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta)}=\sup_\varphi\bigl\lVert e^{\vartheta\varphi}
Me^{-\vartheta\varphi}\bigr\rVert,
\]
the supremum over all $\varphi$ with $|\varphi(a)-\varphi(b)|\le d(a,b)$
for all indices $a,b$, the factors $e^{\pm\vartheta\varphi}$ acting as
scalars on each block. For such $\varphi$ write $w=e^{\vartheta\varphi}$
and $M^w=wMw^{-1}$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:weightednorms}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $\vartheta\le\vartheta'$, $\lVert M\rVert\le\lVert M\rVert_{(
\vartheta)}\le\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta')}$; moreover $\lVert M_1M_2\rVert
_{(\vartheta)}\le\lVert M_1\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\lVert M_2\rVert_{(\vartheta)}$,
$\lVert M^*\rVert_{(\vartheta)}=\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta)}$, and $\lVert
M_{ab}\rVert\le\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta)}e^{-\vartheta d(a,b)}$. If the
blocks of $M$ vanish beyond distance $R$, then $\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta)}
\le e^{\vartheta R}(R_MC_M)^{1/2}$, where $R_M$ and $C_M$ are the largest
row and column sums of the norms of the blocks.
\item If $M$ is Hermitian and $0\le\vartheta\le\vartheta'$, then $\lVert
\operatorname{Re}M^w-M\rVert\le2(\vartheta/\vartheta')^2\lVert M\rVert
_{(\vartheta')}$ for every $\varphi$, where $\operatorname{Re}T=\frac12(T+
T^*)$.
\item If $\operatorname{Re}M^w\ge c>0$ for every $\varphi$, then $\lVert
M^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le1/c$. If $\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}
\lVert E\rVert_{(\vartheta)}<1$, then $\lVert(M+E)^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}
\le\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}/(1-\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}
\lVert E\rVert_{(\vartheta)})$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Take $\varphi=0$ for the first inequality and replace $\varphi$ by
$\vartheta\varphi/\vartheta'$ for the second. Products and adjoints follow
from $(M_1M_2)^w=M_1^wM_2^w$ and $(M^*)^w=(M^{w'})^*$ with $w'=e^{-\vartheta
\varphi}$. With $\varphi=d(\cdot,b)$ the block $(a,b)$ of $M^w$ is $e^{
\vartheta d(a,b)}M_{ab}$, of norm at most $\lVert M^w\rVert$. The last bound
is the Schur test, since the blocks of $M^w$ are $e^{\vartheta(\varphi(a)-
\varphi(b))}M_{ab}$.

(ii) Let $f(z)=e^{z\varphi}Me^{-z\varphi}$, an entire function of $z\in\C$
with values in matrices. For $z=x+iy$, $f(z)=e^{iy\varphi}f(x)e^{-iy\varphi}$
with $e^{iy\varphi}$ unitary, so $\lVert f(z)\rVert\le K=\lVert M\rVert_{(
\vartheta')}$ for $|x|\le\vartheta'$. Since $M$ is Hermitian, $f(x)^*=f(-x)$
for real $x$, so $\operatorname{Re}M^w-M=g(\vartheta)$ with $g(z)=\frac12(f(z)
+f(-z))-f(0)$. The function $g$ is even, vanishes at $0$ and is bounded by
$2K$ on $|z|<\vartheta'$; so $g(z)/z^2$ is holomorphic there, and the maximum
principle on the circles $|z|=\rho<\vartheta'$, applied to $\ell(g(z))/z^2$
for every linear functional $\ell$ of norm one, gives $\lVert g(z)\rVert
\le2K|z|^2/\vartheta'^2$.

(iii) If $\operatorname{Re}T\ge c$, then $\lVert Tu\rVert\lVert u\rVert\ge
\operatorname{Re}\langle u,Tu\rangle\ge c\lVert u\rVert^2$, so $\lVert T^{-1}
\rVert\le1/c$; apply this to $T=M^w$, whose inverse is $(M^{-1})^w$. The
second statement is the Neumann series for $(M^w+E^w)^{-1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:explicitdecay}
Let $G\subset\U(r)$ be compact. Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} holds with
\[
\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4},\qquad c_9=1.2\cdot10^4,
\]
and in~\textup{(iii)} the factor $\lvert X_1\rvert\lvert X_2\rvert$ may be
replaced by $(\lvert X_1\rvert\lvert X_2\rvert)^{1/2}$.
\end{proposition}

So the covariances of local observables under the constrained law on the
chart decay at least like $e^{-d/4000}$, with amplitude $1.2\cdot10^4/
\lambda$, for every compact group; for $\SU(2)$ and the Wilson action the
amplitude is $4.8\cdot10^4/\beta$.

\begin{proof}
Throughout, $\xi\in\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$, $X=S\xi+h(S\xi)$, and the notation is
that of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}. The hypothesis
$4\cdot10^5c_3(\kappa+s)\le\frac1{195}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}(iv)
gives $c_3s\le1.29\cdot10^{-8}$ and $c_3\kappa'\le7.7\cdot10^{-8}$ for
$\kappa'=\kappa+6s$, and $\kappa\le10^{-8}$. Every $\varphi$ below is
defined on all indices; a function on $L'$ with the Lipschitz property
extends to all indices with the same property, by $\varphi(a)=\min_{e\in L'}
(\varphi(e)+d(a,e))$.

\emph{Local operators.} The row $k$ of $B$ has blocks of norm at most $\frac
18+260\kappa$, with sum at most $2+24\cdot260\kappa$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(iv) and the coefficients of $V_{y,\mu}$, eight of
them $\frac18$ and sixteen $\frac1{16}$; every link lies in at most two rows,
and the blocks vanish beyond distance $1$. So $b=\lVert B\rVert_{(\vartheta)}
\le e^\vartheta(\frac12+10^{-4})^{1/2}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}(i).
The row $k$ of $A-B$ has norm at most $c_3N_{y,\mu}(X)\le7.35c_3s=
\varepsilon_A$, since $\lVert X\rVert_\infty\le\frac32s$, so $\lVert A-B
\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le\sqrt{48}\,e^\vartheta\varepsilon_A$. The row $d_k$ of
$S$ is $s_k\xi=-B_{k,d_k}^{-1}\sum_{e\ne d_k}B_{k,e}\xi_e$, of norm $\sigma
\le(\frac{\sqrt{11}}8+260\kappa)/(\frac18-260\kappa)\le3.32$, the squares of
the other coefficients adding up to $\frac{11}{64}$; the other rows of $S$
are those of the identity. If $D_k$ is the diagonal matrix with entries
$e^{\vartheta(\varphi(d_k)-\varphi(e))}$ on the links $e$ of $V_{y,\mu}$,
then the row $d_k$ of $S^w$ is $s_kD_k$, and every link of $L'$ lies in at
most two of these sets, so
\[
\bar s=\lVert S\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le(1+2\sigma^2e^{2\vartheta})^{1/2}.
\]
Finally $Q(Ue^X)=\sum_p\lVert U_p-I\rVert^2=\sum_p(2r-2\ReTr U_p)$. By
Duhamel's formula the derivative of $U_ee^{X_e}$ in $X_e$ is an average of
$U_ee^{\theta X_e}Ye^{(1-\theta)X_e}$, and its second derivative an average,
of total weight one, of products with $Y$ and $Z$ inserted between unitary
factors. With $\lvert\Tr(V_1YV_2ZV_3)\rvert\le\lVert Y\rVert\lVert Z\rVert$
for unitary $V_i$ this gives
\[
\bigl\lvert D^2Q_p[Y,Z]\bigr\rvert\le2\sum_{e\in p}\lVert Y_e\rVert\sum_{e
\in p}\lVert Z_e\rVert,
\]
and, since $\ReTr(VY)=\ReTr((V-I)Y)$ for skew-Hermitian $Y$ and a conjugate
$V$ of $U_p$, $\lvert DQ_p[Y]\rvert\le2\kappa'\sum_{e\in p}\lVert Y_e\rVert$.
A link lies in six plaquettes, so $\lVert D^2Q\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le48
e^\vartheta$ and $\lvert DQ[Y]\rvert\le12\kappa'\lVert Y\rVert_1$.

\emph{Inverses.} The diagonal blocks of $\mathcal G=BB^*$ have norm at most
$\frac3{16}+227\kappa$, each row has two other nonzero blocks, of norm at
most $\frac1{32}+227\kappa$, at distance $2$, and $\mathcal G\ge\frac1{16}-
700\kappa$, by the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:smallfibre}(iii). The blocks of
$\operatorname{Re}\mathcal G^w$ are $\cosh(\vartheta(\varphi(k)-\varphi(l)))
\mathcal G_{kl}$, so $\operatorname{Re}\mathcal G^w\ge\frac1{16}-700\kappa-(
\cosh2\vartheta-1)(\frac1{16}+454\kappa)$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}(iii) bounds $g_0=\lVert\mathcal G^{-1}\rVert
_{(\vartheta)}$ by the inverse of the right-hand side. With $E=(A-B)B^*$, the
same lemma gives
\[
\begin{split}
\lVert(AB^*)^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}&\le\frac{g_0}{1-g_0\lVert E\rVert
_{(\vartheta)}}=h_0,\\
\lVert(AA^*)^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}&\le\frac{g_0}{1-g_0(2\lVert E\rVert
_{(\vartheta)}+\lVert A-B\rVert_{(\vartheta)}^2)}=g_1,
\end{split}
\]
since $AB^*=\mathcal G+E$ and $AA^*=\mathcal G+E+E^*+(A-B)(A-B)^*$. Let
$Y=B^*(AB^*)^{-1}$, so $y=\lVert Y\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le bh_0$. Since $BS=0$,
$\bar P=PS=S-Y(A-B)S$, so $\bar p=\lVert\bar P\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le\bar s(1+
y\lVert A-B\rVert_{(\vartheta)})$; and $M=Y(A-B)S$ takes values in $N_U$,
orthogonal to the values of $S$, so $\bar P^*\bar P=S^*S+M^*M$. Here $S^*S=1+
\sum_ks_k^*s_k$, and $(s_k^*s_k)^w=v^*u$ with $u=s_kD_k$, $v=s_kD_k^{-1}$, so
$\operatorname{Re}(s_k^*s_k)^w=\frac14((u+v)^*(u+v)-(u-v)^*(u-v))\ge-\sigma^2
\sinh^2\vartheta\,J_k$, $J_k$ the projection on the links of $V_{y,\mu}$; and
$\operatorname{Re}(M^*M)^w\ge-2(\vartheta/\vartheta'')^2\lVert M\rVert_{(
\vartheta'')}^2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}(ii), for $\vartheta\le
\vartheta''$. Hence
\[
g_2=\lVert(\bar P^*\bar P)^{-1}\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le\Bigl(1-2\sigma^2\sinh
^2\vartheta-2\frac{\vartheta^2}{\vartheta''^2}\lVert M\rVert_{(\vartheta'')}
^2\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
For the $\ell^1$ norms, $\lVert\mathcal G^{-1}\rVert\le17$ in the norm
$\sum_k\lVert z_k\rVert$ and $E$ has column sums at most $2(2+10^{-4})
\varepsilon_A$, so $(AB^*)^{-1}$ has norm $h_1\le17.001$ there, and $\lVert
B^*z\rVert_1\le(2+10^{-4})\sum_k\lVert z_k\rVert$.

\emph{The Hessian.} Let $u,u'\in\g^{L'}$, $p=wu$ and $q=w^{-1}u'$. Since
$\langle u,(\operatorname{Hess}\bar H)^wu'\rangle=\partial_p\partial_q\bar
H$, it suffices to bound $\lvert\partial_p\partial_q\bar H\rvert$ by $K\lvert
u\rvert\lvert u'\rvert$ for every $\varphi$. Write $x_p=\bar Pp=w\tilde x$ and
$x_q=w^{-1}\tilde y$, with $\lvert\tilde x\rvert\le\bar p\lvert u\rvert$ and
$\lvert\tilde y\rvert\le\bar p\lvert u'\rvert$. The links of $V_{y,\mu}$ lie
within distance $1$ of the position of $k$, so the weights of $x_p$ and $x_q$
on them differ from $e^{\pm\vartheta\varphi(k)}$ by factors at most
$e^\vartheta$, and
\[
\sum_kN_{y,\mu}(x_p)N_{y,\mu}(x_q)\le2e^{2\vartheta}\lvert\tilde x\rvert
\lvert\tilde y\rvert,
\]
every link lying in at most two of these sets. In the same way $A_p=\partial
_pA=D^2c(X)[x_p,\cdot\,]$ equals $w\check A_p$ and $A_q=w^{-1}\check A_q$,
where $\check A_p$ and $\check A_q$ have rows of rank at most $\dim G$, so
their Hilbert--Schmidt norms satisfy
\[
\lVert\check A_p\rVert_2\lVert\check A_q\rVert_2\le2\dim G\,c_3^2e^{2
\vartheta}\bar p^2\lvert u\rvert\lvert u'\rvert,
\]
and conjugating them by $w$ multiplies these norms by at most $e^\vartheta$.
The second derivative $x_{pq}=-YD^2c(X)[x_p,x_q]$ has $\lVert x_{pq}\rVert_1
\le c_3x_1\lvert u\rvert\lvert u'\rvert$ with $x_1=2(2+10^{-4})h_1e^{2
\vartheta}\bar p^2$, and $A_{pq}=D^3c(X)[x_p,x_q,\cdot\,]+D^2c(X)[x_{pq},
\cdot\,]$ has trace norm $\bar a\le2\dim G\,c_3^2(e^{2\vartheta}\bar p^2+x_1)
\lvert u\rvert\lvert u'\rvert$, the weights cancelling in both.

The four parts of $\bar H$ are bounded as follows. First, $\partial_p
\partial_q\lambda Q=\lambda(\langle\tilde x,(D^2Q)^w\tilde y\rangle+DQ[x_{pq}
])$, at most $\lambda(48e^\vartheta\bar p^2+12c_3\kappa'x_1)\lvert u\rvert
\lvert u'\rvert$. Second, the Hessian of $\sum_e\log j(X_e)$ in $X$ is block
diagonal and commutes with $w$, so its part is at most $c_3(\bar p^2+c_3x_1)
\lvert u\rvert\lvert u'\rvert$. Third, for $\mathcal G_1=AA^*$,
\[
\begin{split}
\partial_p\partial_q\log\det\mathcal G_1={}&\Tr(\mathcal G_1^{-1}\partial_p
\partial_q\mathcal G_1)\\
&-\Tr(\mathcal G_1^{-1}\partial_p\mathcal G_1\,\mathcal G_1^{-1}\partial_q
\mathcal G_1),
\end{split}
\]
with $\partial_p\mathcal G_1=A_pA^*+AA_p^*$ and $\partial_p\partial_q\mathcal
G_1=A_{pq}A^*+A_pA_q^*+A_qA_p^*+AA_{pq}^*$. Each term is the trace of a
product in which $w$ and $w^{-1}$ occur once each, next to $\check A_p$ and
$\check A_q$, or not at all, next to $A_{pq}$. A cyclic permutation writes it
as $\Tr(wFw^{-1}F')$, or $\Tr(w^{-1}Fw\,F')$, and $\lvert\Tr(wFw^{-1}F')\rvert
\le\lVert wFw^{-1}\rVert_2\lVert F'\rVert_2$ or $\lVert wFw^{-1}\rVert\lVert
F'\rVert_1$. With $a=\lVert A\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le b+\lVert A-B\rVert_{(
\vartheta)}$ this gives
\[
\begin{split}
\tfrac12\lvert\partial_p\partial_q\log\det\mathcal G_1\rvert\le{}&g_1a\bar a
\\
&+(g_1+2g_1^2a^2)e^{2\vartheta}\lVert\check A_p\rVert_2\lVert\check A_q\rVert
_2.
\end{split}
\]
Fourth, $\partial_p\bar P=-YA_p\bar P$ and $\partial_p\partial_q\bar P=-YA_{pq}
\bar P+YA_qYA_p\bar P+YA_pYA_q\bar P$, and the same counting for $\mathcal G
_2=\bar P^*\bar P$ gives
\[
\begin{split}
\tfrac12\lvert\partial_p\partial_q\log\det\mathcal G_2\rvert\le{}&g_2\bar p^2
y\bar a+(3g_2\bar p^2y^2\\
&+2g_2^2\bar p^4y^2)e^{2\vartheta}\lVert\check A_p\rVert_2\lVert\check A_q
\rVert_2.
\end{split}
\]
So
\[
\lVert\operatorname{Hess}\bar H\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le K=\lambda k_1+\dim
G\,c_3^2k_0,
\]
where $k_1=48e^\vartheta\bar p^2+12c_3\kappa'x_1$ and $k_0$
collects the other three parts, divided by $\dim G\,c_3^2\lvert u\rvert
\lvert u'\rvert$, which is possible as $c_3\ge1$. At $\vartheta=\vartheta'=
0.197$, with $\vartheta''=0.6$, these give $b\le0.862$, $g_0,h_0,g_1\le
17.37$, $y\le14.96$, $\bar s,\bar p\le5.80$, $g_2\le7.41$, $k_1\le1966$ and
$k_0\le4.16\cdot10^9$; and since $\lambda\ge60c_6=4.086\cdot10^7\dim G\,c_3
^2$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants}, $K\le2068\lambda$.

\emph{Decay.} In the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, replace the
bound on $e^{\alpha\varphi}\operatorname{Hess}H_ne^{-\alpha\varphi}-
\operatorname{Hess}H_n$ by the following. Since $D\tau$ and $\Delta_n$ are
block diagonal and symmetric and commute with $w=e^{\alpha\varphi}$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}(ii) with $\vartheta=\alpha$ gives
\[
\bigl\lVert\operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{Hess}H_n)^w-\operatorname{Hess}H
_n\bigr\rVert\le2\frac{\alpha^2}{\vartheta'^2}K\le\frac\lambda{120}=\frac m2
\]
for $\alpha\le\vartheta'(240\cdot2068)^{-1/2}$, which holds for $\alpha\le
2.5\cdot10^{-4}$. Then $\operatorname{Re}\langle u,\mathcal A_wu\rangle\ge
\frac m2\lVert u\rVert^2$ as before, and (ii) follows. For (iii), $\nabla'F
=\bar P^*g$ with $g$ supported on $X_1$ and $\lvert g_a\rvert\le2$, so with
$\varphi=d(\cdot,X_2)$,
\[
\lvert e^{-\alpha\varphi}\nabla'F\rvert=\lvert(\bar P^*)^{w^{-1}}e^{-\alpha
\varphi}g\rvert\le2\bar p_\alpha\lvert X_1\rvert^{1/2}e^{-\alpha d(X_1,X_2)},
\]
where $\bar p_\alpha=\lVert\bar P\rVert_{(\alpha)}\le4.8$ at $\alpha=2.5\cdot
10^{-4}$, and $\lvert e^{\alpha\varphi}\nabla'G\rvert\le2\bar p_\alpha\lvert
X_2\rvert^{1/2}$. Insert these in (ii): $c_9=480\bar p_\alpha^2\le1.2\cdot
10^4$.
\end{proof}

The chart misses only points of the fibre at which some plaquette near $W$
is not small, and under the Wilson measure such points carry little mass on
most fibres.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:offchart}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} and $s\ge1.24
\cdot10^5\kappa$. Every $U'\in F$ with $\delta(U'_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every
plaquette $p$ with a vertex in a block of $W^+$ lies in $\Phi(\Omega_r)$.
Hence the constrained law gives the complement of $\Phi(\Omega_r)$ at most
the mass of the points of $F$ at which such a plaquette exceeds $\kappa$.
\item Let $G=\SU(2)$, let the side $2L$ be a power of two, let $\mu$ be the
Wilson measure in the tree gauge at $\beta_W\ge1$, so that $\lambda=\beta
_W/4$, and let $E$ be the set of fields with $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for
every plaquette with a vertex in a block of $W^+$. For $\mu$-almost every
$U$ let $\mu_U$ be the constrained law on the fibre $F(U)$ through $U$.
Then
\[
\E_\mu\bigl[\mu_U(E^c)\bigr]=\mu(E^c)\le10^4\lvert W\rvert\,q_\kappa(\beta
_W),
\]
with $q_\kappa$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}. If $\kappa$, $s$ and
$\lambda$ satisfy the hypotheses of \textup{(i)} and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
the fields $U\in E$ with $\mu_U(F(U)\setminus\Phi_U(\Omega_r))\le
\varepsilon$, where $\Phi_U$ is the chart at $U$, have probability at least
$1-(1+\varepsilon^{-1})10^4\lvert W\rvert q_\kappa(\beta_W)$.
\item At every such $U$, for $X_1,X_2\subset A_W$ and $\tilde F,\tilde G$
as in Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}\textup{(iii)},
\[
\lvert\Cov_{\mu_U}(\tilde F,\tilde G)\rvert\le\Bigl(\frac{4c_9}{\beta_W}
e^{-\alpha_Gd(X_1,X_2)}+30\varepsilon\Bigr)\lvert X_1\rvert\,\lvert X_2
\rvert .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) The fields $U$ and $U'$ satisfy the hypothesis of
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes} and agree off $A_W$, in particular on the tree
links. An active link $e$ with base in a block $B(y)$, $y\in W$, either lies
inside $B(y)$ or leaves it in a direction $\mu$. In the first case part (i)
of the lemma, at $U$ and at $U'$, gives $\delta(U_e,U'_e)\le6\kappa$. In the
second, let $v$ and $v'$ be the path links of $V_{y,\mu}$ at $U$ and at
$U'$. Part (iv), at both fields, writes the common cut-off average as $v
e^M=v'e^{M'}$ with $\lVert M\rVert,\lVert M'\rVert\le8\pi\kappa$, so by
bi-invariance and Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}
\[
\delta(v,v')=\delta\bigl(e^Me^{-M'},I\bigr)\le\lVert M\rVert+\lVert M'
\rVert\le16\pi\kappa<50.3\kappa,
\]
and part (i) gives $\delta(U_e,U'_e)\le\delta(U_e,v)+\delta(v,v')+\delta(
v',U'_e)\le92.3\kappa$. Let $X_e=\log(U_e^{-1}U'_e)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, $\lVert X_e\rVert\le\frac\pi3\,92.3\kappa<96.7
\kappa\le s/1280$ for every $e\in A_W$. Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}(i)
with $s/32$ in place of $s$, whose chart is the restriction of $\Phi$ by
the uniqueness of the fixed point in its proof, puts $U'=Ue^X$ in $\Phi(K
_{s/32})$, and $K_{s/32}\subset\Omega_r$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(i).

(ii) The tree links span every block, so for every field there is exactly
one gauge transformation, equal to $I$ at the corner of every block, that
makes the tree links equal to $I$. Given the tree links, it multiplies each
active link on both sides by elements that do not depend on that link,
which preserves Haar measure, and $S$ is gauge invariant; so in the tree
gauge the active links have density proportional to $e^{-\beta_WS}$ with
respect to product Haar measure. Since $\beta_WS=\frac{\beta_W}4\sum_p
\delta(U_p,I)^2$, conditionally on the links off $A_W$ the links of $A_W$
have density proportional to $e^{-\lambda Q}$, and conditioning further on
the averages gives the constrained law. So $\mu_U$ is a version of the
conditional law of $\mu$ given the links off $A_W$ and the averages, and
the identity is the tower property of conditional expectation. If $U\notin
E$, some plaquette with a vertex in a block $B(y')$, $y'\in W^+$, is bad for
$\rho=\kappa$. Its corner $z$ differs from that vertex by an element of
$\{0,1\}^4$, so $z$ lies in a block at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most two
from $W$, and the plaquette lies in the unit cube $\mathcal C_z$. There are
at most $5^4\lvert W\rvert$ such blocks, with $16$ sites each, and $E$ is
gauge invariant, so Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} with $\lvert A\rvert=1$ gives
$\mu(E^c)\le10^4\lvert W\rvert q_\kappa(\beta_W)$. For $U\in E$, part (i)
gives $\mu_U(F(U)\setminus\Phi_U(\Omega_r))\le\mu_U(E^c)$, so the
exceptional fields lie in $E^c\cup\{\mu_U(E^c)>\varepsilon\}$, which by
Markov's inequality has probability at most $\mu(E^c)(1+\varepsilon^{-1})$.

(iii) Let $A=\Phi_U(\Omega_r)$, $m=\mu_U$, $m_A=m(\,\cdot\mid A)$ and
$\epsilon'=m(A^c)\le\varepsilon$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(iii) with
$\lambda=\beta_W/4$, $\lvert\Cov_{m_A}(\tilde F,\tilde G)\rvert\le\frac{4c
_9}{\beta_W}\lvert X_1\rvert\lvert X_2\rvert e^{-\alpha_Gd(X_1,X_2)}$. The
group $\SU(2)$ has diameter $\sqrt2\pi$, and $\tilde F$ has gradient at most
$1$ in each link, so after subtracting a constant, which changes no
covariance, $\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\le\frac{\sqrt2\pi}2\lvert X_1
\rvert\le2.23\lvert X_1\rvert$, and likewise for $\tilde G$. Writing
$m=(1-\epsilon')m_A+\epsilon'm_{A^c}$ gives $\lvert m(fg)-m_A(fg)\rvert\le
2\epsilon'\lVert f\rVert_\infty\lVert g\rVert_\infty$ and $\lvert m(f)-m_A(f)
\rvert\le2\epsilon'\lVert f\rVert_\infty$ for bounded $f,g$, so
\[
\lvert\Cov_m(f,g)-\Cov_{m_A}(f,g)\rvert\le6\epsilon'\lVert f\rVert_\infty
\lVert g\rVert_\infty,
\]
and $6\cdot2.23^2<30$.
\end{proof}

So on a fixed set of blocks the constrained law of the $\SU(2)$ Wilson
measure decorrelates, coarea factor and curvature of the fibre included, on
every fibre outside a set of fibres whose probability tends to zero as
$\beta_W\to\infty$. The bound grows linearly in $\lvert W\rvert$, which is
harmless for the fixed cubes of the cube condition, but the thresholds are
far from the one-loop range: with the constants of
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} the hypotheses force $\kappa+s\le
6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ and $s\ge1.24\cdot10^5\kappa$, so $\kappa<4.9\cdot
10^{-18}$, and $q_\kappa(\beta_W)<1$ needs $\beta_W\kappa^2>96(\log\beta_W+
C_0)$, so $\beta_W$ exceeds $3.8\cdot10^{38}$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:offchart}).

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_offchart.png}
\caption{Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}. (a)~A fibre $F$ of the cut-off
average, drawn as a surface: the product chart $\Phi(\Omega_r)$ around the
background $U$ (green) contains every point of $F$ whose plaquettes near $W$
are at most $\kappa$ (inside the blue curve), and the rest of $F$ meets
only points with a large plaquette (red). (b)~The least $\beta_W$ at which
the bound $10^4\lvert W\rvert q_\kappa(\beta_W)$ is at most $\frac12$, for
the $81$ blocks of a cube of side three; it grows like $\kappa^{-2}\log(1/
\kappa)$, and at the largest $\kappa$ the hypotheses allow it is about
$4.0\cdot10^{38}$.}
\label{fig:offchart}
\end{figure*}

The mass off the chart can also be bounded on a single fibre, by a Peierls
argument inside the fibre. Two properties of the cut-off average make this
possible: along a fixed set of links it is a submersion with a constant that
does not depend on the field, and its law under Haar measure on those links
has a bounded density.

Fix $y\in W$ and a direction $\mu$. Write the offsets of the sites of $B(y)$
in the three directions other than $\mu$ as $a\in\{0,1\}^3$, and let $x_a$
and $x'_a$ be the sites of offset $a$ with $o_\mu=0$ and $o_\mu=1$. Let
$\ell_a=(x'_a,\mu)$, which joins $B(y)$ to $B(y+e_\mu)$, and let $u_a=(x_a,
\mu)$ and $w_a=(x'_a+e_\mu,\mu)$, which lie inside $B(y)$ and $B(y+e_\mu)$.
The links $u_0$ and $w_0$ are tree links and $\ell_0=d_k$ is the path link,
so in the tree gauge
\[
P_{2y}=\ell_0,\qquad P_{x_a}=u_a\ell_a,\qquad P_{x'_a}=\ell_aw_a,
\]
and $v_x=P_{2y}^{-1}P_x$ equals $I$ at the two sites of offset $0$. The path
of $V^\sharp_{y',\nu}$ from a site $x$ consists of the link $(x,\nu)$ and
the next link $(x+e_\nu,\nu)$, so $\ell_a$, whose base has $o_\mu=1$, enters
only the paths from $x_a$ and $x'_a$ of the pair $(y,\mu)$. We call $\ell_0,
\dots,\ell_7$ the \emph{private links} of $(y,\mu)$. The $32$ links with
$o_\mu=1$ of $B(y)$ are the private links of the four pairs $(y,\mu)$; the
other $17$ active links of $B(y)$ lie inside it.

Let
\[
\alpha=2\arcsin\frac1{2\sqrt2}=0.7227\ldots,\qquad\Lambda=\frac\alpha
{\sin\alpha}=1.0926\ldots,
\]
so that $1-\frac78\Lambda>0.0439$. Two
facts about $\operatorname{ad}X$ for $X\in\g$, which is skew-adjoint for
the Hilbert--Schmidt product, will be used throughout. If the eigenvalues
$i\psi$ of $\operatorname{ad}X$ satisfy $|\psi|<2\alpha$, then
\begin{gather*}
\log\bigl(e^{tZ}e^X\bigr)=X+tL_XZ+O(t^2),\\
L_X=\frac{\operatorname{ad}X}{e^{\operatorname{ad}X}-1},\qquad\lVert L_X
\rVert\le\Lambda,
\end{gather*}
since the eigenvalues of $L_X$ have modulus $\frac{|\psi|/2}{\sin(|\psi|/2
)}$, which increases with $|\psi|$. For every $Y\in\g$,
\begin{gather*}
\frac d{dt}e^{Y+tZ}\Big|_{t=0}e^{-Y}=E_YZ,\\
E_Y=\frac{e^{\operatorname{ad}Y}-1}{\operatorname{ad}Y},\qquad\lVert E_Y
\rVert\le1,
\end{gather*}
because $|e^{i\psi}-1|\le|\psi|$; in particular $d(e^A,e^B)\le\lVert A-B
\rVert$ for the Riemannian distance $d$ of the bi-invariant metric, along
the curve $e^{A+t(B-A)}$. If $\delta(v,I)<1$ and $e^{i\theta_j}$, $|\theta
_j|\le\pi$, are the eigenvalues of $v$, then $\sum_j4\sin^2(\theta_j/2)<1$;
each $|\theta_j|$ is less than $\frac\pi3$, where $\sin^2(t/2)$ is convex,
so $|\theta_j|+|\theta_k|<2\alpha$ for all $j,k$, and $X=\log v$ satisfies
the hypothesis on $\operatorname{ad}X$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:privatesubmersion}
Let $\sigma_0=(1-\frac78\Lambda)/\sqrt2>0.031$. At every field at which
$V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ is differentiable, its derivative $J:\g^8\to\g$ with
respect to its eight private links, right trivialised, satisfies $JJ^*\ge
\sigma_0^2$. The fields at which it is not differentiable form a null set
for Haar measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $m=\max_x\delta(v_x,I)$ and $\chi=\phi(m/\rho_G)$, so that $V^\sharp=
P_{2y}e^{\chi N}$ with $N=\frac1{16}\sum_x\log v_x$. Where $m>\rho_G$, the
cut-off vanishes near the field, $V^\sharp=\ell_0$, and the derivative along
$\ell_0$ is the identity. Suppose $m<\rho_G$, and that the maximum is attained
at one path $x_*$, after identifying identical path functions, and
$m\ne\rho_G/2$. Copies that coincide because $u_a,w_a$ are tree links
are counted together. Other ties lie in finitely many proper
real-analytic subsets, a null set. The variation below fixes both copies
of an identical pair, since then $u_b=w_b=I$ and $A-1=0$. Then every
$\delta(v_x,I)$ is less than $1$, the logarithms are defined, $\chi$ is
differentiable, and every variation that fixes $v_{x_*}$ to first order
fixes $\chi$ to first order. The site $x_*$ has offset $b\ne0$.

Fix $\zeta\in\g$ and put $\eta=\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0)\zeta$. Move $\ell_0
\mapsto e^{t\eta}\ell_0$, and, if $x_*=x'_b$, $\ell_b\mapsto e^{t\eta}\ell_b$,
or, if $x_*=x_b$, $\ell_b\mapsto e^{t\xi}\ell_b$ with $\xi=\operatorname{Ad}
(u_b^{-1})\eta$, so that $u_b\ell_b\mapsto e^{t\eta}u_b\ell_b$. In both cases
$P_{2y}$ and $P_{x_*}$ are multiplied on the left by $e^{t\eta}$, so
$v_{x_*}$ and $\chi$ are fixed to first order. The other site $\bar x$ of
offset $b$ has $P_{\bar x}\mapsto e^{t\operatorname{Ad}(u_b^{\pm1})\eta}
P_{\bar x}$, and the paths from the remaining twelve sites with $v_x\ne I$
do not move. With the isometry $A=\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0^{-1}u_b^{\pm1}
\ell_0)$,
\[
v_{\bar x}\mapsto e^{t(A-1)\zeta}v_{\bar x}+O(t^2),\qquad v_x\mapsto e^{-t
\zeta}v_x+O(t^2)
\]
for the twelve others, so $N$ moves by $t\,\delta N$ with $16\,\delta N=L_{X
_{\bar x}}(A-1)\zeta-\sum_xL_{X_x}\zeta$, twelve terms, and $\lVert\delta N
\rVert\le\frac{14}{16}\Lambda\lVert\zeta\rVert$. Since $\chi$ is fixed,
\[
\frac d{dt}V^\sharp\,(V^\sharp)^{-1}=\eta+\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0)E_{\chi
N}(\chi\,\delta N)=\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0)\,T\zeta,
\]
with $\lVert T\zeta-\zeta\rVert\le\frac78\Lambda\lVert\zeta\rVert$, as
$\chi\le1$. The variation is $K\zeta$ for a linear map $K:\g\to\g^8$ with two
nonzero components of norm $\lVert\zeta\rVert$, so $\lVert K\rVert=\sqrt2$
and $JK=\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0)T$. For a unit vector $e\in\g$,
\[
\lVert J^*e\rVert\ge\frac{\lVert K^*J^*e\rVert}{\sqrt2}=\frac{\lVert T^*
\operatorname{Ad}(\ell_0)^*e\rVert}{\sqrt2}\ge\frac{1-\frac78\Lambda}
{\sqrt2}=\sigma_0,
\]
since the least singular value of $T$ is at least $1-\frac78\Lambda$.
At the other points of differentiability the same bound follows by
continuity: the cut-off has finitely many smooth branch formulas, at such a
point the formulas of the adjacent full-dimensional branches agree with its
differential, and the lower bound on the singular value is preserved under
limits.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:coareabound}
Let $C=(V^\sharp_{y,\mu})_{y\in W,\,\mu}$, as a function of the links of
$A_W$, the other links being fixed. Wherever $C$ is differentiable,
\[
\det\bigl(DC\,DC^*\bigr)^{-1/2}\le\sigma_0^{-4|W|\dim G}<33^{4|W|\dim G}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The private links of distinct pairs are distinct, and each enters only the
average of its pair, so the columns of $DC$ that belong to private links
form a block diagonal matrix with the blocks of
Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion}. Hence $DC\,DC^*\ge\bigoplus_kJ_kJ_k^*
\ge\sigma_0^2$.
\end{proof}

The coarea factor of the constrained law is therefore bounded on the whole
fibre by a constant per block, for every value of the cut-off and however
far the links inside the blocks are from $I$. The volume of the fibre is
bounded through the law of the averages. From here on $G=\SU(2)$, which with
the metric $\lVert X\rVert^2=\Tr(X^*X)$ is the round sphere of radius
$\sqrt2$, $\rho_G=1$, and $h$ is normalised Haar measure.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:averagedensity}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, fix every link other than the private links of $(y,\mu)$,
and let these eight links be independent and Haar distributed. Then the
law of $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ has a density with respect to $h$ that is at most
\[
M=1+2\Bigl(1-\frac78\Lambda\Bigr)^{-3}<2.4\cdot10^4
\]
at every point, in the version given by the formula~\eqref{eq:densityformula}
of the proof.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $g=\ell_0$, and let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be the largest values of
$\delta(v_{x_a},I)$ and of $\delta(v_{x'_a},I)$. Up to the null set
$m=1$, split $G^8$ into the three regions
\begin{gather*}
 R_0=\{m>1\},\\
 R_1=\{m_1\ge m_2,\ m_1<1\},\qquad R_2=\{m_2>m_1,\ m_2<1\};
\end{gather*}
ties between the two families, including two path functions that
coincide identically, belong to $R_1$. On $R_0$, $\chi=0$ and
$V^\sharp=g$.

On $R_1$ use the coordinates $(g,h_1,\dots,h_7)$ with $h_a=v_{x_a}=g^{-1}u_a
\ell_a$. For fixed $g$ the map $\ell_a\mapsto h_a$ is a left translation, so
these coordinates carry product Haar measure, and
\[
v_{x'_a}=g^{-1}\ell_aw_a=g^{-1}u_a^{-1}g\,h_aw_a .
\]
Fix $h$ and put $m_h=\max_a\delta(h_a,I)<1$. The set $S_h$ of $g$ with $(g,h)
\in R_1$ is the measurable set where $\delta(v_{x'_a},I)\le m_h$ for every $a$; on it
$m=m_h$, so $\chi=\phi(m_h)$ does not depend on $g$, and $V^\sharp=g\,e^{\chi
N(g)}$ with $N(g)=\frac1{16}\sum_a(\log h_a+\log v_{x'_a})$. The set
$\{\delta(v,I)<1\}$ is the ball of angular radius $\alpha$ about $I$ on the
sphere, which is geodesically convex, and on it $\lVert\log v-\log v'\rVert
\le\Lambda\,d(v,v')$. By bi-invariance $d(g^{-1}u^{-1}g,g'^{-1}u^{-1}g')\le
2d(g,g')$, so for $g,g'\in S_h$
\[
\lVert N(g)-N(g')\rVert\le\frac7{16}\,2\Lambda\,d(g,g')=\frac78\Lambda\,
d(g,g').
\]
If $V^\sharp(g)=V^\sharp(g')=c$, then $g=c\,e^{-\chi N(g)}$ and $g'=c\,
e^{-\chi N(g')}$, so $d(g,g')\le\frac78\Lambda\,d(g,g')$ and $g=g'$: the map
$g\mapsto V^\sharp(g)$ is injective on $S_h$. Its derivative is computed as
in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion}: with $\eta=\operatorname
{Ad}(g)\zeta$ the sites $x'_a$ move by $e^{t(A_a-1)\zeta}$, $A_a=
\operatorname{Ad}(g^{-1}u_a^{-1}g)$, the sites $x_a$ do not move, and the
right trivialised derivative is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)T$ with $\lVert T-1
\rVert\le\frac7{16}\,2\Lambda=\frac78\Lambda$, so its determinant is at
least $(1-\frac78\Lambda)^3$ in modulus. On $R_2$ the coordinates $(g,h'_1,
\dots,h'_7)$ with $h'_a=v_{x'_a}=g^{-1}\ell_aw_a$ and $v_{x_a}=g^{-1}u_ag
\,h'_aw_a^{-1}$ give the same conclusions.

For fixed $h$, the smooth formula with $\chi=\phi(m_h)$ fixed extends to
a neighbourhood of each point of $S_h$, where no logarithm meets $-I$; its
restriction to the measurable set $S_h$ is injective and has the Jacobian
bounds above. The change of variables formula for measurable restrictions
therefore applies, even if part of the boundary of $S_h$ has positive
measure, and likewise on $R_2$. The law of $V^\sharp$ has the density
\begin{multline}\label{eq:densityformula}
\rho(c)=h^{\otimes7}\bigl(\{\ell:(c,\ell)\in R_0\}\bigr)\\
+\sum_{i=1,2}\int\sum_{g\in S^{(i)}_h,\ V^\sharp=c}\frac{dh^{\otimes7}}
{\lvert\det DV^\sharp(g)\rvert},
\end{multline}
the inner sum having at most one term, and $\rho(c)\le1+2(1-\frac78\Lambda
)^{-3}$. Finally $1-\frac78\Lambda=0.04391\ldots$ and $M=23621\ldots$.
\end{proof}

The four averages of a block depend on disjoint sets of private links, and
on the links inside the blocks, which are private to none. So, given the
links inside the blocks of $W$, the averages $V^\sharp_k$ are independent,
and the formula~\eqref{eq:densityformula} for each pair defines, for every
value $c$ of $C$, a measure $\nu_c$ on the fibre $F_c=C^{-1}(c)$: in the
coordinates of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity}, chosen for each
pair according to its region, it is the product Haar measure of the links
inside the blocks and of the seven coordinates other than $g$, divided by
the product of the determinants $\lvert\det DV^\sharp_k(g)\rvert$. Then
$h=\int\nu_c\,dh(c)$ on $G^{A_W}$, so $\nu_c$ is a version of the
conditional law, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibrevolume}
\nu_c(F_c)\le M^{4|W|}\qquad\text{for every }c.
\end{equation}
Where $C$ is differentiable,
\[
\nu_c=\operatorname{vol}(G)^{-45|W|}\det\bigl(DC\,DC^*\bigr)^{-1/2}\,
d\mathcal H .
\]
Indeed, if $C(z,g)=c$ is solved for $g$ by $g=\psi(z)$, then $DC=\partial_g
C\,(-D\psi,\,1)$, so
\[
\det\bigl(DC\,DC^*\bigr)^{1/2}=\lvert\det\partial_gC\rvert\det\bigl(1+
D\psi^*D\psi\bigr)^{1/2},
\]
and the second factor is the Jacobian of the graph of $\psi$. So
$\nu_c$ is the coarea version on the charts of
Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart} and~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, where $C$ is smooth,
and we use it on the whole fibre.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:calmfibre}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$ and $0<K\le10^{-8}$, and let $n_P\le384|W|$ be the
number of plaquettes that contain a link of $A_W$. Suppose the fibre $F$
contains a field $U$ with $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every plaquette $p$
with a vertex in a block of $W^+$, where $\kappa\le K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$. Then
the constrained law $\mu_U$ on $F$ gives the set of fields with a
plaquette $p$ with a vertex in a block of $W^+$ and $\delta(U'_p,I)>K$ mass at
most
\[
\varepsilon_W(K,\lambda)=\Bigl(\frac{2\cdot10^9\,n_P^{3/2}}{K^3}\Bigr)
^{45|W|}e^{-3\lambda K^2/4}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $c=C(U)$, let $B$ be the set in question, and let $Q_W$ be the sum of
$\delta(U'_p,I)^2$ over the $n_P$ plaquettes that contain a link of $A_W$; on
$F$ it differs from $Q$ by a constant, so $\mu_U=e^{-\lambda Q_W}\nu_c/
\nu_c(e^{-\lambda Q_W})$. A plaquette that contains no link of $A_W$ has
$U'_p=U_p$ for $U'\in F$, so on $B$ the large plaquette is one of the $n_P$
and $Q_W>K^2$. By~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume},
\[
\int_Be^{-\lambda Q_W}\,d\nu_c\le M^{4|W|}e^{-\lambda K^2}.
\]

For the denominator we solve the constraints for the path links. Let
$L'=A_W\setminus\{d_k\}$, $\rho=K/(360\sqrt{n_P})$ and $R=44\rho$, and let
$D$ be the set of $z\in G^{L'}$ with $d(z_e,U_e)\le\rho$ for every $e\in L'$.
The field $U$ satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}, as
$\kappa\le K/4$, and part (i) of the lemma gives $\delta(U_e,I)\le3\kappa$ for
the links inside the blocks and $\delta(U_e,U_{d_k})\le21\kappa$ for the
private links of $k$, so $\delta(v_x,I)\le24\kappa$ and, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, $d(v_x,I)\le8\pi\kappa$ at every site of every
pair. Fix $z\in D$ and a pair $k$, and let $\ell$ range over the ball $B_k$ of
radius $R$ about $U_{d_k}$. Each $v_x$ is $\ell^{-1}$ times a product of at
most two links of $L'$ and fixed links, so at the field with links $z$ and
$\ell$ it lies within $R+2\rho$ of its value at $U$, and within $8\pi\kappa
+46\rho<0.01$ of $I$. Hence the cut-off equals $1$ near this field and
$V^\sharp_k=\ell\,e^{N_k(\ell)}$, with $N_k$ depending on $z$ and $\ell$. Each
$v_x$ is moved by $d(\ell,\ell')$ when $\ell$ is replaced by $\ell'$, so the
map $\Psi(\ell)=c_k\,e^{-N_k(\ell)}$ satisfies $d(\Psi(\ell),\Psi(\ell'))\le
\frac78\Lambda\,d(\ell,\ell')$. At $U$ the path link solves
$U_{d_k}=c_ke^{-N_k}$, and the sites move by at most $R+2\rho$ between $U$
and the field with links $z$ and $\ell$, so
\[
d\bigl(\Psi(\ell),U_{d_k}\bigr)\le\frac78\Lambda\,(R+2\rho)<0.9561\cdot46
\rho<R .
\]
By the contraction principle $\Psi$ has a
unique fixed point $\psi_k(z)\in B_k$. The path link $d_k$ is private to $k$,
so the field $\Gamma(z)$ with links $z$ on $L'$ and $\psi_k(z)$ on $d_k$ lies
in $F$, and $\Gamma$ is injective.

Near $\Gamma(D)$ every cut-off equals $1$, so $C$ is smooth, and $\partial_g
C$ is block diagonal with the blocks $\partial_{d_k}V^\sharp_k$. Moving
$d_k\mapsto e^{t\eta}d_k$ multiplies every $v_x$ of $k$ by $e^{-t\zeta}$,
$\zeta=\operatorname{Ad}(d_k^{-1})\eta$, so the block is $\operatorname{Ad}
(d_k)(1-E_{N_k}\frac1{16}\sum_xL_{X_x})$, with determinant at most $(1+\frac
78\Lambda)^3<1.957^3$ in modulus. By the identity above, $\nu_c$ restricted
to $\Gamma(D)$ is the image of $h^{\otimes L'}$ on $D$ divided by $\lvert\det
\partial_gC\rvert$, so
\begin{gather*}
\nu_c\bigl(\Gamma(D)\bigr)\ge1.957^{-12|W|}h(B_\rho)^{45|W|},\\
h(B_\rho)=\frac{2\theta-\sin2\theta}{2\pi}\ge\frac{\rho^3}{14},
\end{gather*}
with $\theta=\rho/\sqrt2$ the angular radius, as $2\theta-\sin2\theta\ge
\frac43\theta^3(1-\frac{\theta^2}5)$. A plaquette has at most two path links: two path links $(2y+e_\mu,\mu)$
and $(2y'+e_\mu,\mu)$ of one direction are never opposite sides of a
plaquette, since their bases have exactly one odd coordinate, $\mu$, and
opposite sides differ by $e_\rho$, $\rho\ne\mu$; two of different
directions can be adjacent sides. So on $\Gamma(D)$ each plaquette moves
by at most $2R+2\rho=90\rho$ and $\delta(U'_p,I)\le\kappa+90\rho\le K/(2\sqrt{n_P})$.
Hence $Q_W\le K^2/4$ there and
\[
\int_Fe^{-\lambda Q_W}\,d\nu_c\ge e^{-\lambda K^2/4}\,1.957^{-12|W|}
\Bigl(\frac{\rho^3}{14}\Bigr)^{45|W|}.
\]
Dividing,
\[
\mu_U(B)\le\bigl(M^41.957^{12}\bigr)^{|W|}\Bigl(\frac{14\cdot360^3n_P^{3/2}}
{K^3}\Bigr)^{45|W|}e^{-3\lambda K^2/4},
\]
and $(M^41.957^{12})^{1/45}<2.93$, $2.93\cdot14\cdot360^3<2\cdot10^9$. Finally $n_P\le384|W|$, since each plaquette
that contains a link of $A_W$ has the base of that link, a site of a block of
$W$, as a vertex, and each site is a vertex of $24$ plaquettes.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:calmfibres}
In addition to the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre}, assume
those of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} with $K$ in place of $\kappa$, and
$s\ge1.24\cdot10^5K$. Then $\mu_U(F\setminus\Phi_U(\Omega_r))\le
\varepsilon_W(K,\lambda)$, and for $X_1,X_2\subset A_W$ and $\tilde F,\tilde G$
as in Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}\textup{(iii)},
\[
\lvert\Cov_{\mu_U}(\tilde F,\tilde G)\rvert\le\Bigl(\frac{c_9}\lambda e^{-
\alpha_Gd(X_1,X_2)}+30\,\varepsilon_W(K,\lambda)\Bigr)\lvert X_1\rvert\,
\lvert X_2\rvert .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The field $U$ satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes} with
$K$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(i) with $K$ in place of $\kappa$ puts
every point of $F$ outside $\Phi_U(\Omega_r)$ in the set of
Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre}. The covariance bound follows as in the
proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(iii).
\end{proof}

So the constrained law decorrelates on every fibre through a field whose
plaquettes near $W$ are at most $K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$, with no average over
fibres, once $\lambda K^2$ is a large multiple of $|W|\log(n_P/K)$; with
$K<4.9\cdot10^{-18}$ this needs $\beta_W$ above $1.4\cdot10^{39}|W|$ under the
Wilson measure. The restriction is on the fibre: the links off $A_W$ are
fixed on it, so a fibre whose boundary links carry a large plaquette near
$W$ contains no such field, and neither may a fibre with small boundary
links, and the proposition does not cover these fibres. It is a lower bound
for the fibre measure near one good field against an upper bound for the
whole fibre; it does not compare different fibres.

The hypothesis on $U$ enters the proof twice: through
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}, to place the sixteen sites $v_x$ of every pair
near $I$, and through the bound on $Q_W$ near $U$. Neither needs the links
off $A_W$ or the links inside the blocks to be small, and every fibre
contains a field at which the sites are exactly $I$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:alignedfield}
For every value $c$ of $C$ and every choice of the links off $A_W$, the
fibre $F_c$ contains a field at which $v_x=I$ for every site $x$ of every
pair $(y,\mu)$, $y\in W$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix $\mu$. The links of $A_W$ in the direction $\mu$ are, for each $y\in
W$, the links $u_a$ and $\ell_a$ of the pair $(y,\mu)$, and the links $w_a$
of that pair are the links $u_a$ of the pair $(y+e_\mu,\mu)$ when $y+e_\mu
\in W$, and fixed links otherwise. Whether $u_a$ is a tree link depends only
on the offset, so $u_a$ and $w_a$ are both tree links or neither. For a pair
with path link $g$ and given links $w_a$ put $\ell_0=g$ and, for $a\ne0$,
\[
\ell_a=g,\quad\text{or}\quad\ell_a=g\,w_a^{-1},\ u_a=g\,w_a\,g^{-1},
\]
the first when $u_a$ is a tree link and the second otherwise. Then $v_{x_a}
=g^{-1}u_a\ell_a=I$ and $v_{x'_a}=g^{-1}\ell_aw_a=I$, as $u_a=w_a=I$ in the
first case. The blocks of $W$ along a line in the direction $\mu$ form runs
$y_1,\dots,y_n$ of consecutive blocks. If $y_n+e_\mu\notin W$, choose the
links of the pairs $(y_n,\mu),\dots,(y_1,\mu)$ in this order, with $g=c_{y_j,
\mu}$, the links $w_a$ of $(y_j,\mu)$ being the fixed links for $j=n$ and the
links $u_a$ just chosen for $(y_{j+1},\mu)$ otherwise. If the run closes up
around the torus, put $u_a=I$ and $\ell_a=g$ for every pair of the run. At
the resulting field every $v_x$ equals $I$, so the cut-off equals $1$, $N=0$
and $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}=\ell_0=c_{y,\mu}$. The directions do not interact,
since the pairs $(y,\mu)$ use only links in the direction $\mu$.
\end{proof}

Call a field $U\in F$ \emph{regular} if $\delta(v_x,I)\le\frac14$ at every site
$x$ of every pair, and let $q(F)$ be the infimum of $Q_W$ over the regular
fields of $F$, finite by Lemma~\ref{lem:alignedfield}. Write $\mu_F=e^{-\lambda
Q_W}\nu_c/\nu_c(e^{-\lambda Q_W})$ for the constrained law on $F=F_c$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:everyfibre}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$ and $0<t\le1$. For every fibre $F$, whatever the
links off $A_W$, and every regular $U\in F$,
\begin{gather*}
\mu_F\bigl(\{U'\in F:Q_W(U')>Q_W(U)+t\}\bigr)\le\varepsilon'_W(t,
\lambda),\\
\varepsilon'_W(t,\lambda)=\Bigl(\frac{3.5\cdot10^{11}\,n_P^3}{t^3}\Bigr)
^{45|W|}e^{-3\lambda t/4}.
\end{gather*}
In particular $\mu_F(\{Q_W>q(F)+t\})\le\varepsilon'_W(t,\lambda)$ on every
fibre.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The numerator is bounded by~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume} as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre}, by $M^{4|W|}e^{-\lambda(Q_W(U)+t)}$. For
the denominator take $\rho=t/(2040\,n_P)\le10^{-3}$, $R=44\rho$, and $D$ and
$B_k$ as in that proof. At the field with links $z\in D$ on $L'$ and $\ell\in
B_k$ on $d_k$, each $v_x$ of the pair $k$ lies within $R+2\rho=46\rho<0.043$
of its value at $U$, and $\delta\le d$, so $\delta(v_x,I)<\frac14+0.043<
\frac12$. Hence the cut-off equals $1$ near this field, the logarithms are
$\Lambda$-Lipschitz along the moves, and the contraction argument of that
proof gives the injective map $\Gamma:D\to F$, near whose image $C$ is smooth
with $\lvert\det\partial_gC\rvert\le1.957^{3\cdot4|W|}$. So
\[
\nu_c\bigl(\Gamma(D)\bigr)\ge1.957^{-12|W|}\Bigl(\frac{\rho^3}{14}\Bigr)
^{45|W|}.
\]
On $\Gamma(D)$ each of the $n_P$ plaquettes moves by at most $90\rho$, as in that proof, and
$\delta(U_p,I)\le2\sqrt2$, so
\begin{multline*}
\delta(U'_p,I)^2\le\delta(U_p,I)^2+180\cdot2\sqrt2\,\rho+90^2\rho^2\\
<\delta(U_p,I)^2+510\rho,
\end{multline*}
and $Q_W\le Q_W(U)+510n_P\rho=Q_W(U)+\frac t4$ there. Dividing as before,
\begin{multline*}
\mu_F(\{Q_W>Q_W(U)+t\})\\
\le\bigl(M^41.957^{12}\bigr)^{|W|}\Bigl(\frac{14\cdot2040^3n_P^3}{t^3}
\Bigr)^{45|W|}e^{-3\lambda t/4},
\end{multline*}
and $2.93\cdot14\cdot2040^3<3.5\cdot10^{11}$. For the last statement apply
this to regular fields with $Q_W(U)$ decreasing to $q(F)$ and use the
continuity of $\varepsilon'_W$ in $t$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:everyfibre}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$ and $0<K\le1$. Suppose the fibre $F$ contains a
regular field $U$ with $\delta(U_p,I)\le K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$ on every plaquette
$p$ that contains a link of $A_W$, whatever the plaquettes made of fixed
links. Then $\mu_F$ gives the fields with such a plaquette above $K$ mass at
most $\varepsilon'_W(\frac{15}{16}K^2,\lambda)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
At $U$, $Q_W\le K^2/16$, and a field with one of these plaquettes above $K$
has $Q_W>K^2\ge Q_W(U)+\frac{15}{16}K^2$. Apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:everyfibre} with $t=\frac{15}{16}K^2\le1$.
\end{proof}

The field of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre} is regular, since its sites lie
within $24\kappa$ of $I$, so Corollary~\ref{cor:everyfibre} contains that
proposition up to the constants and drops its hypothesis on the plaquettes
made of fixed links and on the links inside the blocks. It reaches every
fibre whose boundary links carry large plaquettes, provided the sites of the
averages can be made small there together with the plaquettes that move.
Proposition~\ref{prop:everyfibre} holds on every fibre with no hypothesis at
all, but its reference value $q(F)$ need not be small. Where it is of order
one, as it can be when the averages are far from what the boundary links
suggest, the constrained law sits within $t$ of $q(F)$ but away from the
charts of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, which are built at fields
with all plaquettes near $W$ small. The proposition also does not compare
regular with irregular fields, at which some site is far from $I$.

Different fibres with the same links off $A_W$ are compared through the
law of the averages. Call the links off $A_W$ the \emph{exterior} $E$, write
$h$ for product Haar measure on $G^{A_W}$, and let
\[
\pi_E=\frac{e^{-\lambda Q_W}h}{h(e^{-\lambda Q_W})}
\]
on $G^{A_W}$. Under the $\SU(2)$ Wilson measure in the tree gauge, $\pi_E$
with $\lambda=\beta_W/4$ is the conditional law of the links of $A_W$ given
the exterior. Since $h=\int\nu_c\,dh(c)$,
\[
\pi_E=\int\mu_{F_c}\,\frac{\nu_c(e^{-\lambda Q_W})}{h(e^{-\lambda Q_W})}
\,dh(c),
\]
so $\mu_{F_c}$ is the conditional law of $\pi_E$ given $C=c$, and the law
of the fibre through a field drawn from $\pi_E$ is the law of $C$ under
$\pi_E$. Let $Q_*(E)$ be the least value of $Q_W$ on $G^{A_W}$, which is
attained since $G^{A_W}$ is compact.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fibrecompare}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$ and $0<t\le1$. For every exterior $E$,
\begin{gather*}
\pi_E\bigl(\{Q_W>Q_*(E)+t\}\bigr)\le\varepsilon''_W(t,\lambda),\\
\varepsilon''_W(t,\lambda)=\Bigl(\frac{1.05\cdot10^7\,n_P^3}{t^3}\Bigr)
^{49|W|}e^{-3\lambda t/4}.
\end{gather*}
In particular the law of the averages under $\pi_E$ gives the fibres $F$
with $\inf_FQ_W>Q_*(E)+t$ mass at most $\varepsilon''_W(t,\lambda)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $h$ is a probability measure,
\[
\int_{\{Q_W>Q_*+t\}}e^{-\lambda Q_W}\,dh\le e^{-\lambda(Q_*+t)}.
\]
For the normalisation let $U_*$ be a field with
$Q_W(U_*)=Q_*$, let $\rho=t/(90.6\,n_P)$, and let $D$ be the set of fields
with $d(U_e,U_{*,e})\le\rho$ for each of the $49|W|$ links of $A_W$, the
$45|W|$ links of $L'$ and the $4|W|$ path links. Then $h(D)=h(B_\rho)
^{49|W|}\ge(\rho^3/14)^{49|W|}$. Each plaquette contains at most four links
of $A_W$, so on $D$ it moves by at most $4\rho$, and as $\delta\le d$ and
$\delta(U_p,I)\le2\sqrt2$,
\begin{multline*}
\delta(U_p,I)^2\le\delta(U_{*,p},I)^2+16\sqrt2\,\rho+16\rho^2\\
<\delta(U_{*,p},I)^2+22.63\rho,
\end{multline*}
because each link of $A_W$ lies in six plaquettes, so $n_P\ge74$ and $\rho<
1.5\cdot10^{-4}$. Hence $Q_W\le Q_*+22.63\,n_P\rho<Q_*+\frac t4$ on $D$, and
\[
\pi_E\bigl(\{Q_W>Q_*+t\}\bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac{14\cdot90.6^3n_P^3}{t^3}\Bigr)
^{49|W|}e^{-3\lambda t/4},
\]
with $14\cdot90.6^3<1.05\cdot10^7$. A field $U$ with $Q_W(U)\le Q_*+t$ lies
in its own fibre, so $\inf_{F(U)}Q_W\le Q_*+t$, which gives the last
statement.
\end{proof}

Call a field that agrees with $E$ off $A_W$ a \emph{completion} of $E$.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:calmexterior}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$, $0<K\le10^{-8}$ and $\kappa=K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$.
Suppose the exterior $E$ has a completion $U^0$ with $\delta(U^0_p,I)\le
\kappa/(2\sqrt{n_P})$ for every plaquette $p$ with a vertex in a block of
$W^+$. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of completions $U$ with $\delta(U_p,I)\le
\kappa$ for every such plaquette. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\pi_E(\mathcal E^c)\le\varepsilon''_W(\kappa^2/2,\lambda)$;
\item every $U\in\mathcal E$ is regular and its fibre has $q(F(U))<
\kappa^2$, so the law of the averages under $\pi_E$ gives the fibres with
$q(F)\ge\kappa^2$, among them every fibre where $q(F)$ is of order one, mass
at most $\varepsilon''_W(\kappa^2/2,\lambda)$;
\item if $\lambda$, $s$ and $K$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres}, then for every $U\in\mathcal E$ the
constrained law on $F(U)$ gives the complement of the chart $\Phi_U(
\Omega_r)$ at $U$ mass at most $\varepsilon_W(K,\lambda)$, and its
covariances obey the bound of that corollary.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
(i) $Q_*(E)\le Q_W(U^0)\le n_P\kappa^2/(4n_P)=\kappa^2/4$. If $Q_W(U)\le
Q_*+\kappa^2/2$, then $Q_W(U)\le\frac34\kappa^2$, so every plaquette that
contains a link of $A_W$ has $\delta(U_p,I)<\kappa$, and a plaquette with a
vertex in a block of $W^+$ that contains no link of $A_W$ has the value it
has at $U^0$, at most $\kappa/(2\sqrt{n_P})$. So $\mathcal E^c\subset\{Q_W>
Q_*+\kappa^2/2\}$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:fibrecompare} with $t=
\kappa^2/2\le1$ applies. (ii) A field $U\in\mathcal E$ satisfies the
hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}, which places every site of every
pair within $24\kappa<\frac14$ of $I$, as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre}; so $U$ is regular and $q(F(U))\le Q_W(U)
<\kappa^2$. Hence a fibre with $q(F)\ge\kappa^2$ contains no field of
$\mathcal E$, and the law of the averages gives these fibres at most the mass
$\pi_E(\mathcal E^c)$. (iii) The fibre $F(U)$ contains the field $U$, whose
plaquettes with a vertex in a block of $W^+$ are at most $\kappa=K/(4\sqrt
{n_P})$, which is the hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre};
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres} applies at $U$.
\end{proof}

So on every exterior whose plaquettes near $W$ can all be made small by the
links of $A_W$, the fibres where $q(F)$ is of order one, and more generally
the fibres that contain no field with small plaquettes near $W$, carry total
mass at most $\varepsilon''_W(\kappa^2/2,\lambda)$ in the law of the
averages, and every other fibre has the chart decay of
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres}. This is a bound for every such exterior,
not a mean over exteriors as in Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(ii). If
$\lambda\kappa^2\ge196|W|\ln(8.4\cdot10^7n_P^3/\kappa^6)$, then
$\varepsilon''_W(\kappa^2/2,\lambda)\le e^{-\lambda\kappa^2/8}$; with
$n_P\le384|W|$ and $K=4.8\cdot10^{-18}$ this holds under the Wilson measure
for $\beta_W\ge6.4\cdot10^{43}|W|^2(1+\ln|W|)$. The fibres where $q(F)$ is of
order one remain possible in two places: on an exterior with no completion
whose plaquettes near $W$ are small, and as values of $c$ of small mass on
an exterior with one.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:chartdecayopen}
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} is the decay that
Remark~\ref{rem:fibrechartopen}(b) asks for, on the chart $\Phi(\Omega_r)$
with $r=s/32$, which contains $\Phi(K_{s/32})$ and so every $Ue^X\in F$
with $\lVert X\rVert_\infty\le s/1280$. Its constants are explicit by
Propositions~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} and~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}:
the rate $\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$ is the same for every group and lies far
below the decay seen in the computation described at the end of this remark.
What remains open for the small fields:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item the mass of the constrained law outside $\Phi(\Omega_r)$ on the
fibres that contain no field whose plaquettes near $W$ are small:
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres} bounds it on every fibre that contains one,
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmexterior} shows that on every exterior with a
completion whose plaquettes near $W$ are small these fibres, among them those
where $q(F)$ is of order one, have mass at most $\varepsilon''_W$ in the law
of the averages, and Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart} bounds them in mean over all
exteriors; the constrained cube condition of
Remark~\ref{rem:constrainedopen}(a) takes a supremum over boundary
conditions, which include these fibres of small mass and the exteriors with
no such completion, and on them no chart of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} is
available; by Proposition~\ref{prop:calmrare} these are the typical case on
cubes of fixed physical size along the tuning;
\item the passage from the decay of the constrained law on one fibre, at
a fixed background, to the constrained cube condition of
Remark~\ref{rem:constrainedopen}(a), whose supremum runs over boundary
conditions that include large fields.
\end{enumerate}
On the periodic lattice of side twelve, for $\SU(2)$ backgrounds as in the
check of Theorem~\ref{thm:smallfibre} and $W$ a row of five blocks, the
section $S$ has row sums at most $14$, the blocks of $\bar P$ beyond the
range of $S$ decay by a factor about $0.4$ per unit of distance, and the
blocks of the chart Hessian of $Q$ fall from $15$ at distance zero to
$10^{-8}$ at distance nine, a floating-point computation reproduced in the
archive.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Large fields under the Wilson measure}\label{ssec:largefields}

Theorem~\ref{thm:smallscales} needs every plaquette to be small. This
subsection shows that, under the $\SU(2)$ Wilson measure, the plaquettes
that are not small form clusters of microscopic size, and that the cut-off
average departs from the average only next to them. It also shows that
such plaquettes are present along the one-loop tuning, so the composition
has to pass through them.

Let $\Lambda_L=(\Z/L\Z)^4$ with $L=2^m\ge4$, and let $\mu_L$ be the $\SU(2)$
Wilson measure on $\Lambda_L$, with density proportional to $e^{-\beta_W
S(U)}$ with respect to product Haar measure, where
\[
S(U)=\sum_ps_p,\qquad s_p=1-\tfrac12\Tr U_p=\tfrac14\,\delta(U_p,I)^2 .
\]
This is the Wilson measure of Sec.~\ref{sec:state} on the torus, without
gauge fixing; it has $4L^4$ links and $6L^4$ plaquettes. For $0<\rho\le1$ call a
plaquette \emph{bad} if $\delta(U_p,I)>\rho$. The closed unit cube $\mathcal
C_x=x+[0,1]^4$ contains $24$ plaquettes. Let $B_x$ be the event that one of
them is bad. A plaquette lies in exactly four unit cubes, one for each
choice of the two transverse coordinates of the cube's corner.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:wilsonZ}
Let $Z_L$ be the normalising constant of $\mu_L$ and $C_0=\frac12+\frac23
\log(24\pi^3)$. For $\beta_W\ge1$,
\[
-\log Z_L\le6L^4(\log\beta_W+C_0),\qquad
\E_{\mu_L}S\le6L^4\,\frac{\log\beta_W+C_0}{\beta_W}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $U=\cos\theta\,I+\sin\theta\,J$ with $0\le\theta\le\pi$ and $J^2=-I$.
The angle $\theta$ of $g^{-1}h$ is a bi-invariant distance, and under Haar
measure $\theta$ has density $\frac2\pi\sin^2\theta$. Put $r=(4\sqrt{
\beta_W})^{-1}$. If every link has angle at most $r$, every plaquette has
angle at most $4r\le1$ and $s_p\le(4r)^2/2=1/(2\beta_W)$, so $S\le3L^4$.
Each link angle is at most $r$ with probability
\[
\frac2\pi\int_0^r\sin^2t\,dt\ge\frac{8r^3}{3\pi^3}=\frac1{24\pi^3
\beta_W^{3/2}},
\]
by $\sin t\ge2t/\pi$. Hence $Z_L\ge e^{-3L^4}(24\pi^3\beta_W^{3/2})^{-4L^4}$,
which is the first bound. The function $F(b)=-\log Z_L$ at the coupling $b$
is concave with $F(0)=0$ and $F'(b)=\E S$, so $bF'(b)\le F(b)$, which is
the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:defects}
For $\beta_W\ge1$, $0<\rho\le1$ and every set $A$ of unit cubes,
\begin{gather*}
\mu_L\Bigl(\,\bigcap_{x\in A}B_x\Bigr)\le q^{|A|},\\
q=q_\rho(\beta_W)=\min\bigl\{1,\exp\bigl(6(\log\beta_W+C_0)-\beta_W
\rho^2/16\bigr)\bigr\}.
\end{gather*}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The measure $\mu_L$ is reflection positive in every hyperplane through
sites~\cite{OSei78}: the plaquettes are either in the hyperplane or on one
side of it, so conditionally on the links in the hyperplane the weight
factors into two mirror images, and reflection preserves Haar measure and
$\Tr U_p$. On a torus of side $2^m$ this gives the chessboard estimate for
functions of the links of closed unit cubes~\cite{FILS78}, \cite[Section
5.3]{Bis09}:
\[
\mu_L\Bigl(\,\bigcap_{x\in A}B_x\Bigr)\le\mu_L\Bigl(\,\bigcap_{x\in
\Lambda_L}B_x\Bigr)^{|A|/L^4},
\]
since the reflection of $B_x$ into another cube is the event $B_y$ of that
cube. If every cube is bad, there are at least $L^4/4$ bad plaquettes, so
$S\ge\rho^2L^4/16$ and the event has unnormalised weight at most
$e^{-\beta_W\rho^2L^4/16}$. Dividing by $Z_L$ and using
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ} gives the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:defectclusters}
Join two unit cubes when their corners are at $\ell^\infty$ distance one on
the torus. For an integer $r\ge1$,
\[
\mu_L\{\text{some connected set of $r$ bad cubes}\}\le L^4(6400\,q)^r .
\]
Hence, on a torus of fixed physical side $La$, if $a\to0$ along $L=2^m$ and
$\beta_W(a)\to\infty$, the physical diameters of all connected clusters of
bad cubes tend to $0$ in probability, for every fixed $\rho$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A connected set of $r$ cubes containing a given cube is recovered from a
walk of length $2(r-1)$ around a spanning tree, and each cube has $80$
neighbours, so there are at most $80^{2(r-1)}\le6400^r$ such sets. Apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} and sum over the $L^4$ roots. A cluster of
physical diameter at least $R$ contains a connected set of $\lceil R/a
\rceil$ cubes, and once $6400\,q\le\frac12$ the bound is at most $(La/a)^4
2^{-R/a}\to0$.
\end{proof}

The bad cubes control where the cut-off average differs from the average.
For a coarse link $(y,\mu)$ let $\mathcal Z_{y,\mu}$ be the $24$ unit cubes
with corners $2y+te_\mu+w$, $t\in\{0,1,2\}$, $w\in\{0,1\}^4$, $w_\mu=0$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:largefields}).

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_largefields.png}
\caption{Large fields under the $\SU(2)$ Wilson measure. (a)~A plane section of
the lattice: bad unit cubes (red) form clusters, and the cut-off average can
differ from the path average only on coarse links (orange) whose $24$ cubes
$\mathcal Z_{y,\mu}$ meet a bad cube (Corollary~\ref{cor:activelinks}).
(b)~The frustrated exterior of a link $e$: the staple of $p_0$ is $I$ and the
other five staples are $-I$, so $U_e$ is driven to $-I$ and $p_0$ is bad.
(c)~The weight $q_\rho(\beta_W)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} for three values
of $\rho$; below the dashed line the cluster bound of
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters} is summable.}
\label{fig:largefields}
\end{figure*}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:activelinks}
Let $\rho=\frac1{12}$. If no cube of $\mathcal Z_{y,\mu}$ is bad, then
$\chi_{y,\mu}(U)=1$ in the tree gauge, and $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ is the average
of the sixteen paths in the chart at $P_{2y}$. A bad cube lies in
$\mathcal Z_{y,\mu}$ for at most eight coarse links, so the expected
fraction of coarse links with $\chi<1$ is at most $4.5\cdot10^5\,(\log
\beta_W+C_0)/\beta_W$. Along the limits of Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters},
with probability tending to one these links lie within physical distance
$2a$ of clusters of bad cubes of physical diameter less than any fixed
$R>0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallstep}, $P_{2y}^{-1}P_x$ is a
product of at most six conjugates of plaquette holonomies or their
inverses. These plaquettes lie in planes $\{\mu,\alpha\}$ with corners
$2y+te_\mu+w$ as above, and a plaquette lies in the unit cube at its
corner. So $\delta(P_x,P_{2y})\le6\rho=\frac12$, and $\chi=1$. A cube with
corner $z$ lies in $\mathcal Z_{y,\mu}$ only if $z_\mu-2y_\mu\in\{0,1,2\}$
and $z_\alpha-2y_\alpha\in\{0,1\}$ for $\alpha\ne\mu$, which leaves at
most two coarse links in each direction. There are $L^4/4$ coarse links,
the number of bad cubes is at most four times the number of bad
plaquettes, and a bad plaquette has $s_p>\rho^2/4$, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ} the expected fraction is at most $4\cdot8\cdot4
\cdot24\cdot144\,(\log\beta_W+C_0)/\beta_W$. The last assertion is
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters}.
\end{proof}

Small plaquettes everywhere, which Theorem~\ref{thm:smallscales} assumes,
are nevertheless improbable along the one-loop tuning. For $\SU(2)$,
$\beta_W=4g^{-2}$, and the one-loop coupling of
Remark~\ref{rem:constrainedopen}(c) at spacing $a=1/L$ gives $\beta_W=8b_0
\log L+O(1)=\frac{11}{3\pi^2}\log L+O(1)$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:manydefects}
Let $0<\rho\le1$, $v_*=\frac2\pi\int_{\arccos(3/4)}^{\pi/3}\sin^2t\,dt$ and
$p=v_*e^{-3\beta_W}$. Conditionally on all other links, a plaquette through
a link $e$ is bad with probability at least $p$. Hence
\[
\mu_L\{\text{no plaquette is bad}\}\le e^{-\lfloor L/3\rfloor^4p},
\]
which tends to $0$ when $\beta_W\le B\log L+O(1)$ with $B<4/3$, in
particular along the one-loop tuning.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Identify $\SU(2)$ with the unit quaternions. Conditionally on the other
links, $U_e$ has density proportional to $e^{\kappa\,h\cdot u}$ with
$0\le\kappa\le6\beta_W$ and $|h|=1$, the six staples contributing at most
$\beta_W$ each. The plaquette holonomy is $U_e$ or its inverse multiplied
by a fixed element, so it has a density of the same form. Writing the
density as a superposition of indicators of caps centred at $h$, the
probability of a cap about $I$ is largest when $h=I$, and for $h=I$ it
increases with $\kappa$, because its derivative is the covariance of an
increasing function of $\Tr U$ with $\frac12\Tr U$. So the probability of
being bad is at least that of the angle exceeding $\arccos(1-\rho^2/4)\le
\arccos(3/4)$ under the density proportional to $e^{6\beta_W\cos t}\sin^2t$,
which is at least $p$: bound the numerator from below on $[\arccos(3/4),
\pi/3]$, where $\cos t\ge\frac12$, and the denominator by $e^{6\beta_W}
\pi/2$.

Let $M=\lfloor L/3\rfloor$. Choose the links in direction $0$ at the sites
$3z$, $z\in\{0,\dots,M-1\}^4$, and their plaquettes in the plane $\{0,1
\}$. No chosen plaquette contains another chosen link. Removing one chosen
link at a time therefore bounds the probability that all chosen plaquettes
are good by $(1-p)^{M^4}$. With $\beta_W=B\log L+O(1)$ the exponent is of order
$L^{4-3B}$.
\end{proof}

The composition of Theorem~\ref{thm:smallscales} is local, so it continues
across the scales away from the defects, and the defects spread by at most
three spacings of the current scale at each step. For a coarse plaquette $P$
at $y$ let $\mathcal B_P$ be the fine box $2y+[0,4]^4$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:localstep}
Let $U$ be a $G$-valued field in the tree gauge and $P$ a coarse plaquette.
If every plaquette $p$ in $\mathcal B_P$ has $\delta(U_p,I)\le\rho_G$ and
$\lVert\Theta_p\rVert\le\eta\le\rho_G/1000$, then $\chi=1$ on the four sides
of $P$, $\delta(V^\sharp(U)_P,I)\le0.03\,\rho_G$, the inequalities
\eqref{eq:smallstep} hold for $P$, and $\lVert\log V^\sharp(U)_P\rVert\le
4(1+647\eta)\eta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For the plaquette $P$ the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallstep} uses only the
plaquettes of the surfaces $\mathcal U_\ell$ of the four sides $\ell$ of $P$
and those of the sixteen squares $\square_{2y+o}$. A plaquette of $\mathcal
U_\ell$, $\ell=(y_i,\mu_i)$, has its corner $x$ at $x_{\mu_i}-2(y_i)_{\mu_i}
\in\{0,1,2\}$ and $x_\alpha-2(y_i)_\alpha\in\{0,1\}$ for $\alpha\ne\mu_i$,
with $y_i\in\{y,y+e_\mu,y+e_\nu\}$; a plaquette of $\square_{2y+o}$ has
$x-2y\in\{0,1,2\}^4$. So $x-2y\in\{0,1,2,3\}^4$ in every case, and the
plaquette lies in $\mathcal B_P$. The bounds on $\chi$, on $\delta(V^\sharp_P,
I)$, the inequalities~\eqref{eq:smallstep} and the bound $\lVert\bar F_P
\rVert+3.2\,r_P^2\le4(1+647\eta)\eta$ in that proof use only the norms of
these plaquettes.
\end{proof}

Let $a$ be the fine spacing and $a_j=2^ja$. Given $\eta_0>0$ put $\eta_{j+1}=
4(1+647\eta_j)\eta_j$. Let $\mathfrak B_0$ be the set of fine plaquettes with
$\delta(U_p,I)>\rho_G$ or $\lVert\Theta_p\rVert>\eta_0$, and let $\mathfrak
B_{j+1}$ be the set of plaquettes $P$ of the lattice of spacing $a_{j+1}$
whose box $\mathcal B_P$ contains a plaquette of $\mathfrak B_j$. Let
$E^\circ_j$ and $A^\circ_j$ be the sum of squares and the sum of $\lVert
\Theta^{(j)}_P\rVert$ over the plaquettes $P\notin\mathfrak B_j$ of the
$j$-th iterate.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:defectscales}
Let $G\subset\U(r)$ be compact and $U$ a $G$-valued field on the periodic
lattice of side divisible by $2^k$, and suppose that $\eta_j\le\rho_G/1000$
for $j<k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $j\le k$, every plaquette $P\notin\mathfrak B_j$ of the $j$-th
iterate has $\delta(U^{(j)}_P,I)\le\rho_G$ and $\lVert\Theta^{(j)}_P\rVert
\le\eta_j$. For $j<k$ the cut-off is inactive on the sides of every
plaquette outside $\mathfrak B_{j+1}$, and~\eqref{eq:smallstep} holds
there.
\item Every point of a plaquette of $\mathfrak B_j$ lies within $\ell^\infty$
distance $3(a_j-a)$ of a plaquette of $\mathfrak B_0$.
\item With $\sigma=\sum_{j<k}\eta_j$,
\[
E^\circ_k\le e^{12060\sigma}E^\circ_0,\qquad A^\circ_k\le e^{9147
\sigma}4^{-k}A^\circ_0 .
\]
\item If $4^k\eta_0\le10^{-4}\rho_G$, the hypothesis holds, $\eta_j\le1.023
\cdot4^j\eta_0$ for $j\le k$, $\sigma\le0.35\cdot4^k\eta_0$, and
$E^\circ_k\le1.53\,E^\circ_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) By induction on $j$. If $P\notin\mathfrak B_{j+1}$, no plaquette of
$\mathcal B_P$ lies in $\mathfrak B_j$, so by the induction hypothesis all of
them have $\delta\le\rho_G$ and norm at most $\eta_j\le\rho_G/1000$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:localstep}, applied to the $j$-th iterate in the tree gauge,
gives $\delta(U^{(j+1)}_P,I)\le0.03\,\rho_G$ and $\lVert\Theta^{(j+1)}_P
\rVert\le\eta_{j+1}$; the gauge fixing between steps does not change these
norms.

(ii) Let $P$ at $y$ lie in $\mathfrak B_{j+1}$, and let $p\in\mathfrak B_j$
lie in $\mathcal B_P$, with corner $x$, $x-2y\in\{0,1,2,3\}^4$. In units of
$a_j$ every coordinate of a point of $P$ lies in $[2y_c,2y_c+2]$, and $p$
contains a point whose coordinates are $x_c$ or lie in $[x_c,x_c+1]$; so the
two are at distance at most $3$ in each coordinate. Hence every point of a
plaquette of $\mathfrak B_{j+1}$ is within $3a_j$ of a plaquette of
$\mathfrak B_j$, and $\sum_{i<j}3a_i=3(a_j-a)$.

(iii) Repeat the part \emph{Sums} of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallstep}
with the plaquettes $P\notin\mathfrak B_{j+1}$ only. Their squares
$\square_{2y+o}$ and surfaces $\mathcal U_\ell$ consist of plaquettes outside
$\mathfrak B_j$, so the same counts give $\sqrt{E^\circ_{j+1}}\le(1+6030
\eta_j)\sqrt{E^\circ_j}$ and $A^\circ_{j+1}\le(1+9147\eta_j)A^\circ_j/4$,
and $1+t\le e^t$.

(iv) The recursion gives $\eta_j\le e^{647\sigma_j}4^j\eta_0$ with $\sigma_j=
\sum_{i<j}\eta_i$. Suppose $\sigma_j\le0.35\cdot4^j\eta_0$, which holds at
$j=0$. Then $\sigma_j\le3.5\cdot10^{-5}$, $e^{647\sigma_j}\le1.023$,
$\eta_j\le1.023\cdot4^j\eta_0\le1.023\cdot10^{-4}\rho_G$, and $\sigma_{j+1}
\le1.373\cdot4^j\eta_0\le0.35\cdot4^{j+1}\eta_0$. Finally $e^{12060\cdot
3.5\cdot10^{-5}}\le1.53$.
\end{proof}

Under the Wilson measure the defects of Theorem~\ref{thm:defectscales} are
the bad plaquettes of Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}. For $\SU(2)$, $\rho_G=1$;
a plaquette with $\delta(U_p,I)=2\sqrt2\sin(\theta/2)\le\rho\le\frac1{10}$
has $\lVert\Theta_p\rVert=\sqrt2\,\theta\le1.01\,\delta(U_p,I)$, so with
$\eta_0=1.01\rho$ every plaquette of $\mathfrak B_0$ is bad, and lies in a
bad cube.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:defectscales}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $C_1=C_0+\frac16\log12800$, and for $\beta_W\ge1$ let
$\rho(\beta_W)$ be given by $\rho^2=96(\log\beta_W+C_1)/\beta_W$, so that
$6400\,q_\rho(\beta_W)=\frac12$. Let $k_*$ be the largest integer with
$4^{k_*}\cdot1.01\rho\le10^{-4}$. If $1.01\rho\le10^{-4}$, then $k_*\ge0$,
\[
a_{k_*}\ge1.5\cdot10^{-3}\Bigl(\frac{\beta_W}{\log\beta_W+C_1}\Bigr)^{1/4}a,
\]
and with $\mu_L$-probability at least $1-L^42^{-r}$ every connected cluster
of bad cubes has fewer than $r$ cubes, while for every $j\le k_*$ the
defects of the $j$-th iterate lie within $\ell^\infty$ distance $3a_j$ of
these clusters and the iterate satisfies Theorem~\ref{thm:defectscales}(i),
(iii) with $E^\circ_{k_*}\le1.53\,E^\circ_0$. Along the limits of
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters} with $a\,\rho(\beta_W)^{-1/2}\to0$, which
holds along the one-loop tuning, the defects of all iterates up to the
spacing $a_{k_*}$ lie, with probability tending to one, within clusters of
physical size tending to $0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
With this $\rho$, $q_\rho(\beta_W)=\exp(-\log12800)$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters} gives the probability of a connected set
of $r$ bad cubes at most $L^4(6400q)^r=L^42^{-r}$. By maximality, $4^{k_*+1}
\cdot1.01\rho>10^{-4}$, so $2^{k_*}>\frac12\cdot10^{-2}(1.01\rho)^{-1/2}$,
and $\rho^{-1/2}=96^{-1/4}(\beta_W/(\log\beta_W+C_1))^{1/4}$ with $96^{1/4}
<3.14$. The rest is Theorem~\ref{thm:defectscales} with $\eta_0=1.01\rho$,
whose hypothesis holds by part (iv), and $\mathfrak B_0$ contained in the bad
cubes; the bound $\lVert\Theta_p\rVert\le1.01\,\delta(U_p,I)$ applies since
$\rho\le\frac1{10}$. For the limits take $r=\lceil8\log_2L\rceil$, so that
$L^42^{-r}\le L^{-4}$ and $ra\to0$ for a torus of fixed physical side $La$.
The defects then lie in sets of physical diameter at most $ra+6a_{k_*}$, and
$a_{k_*}\le10^{-2}(1.01\rho)^{-1/2}a\to0$.
\end{proof}

The scale $a_{k_*}$ is of the order $(\beta_W/\log\beta_W)^{1/4}a$, the
order of the cube side that the condition (D) needs by
Proposition~\ref{prop:cubesizeN}. So the cut-off average carries the field
through the defects of the Wilson measure, without spreading them, up to
the scale at which (D) can first hold, but not beyond: past $a_{k_*}$ the
bound $\eta_j\le1.023\cdot4^j\eta_0$ no longer keeps the curvature small.
Along the one-loop tuning $\beta_W$ grows like $\log L$, so $k_*$ grows like
$\frac14\log_2\log L$, a vanishing fraction of the $\log_2L$ scales.

The joint bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} is not a conditional one,
and (D) needs a supremum over boundary conditions. The two differ
genuinely. Fix a link $e$ and a plaquette $p_0$ through it. Put all
links on the six staples of $e$ at $I$, except the middle links of the
five staples other than that of $p_0$, which are $-I$. Then the
conditional density of $U_e$ is proportional to $e^{-2\beta_W\Tr U_e}$,
and $p_0$, whose holonomy is $U_e^{\pm1}$, is bad with conditional
probability tending to $1$ as $\beta_W\to\infty$, for every $\rho<2
\sqrt2$. Nearby exteriors behave the same way. So the clusters of
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters} are small in probability, but the
boundary response of a cube to a frustrated exterior is not small, and the
composition beyond the scale $a_{k_*}$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:defectscales}
and the conditional estimate in (D) remain open.

For exteriors that are calm on the boundary of a box and lie in a maximal
torus, the conditional estimate does hold. Let $R=[0,l]^4$, $l\ge2$, be a
box of $\Lambda_L$ with $l<L$. Its boundary $\partial R$ is a cubical
$3$-sphere. Call a link or plaquette of $R$ a \emph{boundary} link or
plaquette if it lies in $\partial R$, and \emph{inner} otherwise. A
plaquette that contains an inner link lies in $R$, so conditionally on all
other links the inner links have the law
\[
\nu_\eta(dU)=Z_\eta^{-1}\exp\Bigl(-\beta_W\sum_{p\in P^\circ}s_p\Bigr)
\prod_edU_e ,
\]
the product over the inner links, where $P^\circ$ is the set of inner
plaquettes. It depends on the exterior $\eta$ only through the boundary
links. Let $T\subset\SU(2)$ be the diagonal torus of the elements
$\exp(tJ)$, $J=\mathrm{diag}(i,-i)$, and for $u\in\SU(2)$ let $\angle u\in
[0,\pi]$ be its angle, so that $\delta(u,I)=2\sqrt2\sin(\angle u/2)$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:boxextension}
Let $0\le\rho_s<\pi/3$. Suppose the boundary links of $R$ lie in $T$ and
$\angle U_p\le\rho_s$ for every boundary plaquette. Then the inner links
can be chosen in $T$ so that $\angle U_p\le C\rho_s$ for every plaquette of
$R$, where
\[
C=\sqrt3\,(24\cdot13118+9)<5.46\cdot10^5 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write a $T$-valued field as $U_e=\exp(a_eJ)$ with $a_e\in\R/2\pi\Z$. For a
plaquette $p$ let $(da)_p$ be the signed sum of $a$ over its four links, so
that $U_p=\exp((da)_pJ)$. For a boundary plaquette let $\theta_p\in(-\pi,
\pi]$ be the representative of $(da)_p$; then $|\theta_p|=\angle U_p\le
\rho_s$.

\emph{Closedness.} The signed angles of the six plaquettes of a unit
$3$-cube of $\partial R$ add up to $0$ modulo $2\pi$, since each link occurs
twice with opposite signs. Their representatives add up to a number of
modulus at most $6\rho_s<2\pi$, hence to $0$. So $\theta$ is a closed real
$2$-cochain on $\partial R$.

\emph{Lift.} We construct a real $1$-cochain $\alpha$ on the boundary links
with $d\alpha=\theta$ and $|\alpha_e|\le13118\,l\rho_s$. The boundary is the
union of the eight facets $F_i^0=\{x\in R:x_i=0\}$ and $F_i^l=\{x\in R:x_i=
l\}$, each a cube $[0,l]^3$. Take them in the order $F_1^l$, $F_2^l$,
$F_2^0$, $F_3^l$, $F_3^0$, $F_4^l$, $F_4^0$, $F_1^0$, and let $\Gamma_k$ be
the union of the intersections of the $k$-th facet with the earlier ones.
In the cube of the $k$-th facet, $\Gamma_k$ is empty for $k=1$, one face for
$k=2,3$, three faces, two of them opposite, for $k=4,5$, five faces for
$k=6,7$ and all six for $k=8$. So $\Gamma_k$ is contractible or a
$2$-sphere, and its first cellular cohomology vanishes.

On a facet with coordinates $t_1,t_2,t_3$, the axial gauge gives
$\alpha^0$ with $d\alpha^0=\theta$ on the facet. Put $\alpha^0=0$ on the
links in direction $t_3$. Determine $\alpha^0$ on the links in direction
$t_2$ from the plaquettes in the planes $\{t_2,t_3\}$, starting from $0$ at
$t_3=0$. On the links in direction $t_1$ at $t_3=0$, determine it from the
