d{dt}\log D\rvert\le3\cdot3.559/(1-\lambda)<11.87$ on the interval. The
same bounds hold for $\log D_1$ and $\log D_2$ near a tie at the top,
since $D_1$ has the form of type $a$ and $D_2$ the flat form, and $G_1$,
$G_2$ move at speed at most $L$ by the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}(ii).

\emph{The events.} Call the following $77$ conditions on $\xi$ the
\emph{events}: $f_{x_a}=m\in\{\frac12,1\}$; $f_{x_a}=f_{x'_c}=m\in[\frac12,
1]$ with $c\ne a$; and $f_{x_a}=f_{x_c}=m\in[\frac12,1]$ with $c\ne a$,
for $a,c\ne0$. Every $f_x$ moves at speed at most $1+\sigma L$, and at
most one of them is moved directly. So for a difference $h$ of two of them,
or of one of them and a level, $\lvert h\rvert\le\omega\,d(e,e')$ before
the move, if $\xi$ meets the event $h=0$ during the move, with $\omega=1+
2\sigma L<1.1825$.

Fix the coordinates other than $\xi_a$ and use $v=\tilde u_a(G(\xi))\xi_a$
in place of $\xi_a$. At fixed $g$, a unit move of $\xi_a$ moves $v_{x_a}$
and $v_{x'_a}$ at unit speed. As in Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}(i), $Y$ then
moves at speed at most $2\cdot\frac78\sqrt2\,\alpha+\frac18\Lambda<1.9256$,
and $G$ at speed at most $L_\xi=1.9256/(1-\lambda)<2.140$. Since $d(\tilde
u\xi,\tilde u'\xi')$ differs from $d(\xi,\xi')$ by at most $d(\tilde u,
\tilde u')\le\sigma L_\xi\,d(\xi,\xi')$, the map $\xi_a\mapsto v$ is a
bi-Lipschitz bijection of $\SU(2)$, with constants $1\pm0.0946$. It is onto
by invariance of domain, and its inverse multiplies Haar measure by at most
$(1/0.9054)^3<1.348$.

Write $v=\exp(\theta\nu)$ with $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ and $\nu$ a unit
direction. The Haar measure is $\frac2\pi\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ times the
uniform measure in $\nu$. Along a ray of fixed $\nu$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $f_{x_a}=2\sqrt2\sin\frac\theta2$ increases at rate $\sqrt2\cos
\frac\theta2>1.3028$ while $f_{x_a}\le1.1$, that is $\theta\le0.7990$;
\item $\xi_a$ moves at speed at most $\sqrt2/0.9054$, so $f_{x_c}$, $c\ne
a$, which depends on $\xi_a$ only through $G$, moves at rate at most
$\sigma L_\xi\sqrt2/0.9054<0.1478$;
\item $f_{x'_c}$, $c\ne a$, and the levels do not move.
\end{itemize}
For each event, $h=f_{x_a}-f_y$ or $f_{x_a}-\frac12$ or $f_{x_a}-1$
therefore increases at rate at least $1.154$ on $\{0.4\le f_{x_a}\le
1.1\}$, and $\{\lvert h\rvert\le t\}$ meets each ray in an interval of
length at most $2t/1.154$. With $\sin^2\theta\le0.5146$ for $\theta\le
0.7990$, its Haar measure in $v$ is at most $\frac2\pi\cdot0.5146\cdot
\frac2{1.154}\,t<0.5678\,t$, and in $\xi_a$ at most $0.766\,t$. For
$d(e,e')\le0.08$ every $\xi$ that meets an event during the move lies in
such a set with $t=\omega\,d(e,e')$. By Fubini these $\xi$ have Haar
measure at most $77\cdot0.766\cdot1.1825\,d(e,e')<69.75\,d(e,e')$, and for
them $\lvert\log D-\log D'\rvert\le3\log\frac{1+\lambda}{1-\lambda}<
0.6034$.

\emph{The ties.} Let $\xi$ meet no event during the move, with $D$ and
$D'$ defined at $\xi$, and let $C$ be the set of parameters $t$ at which
$\xi$ is a tie at the top of some index. Between two times of $C$ the point
$\xi$ keeps one type or stays flat: the maximal path can change only at an
event, at a tie at the top, or between two paths from points $x'_c$, where
$D$ does not jump. At a time $t_0\in C$ of index $a$, Lemma~\ref{lem:ties}
applies with the inside links as parameters, and the times near $t_0$ in
$C$ are the zeros of the analytic function $t\mapsto h_2$; since no event
occurs, $C$ is closed. If $C$ has an interior point, it is open by
analyticity, so $C=[0,d(e,e')]$; otherwise $C$ is finite. Where $D$ is
defined at a tie at the top, $\kappa_0=0$: if $\ell\ne0$, both branches meet
$G$, so $D_gF_1=D_gF_2$, that is $N\otimes\ell=0$ and $N=0$. Hence $\log D=\log D_1=
\log D_2$ at the ends that lie in $C$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ties}(i) and
the bound on the derivatives,
\[
\lvert\log D-\log D'\rvert\le11.87\,d(e,e')+\sum_{t}1.9811\,\lvert
\nabla h_2\rvert ,
\]
the sum over the times $t\in C$ at which $h_2$ changes sign, the terms
with $\nabla h_2=0$ vanishing; so the sum runs over times $t$ with $\xi\in
Z_a(t)$, the set $Z_a$ at the parameter $t$.

For one index $a$, the set $S=\{(t,\xi):\xi\in Z_a(t)\}$ is locally the
zero set of $H(t,\xi)=h_2$ with $\nabla_\xi H\ne0$, a $C^1$ hypersurface of
$[0,d(e,e')]\times\SU(2)^7$. The area formula for the projection $(t,\xi)
\mapsto\xi$, of Jacobian $\lvert\partial_tH\rvert/\lvert\nabla H\rvert$
on $S$, and the coarea formula for $(t,\xi)\mapsto t$, of Jacobian
$\lvert\nabla_\xi H\rvert/\lvert\nabla H\rvert$ on $S$
\cite[3.2.20, 3.2.22]{Fed69}, give
\[
\int\sum_{t:\,\xi\in Z_a(t)}w\;d\mathrm{vol}(\xi)=\int_0^{d(e,e')}\!\!
\int_{Z_a(t)}w\,\frac{\lvert\partial_tH\rvert}{\lvert\nabla_\xi H\rvert}
\,dH^{20}\,dt
\]
for $w\ge0$. Here $H=f^{(1)}(G_2,\xi)-f^{(2)}$ changes at rate at most
$1+\sigma L<1.0913$, since $G_2$ moves at speed at most $L$, $f^{(1)}$ is
$\sigma$-Lipschitz in $g$, and only the moving link enters directly. With
$w=1.9811\lvert\nabla_\xi H\rvert$ and $d\xi=V^{-7}d\mathrm{vol}$, the
ties of index $a$ contribute at most $1.9811\cdot1.0913\,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}}\,
d(e,e')$, and the seven indices at most $15.134\,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}}\,d(e,e')$.

\emph{Conclusion.} Adding the three parts, with $11.87+0.6034\cdot69.75<
53.96$, gives the first bound. The density of $\hat Q$ is at most $1/(Z
(1-\lambda)^3)\le2.00002\,e^{72\beta_W}/0.7285$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:relnorm},
and $2.00002\cdot53.96/0.7285<148.2$, $2.00002\cdot15.134/0.7285<41.6$.
Since $\lvert\log D-\log D'\rvert$ is at most the sum of its increments
along a subdivision of the geodesic into steps of length at most $0.08$,
and the bound on the density does not depend on the step, \textup{(J)}
holds with the stated $K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[the area of the ties]\label{prop:tiearea}
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}}<\infty$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Identify $\SU(2)$ with the unit sphere of $\R^4$; the metric above is
twice the Euclidean one, so $H^{20}$ is $2^{10}$ times the Euclidean
Hausdorff measure on $\SU(2)^7\subset\R^{28}$. Every object of the
construction is definable in the o-minimal structure $\R_{\mathrm
{an}}$ of restricted analytic functions \cite{Dri86}: $\delta$, $\phi$ and
the maximum are semialgebraic; $\log$ on $\{\ReTr v\ge\frac32\}$, which
contains $\{\delta(v,I)\le1\}$, and $\exp$ on $\{\lVert X\rVert\le1\}$ are
restricted analytic; $N$ may be set to $0$ where $m\ge1$ without changing
$Y=\phi(m)N$; and the graph of $G$ is $\{g\exp Y=c_k\}$. The formula for
$dh_2$ in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ties} is a definable function of $g$,
$\xi$ and the parameters $P=(c_k,(u_b,w_b)_{b\ne0})$, so $Z_a(P)$ is a
definable family over a bounded set of parameters, of $C^1$ submanifolds
of dimension $20$. For an orthogonal projection $\varpi$ of $\mathbb
R^{28}$ onto $\R^{20}$ and $y\in\R^{20}$, the sets $Z_a(P)
\cap\varpi^{-1}(y)$ form a definable family with parameters $(P,\varpi,
y)$, so those that are finite have at most $\mathfrak b$ points, with
$\mathfrak b$ independent of $(P,\varpi,y)$ \cite[Ch.~3]{Dri98}; and for
fixed $(P,\varpi)$ the $y$ with an infinite fibre form a definable set of
dimension at most $19$ \cite[Ch.~4]{Dri98}, which is Lebesgue-null. By
the integralgeometric formula, $H^{20}(Z)$ equals a constant depending only
on $(28,20)$ times the average over $\varpi$ of $\int\#(Z\cap\varpi^{-1}
(y))\,dy$ \cite[2.10.15, 3.2.26]{Fed69}, and $\varpi(Z)$ lies in the ball
of radius $\sqrt7$. So $H^{20}(Z_a(P))$ is bounded uniformly in $P$ and
$a$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[condition (J)]\label{thm:jholds}
Let $k$, $B$ and the move be as in Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:relresponse}},
with $d(u_a,I),d(w_a,I)\le\frac1{32}$ for $a\ne0$ along the geodesic. Then
\textup{(J)} holds with $K=(148.2+41.6\,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}})\,e^{72\beta_W}$, where
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}}<\infty$ does not depend on $k$, $c_k$, the inside links or
$\beta_W$. In particular \textup{(J)} holds for $B^{\mathrm{bad}}_r$ on
every configuration that the labels produce.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:jreduce} and Proposition~\ref{prop:tiearea}; the
last statement by Proposition~\ref{prop:eightlabels}.
\end{proof}

The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:tiearea} gives no value for $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tie}}$:
the number $\mathfrak b$ comes from o-minimality. The weight $\lvert\log
D_1-\log D_2\rvert$ in the flux cannot be dropped, since the near-ties need
not be thin.

\begin{proposition}[thick near-ties]\label{prop:thickties}
Fix $a\ne0$, let $u_a=w_a=u$ with $d(u,I)=s\le\frac1{32}$, the other
inside links within $\frac1{32}$ of $I$, and let $T(t)$ be the set of $\xi$
with
\[
\lvert f_{x_a}-f_{x'_a}\rvert\le t,\qquad f_{x_a}\ge m-t,\qquad\tfrac12
-t\le f_{x_a}\le1+t .
\]
Then $T(t)$ contains the open set $U_0=\{\xi:\frac{17}{32}<\delta(\xi_a,I)
<\frac{31}{32},\ \delta(\xi_b,I)<\frac{15}{32}\text{ for }b\ne a\}$ for
every $t\ge2s$, for every $c_k$. For $s=0$ every point of $U_0$ is a tie
at the top of index $a$, and $\nabla h_2=0$ there.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $\delta(v,I)=\lVert v-I\rVert$ and $\lVert\tilde u-I\rVert=\lVert
u-I\rVert\le s$, $\lvert f_{x_a}-\delta(\xi_a,I)\rvert\le s$ and $\lvert
f_{x'_a}-\delta(\xi_a,I)\rvert\le s$, using $\delta(\xi_au,I)=\delta(u
\xi_a,I)$; so on $U_0$ both lie in $(\frac12,1)$ and differ by at most
$\lVert\tilde u-u\rVert\le2s$. For $b\ne a$, $f_{x_b},f_{x'_b}\le
\delta(\xi_b,I)+\frac1{32}<\frac12$, and the paths of offset zero give $0$.
So $m=\max(f_{x_a},f_{x'_a})$ and $f_{x_a}\ge m-2s$. For $s=0$, $f_{x_a}=
f_{x'_a}=\delta(\xi_a,I)$ on $U_0$, so $h_2$ vanishes on the open set
$U_0$.
\end{proof}

So no bound $\operatorname{Haar}(T(t))\le Mt$ holds with $M$ uniform in
the inside links, nor one by $t\lvert\log t\rvert$: the Haar measure of
$T(2s)$ is at least that of $U_0$ as $s\to0$. At $s=0$ the jump vanishes,
since $\ell=0$ when $u_a=I$.

The other inside links of the two blocks are not $\mu$-links, do not
enter $V^\sharp_k$, and lie in at most one plaquette with a private link;
the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly} applies to them unchanged and
bounds the response to each of them by $8\beta_W$ for every $B$. So the
response of the law of the eight private links to every inside link is
bounded, with the constants of Theorem~\ref{thm:relresponse}, as soon as
the Jacobian condition (J) holds: for $B^{\mathrm{bad}}_r$ on every
configuration that the labels produce, since there $d(u_a,I),d(w_a,I)\le r$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:eightlabels}, and for $\SU(2)^7$ on every
configuration whose links $u_a$ lie within $\frac1{32}$ of $I$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:jholds} proves (J) there whenever the links $w_a$ also
lie within $\frac1{32}$ of $I$, in particular for $B^{\mathrm{bad}}_r$;
for $\SU(2)^7$ with some $w_a$ farther from $I$ it is not proved. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}(iii), $D$ lies in $[0.728,1.332]$ for all inside
links, so (J) asks only for its continuity in the mean. The derivative of
$Y=\chi N$ in $g$ contains $N\otimes\phi'(m)D_gm$, and $D_gm$ vanishes when
the largest $\delta(v_x,I)$ is attained at a path from $x'_a$, which does
not depend on $g$; so $D$ jumps across the sets where the maximal path
passes between a path from some $x_a$ and another path while $\frac12<m<1$,
and these sets move with the inside links. Off them $D$ is a smooth
function of the inside links. Condition (J) is the statement that the
$\hat Q$-mass swept by these sets, weighted by the jumps of $\log D$, is
of order $d(e,e')$. The last part of the theorem shows that the obstruction
needs both blocks: if all the inside links of one of them are $I$, the law
responds boundedly to every inside link of the other, without (J). For the
sets $B_\varepsilon$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:eightlinkuniform}, whose inside
links are within $\frac1{32}$ of $I$, Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart} applies and
the fibre is a graph over $\xi$; the bound fails there through the
restricting set, whose boundary is not in the good shell and whose
normaliser tends to zero with $\varepsilon$. For the first set the chart
is available whenever $\sigma_u<1/\kappa$ or $\sigma_w<1/\kappa$, by the
last part of Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}, and the response is then bounded
under (J) in that chart. A chart based at another path does not remove the
condition: with $h=P_{x_b}=u_b\ell_b$ as base and $\xi_a=h^{-1}\ell_a$
($a\ne b$), $\xi_0=h^{-1}g$, the paths are $v_{x_a}=\xi_0^{-1}(h^{-1}u_a
h)\xi_a$, $v_{x'_a}=\xi_0^{-1}\xi_aw_a$, $v_{x_b}=\xi_0^{-1}$ and $v_{x'_b}=
\xi_0^{-1}(h^{-1}u_b^{-1}h)w_b$, the equation $V^\sharp_k=c_k$ reads $h=
c_k\exp(-\chi N)\,\xi_0^{-1}$, and $h$ enters only through $\operatorname
{Ad}(h)$ on the $u_a$, with the contraction constant $\kappa\sigma_u$ again;
basing at $h=P_{x'_b}$ with $\xi_a=\ell_ah^{-1}$ leads in the same way to
$\operatorname{Ad}(h)$ on the $w_a$ and to $\kappa\sigma_w$. When $\sigma_u
\ge1/\kappa$ and $\sigma_w\ge1/\kappa$ the argument of
Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}(i) gives no contraction in these charts, and
nothing is proved. The jumps of $D$ come from the two operations in the
definition of $\chi_{y,\mu}$ before~\eqref{eq:cutoff} that are not
differentiable, the function $\phi$ and the maximum over the sites; that
definition is made in this paper, and every result on the cut-off average
is proved for it. What the cube condition uses can instead be taken from
the site, in a form whose units do not overlap.

The sites of two consecutive bad pairs along $\mu$ share seven inside
links, so the sites themselves do not partition the bad side. The
following units do.

\begin{definition}\label{def:linechain}
Fix a direction $\mu$ and a line of blocks $y_j=y_0+je_\mu$, and join two
bad blocks $y_j,y_{j'}$ of the line when $|j-j'|\le2$. For a connected set
of bad blocks of the line, with smallest index $j_0$ and largest $j_1$,
its \emph{chain} $\mathcal C$ is the set of the following links: the eight
private links of each pair $k_j=(y_j,\mu)$ with $y_j$ bad; the active inside
$\mu$-links of the blocks $y_j$, $j_0\le j\le j_1+1$; and the path links of
the pairs $k_j$, $j_0-1\le j\le j_1+1$, with $y_j$ good. The pairs $k_j$,
$j_0-1\le j\le j_1+1$, are the pairs of the chain, \emph{inner} when $y_j$
is bad and \emph{outer} otherwise. The cost on $\mathcal C$ is $\sum_{e
\in\mathcal C}\delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[the law of a chain]\label{prop:linechain}
Let $r\le\frac1{32}$, let $\mathcal C$ be a chain with $n_b$ inner pairs,
and suppose that the non-path links of every outer pair $k_j$ are within
$r$ of $c_{k_j}$ and the active inside $\mu$-links of the blocks
$y_{j_0-1}$ and $y_{j_1+2}$ within $r$ of $I$. Let $E$ be a measurable set
of values of the links of $\mathcal C$ contained in $\{d(e,I)\le r\}$ for
every inside link $e\in\mathcal C$ of a block $y_j$ with $y_{j-1}$ or $y_j$
good.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Distinct chains, of the same or of different lines and directions,
are disjoint. Every link of $\mathcal C$ is based in a block at
$\ell^\infty$ distance at most one from a bad block of its connected set,
and the cut-off averages that contain a link of $\mathcal C$ are those of
the pairs of the chain.
\item The law of $\mathcal C$ given the other links $\sigma$, the
constraints $V^\sharp_{k_j}=c_{k_j}$ of the pairs of the chain and $E$ is
\[
\frac1Z\,e^{-\beta_WS}\mathbf 1_E\,J_{\mathcal C}^{-1}\mathrm{vol}_{M_
{\mathcal C}}\prod_{k_j\text{ outer}}\frac{\delta_{\Gamma_j}(d\ell_0^{(j)})}
{\lvert\det D_{\ell_0^{(j)}}V^\sharp_{k_j}\rvert},
\]
where $M_{\mathcal C}$ is the set where the constraints of the inner pairs
hold, in the links of $\mathcal C$ other than the outer path links
$\ell_0^{(j)}$, $J_{\mathcal C}\ge\sigma_0^{3n_b}$ almost everywhere, each
$\Gamma_j$ is the unique solution of Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} for
$k_j$, and the determinants lie in $[(1-\kappa_0)^3,(1+\kappa_0)^3]$.
\item If $\sigma,\sigma'$ differ only at one link $e'\notin\mathcal C$,
then for the law $\pi$ of (ii) and $n=|\mathcal C|$,
\[
W_1\bigl(\pi(\cdot\mid\sigma),\pi(\cdot\mid\sigma')\bigr)\le C_{e'}\,
d(\sigma_{e'},\sigma'_{e'})
\]
for the cost on $\mathcal C$, with $C_{e'}=n\,n_p(e')\beta_W$ if $e'$
enters only the Wilson weight, $n_p(e')\le6$ the number of its plaquettes
that contain a link of $\mathcal C$;
\[
C_{e'}=\sqrt2\,n(5.793\beta_W+64.94)+1.1986
\]
if $e'$ is a non-path link of an outer pair; and
\[
C_{e'}=\sqrt2\,n(2.543\beta_W+32.47)+0.5993
\]
if $e'$ is an active inside $\mu$-link of $y_{j_0-1}$ or $y_{j_1+2}$. The
constants do not depend on the $c_{k_j}$, on $E$ or on the rest of
$\sigma$.
\item $n=8n_b+p_\mu(j_1-j_0+2)+(j_1-j_0+3-n_b)\le7n_b+8(j_1-j_0)+17\le
23n_b+1$. For one inner pair and $p_\mu=7$, $\mathcal C$ is the site
$\mathcal S_k$, and (ii), (iii) are Lemma~\ref{lem:sitelaw} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:site}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) A chain for $\mu$ consists of $\mu$-links. A private link belongs to
one pair and an inside link to one block, so chains of different lines are
disjoint. On one line two connected sets satisfy $j'_0\ge j_1+3$, so the
pairs $j_0-1,\dots,j_1+1$ and the blocks $j_0,\dots,j_1+1$ of the first and
those of the second are disjoint. The links of $\mathcal C$ are based in
the blocks $y_j$, $j_0-1\le j\le j_1+1$, and each such block is bad or
adjacent to a bad block of the set, gaps having length one. A private link
of $(y,\mu)$ enters only $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$, and an inside $\mu$-link of
$B(y)$ enters only $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ and $V^\sharp_{y-e_\mu,\mu}$, since the
path of $V^\sharp_{y',\nu}$ from a site $x$ consists of $(x,\nu)$ and
$(x+e_\nu,\nu)$.

(ii) The constraint of an outer pair $k_j$ contains its path link, which
enters no other constraint, its non-path links, fixed within $r$ of
$c_{k_j}$, and the inside $\mu$-links of $y_j$ and $y_{j+1}$, which are
within $r$ of $I$ on $E$ or by hypothesis, because $y_j$ is good. So
Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} applies and gives the atom and the
determinant bounds, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:sitelaw}. The
remaining constraints, of the inner pairs, form a Lipschitz map $\Phi$
into $\SU(2)^{n_b}$, differentiable off a null set by
Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion}, and the coarea formula gives
$J_{\mathcal C}^{-1}\mathrm{vol}_{M_{\mathcal C}}$ with $J_{\mathcal C}=
\det(D\Phi D\Phi^*)^{1/2}$. The private links of an inner pair enter only
its own constraint, so the part of $D\Phi D\Phi^*$ from the private links
is block diagonal with blocks at least $\sigma_0^2$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion}, and $D\Phi D\Phi^*$ dominates it.

(iii) This is the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:site} with the diameter
$24\cdot2\sqrt2$ replaced by $n\cdot2\sqrt2$. By (i) an exterior link
enters the law through the Wilson weight, or as a non-path link of one
outer pair, which moves one atom at speed at most $1.1986$ and shares at
most one plaquette with a link of $\mathcal C$, the path link of its pair,
because the $\mu$-links of a plaquette have a common $\mu$-coordinate and
by the argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly}; or as an inside link of
$y_{j_0-1}$ or $y_{j_1+2}$, which moves one atom at speed at most $0.5993$
and shares no plaquette with a link of $\mathcal C$, the other $\mu$-links
at its $\mu$-coordinate being inside links of its own block. The density
terms are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:goodsidedensity}, and the Wilson terms
are $(1+6\cdot1.1986)/\sqrt2\le5.793$ and $6\cdot0.5993/\sqrt2\le2.543$
as there.

(iv) The chain has $8n_b$ private links of inner pairs, $p_\mu$ inside
links in each of $j_1-j_0+2$ blocks and one path link for each of the
$j_1-j_0+3-n_b$ outer pairs; $p_\mu\le7$, and consecutive bad blocks of
the set differ by at most two in index, so $j_1-j_0\le2(n_b-1)$.
\end{proof}

The chains of all bad blocks are disjoint, contain the eight private links
of every pair based at a bad block, and each responds to every link
outside it with the bound of (iii), uniformly in the exterior. Where the
cube condition calls for the response of the private links of a bad pair,
the law of the chain of that pair can be used, with the constants of
Theorem~\ref{thm:site} in which $24$ is replaced by $n\le23n_b+1$. The chains
cost nothing in the counting of islands, except at the collar $s=1$.

\begin{corollary}[the chains and the islands]\label{cor:linechain}
Let $s\ge1$ be the collar.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item In Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}, every link of a chain of a bad
block of $I_a$ is based at $d_a\le1\le s$ and lies in the class $L_a$, which
is integrated in $a_i$; likewise for $I_b$. So the chains need no change of
the joining distances of Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation},
Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands} and the results built on them.
\item Let $s\ge2$, and let every block at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most
$s$ from a window $W$ be good. Then no link of a chain is freed in the law of
Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw} for $W$, and no constraint of a pair of
$K_W$ contains a link of a chain. So the chains and the windows of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} have disjoint variables and constraints
at the joining distance $2s+1$ of that theorem, with $\varDelta=(4s+3)^4-1$,
and its values for $s\ge2$ stand, among them $\beta^*(10^{-8},5)=5.401
\cdot10^{21}$.
\item For $s=1$ the statement of (ii) fails: if $y$ is bad and every block
at distance at most one from $y+2e_\mu$ is good, the window
$W=\{y+2e_\mu\}$ is admissible, the outer pair $(y+e_\mu,\mu)$ of the chain
of $y$ enters $W$, and its path link is freed in the window law. With the
collar $s=2$ instead, $\varDelta=11^4-1$, $\lvert\log q^*\rvert=25777.3$,
$\beta^*(10^{-8},2)=4.177\cdot10^{21}$ and $\beta^*(10^{-9},2)=4.181\cdot
10^{23}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
(i) By Proposition~\ref{prop:linechain}(i) every link of the chain is
based within distance one of a bad block of its connected set; the bad
blocks lie in $I_a\cup I_b$, whose distance exceeds $2s+7>2$, so a
connected set lies in one of them; and a link based at $d_a\le s$ is
in $L_a$ by the definition of the classes. (ii) A block of $W$ is at
distance at least $s+1\ge3$ from every bad block, a pair entering $W$ is
based at distance at least $s\ge2$, and the constraint of a pair of $K_W$
contains links based in its own block and in the next one along its
direction, both at distance at least $s\ge2$. The links freed for $W$ are
based in $W$ or are path links of pairs entering it. Links of chains are
based at distance at most one. The rest is the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} unchanged. (iii) The window is
admissible because $y$ is at distance two from it; the numbers are those
of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} at $s=2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The projected average}\label{ssec:projected}

The folds of Propositions~\ref{prop:fold} and~\ref{prop:insidefold} and the
obstruction of Theorem~\ref{thm:eightlinkuniform} are zeros of $\det
D_gV^\sharp_k$, the derivative of the cut-off average in its path link. They
come from the two nonlinear parts of~\eqref{eq:cutoff}: the logarithm, whose
differential $L_Y$ grows like $\theta/\sin\theta$ as an eigenangle $\theta$
approaches $\pi$, and the cut-off, whose slope is $2$. If the
logarithm of each relative path is replaced by its orthogonal projection onto
the Lie algebra, no cut-off is needed. The resulting coarse map has the same
derivatives of order at most two as the cut-off average at every field whose
sixteen paths agree, and its derivative in the path link is invertible at
every field. This subsection proves the properties of this map that bear on
the bad side; Remark~\ref{rem:projscope} lists what is not proved for it.
As in the rest of this section $G=\SU(2)$; Remark~\ref{rem:projgroups} gives
the constants for other groups.

Let $\Pi_\g$ be the orthogonal projection of the space of complex $2\times2$
matrices, with the real inner product $\operatorname{Re}\Tr(X^*Y)$, onto
$\g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$.

\begin{definition}\label{def:projavg}
For a coarse link $(y,\mu)$ and the paths $P_x$ of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:pathblocks}, the \emph{projected average} is
\begin{gather*}
\widehat V_{y,\mu}(U)=P_{2y}\exp A_{y,\mu}(U),\\
A_{y,\mu}(U)=\frac1{16}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\Pi_\g\bigl(P_{2y}^{-1}P_x\bigr).
\end{gather*}
\end{definition}

For a pair $k=(y,\mu)$ in the tree gauge write $g=\ell_k$, $z=(\ell_a)_{a\ne0}$,
and $P_{x_a}=u_a\ell_a$, $P_{x'_a}=\ell_aw_a$ for the paths of nonzero offset,
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart}. The two paths of offset zero equal $g$ and
contribute nothing, so
\[
A_k=\frac1{16}\sum_{a\ne0}\Bigl(\Pi_\g(g^{-1}u_a\ell_a)+\Pi_\g(g^{-1}\ell_a
w_a)\Bigr),
\]
a function $A(g;z,u,w)$ of the path link, the non-path links and the inside
links. Let $J(g;z,u,w)=\lvert\det D_g\widehat V_k\rvert$, the Jacobian
between tangent spaces of the bi-invariant metric, as in~\eqref{eq:pathlaw}.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:projection}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $U\in\SU(2)$, $\Pi_\g(U)=\frac12(U-U^{-1})$. The projection
commutes with conjugation by $\SU(2)$, $\Pi_\g(I)=0$, and $\lVert\Pi_\g(U)-
\Pi_\g(U')\rVert\le\delta(U,U')\le d(U,U')$ for $U,U'\in\SU(2)$; in
particular $\lVert\Pi_\g(U)\rVert\le\delta(U,I)$.
\item For $X\in\g$, $\lVert\Pi_\g(e^X)-X\rVert\le\frac1{12}\lVert X
\rVert^3$.
\item For $X\in\g$, the operator $\operatorname{ad}X$ on $\g$ has norm
$\sqrt2\,\lVert X\rVert$, and the operator norm of the matrix $X$ is
$\lVert X\rVert/\sqrt2$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) For $U\in\SU(2)$, $U+U^*=(\Tr U)I$ with $\Tr U$ real, so $U=\frac12
(\Tr U)I+Y$ with $Y=\frac12(U-U^*)\in\g$. Since $\operatorname{Re}\Tr X=0$
for $X\in\g$, $I$ is orthogonal to $\g$, and $\Pi_\g(U)=Y$. Conjugation by
$h\in\SU(2)$ is orthogonal for the inner product and maps $\g$ onto itself,
so it commutes with $\Pi_\g$. As an orthogonal projection, $\Pi_\g$ is a
linear map of norm one, and $\delta$ is the Hilbert--Schmidt distance; a
chord is not longer than an arc, so $\delta\le d$. (ii) In a basis with
$X=\operatorname{diag}(i\theta,-i\theta)$, $\lVert X\rVert=\sqrt2\,
\lvert\theta\rvert$ and $\Pi_\g(e^X)=\operatorname{diag}(i\sin\theta,
-i\sin\theta)$ by (i), so $\lVert\Pi_\g(e^X)-X\rVert=\sqrt2\,\lvert\theta-
\sin\theta\rvert\le\sqrt2\,\lvert\theta\rvert^3/6=\lVert X\rVert^3/12$.
(iii) In the same basis $\operatorname{ad}X$ is skew with eigenvalues $0$
and $\pm2i\theta$, and $X$ has the eigenvalues $\pm i\theta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[the projected average]\label{prop:projavg}
The projected average is real-analytic on all fields, covariant under the
gauge transformations at the block roots, and normalised.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item At a field with $\delta(P_x,P_{2y})\le\frac12$ for every $x\in B(y)$,
with $X_x=\log(P_{2y}^{-1}P_x)$,
\[
d\bigl(\widehat V_{y,\mu},V^\sharp_{y,\mu}\bigr)\le\frac1{192}\sum_{x\in
B(y)}\lVert X_x\rVert^3 .
\]
At every field at which the sixteen paths $P_x$ agree, the derivatives of
order at most two of $\widehat V_{y,\mu}$ and $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ coincide;
in particular $\widehat V_{y,\mu}(e^{t\varphi})=I+t\,V_{y,\mu}(\varphi)+
O(t^2)$, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(i).
\item The four inequalities of Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(ii) hold for
$\widehat V$ with $c=1$, that is with the constants $896$, $56$, $1344$ and
$2696$, for every field in the tree gauge.
\item If $U$ equals $I$ except on one link from $B(y)$ to $B(y+e_\mu)$,
where it equals $h$, then $\widehat V_{y,\mu}(U)=h\exp(-\frac78\Pi_\g(h))$
when the link is on the straight path and $\exp(\frac18\Pi_\g(h))$ at the
seven other positions, for every $h$. The slice windings of
Proposition~\ref{prop:nomean} are $1$ at the straight path and $0$ at the
other positions.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Products of matrices, $\Pi_\g$ and $\exp$ are analytic, and $\widehat V\in
G$ since $A\in\g$. A gauge transformation equal to $h_1$ on $B(y)$ and to
$h_2$ on $B(y+e_\mu)$ maps $P_x$ to $h_1P_xh_2^{-1}$, as in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}, so $P_{2y}^{-1}P_x\mapsto h_2P_{2y}^{-1}P_xh_2^{-1}$,
$A\mapsto h_2Ah_2^{-1}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(i), and $\widehat V
\mapsto h_1\widehat Vh_2^{-1}$. At $U=I$ every term of $A$ is $\Pi_\g(I)=0$.

(i) Under the hypothesis the cut-off is one, and $V^\sharp=P_{2y}e^N$ with
$N=\frac1{16}\sum_xX_x$, by Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(i), while $A=\frac1
{16}\sum_x\Pi_\g(e^{X_x})$. By $d(e^A,e^N)\le\lVert A-N\rVert$ and
Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(ii) the distance is at most $\frac1{16}\sum_x
\frac1{12}\lVert X_x\rVert^3$. Near a field at which the paths agree the
$X_x$ are analytic functions of the links that vanish there, so the two
analytic maps differ by $O(r^3)$ at distance $r$ from it, and their Taylor
expansions in a chart agree to order two. The last statement is
Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(i).

(ii) In the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(ii), $\delta(V^\sharp,P)$ is
bounded by $\frac c4(\sum_x\delta(P_x,P)^2)^{1/2}$, and $V^\sharp=vM$ with
$\delta(M,I)$ at most the same quantity. For $\widehat V=Pe^A$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(i) and the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
\begin{multline*}
\delta(\widehat V,P)=\delta(e^A,I)\le\lVert A\rVert\le\frac1{16}\sum_x
\delta(P_x,P)\\
\le\frac14\Bigl(\sum_x\delta(P_x,P)^2\Bigr)^{1/2},
\end{multline*}
which is that bound with $c=1$, and the rest of the proof is unchanged:
$896/16=56$, $448+896=1344$ and $8+48\cdot56=2696$.

(iii) At the straight path $P_{2y}=h$, the fourteen other paths are $I$,
and $\Pi_\g(h^{-1})=-\Pi_\g(h)$; at another position $P_{2y}=I$ and two
paths equal $h$. For $h=\operatorname{diag}(e^{iq},e^{-iq})$ the two values
are $\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\psi},e^{-i\psi})$ with $\psi=q-\frac78\sin q$
and $\psi=\frac18\sin q$, loops of degree $1$ and $0$ in $q$.
\end{proof}

So $\widehat V$ is a continuous covariant extension of the block averages to
all fields, with the slice windings that Proposition~\ref{prop:nomean}
demands; it departs from the transverse symmetry at third order at every
field, where $V^\sharp$ departs from it only past the cut-off.

\begin{theorem}[the global inverse]\label{thm:projinverse}
Let $k$ be a pair, $c_k\in\SU(2)$, and let the non-path links $z$ and the
inside links $u,w$ be arbitrary.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For all $g,g'$, $\lVert A(g)-A(g')\rVert\le\frac78\,\delta(g,g')$, and
$g\mapsto c_k\exp(-A(g))$ is a contraction of $\SU(2)$ with constant
$\frac78$ for $d$. The equation $\widehat V_k=c_k$ has exactly one solution
$G=G(c_k;z,u,w)$, the fixed point of this contraction, and $G$ is
real-analytic in $(c_k,z,u,w)$.
\item For all $g,g'$,
\[
\tfrac18\,d(g,g')\le d\bigl(\widehat V_k(g),\widehat V_k(g')\bigr)\le
\tfrac{15}8\,d(g,g'),
\]
the singular values of $D_g\widehat V_k$ lie in $[\frac18,\frac{15}8]$ at
every $g$, and $\frac1{512}\le J\le\frac{3375}{512}$. The two bounds on $J$
are attained when all fourteen relative paths $g^{-1}P_x$ of nonzero offset
equal $I$, respectively $-I$.
\item For two configurations,
\begin{multline*}
d(G,G')\le8\,d(c_k,c'_k)+\sum_{a\ne0}d(\ell_a,\ell'_a)\\
+\frac12\sum_{a\ne0}\bigl(d(u_a,u'_a)+d(w_a,w'_a)\bigr).
\end{multline*}
\item Let one link $u_b$ or $w_b$, $b\ne0$, move along a unit-speed geodesic,
with $c_k$, $z$ and the other links fixed, and let $J(t)$ be the value of
$J$ at $(G(t);z,u(t),w(t))$. Then $\lvert\frac d{dt}\log J(t)\rvert\le
\frac{45}4\sqrt2<15.91$. If instead a non-path link $\ell_b$ moves, with
$c_k$, $u$, $w$ and the other non-path links fixed, the bound is $\frac{45}2
\sqrt2<31.82$; if $c_k$ moves, with $z$, $u$, $w$ fixed, it is $\frac{315}2
\sqrt2<222.8$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\emph{The derivative.} Let $v_x=g^{-1}P_x$ for the fourteen paths of nonzero
offset. Along $ge^{t\zeta}$, $\zeta\in\g$, each $v_x$ becomes $e^{-t\zeta}v_x$,
so $A(ge^{t\zeta})=A(g)+tB\zeta+O(t^2)$ with
\[
B\zeta=-\frac1{16}\sum_x\Pi_\g(\zeta v_x),\qquad\lVert B\rVert\le\frac78 ,
\]
since $\lVert\zeta v_x\rVert=\lVert\zeta\rVert$. With $e^{-A}\frac d{dt}
e^{A+tY}|_{t=0}=\int_0^1\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-sA})Y\,ds$ and $R_A=\int_0^1
\operatorname{Ad}(e^{sA})\,ds$, of norm at most one,
\[
\widehat V_k^{-1}\frac d{dt}\widehat V_k(ge^{t\zeta})\Big|_{t=0}=
\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-A})\,D\zeta,\qquad D=I+R_AB .
\]
As $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-A})$ is a rotation of $\g$, $J=\lvert\det D\rvert$;
the maps $I+sR_AB$, $0\le s\le1$, are invertible because $\lVert R_AB\rVert\le
\frac78$, so $\det D>0$, and $\lVert D^{-1}\rVert\le(1-\frac78)^{-1}=8$.

(i) By Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(i) and the invariance of $\delta$ under
multiplication and inversion, $\lVert\Pi_\g(g^{-1}P)-\Pi_\g(g'^{-1}P)
\rVert\le\delta(g^{-1}P,g'^{-1}P)=\delta(g,g')$ for each of the fourteen
paths, which gives the first bound. With $d(e^X,e^Y)\le\lVert X-Y\rVert$
and $\delta\le d$, $d(c_ke^{-A(g)},c_ke^{-A(g')})\le\frac78d(g,g')$, and
$\SU(2)$ is complete, so the contraction has one fixed point; $\widehat
V_k(g)=c_k$ is the equation $g=c_ke^{-A(g)}$. Since $D$ is invertible at
every point, the analytic implicit function theorem gives an analytic
solution near every solution, which by uniqueness is $G$.

(ii) By bi-invariance, $d(ge^{A(g)},g'e^{A(g)})$ equals $d(g,g')$, and
$d(g'e^{A(g)},g'e^{A(g')})\le\lVert A(g)-A(g')\rVert\le\frac78d(g,g')$; the
triangle inequality gives both bounds, and along $ge^{t\zeta}$ they give
$\frac18\lVert\zeta\rVert\le\lVert D\zeta\rVert\le\frac{15}8\lVert\zeta
\rVert$. If every $v_x$ is $I$, respectively $-I$, then $A=0$, $R_A=I$ and
$B=\mp\frac78I$, so $J=8^{-3}$, respectively $(\frac{15}8)^3$; these values
are taken, for instance, at $u=w=I$ and $\ell_a=\pm g$.

(iii) Let $T(g)=c_ke^{-A(g)}$ and $T'$ be the map for the second
configuration. Then $d(G,G')\le d(T(G),T(G'))+d(T(G'),T'(G'))$, the first
term is at most $\frac78d(G,G')$, and the second is at most $d(c_k,c'_k)+
\lVert A(G')-A'(G')\rVert$. A path of nonzero offset changes by at most
$d(u_a,u'_a)+d(\ell_a,\ell'_a)$, respectively $d(\ell_a,\ell'_a)+d(w_a,
w'_a)$, so $\lVert A(G')-A'(G')\rVert$ is at most $\frac1{16}$ times the
sum of these quantities, and multiplying by $8$ gives the bound.

(iv) Let $u_b(t)=u_be^{t\zeta'}$ with $\lVert\zeta'\rVert=1$. By (i) and
(iii), $G(t)$ is analytic and its left velocity $\eta=G^{-1}\dot G$ has
$\lVert\eta\rVert\le\frac12$. Then $\dot A=B\eta+\frac1{16}\Pi_\g(G^{-1}u_b
\zeta'\ell_b)$, so $\lVert\dot A\rVert\le\frac7{16}+\frac1{16}=\frac12$. Next,
$\frac d{dt}\operatorname{Ad}(e^{sA})=\operatorname{ad}(W_s)\operatorname{Ad}
(e^{sA})$ with $W_s=(\frac d{dt}e^{sA})e^{-sA}=s\int_0^1\operatorname{Ad}
(e^{rsA})\dot A\,dr$, so $\lVert W_s\rVert\le s\lVert\dot A\rVert$ and, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(iii), $\lVert\dot R_A\rVert\le\int_0^1\sqrt2\,s
\lVert\dot A\rVert\,ds\le\frac1{2\sqrt2}$. Further $\dot B\zeta=-\frac1{16}
\sum_x\Pi_\g(\zeta\dot v_x)$ with $\dot v_x=-\eta v_x$, except for the
path from $x_b$, which has the additional term $G^{-1}u_b\zeta'\ell_b$; and
$\lVert\zeta M\rVert\le\lVert\zeta\rVert\,\lVert M\rVert_{\rm op}$, $\lVert
\eta v_x\rVert_{\rm op}=\lVert\eta\rVert/\sqrt2$ and $\lVert G^{-1}u_b
\zeta'\ell_b\rVert_{\rm op}=1/\sqrt2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(iii).
Hence $\lVert\dot B\rVert\le\frac1{16}(\frac{14}{2\sqrt2}+\frac1{\sqrt2})=
\frac1{2\sqrt2}$, and $\dot D=\dot R_AB+R_A\dot B$ has
\[
\lVert\dot D\rVert\le\frac78\cdot\frac1{2\sqrt2}+\frac1{2\sqrt2}=\frac{15}
{16\sqrt2} .
\]
Since $\det D>0$, $\frac d{dt}\log J=\Tr(D^{-1}\dot D)$, at most $3\lVert
D^{-1}\rVert\lVert\dot D\rVert\le3\cdot8\cdot\frac{15}{16\sqrt2}=\frac{45}4
\sqrt2$ in modulus on the three-dimensional $\g$. The link $w_b$ is the same
with the path from $x'_b$. If $\ell_b$ moves, $\lVert\eta\rVert\le1$ by
(iii) and two paths have an additional term of operator norm $1/\sqrt2$, so
$\lVert\dot A\rVert\le\frac78+\frac2{16}=1$, $\lVert\dot R_A\rVert\le
\frac1{\sqrt2}$, $\lVert\dot B\rVert\le\frac1{16}(\frac{14}{\sqrt2}+
\frac2{\sqrt2})=\frac1{\sqrt2}$, $\lVert\dot D\rVert\le\frac{15}{8\sqrt2}$,
and the bound is $3\cdot8\cdot\frac{15}{8\sqrt2}=\frac{45}2\sqrt2$. If
$c_k$ moves, $\lVert\eta\rVert\le8$ by (iii) and no path has an additional
term, so $\lVert\dot A\rVert\le7$, $\lVert\dot R_A\rVert\le\frac7{\sqrt2}$,
$\lVert\dot B\rVert\le\frac{14}{16}\cdot\frac8{\sqrt2}=\frac7{\sqrt2}$ and
$\lVert\dot D\rVert\le\frac{105}{8\sqrt2}$, and the bound is $3\cdot8\cdot
\frac{105}{8\sqrt2}=\frac{315}2\sqrt2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[the path-link law of the projected average]\label{cor:projpathlaw}
For every $c_k$, $z$, $u$, $w$ and exterior $\sigma$, the law~\eqref{eq:pathlaw}
with $\widehat V_k$ in place of $V^\sharp_k$ is the point mass at
$G(c_k;z,u,w)$, and for two configurations with the same $c_k$
\begin{multline*}
W_1^d(\pi,\pi')\le\sum_{a\ne0}d(\ell_a,\ell'_a)\\
+\frac12\sum_{a\ne0}\bigl(d(u_a,u'_a)+d(w_a,w'_a)\bigr),
\end{multline*}
with no dependence on $\beta_W$, on $c_k$ or on any other link, and no
restriction on the size of any link.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(i) the sum in~\eqref{eq:pathlaw} has one
term, whose weight cancels against $Z$; the bound is
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iii).
\end{proof}

So for the projected average the original form of item (i) of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}, a Lipschitz bound for the path-link law in the
non-path links, holds at every field, with the constants $1$ and $\frac12$
in place of the constants $1.1986$ and $0.5993$ that
Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} gives for $V^\sharp$ on the good side
only; Propositions~\ref{prop:branches}, \ref{prop:fold}
and~\ref{prop:insidefold} have no counterpart. The rest of
Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} holds with no radius as well: if the
non-path links and the inside links are within $r$ of the reconstruction,
the computation of Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}, with $\lVert A_k\rVert\le
\frac78\max_x\delta(g^{-1}P_x,I)$ in place of the logarithmic bound, gives
$d(G,c_k)\le14r$ and $d(g^{-1}P_x,I)\le16r$ for every $r$, and the density
$1/J$ lies in $[(\frac{15}8)^{-3},512]$. For the law of the eight
private links let $S_{\mathrm{dep}}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:relnorm}, let
$dz$ be Haar measure on $\SU(2)^7$, $\lvert B\rvert$ the Haar measure of a set
$B$, and write
$G(z)=G(c_k;z,u,w)$.

\begin{theorem}[the bad side of the projected average]\label{thm:projresponse}
Let $k$ be a pair and $c_k\in\SU(2)$, fix every link other than the eight
private links of $k$ at arbitrary values, and let $B\subset\SU(2)^7$ be a
measurable set of values of the non-path links with $\lvert B\rvert>0$. Put
\begin{gather*}
\rho_B(z)=\mathbf1_B(z)\,e^{-\beta_WS_{\mathrm{dep}}(G(z),z)}\,
J\bigl(G(z);z,u,w\bigr)^{-1},\\
Q_B(f)=\frac1{Z_B}\int f\bigl(G(z),z\bigr)\,\rho_B(z)\,dz,\qquad
Z_B=\int\rho_B\,dz .
\end{gather*}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $c_k$, $Q_B$ is the law of the eight private links given the
other links, $\widehat V_k=c_k$ and $z\in B$, in the version of the
disintegration that is continuous in $c_k$, and
\[
(\tfrac8{15})^3e^{-72\beta_W}\lvert B\rvert\le Z_B\le512\,\lvert B\rvert .
\]
\item If one inside link $u_b$ or $w_b$, $b\ne0$, moves from $e$ to $e'$,
with $c_k$, $B$ and every other link fixed, then for the cost
$\sum_{a=0}^7\delta(\ell_a,\ell'_a)$
\[
W_1(Q_B,Q'_B)\le(24\beta_W+180.5)\,d(e,e').
\]
\item If one link $e'$ that is neither a private link of $k$ nor one of the
links $u_a$, $w_a$ changes, then $W_1(Q_B,Q'_B)\le8\beta_W\,d(\sigma_{e'},
\sigma'_{e'})$.
\item If $c_k$ moves, with $B$ and every link other than the private links
of $k$ fixed, then
\[
W_1(Q_B,Q'_B)\le(384\beta_W+2528)\,d(c_k,c'_k).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The constants depend neither on $B$ nor on $\lvert B\rvert$, nor on $c_k$ or the
values of the other links; no inside link needs to be near $I$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) Let $\Phi(g,z)=(\widehat V_k(g;z,u,w),z)$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(i), $\Phi$ is a bijection of $\SU(2)^8$, analytic with the analytic
inverse $(c,z)\mapsto(G(c;z,u,w),z)$, and its Jacobian is $J$, the
derivative being triangular with the identity in $z$. Haar measure is a
constant multiple of the volume of the bi-invariant metric, so the change of
variables gives, for bounded measurable $F$,
\[
\int F(g,z)\,dg\,dz=\int\!dc\int F\bigl(G(c;z,u,w),z\bigr)\,J^{-1}\,dz ,
\]
with $J$ at $(G(c;z,u,w);z,u,w)$. Taking $F$ equal to $f$ times the
Wilson weight and $\mathbf1_B(z)$, and cancelling the plaquettes without a
private link as in Lemma~\ref{lem:relnorm}, the normalised inner integral is
$Q_B$ at $c=c_k$; it is weakly continuous in $c$ by the continuity of $G$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:relnorm} gives $0\le S_{\mathrm{dep}}\le72$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(ii) gives $J\in[8^{-3},(\frac{15}8)^3]$.

(ii) Move $e$ along a unit-speed geodesic $e(t)$, $0\le t\le T=d(e,e')$,
write $G_t(z)$, $\rho_t$, $Q_t$, and let $\nu_t$ be the law
$\rho_t\,dz/Z_t$ on $B$. The link $e$ shares no plaquette with a private link,
since the two $\mu$-links of a plaquette have one $\mu$-coordinate; so at
fixed $z$, $S_{\mathrm{dep}}$ changes only through the path link $G_t(z)$,
which moves at speed at most $\frac12$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iii) and lies in six plaquettes, each
changing at rate at most $\frac12/\sqrt2$, by the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly}. With Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iv),
\[
\lvert\partial_t\log\rho_t(z)\rvert\le\omega:=\frac3{\sqrt2}\beta_W+
\frac{45}4\sqrt2
\]
for every $z\in B$ and $t$. Let $f$ be $1$-Lipschitz for the cost, and put
$\Phi_t(z)=(G_t(z),z)$. Then
\[
Q_T(f)-Q_0(f)=(\nu_T-\nu_0)(f\circ\Phi_T)+\nu_0(f\circ\Phi_T-f\circ
\Phi_0).
\]
In the second term only the path link differs, by at most $\frac T2$ in $d$
and so in $\delta$. In the first, $\frac d{dt}\nu_t(\varphi)=\Cov_{\nu_t}
(\varphi,\partial_t\log\rho_t)$ for the fixed bounded function $\varphi=
f\circ\Phi_T$, by differentiation under the integral over the fixed set $B$,
and $\lvert\Cov(\varphi,\psi)\rvert\le\frac14\operatorname{osc}\varphi\,
\operatorname{osc}\psi$; the oscillation of $\varphi$ is at most the diameter
$8\cdot2\sqrt2$ of the eight links for the cost, so the first term is at
most $\frac14\cdot16\sqrt2\cdot2\omega\,T=8\sqrt2\,\omega\,T$. The
normaliser $Z_t$ cancels from the covariance. Hence $Q_T(f)-Q_0(f)\le
(\frac12+8\sqrt2\,\omega)T=(24\beta_W+180.5)T$, and the Kantorovich duality
gives the bound.

(iii) The measure $\rho_B\,dz$ without its Wilson factor, and the map $\Phi$,
do not depend on $e'$; the link $e'$ lies in at most one plaquette with a
private link, by the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly} and, for an inside
link of another direction, by the remark after
Theorem~\ref{thm:relresponse}. The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly}
gives the bound.

(iv) As in (ii), with the path link moving at speed at most $8$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iii), so that $S_{\mathrm{dep}}$ changes at
rate at most $6\cdot8/\sqrt2$, and with the bound $\frac{315}2\sqrt2$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iv): $\lvert\partial_t\log\rho_t\rvert\le24
\sqrt2\,\beta_W+\frac{315}2\sqrt2$, and $8+8\sqrt2(24\sqrt2\,\beta_W+
\frac{315}2\sqrt2)=384\beta_W+2528$.
\end{proof}

The theorem applies to the two sets $\SU(2)^7$ and $B^{\mathrm{bad}}_r$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:eightlabels}, defined with $c_k=\widehat V_k$, and to
the sets $B_\varepsilon$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:eightlinkuniform}, at every
$\varepsilon$; it needs neither the relative chart nor condition (J) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:relresponse}, and its constants have no factor
$e^{72\beta_W}$. The reason is the following. The obstruction of
Theorem~\ref{thm:eightlinkuniform} lives at a point where the projection of
the fibre $\{V^\sharp_k=c_k\}$ to the non-path links folds, that is, where
$\det D_gV^\sharp_k=0$; as $\varepsilon\to0$ the law over $B_\varepsilon$
becomes the path-link law at the fold, which jumps. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(i) and (ii) the fibre of $\widehat V_k$ is, for every
value of the inside links, the graph of $z\mapsto G(z)$ over the non-path
links themselves. A set of non-path links held fixed while an inside link
moves is therefore a fixed set of parameters of the fibre; only the density
$\rho_B$ and the position of the path link move, the first with a logarithmic
derivative bounded at every point, the second at speed $\frac12$. In the
relative chart of Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart} the fibre of $V^\sharp_k$ is a
graph over $\xi_a=g^{-1}\ell_a$ instead, a fixed set $B$ of non-path links is
the moving set $\{\xi:G(\xi)\xi\in B\}$, and the terms with $\iota$ and $K$
in Theorem~\ref{thm:relresponse} come from this motion and from the jumps of
the Jacobian $D$. The bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:projresponse} grows linearly
in $\beta_W$; it is a bound on the response of one pair at a fixed coarse
field, not a contraction, and it does not give the cube condition (D).

On the whole torus the coarse fibre of the projected average has a global
product parametrisation. On the periodic lattice of side $2L$, $L\ge2$, in
the tree gauge, with $\mathcal B$ blocks, the $49$ active links of a block
are the four path links $\ell_k$ of the pairs based at it and $45$ other
links, the $28$ non-path private links and the $17$ active links inside it;
let $z$ be the family of these $45\mathcal B$ links.

\begin{proposition}[projected fibres]\label{prop:projfibre}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The map $\Psi(U)=(\widehat V(U),z)$ of the active links $U$,
\[
\Psi\colon\SU(2)^{49\mathcal B}\to
\SU(2)^{4\mathcal B}\times\SU(2)^{45\mathcal B}
\]
is an analytic diffeomorphism. Its inverse $(c,z)\mapsto\Gamma(c,z)$ puts $G_k=G(c_k;z,u,w)$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse} on each path link, and its Jacobian is
$\prod_kJ_k$, with $J_k$ the Jacobian of the pair $k$.
\item For every $c$, the law of the active links given $\widehat V=c$, in the
version continuous in $c$, is the image under $\Gamma(c,\cdot)$ of
\[
\frac1{Z(c)}\,e^{-\beta_WS(\Gamma(c,z))}\prod_kJ_k^{-1}\,dz ,
\]
whose density is positive at every $z$. The factor of a plaquette depends on
$c$ and on links of $z$ based in blocks at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most two
from the block of its base point, and $J_k$ on $c_k$ and on links of $z$
based in the two blocks of $k$.
\item Let $H_c(z)=\beta_WS(\Gamma(c,z))+\sum_k\log J_k$. Along a unit-speed
geodesic in one link of $z$, $\lvert\frac d{dt}H_c\rvert\le6\sqrt2\,\beta_W+
\frac{45}2\sqrt2$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) The paths of a pair $(y',\nu)$ consist of $\nu$-links with base in
$B(y')$ or $B(y'+e_\nu)$, and the path link of $k=(y,\mu)$ is a $\mu$-link
with $o_\mu=1$ based in $B(y)$, a private link of $k$; so it enters only
$\widehat V_k$. A non-path private link of $k$ enters only $\widehat V_k$,
and an active inside $\mu$-link of $B(y)$ enters $\widehat V_{y,\mu}$ and
$\widehat V_{y-e_\mu,\mu}$; since $L\ge2$ these are two different pairs.
For fixed $z$ the map from the path links to $\widehat V$ is therefore the
product over $k$ of the maps $g\mapsto\widehat V_k(g;z,u,w)$, each a
bijection with analytic inverse by Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(i). The map
$(\ell,z)\mapsto(\widehat V,z)$ is a bijection with inverse $\Gamma$; its
derivative is triangular, with the identity in $z$ and the block diagonal
part $(D_{\ell_k}\widehat V_k)_k$ in the path links, which gives the
Jacobian.

(ii) The tree gauge has unit Jacobian, so the active links carry product
Haar measure times the Wilson weight. The change of variables of (i), as in
the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:projresponse}(i), gives the law, and the
density is positive by Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(ii). A plaquette has
its links based in blocks at distance at most one from the block of its base
point; a path link among them is $G_k$, which depends on $c_k$ and on links
based in the two blocks of $k$, at distance at most one further. The
Jacobian $J_k$ depends on the same variables as $G_k$.

(iii) If the link of $z$ is a non-path link of $k$, only $G_k$ moves, at
speed at most $1$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iii); the two moving
links lie in six plaquettes each, which changes $S$ at rate at most
$12/\sqrt2=6\sqrt2$, and only $J_k$ changes, at the rate $\frac{45}2\sqrt2$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iv). If it is an active inside link of
$B(y)$ of direction $\mu$, the path links of $(y,\mu)$ and $(y-e_\mu,\mu)$
move at speed at most $\frac12$ each, so $S$ changes at rate at most
$(6+3+3)/\sqrt2$, and the two Jacobians at rate at most $\frac{45}4\sqrt2$
each.
\end{proof}

The coarse curvature of the projected average has a fine witness at every
size of the fine plaquettes, with a smaller constant than
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}. For a transverse offset $a\in\{0,1\}^4$,
$a_\mu=0$, let $\lvert a\rvert$ be the number of its nonzero coordinates
and $\lvert a\rvert_{>\mu}$ the number of those with index above $\mu$.

\begin{proposition}[a fine witness for the projected average]\label{prop:projwitness}
Let $P$ be the coarse plaquette at $y$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, $\mu<\nu$,
let $\kappa\ge0$, and suppose that $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every fine
plaquette $p$ whose vertices lie in $B(y)\cup B(y+e_\mu)\cup B(y+e_\nu)\cup
B(y+e_\mu+e_\nu)$. Then $c=\widehat V(U)$ satisfies $\delta(c_{y',\mu'},
\ell_{y',\mu'})\le\frac{9-\mu'}2\kappa$ for the four sides $(y',\mu')$ of
$P$, and
\[
\delta(c_P,I)\le(22-\mu-\nu)\,\kappa\le21\,\kappa .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take the side $k=(y,\mu)$; the others are the same. Write $x_a=2y+a$ and
$x'_a=x_a+e_\mu$, so that $P_{x_a}=u_a\ell_a$ and $P_{x'_a}=\ell_aw_a$ with
$u_a=U_{x_a,\mu}$ and $w_a=U_{x_a+2e_\mu,\mu}$, and $P_{x_0}=g=\ell_k$.

\emph{The paths from $x_a$.} Let $\nu_1<\dots<\nu_m$ be the directions with
$a_\nu=1$, $m=\lvert a\rvert$, and $a^{(j)}=e_{\nu_1}+\dots+e_{\nu_j}$.
The $\nu_j$-links at $x_{a^{(j-1)}}$ and at $x_{a^{(j-1)}}+2e_\mu$ have
offset $a^{(j-1)}$, whose coordinates of index $\nu_j$ and above vanish; they
are tree links. So $P_{x_{a^{(j-1)}}}P_{x_{a^{(j)}}}^{-1}$ is
the holonomy of the boundary of the rectangle formed by the plaquettes at
$x_{a^{(j-1)}}$ and $x_{a^{(j-1)}}+e_\mu$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu_j\}$, the
product of their holonomies with one of them conjugated, and
$\delta(P_{x_{a^{(j-1)}}},P_{x_{a^{(j)}}})\le2\kappa$. Hence $\delta(P_{x_a},
g)\le2\lvert a\rvert\kappa$.

\emph{The inside links.} If $\lvert a\rvert_{>\mu}=0$, $u_a$ is a tree link.
Otherwise let $\nu>\mu$ be the largest direction with $a_\nu=1$. In the
plaquette at $x_a-e_\nu$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ the two $\nu$-links have
offsets $a-e_\nu$ and $a-e_\nu+e_\mu$, whose coordinates of index $\nu$ and
above vanish, so they are tree links and $\delta(u_a,U_{x_a-e_\nu,\mu})\le
\kappa$. By induction $\delta(u_a,I)\le\lvert a\rvert_{>\mu}\kappa$, and in
$B(y+e_\mu)$ likewise $\delta(w_a,I)\le\lvert a\rvert_{>\mu}\kappa$. Since
$P_{x'_a}=u_a^{-1}P_{x_a}w_a$, $\delta(P_{x'_a},g)\le2(\lvert a\rvert+\lvert
a\rvert_{>\mu})\kappa$.

\emph{The coarse link.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(i), $\lVert\Pi_\g(g^{-1}
P_x)\rVert\le\delta(P_x,g)$. Over the eight transverse offsets $\sum_a\lvert
a\rvert=12$ and $\sum_a\lvert a\rvert_{>\mu}=4(3-\mu)$, so
\[
\lVert A_k\rVert\le\frac\kappa{16}\sum_a\bigl(4\lvert a\rvert+2\lvert
a\rvert_{>\mu}\bigr)=\frac{9-\mu}2\,\kappa ,
\]
and $\delta(c_k,g)=\delta(e^{A_k},I)\le\lVert A_k\rVert$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}. All plaquettes used lie in $B(y)\cup B(y+e_\mu)$.

\emph{The coarse plaquette.} As in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}, the four path links around $P$ form the
holonomy $\ell_P$ of the square of side two at $2y$, and $\delta(\ell_P,I)\le
4\kappa$. Replacing the two path links of direction $\mu$ and the two of
direction $\nu$ by the coarse links one at a time adds at most $(9-\mu)
\kappa+(9-\nu)\kappa$, and $\mu+\nu\ge1$.
\end{proof}

At the background of Proposition~\ref{prop:roughbackground} the conclusion
on the Hessian holds for $\widehat V$ as well: at $U=R(c)$ all sixteen paths
of every pair agree, so by Proposition~\ref{prop:projavg}(i) the tangent
space of the fibre of $\widehat V$, a submanifold by
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(ii), is that of the fibre of $V^\sharp$ and
contains $\xi$; as every first derivative of $S$ vanishes at $U$, the second
derivative of $\beta_WS$ along any curve in the fibre with velocity $\xi$ is
$-\beta_W$. So the projected average also needs a coarse-curvature label,
for which Proposition~\ref{prop:projwitness} gives the witness.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:projgroups}
For a compact connected group $G\subset\U(N)$ with Lie algebra $\g$, let
$\Pi_\g$ be the orthogonal projection of the complex $N\times N$ matrices
onto $\g$, which for $\SU(N)$, $N\ge3$, is not the skew-Hermitian part. The
proofs above use Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(iii) only for the constants; with
$\lVert\operatorname{ad}X\rVert\le2\lVert X\rVert$ and $\lVert X\rVert_{\rm
op}\le\lVert X\rVert$ instead they give, with $s_p=1-\frac1N\ReTr U_p$:
the contraction constant $\frac78$, the responses $8$, $1$ and $\frac12$,
$J\in[8^{-\dim\g},(\frac{15}8)^{\dim\g}]$, the bounds $\frac{15}2\dim\g$ and
$15\dim\g$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(iv), the constant
$\frac12+24\beta_W+60\dim\g\sqrt N$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:projresponse}(ii),
and $\frac{12}{\sqrt N}\beta_W+15\dim\g$ in
Proposition~\ref{prop:projfibre}(iii). Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(ii)
becomes $\lVert\Pi_\g(e^X)-X\rVert\le\frac16\lVert X\rVert_{\rm op}^2\lVert
X\rVert$, since the Hermitian part of $e^X$ is orthogonal to $\g$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:projwitness} holds unchanged.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[the chart for the projected average]\label{prop:projtransfer}
Let $G\subset\U(r)$ be compact and connected, $\Pi_\g$ as in
Remark~\ref{rem:projgroups}, and replace $V^\sharp$ by $\widehat V$ in the
fibre $F$ and in the constrained law.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Under the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes},
\[
\Bigl\lVert\widehat V_{y,\mu}(U)^{-1}\frac d{dt}\widehat V_{y,\mu}(Ue^{t
\xi})\Big|_{t=0}-V_{y,\mu}(\tilde\xi)\Bigr\rVert\le166\,\kappa\,N_{y,\mu}
(\xi).
\]
\item Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} holds with the same $c_3$
and $c_6$ for $\SU(2)$, and with $c_3=\max\{1.5\cdot10^4r^2,\dim G\}$ and
$c_6=6.81\cdot10^5\dim G\,c_3^2$ for general $G$.
\item Theorems~\ref{thm:smallfibre}, \ref{thm:fibrechart},
\ref{thm:chartdecay} and~\ref{thm:offchart} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay} hold with these constants; in
particular $\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$ and $c_9=1.2\cdot10^4$.
\item For $\SU(2)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion} holds with $\sigma_0=
\frac18$ at every field, Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity} with $M=512$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre} with the same $\varepsilon_W$.
\item $\widehat V(R(c))=c$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp} holds
for $\widehat V$ with the same bound $4\kappa+7700\kappa^2$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Hermitian matrices are orthogonal to $\g$, so $\Pi_\g(w)=\Pi_\g(w-I)$ has
norm at most $\delta(w,I)$ for unitary $w$, and for $Y\in\g$, $\Pi_\g(wY)-
Y=\Pi_\g((w-I)Y)$ has norm at most $\lVert w-I\rVert_{\rm op}\lVert Y
\rVert\le\delta(w,I)\lVert Y\rVert$.

(i) Use the notation of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(iv),
with $A=A_{y,\mu}$ in place of $M$. From $\delta(w_x,I)\le24\kappa$ and the
two paths of offset zero, $\lVert A\rVert\le\frac{14}{16}24\kappa=21\kappa$,
and $\widehat V^{-1}\dot{\widehat V}=\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-A})\alpha+R
\dot A$ with $R=\int_0^1\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-sA})\,ds$, $\lVert R-1\rVert
\le\lVert A\rVert$. Here $\dot A=\frac1{16}\sum_x\Pi_\g(w_xY_x)$ with $Y_x=
\beta_x-\operatorname{Ad}(w_x^{-1})\alpha$, so $\lVert\dot A\rVert\le m_
\beta+\lVert\alpha\rVert$, and $\Pi_\g(w_xY_x)-(\beta_x-\alpha)=(\Pi_\g(w_x
Y_x)-Y_x)+(\alpha-\operatorname{Ad}(w_x^{-1})\alpha)$. The four differences
of that proof are at most $42\kappa\lVert\alpha\rVert$, $21\kappa(m_\beta+
\lVert\alpha\rVert)$, $24\kappa m_\beta+72\kappa\lVert\alpha\rVert$ and
$42\kappa m_\xi$, and their sum is at most $(135+45\cdot0.434+42/4)\kappa
N_{y,\mu}<166\kappa N_{y,\mu}$.

(ii) Follow the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants}. On
unitary matrices $\Pi_\g(w)=L(w)$ with $L(w)=P_\C(\frac12(w-w^{-1}))$,
$P_\C$ the orthogonal projection onto $\g\otimes\C$ for the Hermitian
inner product, which agrees with $\Pi_\g$ on skew-Hermitian matrices; $L$
is holomorphic on $\mathrm{GL}(r,\C)$. Since $e^{X+Z}=e^X(I+F)$ gives
$(I+F)^{-1}=I+F'$, $w_x^{-1}$ has the same factorisation as $w_x$, and
$\lVert L(w_x)-L(w'_x)\rVert_{\rm op}\le\lVert L(w_x)-L(w'_x)\rVert\le
\sqrt r\,\psi$. The two paths of offset zero have $w_x=I$, so the exponent
moves by at most $d_L=\frac78\sqrt r\,\psi$, which replaces $d$, and no
domain condition on the sites is needed. At real points $\lVert A'-A_0
\rVert\le\frac78\cdot3x_0$, so $\gamma_0=x_0+\frac{21}8x_0<0.0037$. For
$\SU(2)$, $r=2$: at $R=0.07$, $\varphi<0.0726$, $\psi<0.2337$, $d_L<
0.2892$, $\eta<0.4322$, $S<0.767$, $6S/R^3<13417$ and $2S/R^2<314$; at
$R=10^{-3}$, $S/R<4.8$; on $\lvert z\rvert\le0.1$, $\gamma_0+\eta<0.71$.
All are below $1.5\cdot10^4$. For general $G$ take the radii $R/\sqrt r$:
by convexity $\varphi(R/\sqrt r)\le\varphi(R)$ and $\sqrt r\,\psi(R/\sqrt
r)\le\psi(R)$, so $S(R/\sqrt r)$ is at most the value above, and the
Cauchy estimate loses $r^{m/2}\le r^{3/2}$. The derivatives of $\log j$ do
not involve the average.

(iii) These proofs use the average in three places only: the derivative
bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(iv), whose constant $260\kappa$ is
improved by (i); the constants $c_3$ and $c_6$; and, in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(i), the form $V^\sharp=ve^M$ with $\lVert M
\rVert\le8\pi\kappa$. For $\widehat V$ the bound $\lVert A\rVert\le21
\kappa$ gives $\delta(v,v')\le42\kappa$ and $\delta(U_e,U'_e)\le84\kappa<
92.3\kappa$.

(iv) The derivative in the eight private links satisfies $JJ^*\ge D_g
\widehat V(D_g\widehat V)^*\ge\frac1{64}$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}(ii). For fixed non-path links, $g\mapsto
\widehat V$ is a diffeomorphism with Jacobian at least $8^{-3}$, so the
image of Haar measure has density at most $512$, and so has its average
over the non-path links. In the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre},
$\frac78\Lambda$ becomes $\frac78$, $1.957$ becomes $\frac{15}8$, and
$(512^4(\frac{15}8)^{12})^{1/45}<2.06<2.93$.

(v) At $R(c)$ every relative path is $I$. In the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp}, Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(ii) gives
$\delta(\widehat c_k,c_k)\le\frac{14}{16}\cdot\frac1{12}a^3$ for each side,
and replacing the four $c_k$ by $\widehat c_k$ adds at most $\frac7{24}a^3<
4100\kappa^3<10\kappa^2$ for $\kappa\le10^{-8}$, which the bound $4\kappa+
7685\kappa^2$ of that proof absorbs.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[what is proved for which map]\label{rem:projscope}
The projected average is a different coarse map: it defines different
coarse fields $c=\widehat V(U)$ and different conditional laws $\mu^c$.
Proved for it are Proposition~\ref{prop:projavg},
Theorems~\ref{thm:projinverse} and~\ref{thm:projresponse},
Corollary~\ref{cor:projpathlaw}, Propositions~\ref{prop:projfibre},
\ref{prop:projwitness} and~\ref{prop:projtransfer},
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly}, whose proof applies unchanged, and the Hessian
statement after Proposition~\ref{prop:projwitness}. Through
Proposition~\ref{prop:projtransfer} this includes the chart of
Theorems~\ref{thm:smallfibre} and~\ref{thm:fibrechart}, the chart decay of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} and Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}. The results of Sec.~\ref{ssec:largefields}
that concern only the Wilson measure and its plaquettes,
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}, Corollary~\ref{cor:localcalm} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:calmrare} among them, do not involve the coarse map.
Not proved here for $\widehat V$: the composition across scales of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:scales}; the energy bounds of Sec.~\ref{ssec:coarse}, which
on torus-valued fields use that $V^\sharp$ is the abelian average of the
angles, while $\widehat V$ averages their sines; the labels, sites and
chains of Secs.~\ref{ssec:branches} and~\ref{ssec:pathlaw},
Proposition~\ref{prop:nonconvex} among them; the islands, their threshold
and the label covariance of Secs.~\ref{ssec:counting}
to~\ref{ssec:labelcov}, including Theorems~\ref{thm:badcross}
and~\ref{thm:offchartmass} and Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}; and the
one-step and multiscale results of Secs.~\ref{ssec:relstep}
to~\ref{ssec:allscales}. Proposition~\ref{prop:projavg}(i) bounds the
distance between the two maps; it does not transfer these results.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[the route to (D) with $\widehat V$]\label{rem:projroute}
With $\widehat V$ in place of $V^\sharp$, the chart decay holds at
$\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:projtransfer}), the good
side holds at every field (Corollary~\ref{cor:projpathlaw}), and the bad
side of item~(i) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains} holds for every restricting
set, uniformly in the exterior and in the inside links, with no condition
(Theorem~\ref{thm:projresponse}). The statements that the cube
condition~(D) still needs are items (ii)--(iv) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}
with $\widehat V$ for $V^\sharp$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item the island comparison: a covariance bound for every coarse field,
uniform in the exterior, decaying at the rate $2\alpha_G$ without a
floor, and the mixed differences in tree form;
\item the island threshold at the scale of the cube;
\item the effective action at every scale with summable one-step errors.
\end{enumerate}
The results that the paper proves towards (a) and (b) for $V^\sharp$, and
the energy bounds of Sec.~\ref{ssec:coarse}, are not re-derived for
$\widehat V$ (Remark~\ref{rem:projscope}). Neither (D) nor the mass gap is
proved.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Counting bad labels}\label{ssec:counting}

A label is bad when some fine plaquette in a fixed neighbourhood is bad:
for the relative link labels this is the content of
Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff} and Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}, and for the
coarse-curvature labels it is Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}. The chessboard
estimate of Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} bounds the probability that a set of
fine plaquettes is simultaneously bad by a product. The following lemma
transfers such a bound to the labels, and the proposition after it shows
that the loss it incurs is the true loss of this kind of argument.

\begin{lemma}[coverage counting]\label{lem:coverage}
Let a family of events $E_y$, indexed by a finite set, be such that each
$E_y$ forces at least one of a specified set $Q_y$ of at most $M$ sites to
be bad, and suppose that each site lies in at most $H$ of the sets $Q_y$
and that $\Pr(\text{all sites of }T\text{ bad})\le p^{|T|}$ for every
finite set $T$ of sites. Then for every nonempty set $S$ of $n$ labels and
$k=\lceil n/H\rceil$,
\[
\Pr\Bigl(\bigcap_{y\in S}E_y\Bigr)\le\binom{Mn}k\,p^k\le(eMHp)^k ,
\]
and if $A=eMHp<1$ then $\Pr(\bigcap_{y\in S}E_y)\le A^{n/H}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the intersection, the union of the witness sets $Q_y$, $y\in S$,
contains at least $k$ distinct bad sites, since one site witnesses at most
$H$ labels; the union has at most $Mn$ sites. A union bound over its
$k$-subsets and the product bound for each give the first inequality, and
$\binom{Mn}k\le(eMn/k)^k\le(eMH)^k$ since $n/k\le H$. No choice of witness
is required to be measurable, and no independence is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[the exponent $1/H$ cannot be improved]\label{prop:coverageopt}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:coverage} let $H$ labels share one site
and let each be bad exactly when that site is bad, with probability $p$.
Then $\Pr(\text{all }H\text{ labels bad})=p$, so every bound of the form
$q^{|S|}$ valid for this class of families has $q\ge p^{1/H}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The event that all $H$ labels are bad is the event that the one site is
bad.
\end{proof}

For the labels of Sec.~\ref{ssec:branches} the witness sets are boxes of
side $7$ for the relative link labels, $M=7^4$, $H=4^4$, and of side $11$
when the coarse-curvature labels are included, $M=11^4$, $H=6^4$, with $p$
the chessboard bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} at the threshold of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}. Lemma~\ref{lem:coverage} then charges a bad
island of $n$ blocks at the rate $A^{n/H}$; the proposition shows that
the denominator $H$ is not an artefact of the union bound but the price of
knowing only that each label has a witness, and that a better exponent
needs joint information on the gauge field.

\subsection{Islands and the environment}\label{ssec:environment}

Two bad islands are separated by good blocks, and the question is how the
weight of one island depends on the state of the other. The following
lemma answers it in terms of a single quantity: the cross-ratio of a
kernel on the good layer between them. It integrates arbitrary measures on
the two islands, including hard constraints and sums over branches, and
their masses do not enter.

\begin{lemma}[integration through a common kernel]\label{lem:kernel}
Let $K(x,y)>0$ be measurable, let $a_0,a_1$ and $b_0,b_1$ be finite
positive measures on the spaces of $x$ and of $y$, and suppose that
$Z_{ij}=\iint K\,da_i\,db_j$ is finite and positive for the four pairs
$i,j\in\{0,1\}$. If
\[
e^{-\varDelta}\le\frac{K(x_1,y_1)K(x_0,y_0)}{K(x_1,y_0)K(x_0,y_1)}\le
e^{\varDelta}
\]
for all $x_i$ in the support of $a_i$ and $y_j$ in the support of $b_j$,
then
\[
\bigl|\log Z_{11}+\log Z_{00}-\log Z_{10}-\log Z_{01}\bigr|\le\varDelta .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Multiply the upper inequality by $K(x_1,y_0)K(x_0,y_1)$ and integrate
against $da_1(x_1)\,da_0(x_0)\,db_1(y_1)\,db_0(y_0)$; by Tonelli the left
side integrates to $Z_{11}Z_{00}$ and the right side to $e^{\varDelta}
Z_{10}Z_{01}$. The lower inequality gives the reverse bound, and the four
numbers are positive, so logarithms may be taken.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[two labels]\label{cor:twolabels}
Let $(A,B)$ be a pair of binary labels with joint law $\Pr(A=i,B=j)=Z_{ij}
/\sum Z$, all $Z_{ij}>0$, and let $\varDelta$ bound the connected
normaliser as in Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel}. Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
\bigl|\Pr(B=1\mid A=1)-\Pr(B=1\mid A=0)\bigr|\le\tanh\frac\varDelta4,\\
|\Cov(A,B)|\le\frac14\tanh\frac\varDelta4 ,
\end{gathered}
\]
and both bounds are attained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The conditional odds of $B=1$ given $A=1$ and given $A=0$ are $Z_{11}/
Z_{10}$ and $Z_{01}/Z_{00}$, whose logarithms differ by $\log(Z_{11}Z_{00}/
Z_{10}Z_{01})$, of modulus at most $\varDelta$. For logistic probabilities
$\sigma(u)=(1+e^{-u})^{-1}$ the difference $\sigma(u+s)-\sigma(u)$ is
largest at $u=-s/2$ by the symmetry $\sigma(-u)=1-\sigma(u)$, where it
equals $\sigma(s/2)-\sigma(-s/2)=\tanh(s/4)$, and it increases in $s$. The
covariance is $\Pr(A=1)\Pr(A=0)$ times the difference of the conditional
probabilities, and $\Pr(A=1)\Pr(A=0)\le\frac14$. The weights
$Z_{11}=Z_{00}=e^{\varDelta/2}$, $Z_{10}=Z_{01}=1$ have $\Pr(A=1)=\frac12$
and conditional probabilities $\sigma(\pm\varDelta/2)$, so both bounds are
equalities.
\end{proof}

When the kernel is the partition function of a calm layer, its cross-ratio
is a connected second derivative of a log-normaliser, and that derivative
is a covariance under the law of the layer.

\begin{lemma}[connected normalisers]\label{lem:connected}
Let $D$ be a fixed product of balls in the coordinates $z$ of a window, let
$\mathcal U(z;\eta,\zeta)$ be smooth in all variables, with $\eta$ and
$\zeta$ exterior parameters, and let $Z(\eta,\zeta)=\int_De^{-\mathcal U}
dz$. Then for directions $u$ in $\eta$ and $v$ in $\zeta$,
\[
\partial_u\partial_v\log Z=-\E\bigl[\partial_u\partial_v\mathcal U\bigr]+
\Cov\bigl(\partial_u\mathcal U,\partial_v\mathcal U\bigr),
\]
expectation and covariance under $e^{-\mathcal U}dz/Z$ on $D$. If
$\mathcal U$ is a sum of local terms and the supports of $\eta$ and
$\zeta$ are farther apart than its range, the first term vanishes. If in
addition, at every point of two segments $\eta_0\to\eta_1$ and
$\zeta_0\to\zeta_1$, the law on $D$ satisfies
\[
|\Cov(F,H)|\le\mathcal A\,\lVert\nabla F\rVert\,\lVert\nabla H\rVert\,
e^{-\alpha\dist(\operatorname{supp}\nabla F,\operatorname{supp}\nabla H)}
\]
for all smooth $F$ and $H$, then
\[
\begin{split}
&\bigl|\log Z(\eta_1,\zeta_1)-\log Z(\eta_1,\zeta_0)-\log Z(\eta_0,\zeta_1)
+\log Z(\eta_0,\zeta_0)\bigr|\\
&\qquad\le\mathcal AL_\eta L_\zeta\,
\lVert\eta_1-\eta_0\rVert\,\lVert\zeta_1-\zeta_0\rVert\,e^{-\alpha d'},
\end{split}
\]
where $L_\eta,L_\zeta$ bound the gradients in $z$ of $\partial_u\mathcal U$
and $\partial_v\mathcal U$ per unit of $u,v$ along the segments, and $d'$
is a lower bound there for the distance between the supports of those
gradients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Differentiating under the integral sign on the fixed domain $D$ gives
$\partial_v\log Z=-\E[\partial_v\mathcal U]$ and then the identity, the
covariance arising from the derivative of the normalised density. The
left side of the integrated bound is the integral of $\partial_u\partial_v
\log Z$ over the product of the two segments, in which the first term of
the identity vanishes and the second is bounded by the covariance
hypothesis.
\end{proof}

On a good window the law of Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw}, with the
Hessian bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} on the graph, supplies a
covariance bound of the required form, so Lemma~\ref{lem:connected}
controls the connected normaliser for continuous changes of the sources
inside the chart, and Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} then integrates the hard
island weights on the two sides. What the three statements do not supply
is the kernel bound when a label change moves the domain $D$, enters an
island, or adds a branch of Proposition~\ref{prop:branches}; that is the
open comparison of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}. The last result of this
subsection shows that the comparison cannot be replaced by rarity, however
strong.

\begin{proposition}[rarity does not control the environment]\label{prop:hiddenbit}
Fix $q\in(0,1)$. Let $S$ be a fair bit and, given $S$, let the labels $B_x$
be independent Bernoulli variables with parameter $q/2$ if $S=0$ and $q$
if $S=1$. Then $\Pr(B_x=1\ \forall x\in T)\le q^{|T|}$ for every finite
$T$, and for all distinct $x,y$,
\[
\Cov(B_x,B_y)=\frac{q^2}{16} .
\]
If the configuration is a function of the labels, every covariance under
the law conditioned on all labels vanishes, and the covariance of two
observables is the covariance of their conditional expectations. More
generally, for a binary label $B$ with $p=\Pr(B=1\mid\xi)\in(0,1)$ given
the other labels $\xi$ and $\varDelta_F=\mu(F\mid B=1,\xi)-\mu(F\mid
B=0,\xi)$,
\[
\begin{gathered}
\Cov(F,\mathbf 1_B\mid\xi)=p(1-p)\varDelta_F,\\
\Cov\bigl(\E[F\mid B,\xi],\E[H\mid B,\xi]\bigm|\xi\bigr)=p(1-p)\varDelta_F
\varDelta_H .
\end{gathered}
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Given $S$ the labels are independent, so $\Pr(B_x=1\ \forall x\in T)=
\frac12((q/2)^{|T|}+q^{|T|})\le q^{|T|}$, and $\Cov(B_x,B_y)=\Var(\Pr(B_x=
1\mid S))=\frac14(q-q/2)^2=q^2/16$ by the conditional covariance formula.
The two identities follow by expanding the expectations over the two
values of $B$.
\end{proof}

The example satisfies every finite-intersection rarity bound at every
order, yet its labels have a covariance with a positive floor at all
distances. A labelling argument must therefore bound $\varDelta_F
\varDelta_H$, the change of the conditional expectations under a label
flip, and not only the probability of the flip: small $p$ does not help
when $\varDelta_F\varDelta_H$ does not decay, and normalising by $p$ can
cancel it. That bound is the connected normaliser of
Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel}, which is where the island comparison enters.

\subsection{Coupling cost and the comparison lemma}\label{ssec:couplingcost}

The proofs of Lemmas~\ref{lem:blockK} and~\ref{lem:comparison} take a
coupling that minimises a weighted sum of expected displacements and
derive, from its minimality, one inequality per site. The following lemma
isolates this step; it needs neither stationarity of the optimal coupling
under the local updates nor any property of the updates beyond the two
stated ones, and its conclusion is exactly the recurrence that
Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison} iterates.

\begin{lemma}[minimality gives the recurrence]\label{lem:minimality}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $\Pi$ be a set of couplings of two
probability measures on a product of metric spaces indexed by $I$, let
$d_i(\pi)=\E_\pi\dist(x_i,x'_i)$, let $w_i>0$, and let $S\subset I$.
Suppose $\pi\in\Pi$
minimises $\sum_iw_id_i$ over $\Pi$, and that for each $i\notin S$ there
is $\pi^{(i)}\in\Pi$ with $d_j(\pi^{(i)})=d_j(\pi)$ for $j\ne i$ and
$d_i(\pi^{(i)})\le\sum_jC_{ij}d_j(\pi)$. Then $d_i(\pi)\le\sum_jC_{ij}
d_j(\pi)$ for every $i\notin S$. If $\pi$ is minimal only up to
$\varepsilon_i$ against $\pi^{(i)}$, then $d_i(\pi)\le\sum_jC_{ij}d_j(\pi)
+\varepsilon_i/w_i$. Consequently, if $C_{ij}\ge0$, $\sum_iw_iC_{ij}\le
\theta w_j$ with $\theta<1$ and $d_i(\pi)\le D$ for $i\in S$, then
$\sum_{i\notin S}w_id_i(\pi)\le\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}\sum_{j\in S}w_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $\pi^{(i)}$ changes only the $i$-th displacement, minimality gives
$w_id_i(\pi)\le w_id_i(\pi^{(i)})+\varepsilon_i$, and the bound on
$d_i(\pi^{(i)})$ gives the recurrence. The last statement is the arithmetic
of Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison}: with $X=\sum_{i\notin S}w_id_i$ and $Y=
\sum_{i\in S}w_id_i\le D\sum_{i\in S}w_i$, the recurrence and the column
condition give $X\le\sum_jd_j\sum_iw_iC_{ij}\le\theta(X+Y)$, so $X\le
\theta Y/(1-\theta)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[minimal couplings exist]\label{lem:minimiser}
Let $\mu,\nu$ be probability measures on a compact metric space $\Omega$
and $c$ a continuous cost on $\Omega\times\Omega$. The set of couplings of
$\mu$ and $\nu$ is nonempty and compact in the weak topology, and $c$
attains its minimum on it.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The product $\mu\otimes\nu$ is a coupling; the marginal conditions are
closed in the weak topology, and the probability measures on the compact
space $\Omega\times\Omega$ form a compact set, so the couplings form a
compact set on which the continuous functional $\pi\mapsto\int c\,d\pi$
attains its minimum.
\end{proof}

The displacements $d_i$ are continuous costs on the compact product of
copies of $\SU(2)$, so the minimal couplings of Lemma~\ref{lem:blockK} and
of the block comparison exist by Lemma~\ref{lem:minimiser}, and the
coupled update of one site is the choice of $\pi^{(i)}$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:minimality}. The recurrence, the column-weighted and
row-weighted comparisons of Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison}, the decay with a
floor of Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcomparison}, and the two lemmas above are
also written in Lean~4 in the archive, with Mathlib as the library; the
specification of $\SU(2)$ enters only through the
hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:minimality}, which the proofs of
Secs.~\ref{sec:plaqblocks} and~\ref{sec:bypass} supply by hand.

The block response that Lemma~\ref{lem:blockK} bounds can also be
computed exactly in one direction, which measures the room that the
coupling argument leaves.

\begin{proposition}[the block response at zero field]\label{prop:blockresponse}
Let $\mu_0$ be the law of three unit quaternions $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ with
density proportional to $\exp(\beta_W\operatorname{Re}(y_1y_2y_3))$ with
respect to Haar measure, and $h$ a unit quaternion. Then $f=\ip{y_1}h+
\ip{\overline{y_2y_3}}h$ is $1$-Lipschitz for the sum of the three chordal
distances and
\[
\begin{split}
\Cov_{\mu_0}\bigl(f,\ip{y_1}h\bigr)&=\frac14\Bigl(1+\frac{I_2(\beta_W)}
{I_1(\beta_W)}\Bigr)\\
&=\frac14\Bigl(1+\frac{\beta_W}4-\frac{\beta_W^3}{96}+O(\beta_W^5)\Bigr),
\end{split}
\]
which lies between $0.2718$ and $0.27183$ at $\beta_W=0.351$. Hence the
Kantorovich modulus of the block in the field at $y_1$ is at least this
number, and $10\beta_W$ times it exceeds one for $\beta_W>0.3667$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Given $y_1$, the product $w=y_2y_3$ is Haar distributed a priori, and the
weight is $\exp(\beta_W\ip{y_1}{\bar w})$ since $\operatorname{Re}(pq)=
\ip p{\bar q}$ for unit quaternions. So $\bar w$ given $y_1$ follows the
von Mises--Fisher law on $S^3$ with mean direction $y_1$, whose mean
resultant is $\E[\bar w\mid y_1]=A(\beta_W)y_1$ with $A=I_2/I_1$, the ratio
of the Bessel functions of orders $\frac p2$ and $\frac p2-1$ for $p=4$,
and the marginal of $y_1$ is Haar. Multiplication and conjugation preserve
the chordal distance, so $f$ changes by at most the sum of the three
displacements. Since $y_1$ is uniform, $\Var\ip{y_1}h=\frac14$ and
$\Cov(\ip{\bar w}h,\ip{y_1}h)=\E[A\ip{y_1}h^2]=A/4$. The series of $A$
follows from $I_\nu(x)=\sum_m(x/2)^{2m+\nu}/(m!\,\Gamma(m+\nu+1))$, and
the derivative of $\mu_b(f)$ in the field $b_1$ at $b=0$ in the direction
$h$ is the covariance, which bounds the modulus below. By
Lemma~\ref{q-lem:moments}(ii) and~(iv), $0.08721\le A(0.351)\le0.08731$,
because $6.373201\le2.52453^2$ and $9.123201\ge3.02046^2$; this gives the
two bounds at $0.351$. The function $\frac52\beta_W(1+A(\beta_W))$
increases, since $A'$ is a variance by Lemma~\ref{q-lem:moments}(i), and at
$\beta_W=0.3667$, where $0.3667^2+\frac{25}4\le2.52676^2$,
Lemma~\ref{q-lem:moments}(iv) gives $A\ge0.3667/4.02676>0.09106>
\frac4{3.667}-1$, so it exceeds one there.
\end{proof}

\subsection{From one scale to the next}\label{ssec:scalestep}

A multiscale version of Sec.~\ref{ssec:scales} would eliminate the fine
coordinates of a window scale by scale. The following statements say what
one elimination step preserves and what it does not, for the quadratic
forms that Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} controls at one scale. They are
finite matrix lemmas; no all-scale construction is made here.

\begin{lemma}[weighted Schur complements]\label{lem:schur}
Let $H=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ be
positive definite in retained and eliminated coordinates, with
$S=A-BD^{-1}B^*$ its constrained minimum form on the retained ones. Give
both index sets a metric, and for a $1$-Lipschitz function $\phi$ and
$\alpha\ge0$ write $\lVert M\rVert_\alpha$ for the supremum over $\phi$ of
the operator norms of $e^{\alpha\phi}Me^{-\alpha\phi}$. If $\lVert A
\rVert_\alpha\le a$, $\lVert B\rVert_\alpha\le b$ and $\lVert D^{-1}
\rVert_\alpha\le g$, then $\lVert S\rVert_\alpha\le a+b^2g$, and
$|S_{ij}|\le(a+b^2g)e^{-\alpha\dist(i,j)}$. If $H_0$ has blocks $A_0,B_0,
D_0$ with the same bounds and $\lVert A-A_0\rVert_\alpha,\lVert B-B_0
\rVert_\alpha,\lVert D-D_0\rVert_\alpha\le\varepsilon$, then
\[
\lVert S-S_0\rVert_\alpha\le\varepsilon(1+bg)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Conjugation by $e^{\alpha\phi}$ respects products and inverses, so the
weighted norm is submultiplicative on compatible blocks, and $\lVert B^*
\rVert_\alpha=\lVert B\rVert_\alpha$ because $-\phi$ is admissible; the
bound on $S$ follows from its formula. For the entry bound take $\phi(x)=
\dist(x,j)$. For the difference,
$S-S_0=(A-A_0)-(B-B_0)D^{-1}B^*-B_0D^{-1}(B-B_0)^*-B_0(D^{-1}-D_0^{-1})
B_0^*$ with $D^{-1}-D_0^{-1}=-D^{-1}(D-D_0)D_0^{-1}$, and the four terms
are bounded by $\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon bg$, $\varepsilon bg$ and
$\varepsilon b^2g^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[what form comparison preserves]\label{prop:formstability}
Let $H_0,H$ be positive definite with $(1-\varepsilon)H_0\le H\le(1+
\varepsilon)H_0$, $0\le\varepsilon<1$, and for a surjective linear map $Q$
let $S(v)=\inf_{Qx=v}x^{\mathsf T}Hx$ and $S_0$ likewise. Then $(1-
\varepsilon)S_0\le S\le(1+\varepsilon)S_0$. Form comparison does not
preserve locality: on a path of $n$ sites, $H_0=I$ and $H=I+\varepsilon
