$\lvert\log Z_{11}+\log Z_{00}-\log Z_{10}-\log Z_{01}\rvert\le\varDelta$
and the two island labels have conditional covariance at most
$\frac14\tanh(\varDelta/4)$ given the labels of the layer and
$U^{\mathrm{ext}}$. Moreover, for every bounded $F\ge0$ depending on the
links of $L_a\cup p_a\cup x$ only, with $\E_{ij}$ the expectation in
sector $(i,j)$,
\[
e^{-\varDelta}\le\frac{\E_{i1}[F]}{\E_{i0}[F]}\le e^{\varDelta}
\qquad(i=0,1)
\]
whenever the four expectations are positive.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$D_x$ and $D_y$ are convex, so the segments $x(\sigma)$, $y(\tau)$ stay in
them, and $\log K$ is smooth near $D_x\times D_y$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}(iv), so the cross-ratio is the double
integral of $\partial_\sigma\partial_\tau\log K$ over the unit square.
Lemma~\ref{lem:connected} with the fixed domain $D_z$ gives
$\partial_\sigma\partial_\tau\log K=-\E[\partial_\sigma\partial_\tau
\mathcal U]+\Cov(\partial_\sigma\mathcal U,\partial_\tau\mathcal U)$, and
the first term vanishes by Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}(v). Put
$F=\partial_\sigma\mathcal U$, $H=\partial_\tau\mathcal U$: $\nabla_zF$ is
supported on the $z$-links at $d_a\le s+4$, $\nabla_zH$ on those at
$d_b\le s+4$, at distance at least $d'$, with
$\lVert\nabla_zF\rVert\le\Lambda_2\lVert x_1-x_0\rVert$ and
$\lVert\nabla_zH\rVert\le\Lambda_2\lVert y_1-y_0\rVert$ pointwise. Apply
\eqref{eq:layerbound} with $\varphi(e)=-\dist(e,\operatorname{supp}
\nabla_zF)$, which is $1$-Lipschitz, equal to $0$ on the support of
$\nabla_zF$ and at most $-d'$ on that of $\nabla_zH$; this gives the bound
on the covariance uniformly in $(\sigma,\tau)$, and
$\lVert x_1-x_0\rVert\le2r\sqrt{n_x}$ since each coordinate is a vector of
$\g$ of norm at most $r$. The consequences are Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel}
applied to $a_i,b_j,K$ and Corollary~\ref{cor:twolabels}. For the last
statement, $F\Phi_a^i$ is again a product of $a$-factors, so the
factorisation holds with the measures $Fa_i$ and $a_i$, the same $K$ and
the same $b_j$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} for these gives
$\lvert\log Z(Fa_i,b_1)+\log Z(a_i,b_0)-\log Z(Fa_i,b_0)-\log Z(a_i,b_1)
\rvert\le\varDelta$ with $Z(Fa_i,b_j)/Z(a_i,b_j)=\E_{ij}[F]$.
\end{proof}

The last bound is the quantity that Proposition~\ref{prop:hiddenbit} says
a labelling argument must control: the change of the conditional
expectation of an observable of one island under a flip of the label of
the other, with the branches, the hard label constraints and the
disintegration densities of both islands integrated, not compared. The
hypothesis~\eqref{eq:layerbound} is Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(ii) for
the layer law, but in other coordinates. The chart law of that theorem is
written in the coordinates $\xi$ of $T_U$, on the product of balls
$\mathrm{Box}_r$; the label coordinate of a non-path link is
$\zeta_e=\xi_e+h_e(S\xi)$, so the label event
$\prod_e\{\lVert\zeta_e\rVert\le r\}$ is a deformation of
$\mathrm{Box}_r$, convex in $\zeta$ and not in $\xi$, and the Hessian of
the density in $\zeta$ acquires the term $\langle\nabla_\xi\bar H,
D^2\xi\rangle$, which is not coordinate invariant. The next theorem
carries the proof over to the coordinates $\zeta$; it needs the layer
calmer than Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} needs a chart, and a coupling
four times larger.

\begin{theorem}[the layer law obeys the chart bound]\label{thm:layerbound}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda=\beta_W/4$, and let the data be those of
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}. Let $W'$ be the set of blocks of
$\Lambda$ at distance at least $s+3$ from both islands, and assume
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $r\le8\cdot10^{-5}$ and $4\cdot10^5c_3(\eta+62r)\le\frac1{195}$,
which holds when $\eta+62r\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$;
\item $\lambda\ge240\,c_6$, which holds when $\beta_W\ge8.93\cdot10^{17}$;
\item every block outside $\Lambda$ at distance at most two from $W'$ is
good and the constraints of its pairs hold; this is void when $\Lambda$
contains the blocks at distance at most two from $W'$.
\end{enumerate}
Then~\eqref{eq:layerbound} holds with $\mathcal A=120/\lambda=480/
\beta_W$ and every $\alpha\le\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$, uniformly in
$(x,y)\in D_x\times D_y$, in $U^{\mathrm{ext}}$, in $\Lambda$ and in the
width $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All constants without a name are those of the proofs of
Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart} and~\ref{thm:chartdecay} and of
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}, at $\vartheta=0$ unless a weight is
written: $\mathcal G=BB^*\ge\frac1{17}$, $\lVert B^*z\rVert_\infty\le0.88
\max_k\lVert z_k\rVert$, $\lVert R_k(X)\rVert\le12c_3\lVert X
\rVert_\infty^2$, the rows of $A-B$ of norm at most $7.35c_3s$,
$Y=B^*(AB^*)^{-1}$ with $\lVert Y\rVert\le11.32$, $\bar P=S-Y(A-B)S$ with
$\lVert\bar P\rVert\le4.80$ and $\lVert\bar P\rVert_{1\to1}\le3.003$,
$x_v=\bar Pv$ and $x_{vv'}=-YD^2c(X)[x_v,x_{v'}]$ with
$\lVert x_{vv'}\rVert_1\le1564.3\,c_3\lvert v\rvert\lvert v'\rvert$. Put
$s'=32r$ for the chart radius.

\emph{Step 1: the background is calm.} Let $U$ be the point of the fibre
whose non-path links in $W'$ are $R(c)$ and whose path links there are
the solutions $\Gamma_k(0)$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}. Take a
plaquette $p$ with a vertex in a block of $W'^+$. Its links are based in
blocks at distance at most two from $W'$, which are good, by the sector
event inside $\Lambda$ and by (c) outside it. A plaquette contains at most
two path links, one of each of its directions: a path link $(2y+e_\mu,\mu)$
has exactly one odd coordinate at its base, and two such links of one
direction on one plaquette would have to be opposite sides with bases
differing by $e_\rho$, $\rho\ne\mu$, which gives one of them two odd
coordinates. The plaquette of $R(c)$ at
$p$ is $I$ unless both coordinates of the corner in its plane are odd, and
it is then the coarse plaquette of a good block, so
$\delta(R(c)_p,I)\le\eta$. Replacing the four links one at a time, with
$\delta\le d$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}), bi-invariance and
$d(\Gamma_k,c_k)\le14r$, gives $\delta(U_p,I)\le\eta+2\cdot14r+2r$. So the
defect $\kappa_0$ of the background satisfies
$\kappa_0+s'\le\eta+62r$, and (a) is the hypothesis
$4\cdot10^5c_3(\kappa_0+s')\le\frac1{195}$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}(iv) at radius $s'$; by
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} it implies $s'\le1/(6000c_3)$,
$\kappa_0+6s'\le10^{-8}$ and $c_3s'\le1.29\cdot10^{-8}$.

\emph{Step 2: the two coordinates.} Let $\rho_1=\frac54r$, which is at
most $10^{-4}$ by (a). For $\zeta$ with every $\lVert\zeta_e\rVert\le
\rho_1$ let $U'$ be the point of the fibre with non-path links
$R_e(c)e^{\zeta_e}$, and $X=\log(U^{-1}U')$ link by link. On the non-path
links $\lVert X_e\rVert\le\rho_1$; on a path link, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound} at the radii $r$ and $\rho_1$,
$\lVert X_{d_k}\rVert\le14r+14\rho_1=31.5r$. So $t=\lVert X\rVert_\infty
<s'$, and $BX=-R(X)$ with $\lVert R_k(X)\rVert\le12c_3t^2$. With
$z=\mathcal G^{-1}BX$ and $\nu=X-B^*z\in T_U$ we get $\max_k\lVert z_k
\rVert\le204c_3t^2\le8.2\cdot10^{-5}r$ and $\lVert\nu\rVert_\infty\le
t(1+180c_3t)\le31.51r<s'$, and $z$ is the fixed point that defines
$h(\nu)$, so $U'=\Phi(\nu)$ with $\lVert h(\nu)\rVert_\infty\le
7.2\cdot10^{-5}r$. Hence the map $\Psi(\xi)=\xi+g(\xi)$,
$g(\xi)=h(S\xi)$ restricted to the non-path links, which sends the chart
coordinate to the label coordinate, maps a subset of
$\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$ onto $\{\lVert\zeta_e\rVert\le\rho_1\}$; it is
injective there because two chart points with the same non-path links
within $\rho_1$ of $R(c)$ have the same path links by
Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}. Its derivative is $1+Dg$ with
$Dg=-Y(A-B)S$ restricted to the non-path links, so
\[
\begin{gathered}
\lVert Dg\rVert\le3.6\cdot10^{-5},\qquad\lVert Dg\rVert_{(0.197)}\le
7.0\cdot10^{-5},\\
\lVert Dg\rVert_{1\to1}\le2.0\cdot10^{-5},
\end{gathered}
\]
from $\lVert S\rVert_{1\to1}\le1+2\cdot8.01(\frac18+260\kappa_0)$, the
rows of $A-B$, and the weighted bounds of
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}. Thus $\Psi$ is a diffeomorphism
onto the $\rho_1$-balls, and $J=D\xi=(1+Dg)^{-1}$ has the norms
$j_0=1+3.6\cdot10^{-5}$, $j_\vartheta=1+7.0\cdot10^{-5}$ and
$j_1=1+2.0\cdot10^{-5}$ in the three norms.

\emph{Step 3: the density.} By Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}(iii) and the
proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, the constrained law on the chart
has density $e^{-\bar H(\xi)}$ in $\xi$. By Step 2 and the change of
variables $\zeta=\Psi(\xi)$, the law conditioned on the label event has
density $e^{-\tilde U}\mathbf 1_{\{\lVert\zeta_e\rVert\le r\}}$ with
\[
\tilde U(\zeta)=\bar H(\xi(\zeta))+\log\det\bigl(1+Dg(\xi(\zeta))\bigr),
\]
smooth on the $\rho_1$-balls. It is the law of
Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw}, since the disintegration of a smooth
positive density along a submersion is unique up to a factor constant on
each fibre, and the layer law $\mu_{x,y}$ is this law with the inside
links at distance $s+3$ frozen.

\emph{Step 4: the lower bound on the Hessian.} By the chain rule, with
$a=Jv$ and $M=1+Dg$,
\[
\begin{split}
\partial_v^2\tilde U={}&\operatorname{Hess}_\xi\bar H[a,a]+\bigl\langle
\nabla_\xi\bar H,D^2\xi[v,v]\bigr\rangle\\
&+\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(M^{-1}M''\bigr)-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((M^{-1}
M')^2\bigr),
\end{split}
\]
where $M'=D^2g[a,\cdot\,]$, $M''=D^3g[a,a,\cdot\,]+D^2g[D^2\xi[v,v],\cdot\,]$
and $D^2\xi[v,v]=-JD^2g[a,a]$. The first term is at least
$(\frac\lambda{30}-c_6)\lvert a\rvert^2$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}(ii), (iii), since
$\frac1{26}-4\cdot10^5c_3(\kappa_0+s')\ge\frac1{30}$. For the second, the
gradient of $\bar H$ in one link is the sum of $\lambda DQ[x_v]$, the
derivative of the Haar densities and the derivatives of the two
determinants; $\lvert DQ[x_v]\rvert\le12(\kappa_0+6s')\lVert x_v\rVert_1$,
the Haar part is at most $0.84\lVert x_v\rVert_1$, and the determinants
give $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(A^*(AA^*)^{-1}A_v)$ and
$\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\bar P(\bar P^*\bar P)^{-1}\bar P^*
YA_v)$ with $A_v=D^2c(X)[x_v,\cdot\,]$, bounded by $5\lVert A_v\rVert_1$ and
$11.32\lVert A_v\rVert_1$ since $AA^*\ge\frac1{25}$ and the second operator
is $Y$ followed by a projection; and $\lVert A_v\rVert_1\le2\dim G\,c_3
\lVert x_v\rVert_1$ because each row of $D^2c$ has rank at most $\dim G$
and each link enters two rows. So every component of $\nabla_\xi\bar H$
is at most $12\lambda(\kappa_0+6s')\cdot3.003+296.5\,c_3$, and with
$\lVert D^2\xi[v,v]\rVert_1\le j_1j_0^2\cdot1564.3\,c_3\lvert v\rvert^2$ the
second term is at most $(4.35\cdot10^{-3}\lambda+4.64\cdot10^5c_3^2)
\lvert v\rvert^2$. The derivatives of $g$ are those of $X$:
$D^2g[a,\cdot\,]=-YA_a\bar P$ and
\[
\begin{split}
D^3g[a,b,\cdot\,]={}&YA_aYA_b\bar P+YA_bYA_a\bar P\\
&-YD^3c[x_a,x_b,\cdot\,]\bar P-YD^2c[x_{ab},\cdot\,]\bar P,
\end{split}
\]
restricted to the non-path links, and the Hilbert--Schmidt bound
$\lVert A_a\rVert_2^2\le2\dim G\,c_3^2\lVert\bar P\rVert^2\lvert a\rvert^2$
together with $\lvert\operatorname{Tr}(ST)\rvert\le\lVert S\rVert
\lVert T\rVert_1$ and $\lVert ST\rVert_1\le\lVert S\rVert_2\lVert T
\rVert_2$ bounds the two traces term by term by
$(4.07+1.70+0.08+5.10+15.30)\cdot10^5c_3^2\lvert v\rvert^2$. Since
$c_6=6.81\cdot10^5\dim G\,c_3^2$, the part of $\partial_v^2\tilde U$
that does not grow with $\lambda$, beyond the $c_6$ of the first term, is
at most $1.512\,c_6\lvert v\rvert^2$, and by (b)
\[
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hess}_\zeta\tilde U&\ge\lambda\Bigl(\frac{1/30-1/240}
{(1+3.6\cdot10^{-5})^2}-4.35\cdot10^{-3}-\frac{1.512}{240}\Bigr)\\
&\ge0.0185\,\lambda\ge\frac\lambda{60}.
\end{split}
\]
\emph{Step 5: locality of the Hessian.} The same four terms, with the
vectors $p=wu$, $q=w^{-1}u'$ for $w=e^{\vartheta\varphi}$,
$\vartheta=0.197$, are bounded as in the paragraph ``The Hessian'' of the
proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}: the weights of $x_p$ and
$x_q$ on the links of one pair cancel up to $e^{2\vartheta}$, the
conjugation of $A_a$ by $w$ costs at most $e^\vartheta$, and the other
factors are bounded in $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{(\vartheta)}$ by
$\bar p\le5.80$, $y\le14.96$ and $j_\vartheta$. With
$\lVert\operatorname{Hess}_\xi\bar H\rVert_{(0.197)}\le2068\lambda$ this
gives
\[
\begin{split}
\lVert\operatorname{Hess}_\zeta\tilde U\rVert_{(0.197)}&\le\lambda\Bigl(
2068\,j_\vartheta^2+9.41\cdot10^{-3}+\frac{5.88}{240}\Bigr)\\
&\le2068.4\,\lambda .
\end{split}
\]
\emph{Step 6: the covariance bound.} The proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(ii) now applies word for word with
$\mathrm{Box}_r$ replaced by the product of the $r$-balls in $\zeta$, both
being products of balls in the coordinates in which the Hessian bounds of
Steps 4 and 5 hold, and with the radii of the approximation
$\frac32r,\frac74r,2r$ replaced by $1.1r,1.2r,1.25r$, for which the
convex penalty has Hessian at least $\frac1{22}$ outside $1.1r$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}(ii) gives
$\lVert\operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{Hess}H_n)^w-\operatorname{Hess}
H_n\rVert\le\frac\lambda{120}$ for $\alpha\le0.197(240\cdot2068.4)^{-1/2}
=2.79\cdot10^{-4}$, which contains $\alpha_G$, and the weighted
Helffer--Sjöstrand representation gives the bound with $\mathcal A=2/m=
120/\lambda$. Freezing the inside links at distance $s+3$ restricts the
Hessian to a principal submatrix, which keeps both bounds, and the
argument runs on the free links with the same constants.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[two islands in a good region]\label{cor:twoislands}
Under the hypotheses of Theorems~\ref{thm:factorisation}
and~\ref{thm:layerbound}, with $w\ge2s+8$, every pair of label patterns
with all $Z_{ij}>0$ satisfies
\[
\begin{gathered}
\bigl\lvert\log Z_{11}+\log Z_{00}-\log Z_{10}-\log Z_{01}\bigr\rvert
\le\varDelta,\\
\varDelta=\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{n_xn_y}\,
e^{-2\alpha_G(w-2s-8)},
\end{gathered}
\]
the two island labels have conditional covariance at most
$\frac14\tanh(\varDelta/4)$, and every observable of one island and its
collars changes by a factor in $[e^{-\varDelta},e^{\varDelta}]$ when the
label of the other island is flipped. In the normalisation $r=43\rho$,
$\eta=92\rho$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}, hypothesis (a) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} holds for $\rho\le2.17\cdot10^{-16}$, where
the island threshold with the joining distance $2s+8$ is
$\beta^*=1.122\cdot10^{37}$ for $s=1$ and $1.322\cdot10^{37}$ for $s=5$,
and hypothesis (b) holds at every $\beta_W\ge\beta^*$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:layercross} with $\mathcal A=480/\beta_W$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} and $d'=2(w-2s-8)$. For the numbers,
$\eta+62r=(92+62\cdot43)\rho=2758\rho$, and the threshold is the largest
root of the equation of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} with
$(4s+17)^4-1$ neighbours, the count for the joining distance $2s+8$,
which makes every layer between two islands of width at least $2s+8$:
$\lvert\log q^*\rvert=32481.7$ for $s=1$ and $38354.1$ for $s=5$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[the mixed derivatives of the layer action]\label{lem:lambdatwo}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, let the data be those of
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation} with $r\le8\cdot10^{-5}$, and let
$\kappa\le10^{-8}$ be such that $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ on
$D_z\times D_x\times D_y$ for every plaquette $p$ of $S_K$ that contains
the solved path link of a pair one of whose arguments, the non-path
links of its paths, is a $z$-link.
Then
\[
\Lambda_2\le\beta_Wc_W+c_\psi,\qquad c_W\le101.11,\qquad
c_\psi\le4.94\cdot10^6,
\]
with $c_W$ and $c_\psi$ the explicit functions of $r$ and $\kappa$ given
in~\eqref{eq:cwcpsi}. Under hypotheses (a) and (c) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} the condition holds with
$\kappa=\eta+30r\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, and
\[
\Lambda_2\le99.0001\,\beta_W+4.65\cdot10^6 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Norms on $\g$ are Hilbert--Schmidt norms, $\delta(g,h)=\lVert g-h\rVert$
on $\SU(2)$, and the coordinates are the $\zeta_e$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}, $U_e=R_e(c)e^{\zeta_e}$, with the
reconstruction value $R_e(c)=I$ for a link inside a block and
$R_e(c)=c_k$ for a private link of the pair $k$. For a function $f$ of
the coordinates and two coordinates $g\ne g'$ write
$\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}f\rVert$ for the supremum of
$\lvert\partial_s\partial_tf(\zeta+sv_g+tw_{g'})\rvert$ at $s=t=0$ over
$v,w\in\g$ of norm one placed at $g$ and $g'$: it is the operator norm of
the $(g,g')$ block of the Hessian.

\emph{Step 1: reduction to row sums.} Let $M=\partial_x\nabla_z\mathcal U$,
with blocks $M_{ef}$ for $z$-links $e$ and $x$-links $f$. For vectors $u$
on the $z$-links and $v$ on the $x$-links,
$\lvert\ip u{Mv}\rvert\le\sum_{e,f}\lVert M_{ef}\rVert\lVert u_e\rVert
\lVert v_f\rVert$, and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
$\lVert M\rVert\le\max\{\max_e\sum_f\lVert M_{ef}\rVert,\max_f\sum_e
\lVert M_{ef}\rVert\}$. A term $-\log j(\zeta_e)$ of $\psi$ depends on
one coordinate, so $M_{ef}$ is the sum of the blocks of the Wilson terms
$\beta_WW_p$, $W_p=1-\frac12\ReTr U_p$, of $S_K$ and of the terms
$-\log J_k=\log\det(1-DF_k)$ of $\psi$, $J_k$ the inverse Jacobian of
Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw} and $DF_k$ the differential in $X$ of the
map $F$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound} at the fixed point, that depend on
$e$ and on $f$. It therefore suffices to prove that for every $x$- or
$z$-coordinate $g$
\[
R_g=\sum_{g'}\sum_\tau\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}\tau\rVert\le
\beta_Wc_W+c_\psi ,
\]
$g'$ running over the coordinates of the other class ($z$ if $g$ is an
$x$-coordinate, $x$ if $g$ is a $z$-coordinate) and $\tau$ over the
Wilson terms and the Jacobians that depend on $g$ and $g'$; the bound for
$\partial_y\nabla_z\mathcal U$ is the mirror statement.

\emph{Step 2: the geometry.} (i) Every link lies in six plaquettes.
(ii) The solved path link $\Gamma_k$ of $k=(y,\mu)$ is a function of the
$21$ non-path links of the fourteen paths of nonzero offset
(Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}), its \emph{arguments}: the seven non-path
private links, each in two of these paths, and the fourteen links of
direction $\mu$ in $B(y)$ and $B(y+e_\mu)$ other than $(2y,\mu)$ and
$(2y+2e_\mu,\mu)$, each in one path, the tree links among them being
fixed at $I$. A path of $k$ consists of links of direction $\mu$, so a
non-path private link is an argument of its own pair only, and a link of
direction $\mu$ inside $B(y)$ of the two pairs $(y,\mu)$ and
$(y-e_\mu,\mu)$. Let $K(g)$ be the set of solved pairs having $g$ as an
argument and $n_g$ the number of paths of each containing $g$: $n_g=2$,
$\lvert K(g)\rvert\le1$ for a private link, $n_g=1$,
$\lvert K(g)\rvert\le2$ for an inside link.
(iii) Let $\ell=(a,\mu)$, $a=2y+e_\mu$, be a path link and $\nu\ne\mu$. The
plaquette at $a$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ has the further links
$(a,\nu)$, of offset $e_\mu$, inside $B(y)$; $(a+e_\mu,\nu)$, based at
the root $2y+2e_\mu$, a tree link; and $(a+e_\nu,\mu)$, of offset
$e_\mu+e_\nu$, a non-path private link of $(y,\mu)$. The plaquette at
$a-e_\nu$ has the further links $(a-e_\nu,\mu)$ and $(a-e_\nu,\nu)$, both
based at $2(y-e_\nu)+e_\mu+e_\nu$ and so non-path private links of
$(y-e_\nu,\mu)$ and $(y-e_\nu,\nu)$, and $(a+e_\mu-e_\nu,\nu)=
(2(y+e_\mu-e_\nu)+e_\nu,\nu)$, the path link of $(y+e_\mu-e_\nu,\nu)$.
Hence each of the six plaquettes of a path link carries at most two
non-path links, exactly three of them, those at $a-e_\nu$, carry a
second path link, and no plaquette carries three path links.
(iv) By (iii) a non-path link lies on a plaquette with a path link only
if it is an inside link $(2y+e_\mu,\nu)$ with $\nu<\mu$, the only other
case $\nu>\mu$ being a tree link, or a private link of offset
$e_\mu+e_\nu$ and direction $\mu$ or $\nu$. The first lies on one such
plaquette, the one at $2y+e_\mu$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, with one path
link. The second, $(b,\mu)$ with $b=2y+e_\mu+e_\nu$, plays the role of
$(a+e_\nu,\mu)$ for $a=2y+e_\mu$, on a plaquette with one path link, and
the roles of $(a-e_\nu,\mu)$ for $a=2(y+e_\nu)+e_\mu$ and of
$(a-e_\mu,\mu)$ for $a=2(y+e_\mu)+e_\nu$, which are one plaquette, the
one at $b$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, with two path links. So the six
plaquettes of a non-path link carry at most three path links in all.

\emph{Step 3: one Wilson term.} Let $V_1,\dots,V_4$ be smooth functions
of $(s,t)$ with values in $\SU(2)$, $P=V_1V_2V_3V_4$, and
$a_i=\lVert\partial_sV_i\rVert$, $b_i=\lVert\partial_tV_i\rVert$,
$c_i=\lVert\partial_s\partial_tV_i\rVert$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wilsonmixed}
\bigl\lvert\partial_s\partial_t\tfrac12\ReTr P\bigr\rvert\le\tfrac12
\Bigl(\sum_ia_i\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_jb_j\Bigr)+\tfrac12\,\delta(P,I)
\sum_ic_i .
\end{equation}
Indeed $\partial_s\partial_tP$ is the sum of the products with
$\partial_sV_i$ and $\partial_tV_j$ in two places $i\ne j$, whose traces
have modulus at most $a_ib_j$ by $\lvert\Tr(AB)\rvert\le\lVert A\rVert
\lVert B\rVert$ and unitarity of the other factors, and of the products
with $\partial_s\partial_tV_i$ in place $i$, whose trace is
$\Tr(\tilde P_iQ_i)$ with $Q_i=V_i^{-1}\partial_s\partial_tV_i$ and
$\tilde P_i$ a conjugate of $P$. Differentiating $V_i^*V_i=I$ twice gives
$Q_i+Q_i^*=-(\partial_sV_i)^*\partial_tV_i-(\partial_tV_i)^*\partial_sV_i$,
so $\lvert\ReTr Q_i\rvert\le a_ib_i$, and $\lvert\Tr((\tilde P_i-I)Q_i)
\rvert\le\delta(P,I)c_i$. The orientation of a link does not change
$a_i,b_i,c_i$.

\emph{Step 4: first derivatives.} For $W\in\g$ the map
$\operatorname{ad}W$ is skew for the trace form, with eigenvalues $0$ and
$\pm i\theta$, $\theta=\sqrt2\lVert W\rVert$: in a basis diagonalising
$W=\operatorname{diag}(i\varphi,-i\varphi)$, $\lVert W\rVert=\sqrt2\varphi$,
it multiplies the off-diagonal entries by $\pm2i\varphi$. A power series
$f(\operatorname{ad}W)$ is therefore normal with norm $\max\{\lvert f(0)
\rvert,\lvert f(\pm i\theta)\rvert\}$. For
$\varpi(u)=(1-e^{-u})/u$ one has $\varpi(i\theta)=e^{-i\theta/2}
\frac{\sin(\theta/2)}{\theta/2}$, so with $m(\theta)=\frac{\theta/2}
{\sin(\theta/2)}$, increasing on $(0,2\pi)$,
\begin{gather*}
\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}W)\rVert=1,\quad
\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}W)^{-1}\rVert=m(\theta),\\
\lVert e^{\operatorname{ad}W}-1\rVert\le\theta,\quad
\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}W)-1\rVert\le1-\tfrac1{m(\theta)}+
\tfrac\theta2,\\
\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}W)^{-1}-1\rVert\le m(\theta)-1+m(\theta)
\tfrac\theta2 .
\end{gather*}
The derivative of the exponential is $\frac d{dt}e^{W(t)}=e^{W}\varpi(
\operatorname{ad}W)W'$. Hence a non-path link has
$\lVert\partial_gU_g[v]\rVert=\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}\zeta_g)v\rVert
\le\lVert v\rVert$. Let $k=(y,\mu)$ be solved, $\Gamma_k=c_ke^X$. For a
path $x$ of nonzero offset, $c_k^{-1}P_x=e^{\alpha_x}e^{\beta_x}$, where
$(\alpha_x,\beta_x)$ is $(\operatorname{Ad}(c_k^{-1})\zeta_u,\zeta_q)$
when $P_x=uq$ with $u$ inside $B(y)$ and $q$ private, and
$(\zeta_q,\zeta_{u'})$ when $P_x=qu'$ with $u'$ inside $B(y+e_\mu)$, a
tree link contributing $0$; so $\lVert\alpha_x\rVert,\lVert\beta_x\rVert
\le r$. Put $Z_x=\log(e^{-X}e^{\alpha_x}e^{\beta_x})$; by
Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}, $\lVert X\rVert\le14r$ and $\lVert Z_x\rVert
\le16r$. With $Y=e^{Z_x}$ and $Y^{-1}\partial Y=\varpi(\operatorname{ad}
Z_x)\partial Z_x$,
\begin{align*}
\partial_XZ_x[h]&=-T_xh,\\
T_x&=\varpi(\operatorname{ad}Z_x)^{-1}
\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\beta_x}e^{-\alpha_x})\,\varpi(-\operatorname{ad}X),\\
\partial_{\beta}Z_x[w]&=\varpi(\operatorname{ad}Z_x)^{-1}\varpi(
\operatorname{ad}\beta_x)w,\\
\partial_{\alpha}Z_x[v]&=\varpi(\operatorname{ad}Z_x)^{-1}
\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\beta_x})\varpi(\operatorname{ad}\alpha_x)v .
\end{align*}
With $\theta_Z=16\sqrt2r$, $\theta_X=14\sqrt2r$, $m_1=m(\theta_Z)$, the
last two have norm at most $m_1$, and writing $T_x-1$ as
$(\varpi(\operatorname{ad}Z_x)^{-1}-1)\operatorname{Ad}(\cdot)
\varpi(\cdot)+(\operatorname{Ad}(\cdot)-1)\varpi(\cdot)+(\varpi(-\operatorname{ad}
X)-1)$,
\[
\lVert T_x-1\rVert\le\varepsilon_T=m_1-1+m_1\tfrac{\theta_Z}2+2\sqrt2r
+1-\tfrac1{m(\theta_X)}+\tfrac{\theta_X}2 .
\]
Since $F=-\frac1{16}\sum_xZ_x$ over the fourteen paths, $1-DF_k=\frac18
-\frac1{16}\sum_x(T_x-1)$, so $1-DF_k$ is invertible with
\[
\lVert(1-DF_k)^{-1}\rVert\le\mathsf m=\frac8{1-7\varepsilon_T},
\]
and $\det(1-DF_k)>0$, every eigenvalue of $8(1-DF_k)$ lying within
$7\varepsilon_T<1$ of $1$. The implicit function theorem gives
$\partial_gX=(1-DF_k)^{-1}\partial_gF$ and $\lVert\partial_gF\rVert\le
n_gm_1/16$, and $\lVert\partial_g\Gamma_k[v]\rVert=\lVert e^X\varpi(
\operatorname{ad}X)\partial_gX[v]\rVert\le\lVert\partial_gX[v]\rVert$, so
\[
\lVert\partial_g\Gamma_k\rVert\le\lVert\partial_gX\rVert\le\gamma_g=
\frac{n_gm_1}{2(1-7\varepsilon_T)} :
\]
$\gamma_g=\gamma$ for a private link and $\gamma_g=\frac\gamma2$ for an
inside link, with $\gamma=m_1/(1-7\varepsilon_T)$. In both cases
$\gamma_g\lvert K(g)\rvert\le\gamma$, and the sum of $\gamma_{g'}$ over
the arguments of one pair is at most $7\gamma+14\frac\gamma2=14\gamma$.

\emph{Step 5: higher derivatives.} Let $G(X,\alpha,\beta)=
\log(e^{-X}e^\alpha e^\beta)$ for $X,\alpha,\beta\in\g\otimes\C$ with
$\lVert X\rVert+\lVert\alpha\rVert+\lVert\beta\rVert\le\sigma=\frac12$.
The Hilbert--Schmidt norm is submultiplicative, so
$\lVert e^{-X}e^\alpha e^\beta-I\rVert\le e^\sigma-1<1$, the logarithmic
series converges, $G$ is holomorphic and agrees with the principal
logarithm at real arguments, and $\lVert G\rVert\le M_G=-\log(2-e^{1/2})$.
At a real point with $\lVert X\rVert+\lVert\alpha\rVert+\lVert\beta
\rVert\le16r$ and for unit vectors $v_1,\dots,v_j$ of $\g$ placed in any
of the three slots, $t\mapsto G(\cdot+\sum_it_iv_i)$ is holomorphic on the
polydisc $\lvert t_i\rvert\le\rho_j=(\frac12-16r)/j$, and the Cauchy
estimates give
\[
\lVert D^jG[v_1,\dots,v_j]\rVert\le B_j=M_G\rho_j^{-j}\qquad(j=2,3).
\]
For $g,g'$ arguments of $k$ let $s_{gg'}\le1$ be the number of paths
containing both. Differentiating $X=F(X,\zeta)$ twice and using
$\lVert D_X^2F\rVert\le\frac{14}{16}B_2$,
$\lVert D_XD_gF\rVert\le\frac{n_g}{16}B_2$,
$\lVert D_gD_{g'}F\rVert\le\frac{s_{gg'}}{16}B_2$,
\begin{align*}
\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}X\rVert&\le\frac{\mathsf mB_2}{16}
\bigl(14\gamma_g\gamma_{g'}+n_{g'}\gamma_g+n_g\gamma_{g'}+s_{gg'}\bigr)\\
&\le X_2=\frac{\mathsf mB_2}{16}(14\gamma^2+4\gamma+1).
\end{align*}
The second differential of $\exp$ at $X$ has norm at most
$e^{\lVert X\rVert}$ (each of the $n(n-1)$ terms of the second
derivative of $X^n/n!$ has norm at most $\lVert X\rVert^{n-2}$), so
$\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}\Gamma_k\rVert\le C_2=e^{14r}\gamma^2+X_2$.
For $\mathcal M=1-DF_k$, the chain rule and the same bounds with $B_3$
for the third derivatives of $F$ give
\begin{gather*}
\lVert\partial_g\mathcal M\rVert\le M_1=\frac{B_2}{16}(14\gamma+2),\\
\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}\mathcal M\rVert\le M_2=\frac{B_3}{16}
(14\gamma^2+4\gamma+1)+\frac{14}{16}B_2X_2 ,
\end{gather*}
the terms of $\partial_g\partial_{g'}\mathcal M$ being
$D_X^3F[\partial_gX,\partial_{g'}X]$, $D_X^2D_{g'}F[\partial_gX]$,
$D_X^2D_gF[\partial_{g'}X]$, $D_X^2F[\partial_g\partial_{g'}X]$ and
$D_XD_gD_{g'}F$.

\emph{Step 6: the Wilson terms.} For a plaquette $p$ and a coordinate
$g$ let $A_g(p)$ be the sum over the links of $p$ of the bounds of Step 4
for their derivatives in $g$: $A_g(p)=\mathbf 1_{g\in p}+\gamma_g\,
\#\{k\in K(g):\Gamma_k\in p\}$. By~\eqref{eq:wilsonmixed},
$\lVert\partial_g\partial_{g'}W_p\rVert\le\frac12A_g(p)A_{g'}(p)+\frac12
\delta(U_p,I)C_{gg'}(p)$, with $C_{gg'}(p)\le C_2$ times the number of
solved path links of $p$ with both $g$ and $g'$ as arguments. Put
$S_g(p)=\sum_{g'\ne g}A_{g'}(p)$. A non-path link contributes at most one
to $S_g(p)$ and a solved path link at most $14\gamma$ (Step 4), so
$S_g(p)\le N+14\gamma\Pi$ with $N$ the number of non-path links of $p$
other than $g$ and $\Pi$ the number of path links of $p$. If $g\in p$
then $N+\Pi\le3$ and $S_g(p)\le3+14\gamma\Pi$, and by Step 2(iv) the sum
over the six plaquettes of $g$ is at most $18+42\gamma$. If
$\Gamma_k\in p$ then $N\le2$ and $\Pi\le2$, with $\Pi=2$ on three of the
six plaquettes of $\Gamma_k$ (Step 2(iii)), so the sum over them is at
most $12+14\gamma(6+3)=12+126\gamma$. Hence
\begin{align*}
\sum_p A_g(p)S_g(p)&\le18+42\gamma+\gamma_g\lvert K(g)\rvert
(12+126\gamma)\\
&\le18+54\gamma+126\gamma^2 .
\end{align*}
The sum of the first part over all $g'\ne g$ bounds its sum over the
other class. The second part of~\eqref{eq:wilsonmixed} enters only
through a solved path link $\Gamma_k\in p$ with $g$ and $g'$ among its
arguments; one of $g,g'$ is a $z$-coordinate, so $k$ has a $z$-link among
its arguments and the hypothesis gives $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$. There are at most
$\lvert K(g)\rvert\le2$ such pairs, six plaquettes for each and twenty
coordinates $g'$, so this part adds at most $\frac12\kappa\cdot240\,C_2$.
The Wilson terms contribute at most $\beta_Wc_W$ to $R_g$.

\emph{Step 7: the Jacobians.} The term $\log\det\mathcal M$ of a solved
pair depends on $g$ only if $k\in K(g)$, and on $g'\ne g$ only if $g'$ is
one of the other twenty arguments. With $\lvert\Tr A\rvert\le3\lVert A
\rVert$ on $\g$ and $\lVert\mathcal M^{-1}\rVert\le\mathsf m$,
\begin{multline*}
\bigl\lvert\partial_g\partial_{g'}\log\det\mathcal M\bigr\rvert=
\bigl\lvert\Tr(\mathcal M^{-1}\partial_g\partial_{g'}\mathcal M)\\
-\Tr(\mathcal M^{-1}\partial_{g'}\mathcal M\,\mathcal M^{-1}\partial_g
\mathcal M)\bigr\rvert\le L=3\mathsf mM_2+3\mathsf m^2M_1^2,
\end{multline*}
and the Jacobians contribute at most $c_\psi=2\cdot20\cdot L$ to $R_g$.
Together,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cwcpsi}
c_W=9+27\gamma+63\gamma^2+120\kappa C_2,\qquad c_\psi=40L .
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 8: the numbers.} Since $\sin x\ge x-x^3/6$, $m(\theta)\le
(1-\theta^2/24)^{-1}$ and $1-1/m(\theta)\le\theta^2/24$; the series of
$e^{1/2}$, whose tail after the term $k=8$ is at most twice its first term,
gives $e^{1/2}\le1.6487213$ and $M_G\le1.046176$; and $e^{14r}\le
(1-14r)^{-1}$ in $C_2$. Every constant of Steps 3 to 7 increases with $r$,
and $c_W$ with $\kappa$, so it suffices to take $r$ and $\kappa$ at their
largest values; each bound below is computed from the rounded bounds before
it, with $\sqrt2\le1.4142136$. At $r=8\cdot10^{-5}$: $\theta_Z\le1.8102\cdot
10^{-3}$, $\theta_X\le1.5840\cdot10^{-3}$, $m_1\le1+1.4\cdot10^{-7}$,
$1-1/m(\theta_X)\le1.046\cdot10^{-7}$, $\varepsilon_T\le1.924\cdot10^{-3}$,
$\mathsf m\le8.110$, $\gamma\le1.01366$, $B_2\le16.825$, $B_3\le227.72$,
$14\gamma^2+4\gamma+1\le19.44$, $X_2\le165.8$, $C_2\le166.9$, $M_1\le17.03$,
$M_2\le2718$ and $L\le1.234\cdot10^5$; so for $r\le8\cdot10^{-5}$ and
$\kappa\le10^{-8}$, $c_W\le101.11$ and $c_\psi\le4.94\cdot10^6$. Under
hypothesis (a) of Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound}, $62r\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, so
$r\le9.68\cdot10^{-15}$, and the same chain gives $m_1\le1+10^{-26}$,
$\varepsilon_T\le2.328\cdot10^{-13}$, $\gamma\le1+1.7\cdot10^{-12}$,
$\mathsf m\le8(1+1.7\cdot10^{-12})$, $B_2\le16.73882$, $B_3\le225.975$,
$14\gamma^2+4\gamma+1\le19+10^{-10}$, $X_2\le159.019$, $C_2\le160.02$,
$M_1\le16.7389$, $M_2\le2597.5$, $L\le1.1614\cdot10^5$, and
$9+27\gamma+63\gamma^2\le99+4\cdot10^{-10}$. For the condition on
$\kappa$, let $k=(y,\mu)$ be solved with a $z$-link among its arguments.
A $z$-link is based in a block of $W'$, so $y$ or $y+e_\mu$ lies in $W'$,
and by Step 2(iii) the links of a plaquette $p$ through $\Gamma_k$ are
based in blocks at distance at most one from $B(y)$, hence at distance at
most two from $W'$; they are $\Gamma_k$, non-path links, a tree link, and
possibly the path link of $k'=(y+e_\mu-e_\nu,\nu)$, both of whose blocks
are at distance at most two from $W'$. These blocks are good, by the
sector event inside $\Lambda$, since they lie at distance at least $s+1$
from both islands, and by (c) outside it, so every non-path link of $p$
is within $r$ of its reconstruction value. The path link of $k'$ is within
$14r$ of $c_{k'}$: if $k'$ is based in $\Lambda$ it is solved, since a
pair based at distance at most $s+1$ from an island has its path link in
$L_a\cup p_a$ or $L_b\cup p_b$ and its plaquettes are not $K$-factors, and
otherwise Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound} applies by (c). Step 1 of the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} gives $\delta(R(c)_p,I)\le\eta$ for these
plaquettes, and replacing the links one at a time with bi-invariance and
$\delta\le d$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}) gives
$\delta(U_p,I)\le\eta+2\cdot14r+2r=\eta+30r\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$. Hence
$120\kappa C_2\le1.2\cdot10^{-8}$, $c_W\le99.0001$ and $c_\psi\le40L\le
4.65\cdot10^6$.
\end{proof}

With Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}, $\Lambda_2^2\le\beta_W^2(c_W+c_\psi/
\beta_W)^2$ and the bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands} becomes
\[
\varDelta\le1920\,\beta_W\Bigl(c_W+\frac{c_\psi}{\beta_W}\Bigr)^2r^2
\sqrt{n_xn_y}\,e^{-2\alpha_G(w-2s-8)},
\]
which grows linearly in $\beta_W$; at
$\beta_W=1.13\cdot10^{37}$, just above $\beta^*$, $s=1$ and $r=43\rho$,
$\rho=2.17\cdot10^{-16}$, where $\beta_Wr^2=9.84\cdot10^8$, and for
islands of one block, $n_x=n_y=45(544+1776)+17\cdot4160=175120$, it reads
$\varDelta\le3.25\cdot10^{21}e^{-2\alpha_G(w-10)}$. This is not small at
the threshold: the bound is at most one exactly when $w\ge99072$, at
fixed $r$ every factor $e$ in $\beta_W/\beta^*$ adds $1/(2\alpha_G)=2000$
to this width, and islands of
$\lvert I_a\rvert$ and $\lvert I_b\rvert$ blocks, for which
$N_d\le\lvert I_a\rvert((2d+1)^4-(2d-1)^4)$, add at most
$1000\log(\lvert I_a\rvert\lvert I_b\rvert)$.

The covariance therefore decays exponentially in the width of the good
layer (Figure~\ref{fig:layer}), at the rate of the chart, with the amplitude of
Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}, which is below one at the threshold only
across good layers about $10^5$ blocks wide. If further bad blocks lie in $\Lambda$ at
distance at least $s+4$ from both islands, the factorisation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation} through $K$ still holds as an identity of
measures, with the constraints of the bad pairs of the layer kept as hard
factors inside $K$, but $\mu_{x,y}$ is then no longer a good-window law,
and the cross-ratio of $K$ is the comparison for the remaining islands:
the corollary is the inductive step for two islands, and
Sec.~\ref{ssec:manyislands} keeps those constraints out of the layer and
performs the induction.

\subsection{Many islands}\label{ssec:manyislands}

The paragraph after Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands} leaves the case in which
the layer between two islands contains further islands. If the constraints
of those islands are kept inside the kernel, the law of the layer carries
hard constraints and branches, and Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} does not
apply to it. This subsection keeps them out of the layer. Every island
receives its own collar, the integral over the island and its collar
becomes a positive measure on the collar coordinates of that island, as
$a_i$ and $b_j$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}, and the layer between
all the islands is a good window. The kernel of two islands is then a
mixture, over the collar coordinates of the others, of good-window
kernels. A mixture of kernels with small cross-ratios can have a large
one, and Proposition~\ref{prop:hiddenbit} is such a mixture over one bit.\footnote{The cross-ratio $Z_{11}Z_{00}/(Z_{10}Z_{01})$ of the four
weights with the two islands in their two patterns measures how much the
pattern of one island changes the odds of the pattern of the other: it is
one exactly when the two islands are independent. A mixture of independent
pairs need not be independent: if a hidden switch raises the chance of both
patterns at once, the two islands are correlated however weakly each one
depends on the switch.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} bounds the additional cross-ratio by the
product of the sensitivities of the two islands to the collars of the
others, with no condition on the other islands, and by a sum over chains
of islands under a Dobrushin condition on them.\footnote{Dobrushin's
condition asks that the conditional law of each island move by less than a
fixed fraction $\theta<1$ in total when the islands around it are changed;
an influence then fades by the factor $\theta$ at each island it passes
through, and the sum over chains converges.} The measures of the other
islands enter only through their positivity.

\emph{The data.} The data are those of Sec.~\ref{ssec:factorisation} with
the following changes. Let $\mathcal I=\{a,b\}\cup\mathcal Q$ be a finite
index set and $I_u\subset\Lambda$, $u\in\mathcal I$, pairwise disjoint sets
of blocks with
\[
w_{uv}=\dist(I_u,I_v)-1\ge2s+7\qquad(u\ne v),
\]
which holds for distinct islands formed with the joining distance $2s+7$ of
the paragraph after Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}, and with $w_{uv}\ge
2s+8$ for the joining distance $2s+8$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}.
Every block of $\Lambda\setminus\bigcup_uI_u$ is good; on $I_a$ two patterns
$\omega_a^0,\omega_a^1$ are prescribed, on $I_b$ two patterns
$\omega_b^0,\omega_b^1$, and on each $I_q$, $q\in\mathcal Q$, one pattern
$\omega_q$. The sector $(i,j)$ is the event that the labels of $\Lambda$ are
these, with $\omega_a^i$ on $I_a$ and $\omega_b^j$ on $I_b$, and its weight
$Z_{ij}$ is defined as in Sec.~\ref{ssec:factorisation}. With
$d_u(y)=\dist(y,I_u)$, form for every $u\in\mathcal I$ the classes $L_u$,
$p_u$, $x_u$ of Sec.~\ref{ssec:factorisation}, with $d_a$ replaced by $d_u$,
let $z$ be every other non-path active link based in $\Lambda$, and solve
the path link of every pair based at $d_u\ge s+2$ for every $u$. A link at
$d_u\le s+3$ has $d_v\ge w_{uv}+1-(s+3)\ge s+5$ for $v\ne u$, so the classes
are disjoint, and every block at $d_u\in\{s+1,s+2,s+3\}$ is good in all
four sectors. Let $D_u$ be the product of the $r$-balls in the coordinates
$\zeta_e$ of $x_u$ and $D_z$ that of $z$, let $n_u=45(N^u_{s+1}+N^u_{s+2})+
17N^u_{s+3}$, with $N^u_d$ the number of blocks of $\Lambda$ at $d_u=d$, be
the number of $x_u$-links, let $\Lambda_2$ be the largest operator norm of
$\partial_{x_u}\nabla_z\mathcal U$ over $u\in\mathcal I$ and over
$D_z\times\prod_uD_u$, and put
\[
\varDelta_{uv}=\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{n_un_v}\,
e^{-2\alpha_G(w_{uv}-2s-8)_+}\qquad(u\ne v),
\]
the quantity $\varDelta$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands} for the pair
$I_u,I_v$ when $w_{uv}\ge2s+8$.

\begin{lemma}[many islands, one kernel]\label{lem:manykernel}
Let $s\ge1$ and $r\le10^{-4}$. There are finite positive measures $a_i$ on
$D_a$, $b_j$ on $D_b$, $i,j\in\{0,1\}$, and $\gamma_q$ on $D_q$,
$q\in\mathcal Q$, and a smooth function $\tilde K:\prod_{u\in\mathcal I}D_u
\to(0,\infty)$ with
\[
Z_{ij}=\int\tilde K(x)\,a_i(dx_a)\,b_j(dx_b)\prod_{q\in\mathcal Q}
\gamma_q(dx_q)\qquad(i,j\in\{0,1\}),
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\tilde K$ and every $\gamma_q$ are the same in all four sectors;
$a_i$ depends on $\omega_a^i$, $c$, $\beta_W$, $U^{\mathrm{ext}}$ only, and
likewise $b_j$;
\item $\tilde K(x)=\int_{D_z}e^{-\mathcal U(z;x)}dz$ with $\mathcal U=
\beta_WS_K+\psi$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}(iv), smooth on a
neighbourhood of $D_z\times\prod_uD_u$; no term of $\mathcal U$ depends on
coordinates of $x_u$ and of $x_v$ for $u\ne v$, and $\nabla_z\partial_{x_u}
\mathcal U$ is supported on the $z$-links based at $d_u\le s+4$;
\item for $u\ne v$ the supports of $\nabla_z\partial_{x_u}\mathcal U$ and
$\nabla_z\partial_{x_v}\mathcal U$ are at fine distance at least
$d'_{uv}=2(w_{uv}-2s-8)_+$ between link midpoints.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation} treats each island through
its own distance function, and runs with one class per island. Steps~1
and~2 are unchanged, a pair being solved when it is based at distance at
least $s+2$ from every island; its non-path links are then based at
distance at least $s+1$ from every island, in good blocks. In Step~3 call a
factor a $u$-factor if it depends on a coordinate of $L_u\cup p_u$, and
assign the factors depending on $x_u$ alone to $u$. A $u$-factor depends
only on $L_u$, $p_u$, $x_u$ and $U^{\mathrm{ext}}$, through links at
$d_u\le s+2$, which have $d_v\ge w_{uv}+1-(s+2)\ge s+6$ for every $v\ne u$;
so no factor is a $u$-factor and a $v$-factor, and the product $\Phi_K$ of
the remaining factors, the $K$-factors, does not depend on the sector,
which changes only the indicators of $I_a$ and $I_b$. The indicators of the
bad blocks of $I_q$ involve links at $d_q\le1\le s$ and are $q$-factors.
Step~4 with one bracket for each island gives the identity, with
$\gamma_q(dx_q)$ the integral of the product of the $q$-factors over $L_q$
and $p_q$ times $\prod_{e\in x_q}j\,d\zeta_e$ on $D_q$, and $a_i$, $b_j$,
$\tilde K$ as there; this is (i). Step~5 gives the first clause of (ii).
Step~6 is a statement about one island at a time, so it gives the support
of $\nabla_z\partial_{x_u}\mathcal U$, and a $K$-term depending on $x_u$
and on $x_v$ would contain a link at $d_u\le s+3$ and a link at $d_v\le
s+3$ in blocks at distance at most one, so that $w_{uv}+1\le2s+7$, which
is excluded. The two supports are at coarse distance at least
$w_{uv}+1-2(s+4)=w_{uv}-2s-7$, and links based in blocks at coarse
distance $D\ge1$ have midpoints at fine distance at least $2D-2$; this is
(iii) for $w_{uv}\ge2s+8$, and (iii) is trivial for $w_{uv}=2s+7$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[the layer between many islands]\label{lem:manylayer}
In addition, assume hypotheses (a)--(c) of Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound},
with $W'$ the set of blocks of $\Lambda$ at distance at least $s+3$ from
every island. Then for every $x\in\prod_uD_u$ the law $\mu_x=e^{-\mathcal U
(z;x)}dz/\tilde K(x)$ on $D_z$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:layerbound} with
$\mathcal A=480/\beta_W$ and $\alpha=\alpha_G$, and for $u\ne v$ and vectors
$h_u$, $h_v$ in the coordinates of $x_u$ and $x_v$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\partial_{h_u}\partial_{h_v}\log\tilde K(x)\bigr\rvert\le
\frac{480}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2\lVert h_u\rVert\lVert h_v\rVert
e^{-2\alpha_G(w_{uv}-2s-8)_+}.
\]
In particular the logarithm of the cross-ratio of $\tilde K$ in
$(x_u,x_v)$, between two points of $D_u$ and two points of $D_v$ with the
other arguments fixed, has modulus at most $\varDelta_{uv}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The law $\mu_x$ is the law of Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw} for the
window $W'$ in the coordinates of the labels, with the inside links of the
blocks at distance $s+3$ from some island frozen and the exterior given by
$x$ and $U^{\mathrm{ext}}$, by the identification in the paragraph on the
layer law after Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation}, which uses only that the
$z$-links are the free non-path links of $W'$ and that the solved pairs are
those of Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}. The proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} uses the islands only in Step~1, through the
goodness of the blocks at distance at most two from $W'$; these are at
distance at least $s+1$ from every island, hence good in all sectors inside
$\Lambda$ and good by (c) outside it. Steps~2 to~6 concern the window $W'$
and are uniform in its exterior, and freezing the inside links at distance
$s+3$ from any island restricts the Hessian to a principal submatrix. So
\eqref{eq:layerbound} holds with the stated constants. For the derivative,
Lemma~\ref{lem:connected} on the fixed domain $D_z$ gives
$\partial_{h_u}\partial_{h_v}\log\tilde K=-\E_{\mu_x}[\partial_{h_u}
\partial_{h_v}\mathcal U]+\Cov_{\mu_x}(\partial_{h_u}\mathcal U,
\partial_{h_v}\mathcal U)$, and the first term vanishes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}(ii). As in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:layercross}, apply~\eqref{eq:layerbound} with
$\varphi(e)=-\dist(e,\operatorname{supp}\nabla_z\partial_{h_u}\mathcal U)$,
which vanishes on that support and is at most $-d'_{uv}$ on the support of
$\nabla_z\partial_{h_v}\mathcal U$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}(iii), with
$\lVert\nabla_z\partial_{h_u}\mathcal U\rVert\le\Lambda_2\lVert h_u\rVert$
and $\lVert\nabla_z\partial_{h_v}\mathcal U\rVert\le\Lambda_2\lVert h_v
\rVert$ pointwise. For the cross-ratio, $D_u$ and $D_v$ are convex, the
logarithm of the cross-ratio is the integral of the mixed derivative over
the unit square, and two points of $D_u$ differ by at most $2r\sqrt{n_u}$.
\end{proof}

The other islands now enter only through the measures $\gamma_q$, and the
kernel of $a$ and $b$ is $K(x_a,x_b)=\int\tilde K(x)\prod_q\gamma_q(dx_q)$,
an integral against the probability law on $\prod_qD_q$ proportional to
$\tilde K(x_a,x_b,\cdot\,)\prod_q\gamma_q$. The next lemma bounds the
covariances of that law in terms of the cross-ratios of its density alone.

\begin{lemma}[covariances over the islands]\label{lem:islandcov}
Let $\mathcal Q$ be finite, $X_q$ compact metric spaces, $\gamma_q$ nonzero
finite Borel measures on $X_q$, $X=\prod_qX_q$, $k:X\to(0,\infty)$
continuous, and $P=k\prod_q\gamma_q/\int k\prod_q\gamma_q$. For $\xi\in X$
and $\eta_q\in X_q$ let $\xi^{\eta_q}$ be $\xi$ with its $q$-coordinate
replaced by $\eta_q$. For $q\ne q'$ let $\kappa_{qq'}$ bound
$\lvert\log k(\xi^{\eta_q\eta_{q'}})+\log k(\xi)-\log k(\xi^{\eta_q})-\log
k(\xi^{\eta_{q'}})\rvert$ for all $\xi,\eta_q,\eta_{q'}$, let $C_{qq'}=
\tanh(\kappa_{qq'}/4)$ and $C_{qq}=0$, and for continuous $f$ on $X$ let
$\delta_q(f)=\sup\{\lvert f(\xi^{\eta_q})-f(\xi)\rvert\}$. Then for
continuous $f,g$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\lvert\Cov_P(f,g)\rvert\le\frac14\sum_q\delta_q(f)\sum_q\delta_q(g)$;
\item if $\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}\le\theta<1$ for every $q$, then $D=\sum_{n\ge0}
C^n$ converges and
\[
\lvert\Cov_P(f,g)\rvert\le\frac14\sum_{q,q'}\delta_q(f)\,D_{qq'}\,
\delta_{q'}(g);
\]
\item if $\ell$ is a pseudometric on $\mathcal Q$, $\lambda\ge0$ and
$\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}e^{\lambda\ell(q,q')}\le\theta<1$ for every $q$, then
$0\le D_{qq'}\le e^{-\lambda\ell(q,q')}/(1-\theta)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Conditional laws.} The law
\[
P_q(d\eta\mid\xi)=\frac{k(\xi^\eta)\,\gamma_q(d\eta)}{\int k(\xi^{\eta'})
\,\gamma_q(d\eta')}
\]
on $X_q$ depends on $\xi$ through $\xi_{-q}$ only, its density with respect
to $\gamma_q$ is continuous in $(\eta,\xi)$, and $P$ is invariant under
resampling the $q$-coordinate from it.

\emph{Tilts.} Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and $\mu'=h\mu/\mu(h)$
with $h$ measurable and $0<\inf h\le\sup h\le e^\kappa\inf h$. For a Borel
set $E$ with $0<\mu(E)<1$ the odds of $E$ under $\mu'$ and under $\mu$ have
the ratio $\frac{\mu(h\mathbf 1_E)/\mu(E)}{\mu(h\mathbf 1_{E^c})/\mu(E^c)}
\in[e^{-\kappa},e^\kappa]$, so the logistic bound in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:twolabels} gives $\lvert\mu'(E)-\mu(E)\rvert\le\tanh
(\kappa/4)$, and $\mu'(E)=\mu(E)$ when $\mu(E)\in\{0,1\}$. Hence
$\lVert\mu'-\mu\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\tanh(\kappa/4)$. If $\xi$ and $\xi'$
differ only in the coordinate $q'\ne q$, the density of $P_q(\cdot\mid\xi')$
with respect to $P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)$ is proportional to
$k(\xi'^{\eta})/k(\xi^\eta)$, whose logarithm oscillates in $\eta$ by at
most $\kappa_{qq'}$, so $\lVert P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)-P_q(\cdot\mid\xi')\rVert_
{\mathrm{TV}}\le C_{qq'}$.

\emph{Comparison.} Let $g$ be continuous, $t\in\R$, and $P^t=e^{tg}P/
P(e^{tg})$, again of the form of the lemma; its conditional law at $q$ is
the tilt of $P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)$ by $e^{tg(\xi^\eta)}$, so $b_q=\sup_\xi
\lVert P^t_q(\cdot\mid\xi)-P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\tanh
(\lvert t\rvert\delta_q(g)/4)$. The couplings of $P$ and $P^t$ form a
weakly compact set (Lemma~\ref{lem:minimiser}), and $\Psi(\pi)=\sum_q
\varrho_q(\pi)$, $\varrho_q(\pi)=\pi\{\xi_q\ne\xi'_q\}$, is weakly lower
semicontinuous, since $\{\xi_q\ne\xi'_q\}$ is open; let $\pi$ minimise it.
For $q\in\mathcal Q$ replace $(\xi_q,\xi'_q)$ by a sample of the maximal
coupling of $P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)$ and $P^t_q(\cdot\mid\xi')$, which, with
$p,p'$ the two densities with respect to $\gamma_q$ and $m=\int\min\{p,p'\}
d\gamma_q$, draws $\eta=\eta'$ from $\min\{p,p'\}\gamma_q/m$ with probability
$m$ and otherwise, when $m<1$, $\eta$ and $\eta'$ independently from $(p-\min\{p,p'\})
\gamma_q/(1-m)$ and $(p'-\min\{p,p'\})\gamma_q/(1-m)$; it is measurable in
$(\xi,\xi')$ by the continuity of the densities, and it gives
$\{\eta\ne\eta'\}$ probability at most $1-m=\lVert P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)-P^t_q
(\cdot\mid\xi')\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}$. Both marginals are invariant, so the
result $\pi^{(q)}$ is again a coupling; it changes only $\varrho_q$, and
changing the coordinates of $\xi_{-q}$ to those of $\xi'_{-q}$ one at a
time,
\[
\varrho_q(\pi^{(q)})\le\E_\pi\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}\mathbf 1_{\xi_{q'}\ne
\xi'_{q'}}+b_q=\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}\varrho_{q'}(\pi)+b_q .
\]
By minimality $\varrho_q(\pi)\le\varrho_q(\pi^{(q)})$, which is the argument
of Lemma~\ref{lem:minimality} for the discrete metric, so $\varrho\le
C\varrho+b$ componentwise. Under the hypothesis of (ii), $C^n\mathbf 1\le\theta^n
\mathbf 1$ and $\varrho\le\mathbf 1$, so iterating gives $\varrho\le
\sum_{k<n}C^kb+\theta^n\mathbf 1$ and, as $n\to\infty$, $\varrho\le Db$.
Changing the coordinates one at a time,
\[
\begin{split}
\lvert P^t(f)-P(f)\rvert&=\bigl\lvert\E_\pi[f(\xi')-f(\xi)]\bigr\rvert\\
&\le\sum_q\delta_q(f)\varrho_q(\pi)\le\sum_{q,q'}\delta_q(f)D_{qq'}b_{q'} .
\end{split}
\]
\emph{Covariances.} The functions $f$ and $g$ are bounded, so the
derivative of $P^t(f)$ at $t=0$ is $\Cov_P(f,g)$, and $b_{q'}\le\lvert t
\rvert\delta_{q'}(g)/4$; dividing by $\lvert t\rvert$ and letting $t\to0$
gives (ii). For (i),
$\lvert\Cov_P(f,g)\rvert\le(\Var_Pf\,\Var_Pg)^{1/2}$, a variance is at most
a quarter of the squared oscillation, and changing the coordinates one at
a time bounds the oscillation of $f$ by $\sum_q\delta_q(f)$; the bound on
the variance is Popoviciu's inequality~\cite{Pop35}. Part (ii) is
F\"ollmer's covariance estimate~\cite{Fol82} under Dobrushin's
condition~\cite{Dob68,Dob70}, with the coefficients $C_{qq'}$ read off
from the cross-ratios of $k$. For (iii), by
induction $(C^n)_{qq'}\le\theta^ne^{-\lambda\ell(q,q')}$: the case $n=0$ is
$\ell(q,q)=0$, and $(C^{n+1})_{qq'}=\sum_kC_{qk}(C^n)_{kq'}\le\theta^ne^{-
\lambda\ell(q,q')}\sum_kC_{qk}e^{\lambda\ell(q,k)}$ by the triangle
inequality; summing over $n$ gives the bound, and the hypothesis of (iii)
contains that of (ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[many islands]\label{thm:manyislands}
Let $s\ge1$, let the data be those above, assume hypotheses (a)--(c) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} with $W'$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:manylayer}, and
suppose $Z_{ij}>0$ for $i,j\in\{0,1\}$. Put $S_u=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
\varDelta_{uq}$ for $u\in\{a,b\}$, let $C$ be the $\mathcal Q\times\mathcal Q$
matrix with $C_{qq}=0$ and $C_{qq'}=\tanh(\varDelta_{qq'}/4)$, and let
\[
\varDelta_*=\varDelta_{ab}+\frac14\,S_aS_b ;
\]
when $\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}<1$ for every $q$, let instead, with $D=\sum_{n\ge0}C^n$,
\[
\varDelta_*=\varDelta_{ab}+\frac14\min\Bigl\{S_aS_b,\ \sum_{q,q'\in
\mathcal Q}\varDelta_{aq}D_{qq'}\varDelta_{q'b}\Bigr\}.
\]
Then
\[
\bigl\lvert\log Z_{11}+\log Z_{00}-\log Z_{10}-\log Z_{01}\bigr\rvert\le
\varDelta_* ,
\]
the two island labels, the pattern of $I_a$ among $\omega_a^0,\omega_a^1$
and that of $I_b$ among $\omega_b^0,\omega_b^1$, have conditional covariance at most
$\frac14\tanh(\varDelta_*/4)$ given the labels of all other blocks of
$\Lambda$, the coarse field and $U^{\mathrm{ext}}$, and for every bounded
measurable $F\ge0$ of the links of $L_a\cup p_a\cup x_a$,
\[
e^{-\varDelta_*}\le\frac{\E_{i1}[F]}{\E_{i0}[F]}\le e^{\varDelta_*}
\qquad(i=0,1)
\]
whenever the four expectations are positive. For $\mathcal Q=\emptyset$,
$\varDelta_*=\varDelta_{ab}$, which for $w_{ab}\ge2s+8$ is the bound of
Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}, $Z_{ij}=\iint K\,da_i\,db_j$ with $K(x_a,x_b)
=\int\tilde K(x)\prod_q\gamma_q(dx_q)$; $Z_{ij}>0$ forces every
$\gamma_q\ne0$, and $K$ is smooth and positive on $D_a\times D_b$. Fix
$x_a^0,x_a^1\in D_a$, $x_b^0,x_b^1\in D_b$, and let $x_a(\vartheta)=x_a^0+
\vartheta(x_a^1-x_a^0)$, $x_b(\varphi)$ likewise, which stay in the convex
sets $D_a$, $D_b$. The logarithm of the cross-ratio of $K$ at these points
is $\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\partial_\vartheta\partial_\varphi\log K\,d\vartheta\,
d\varphi$. With $P$ the law on $\prod_qD_q$ proportional to $\tilde K(x_a
(\vartheta),x_b(\varphi),\cdot\,)\prod_q\gamma_q$, differentiation under
the integral sign gives
\[
\partial_\vartheta\partial_\varphi\log K=\E_P\bigl[\partial_\vartheta
\partial_\varphi\log\tilde K\bigr]+\Cov_P\bigl(\partial_\vartheta\log
\tilde K,\partial_\varphi\log\tilde K\bigr).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:manylayer} with $h_a=x_a^1-x_a^0$, $h_b=x_b^1-x_b^0$, the
first term has modulus at most $\varDelta_{ab}$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov} with $X_q=D_q$, $k=\tilde K(x_a(\vartheta),
x_b(\varphi),\cdot\,)$, $f=\partial_\vartheta\log\tilde K$ and $g=
\partial_\varphi\log\tilde K$. Changing $x_q$ along the segment between two
points of $D_q$ and integrating the mixed derivative of
Lemma~\ref{lem:manylayer} for the pair $(a,q)$ gives $\delta_q(f)\le
\varDelta_{aq}$, likewise $\delta_q(g)\le\varDelta_{bq}$, and the last
statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:manylayer} for the pair $(q,q')$ shows that
$\kappa_{qq'}=\varDelta_{qq'}$ is admissible, so the matrix of
Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov} is $C$. Parts (i) and (ii) of that lemma bound the covariance by
$\varDelta_*-\varDelta_{ab}$, uniformly in $(\vartheta,\varphi)$. So the
cross-ratio of $K$ is at most $e^{\varDelta_*}$ and at least
$e^{-\varDelta_*}$ on $D_a\times D_b$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} gives the
first bound. The joint law of the two labels given the others is
$Z_{ij}/\sum Z$, so Corollary~\ref{cor:twolabels} gives the second. For the
third, $F\Phi_a^i$ is a product of $a$-factors, so the identity holds with
$Fa_i$ in place of $a_i$ and the same $K$ and $b_j$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} applied to $Fa_i$, $a_i$ and $b_1$, $b_0$ gives it,
since $Z(Fa_i,b_j)/Z(a_i,b_j)=\E_{ij}[F]$.
\end{proof}

The first form of $\varDelta_*$ needs nothing of the other islands: their
hard constraints, branches and masses are integrated in the $\gamma_q$ and
never compared. Its mediated term $\frac14S_aS_b$ does not decay with
$w_{ab}$ when other islands lie near both $I_a$ and $I_b$, since it treats
every collar coordinate as able to reach every other. The second form
keeps the interaction between the islands, through the matrix $C$, and
under a weighted form of the Dobrushin condition
$\sum_{q'}\tanh(\varDelta_{qq'}/4)<1$ it decays along chains of islands.

\begin{corollary}[decay along chains of islands]\label{cor:islandchains}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}, let $\ell$ be the
pseudometric on $\mathcal I$ given by the least value of $\sum_i(w_{u_iu_{i+1}}
-2s-8)_+$ over the chains $u=u_0,u_1,\dots,u_k=v$ in $\mathcal I$, let
$0\le\vartheta\le1$, and suppose
\[
\theta=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q}\sum_{q'\in\mathcal Q\setminus\{q\}}\tanh
\frac{\varDelta_{qq'}}4\,e^{2\vartheta\alpha_G\ell(q,q')}<1 .
\]
Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
\varDelta_*\le\varDelta_{ab}+\frac{e^{-2\vartheta\alpha_G\ell(a,b)}}
{4(1-\theta)}\,T_aT_b ,\qquad T_u=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\varDelta_{uq}
e^{2\vartheta\alpha_G\ell(u,q)},\\
T_u\le\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{n_u}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
\sqrt{n_q}\,e^{-2(1-\vartheta)\alpha_G(w_{uq}-2s-8)_+}.
\end{gathered}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
$\ell$ is a pseudometric since it is a least sum over chains, and
$\ell(u,v)\le(w_{uv}-2s-8)_+$. Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov}(iii) on $\mathcal Q$
with $\lambda=2\vartheta\alpha_G$ gives $D_{qq'}\le e^{-\lambda\ell(q,q')}
/(1-\theta)$ and the hypothesis of the second form of $\varDelta_*$, and
$-\ell(q,q')\le-\ell(a,b)+\ell(a,q)+\ell(q',b)$ gives the first bound. The
second is $\ell(u,q)\le(w_{uq}-2s-8)_+$ in each term.
\end{proof}

A chain crosses each island at no cost in $\ell$: an island is a set on
which nothing is known, and the corollary charges only the good layers
between consecutive islands of the chain. With $\vartheta=0$ the
hypothesis is the Dobrushin condition $\sum_{q'}C_{qq'}\le\theta<1$.

The sums $S_u$ and $T_u$ are sums over the islands near $I_u$, and the
rarity of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} controls them in the mean. For
a bad block $y$ let $\lvert I(y)\rvert$ be the number of blocks of its
island, and $\lvert I(y)\rvert=0$ for a good block.

\begin{proposition}[the island sums in the mean]\label{prop:islandmass}
Form the islands with the joining distance $2s+8$, so that $w_{uv}\ge2s+8$
for distinct islands, let $N_s=(4s+17)^4-1$ be the number of neighbours of
a block, $\varGamma\ge1$, and $\beta_W\ge\beta^*(\rho,s,\varGamma)$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}(iii) with $N_s$ neighbours. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item for every block $y$, $\E_{\mu_L}\lvert I(y)\rvert\le2\varGamma(2
\varGamma-1)^{-2}N_s^{-2}$;
\item for every set $J$ of blocks of the torus and every $\kappa>0$,
\[
\E_{\mu_L}\sum_{y\notin J}\lvert I(y)\rvert e^{-\kappa\dist(J,y)}\le
\frac{2\varGamma}{(2\varGamma-1)^2N_s^2}\,\lvert J\rvert\,\sigma(\kappa),
\]
where, with $x=e^{-\kappa}$,
\[
\sigma(\kappa)=\sum_{y\in\Z^4}e^{-\kappa\lVert y\rVert_\infty}=1+\frac{64x
(1+4x+x^2)}{(1-x)^4}+\frac{16x}{(1-x)^2};
\]
\item in the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}, when every $I_q$,
$q\in\mathcal Q$, is an island, with $B'=\bigcup_qI_q$,
$0\le\vartheta\le1$ and $\kappa=2(1-\vartheta)\alpha_G$,
\[
\begin{split}
T_u\le{}&\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{45\,n_u}\,(2s+7)^2
e^{\kappa(2s+9)}\\
&\times\sum_{y\in B'}\lvert I(y)\rvert e^{-\kappa\dist(I_u,y)} .
\end{split}
\]
\end{enumerate}
At $\kappa=2\alpha_G=5\cdot10^{-4}$, $\sigma(\kappa)\le6.151\cdot10^{15}$,
and at $\varGamma=1$ the bound of (ii) is at most $3.253\cdot10^5\lvert J\rvert$
for $s=1$ and $3.503\cdot10^3\lvert J\rvert$ for $s=5$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) The island paragraph of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}
gives $\mu_L\{\lvert I(y)\rvert=n\}\le N_s^{2(n-1)}A^{n/H}$, and its proof
of (iii) gives $\varGamma N_s^2A^{1/H}\le\frac12$ at $\beta_W\ge\beta^*(\rho,
s,\varGamma)$, so $\mu_L\{\lvert I(y)\rvert=n\}\le N_s^{-2}(2\varGamma)^{-n}$
and $\E\lvert I(y)\rvert\le N_s^{-2}\sum_nn(2\varGamma)^{-n}=2\varGamma(2
\varGamma-1)^{-2}N_s^{-2}$. (ii) By linearity it suffices that
$\sum_ye^{-\kappa\dist(J,y)}\le\lvert J\rvert\sigma(\kappa)$; since
$e^{-\kappa\dist(J,y)}\le\sum_{z\in J}e^{-\kappa\dist(z,y)}$, it suffices
that $\sum_ye^{-\kappa\dist(z,y)}\le\sigma(\kappa)$ on the torus, which
holds because each block of the torus has a preimage in $\Z^4$ at
$\ell^\infty$ distance $\dist(z,y)$ from a preimage of $z$, distinct blocks
having distinct preimages. The closed form counts the $(2k+1)^4-(2k-1)^4=
64k^3+16k$ points of $\Z^4$ at distance $k\ge1$ and sums $\sum kx^k$ and
$\sum k^3x^k$. (iii) In the second bound of
Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains}, $n_q\le45(2s+7)^4\lvert I_q\rvert$, since
every $x_q$-link is based in a block at distance at most $s+3$ from $I_q$,
so $\sqrt{n_q}\le\sqrt{45}(2s+7)^2\lvert I_q\rvert$; and $(w_{uq}-2s-8)_+
\ge\dist(I_u,I_q)-2s-9$, while $\lvert I_q\rvert e^{-\kappa\dist(I_u,I_q)}$
is the term of $\sum_{y\in I_q}\lvert I(y)\rvert e^{-\kappa\dist(I_u,y)}$ at
a block of $I_q$ nearest to $I_u$. For the numbers, $x\le1$ and $1-x\ge
\kappa-\kappa^2/2$ give $\sigma(\kappa)\le1+384(\kappa-\kappa^2/2)^{-4}+16
(\kappa-\kappa^2/2)^{-2}\le6.151\cdot10^{15}$ at $\kappa=5\cdot10^{-4}$, and
$N_1=21^4-1=194480$, $N_5=37^4-1=1874160$, so that $2\cdot6.151\cdot10^{15}/
N_1^2\le3.253\cdot10^5$ and $2\cdot6.151\cdot10^{15}/N_5^2\le3.503\cdot10^3$.
\end{proof}

The proposition is annealed: it bounds the mean of the island sums under
$\mu_L$ for a fixed set $J$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} is a
statement given all the labels, and it says nothing about the law of the
islands near $I_u$ given that $I_u$ is an island. At $\varGamma=1$ its
bound exceeds one, because the weighted volume $\sigma(2\alpha_G)=6.1\cdot
10^{15}$ of the decay length $1/(2\alpha_G)=2000$ blocks of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} exceeds $N_s^2$; for $\varGamma\ge2$ the bound of (ii) is at most $\lvert J\rvert
\sigma(\kappa)/(\varGamma N_s^2)$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}(iii)
reaches every $\varGamma$ at the coupling $\beta^*(\rho,s,\varGamma)$.

With Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} the comparison of item (ii) of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains} holds with any number of islands, given the labels
of all of them: the cross-ratio of two islands is at most $\varDelta_*$,
explicit in the two-island quantities $\varDelta_{uv}$ of
Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}, and the observables of one island change
by a factor in $[e^{-\varDelta_*},e^{\varDelta_*}]$ under a flip of the
other. The prefactor $\Lambda_2$ is bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo},
whose proof uses only the plaquettes at one collar and applies to each
island $I_u$ when $r\le8\cdot10^{-5}$. Two things remain. The Dobrushin condition of the second form
and the smallness of $S_u$ or $T_u$ are conditions on the configuration of
the islands, which Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass} controls only in the
mean. And the covariance of the two labels with the other labels averaged
out differs from the conditional covariance by the covariance of the
conditional probabilities of the two labels given the others, which is the
term of Proposition~\ref{prop:hiddenbit} and is not bounded here.

The first of them, the smallness of the island sums together with the
Dobrushin condition, holds in every window of bounded size
outside an event whose probability is at most the size of the window times
the product of two rarities: that of one bad block and that of a second bad
block or island. Two facts give this. The bound of
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(i) charges an island of $n$ blocks the
factor $A^{n/H}$, while Lemma~\ref{lem:coverage} gives $A^{\lceil n/H
\rceil}$, which is $A$ for $n\le H$; with the ceiling, the mean mass of the
island of a block is at most $G_0$ below, about $H$ times the rarity of
one bad block, instead of $2N_s^{-2}$. And two bad
blocks at distance at least six have disjoint witness boxes, so that two
islands near each other cost the product of two rarities. For two islands
$I_u\ne I_v$ of the torus, formed with the joining distance $2s+8$, put
\begin{gather*}
\bar n_u=45\,\bigl\lvert\{y:\dist(y,I_u)\le s+3\}\bigr\rvert,\\
\bar\Lambda_2=99.0001\,\beta_W+4.65\cdot10^6,\\
\bar\varDelta_{uv}=\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\bar\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{\bar n_u
\bar n_v}\,e^{-2\alpha_G(w_{uv}-2s-8)},
\end{gather*}
and, for $0\le\vartheta<1$, $\bar T_u=\sum_v\bar\varDelta_{uv}e^{2\vartheta
\alpha_G(w_{uv}-2s-8)}$, the sum over all islands $I_v\ne I_u$ of the
torus. These are functions of the labels alone. In the setting of
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}, when the sets $I_u$ are islands,
$n_u\le\bar n_u$, Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}, applied to each island as
above, gives $\Lambda_2\le\bar\Lambda_2$, and $\ell(u,v)\le w_{uv}-2s-8$;
hence $\varDelta_{uv}\le\bar\varDelta_{uv}$, and $S_u\le\bar T_u$ and
$T_u\le\bar T_u$ for the $T_u$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} with
the same $\vartheta$. Write $W^{+t}$ for the set of blocks at distance at
most $t$ from a set $W$ of blocks.

\begin{theorem}[the island sums in a window]\label{thm:islandwindow}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $s\ge1$, $2758\rho\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, $r=43\rho$,
$\eta=92\rho$, form the islands of the torus with the joining distance
$2s+8$, and let $N_s=(4s+17)^4-1$. Let $\beta^*$ be the largest solution
of the equation of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} with $N_s$ in place of
$\varDelta$, $\log q^*=-H(\log2+2\log N_s)-\log(eMH)$ its right side, $C_0$ that of
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ},
$\beta_W\ge\beta^*$, and
\[
G_0=H\Bigl(Mq^*+\frac{A^*2^{-H}}{1-2^{-H}}\Bigr),\qquad A^*=eMHq^*.
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every block $y$, $\E_{\mu_L}\lvert I(y)\rvert\le G_0$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(ii) holds at $\varGamma=1$ with
$2\varGamma(2\varGamma-1)^{-2}N_s^{-2}$ replaced by $G_0$.
\item Let $0\le\vartheta<1$, $\kappa=2(1-\vartheta)\alpha_G$, let $R\ge
2s+13$ be an integer, $\sigma>0$, $W$ a set of blocks,
\begin{gather*}
c_2=\frac{1920}{\beta^*}\bar\Lambda_2(\beta^*)^2r^2\cdot45(2s+12)^2
(2s+7)^2e^{\kappa(2s+14)},\\
\tau=\min\bigl\{\sigma(\kappa),\,e^{-\kappa R/2}\sigma(\kappa/2)\bigr\},
\end{gather*}
with $\bar\Lambda_2(\beta^*)$ the value of $\bar\Lambda_2$ at $\beta_W=
\beta^*$ and $\sigma(\cdot)$ as in Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}.
Outside an event of $\mu_L$-probability at most
\[
\epsilon=\lvert W\rvert\,Mq^*\Bigl(11^4(2R+1)^4Mq^*+\frac{c_2G_0\tau}
\sigma\Bigr),
\]
every island $I_u$ meeting $W$ has $\ell^\infty$ diameter at most $5$,
hence at most $6^4$ blocks, lies at distance more than $R$ from every other
island, and satisfies $\bar T_u\le\sigma$.
\item Outside the same event, in the setting of
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} with $I_a$, $I_b$ and every $I_q$ islands
meeting $W$: $S_a,S_b\le\sigma$ and $\varDelta_*\le\varDelta_{ab}+\frac14
\sigma^2\le\sigma+\frac14\sigma^2$; if $\sigma<4$, the weighted Dobrushin
condition of Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} holds with $\theta\le\sigma/4$,
and
\[
\varDelta_*\le\varDelta_{ab}+\frac{e^{-2\vartheta\alpha_G\ell(a,b)}\sigma^2}
{4-\sigma}\le\sigma+\frac{\sigma^2}{4-\sigma}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
At $\rho=2.17\cdot10^{-16}$ and $s=1$: $\beta^*\in[1.1220,1.1221]\cdot10^{37}$,
$\lvert\log q^*\rvert=32481.67$, $Mq^*\le10^{-14102.4}$, the bound $A$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}(i) is at most $10^{-14098.8}$,
$G_0\le10^{-14099.3}$, and the bound of (i) for
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(ii) at $\kappa=2\alpha_G$ is
$G_0\sigma(2\alpha_G)\lvert J\rvert\le10^{-14083.5}\lvert J\rvert$, in place of
$3.253\cdot10^5\lvert J\rvert$. For $\vartheta=0$, $c_2\le10^{22.13}$; with
$R=15$, $\epsilon\le\lvert W\rvert(10^{-28194}+10^{-28163.8}/\sigma)$, and
with $R=2\cdot10^8$, $\epsilon\le10^{-28166}\lvert W\rvert$ for every
$\sigma\in[10^{-1000},4)$; for $\vartheta=\frac12$ and $R=4\cdot10^8$,
$\epsilon\le10^{-28165}\lvert W\rvert$ on the same range. At $s=5$:
$\beta^*\in[1.3216,1.3217]\cdot10^{37}$, $Mq^*\le10^{-16652.7}$, $G_0\le
10^{-16649.6}$, and with $\vartheta=0$, $R=2\cdot10^8$,
$\epsilon\le10^{-33267}\lvert W\rvert$ for $\sigma\in[10^{-1000},4)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $p=q_\rho(\beta_W)$ and $B$ for the set of bad blocks, and let $Q_y$
be the set of unit cubes with corner at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most five
from $2y$. By the witness paragraph of the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}, which applies since $\rho\le10^{-8}$, a
bad block $y$ has a cube of $Q_y$ on which the event of
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} holds; $\lvert Q_y\rvert\le M$, and a cube lies
in at most $H$ of the sets $Q_y$. For a set $S$ of blocks put
$Q_S=\bigcup_{y\in S}Q_y$.

\emph{Step 1: separated sets.} Let $S_1,\dots,S_m$ be nonempty sets of
blocks with $\dist(S_i,S_j)\ge6$ for $i\ne j$, and $k_i=\lceil\lvert S_i
\rvert/H\rceil$. Then
\[
\mu_L\Bigl(\,\bigcup_iS_i\subset B\Bigr)\le\prod_i\binom{M\lvert S_i\rvert}
{k_i}p^{k_i}\le\prod_iA^{k_i},
\]
and the factor of a set of one block is $Mp$. Two blocks at distance at
least six have a coordinate in which the corners $2y$ differ by at least
twelve modulo the side of the torus, while a cube of $Q_y\cap Q_{y'}$ would
put $2y$ and $2y'$ within ten of each other in every coordinate; so the sets
$Q_{S_i}$ are pairwise disjoint. On the event, $Q_{S_i}$ contains at least $k_i$ distinct bad
cubes, since one cube witnesses at most $H$ blocks; choosing $k_i$ of them
in each $Q_{S_i}$ gives $\sum_ik_i$ distinct bad cubes, and the union bound
over the choices with Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} gives the first
inequality. The second is that of Lemma~\ref{lem:coverage}.

\emph{Step 2: the mass of an island.} Let $u=N_s^{2H}A$, which is at
most $2^{-H}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}(i), and let $T$ be a
set of blocks at distance at least $6$ from a block $y$, or empty. Let
$n\ge1$ and $k=\lfloor(n-1)/H\rfloor$. If $\lvert I(y)\rvert\ge n$, a
spanning tree of $I(y)$ in the graph of the joining distance, cut at
$kH+1$ vertices from $y$, gives a connected set $C\ni y$ of exactly $kH+1$
bad blocks; there are at most $N_s^{2kH}$ such sets, since a walk around a
spanning tree of $C$ from $y$ has $2kH$ steps. By Step~1, $\mu_L(T\subset B,
\,C\subset B)\le\mu_L(T\subset B)'A^{k+1}$ when $T$ is at distance at least
$6$ from $C$, with $\mu_L(T\subset B)'$ the factor of Step~1 for $T$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:islandmassG}
\mu_L\bigl(T\subset B,\,\lvert I(y)\rvert\ge n\bigr)\le\mu_L(T\subset B)'
\min\{Mp,\,Au^k\}.
\end{equation}
Summing over $n$ in groups of $H$, with $Mp$ for $n\le H$ and $Au^k$ for
$kH<n\le(k+1)H$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{T\subset B}\lvert I(y)\rvert\bigr]
&\le\mu_L(T\subset B)'\,H\Bigl(Mp+\frac{Au}{1-u}\Bigr)\\
&\le\mu_L(T\subset B)'\,G_0,
\end{aligned}
\]
since $p\le q^*$ and $A\le A^*$ by Step~6. With $T$ empty, $\E\lvert I(y)
\rvert\le G_0$. The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(ii) uses
only this mean, which gives (i).

\emph{Step 3: no near pair.} Let $\mathcal G$ be the event that no two
bad blocks $y\in W^{+5}$ and $y'$ satisfy $6\le\dist(y,y')\le R$. On
$\mathcal G$ let $I_u$ be an island meeting $W$ at $y_0$. Every block of
$I_u$ is within distance $5$ of $y_0$: otherwise a path $y_0=z_0,z_1,\dots$
in $I_u$ with steps at most $2s+8$ has a first block $z_k$ at distance more
than $5$ from $y_0$, and $6\le\dist(y_0,z_k)\le5+2s+8\le R$. So
$I_u\subset W^{+5}$, two blocks of $I_u$ are at distance at most $10<R$,
hence at most $5$, and $I_u$ lies in a box of side $6$. If another island
$I_q$ had $\dist(I_u,I_q)\le R$, a pair realising this distance would
consist of a bad block of $W^{+5}$ and a bad block at distance between
$2s+9\ge6$ and $R$. This proves the first two assertions of (ii) on
$\mathcal G$.

\emph{Step 4: the island sums on $\mathcal G$.} For $y\in B$ put
\[
F(y)=\sum_{y'}\lvert I(y')\rvert e^{-\kappa\dist(y,y')},
\]
the sum over $y'\in B\setminus I(y)$ with $\dist(y,y')>R$, and let
$c_2(\beta_W)$ be $c_2$ with $\beta_W$ in place of $\beta^*$. On
$\mathcal G$, let $I_u$ meet $W$ at $y$. For an island $I_q\ne I_u$ let
$y_q\in I_q$ realise $\dist(I_u,I_q)$; then $\dist(y,y_q)\le\dist(I_u,I_q)
+5$, $\dist(y,y_q)>R$ by Step 3, and $w_{uq}-2s-8=\dist(I_u,I_q)-2s-9\ge
\dist(y,y_q)-2s-14$. The box of side $2s+12$ around $I_u$ contains every
block at distance at most $s+3$ from it, so $\bar n_u\le45(2s+12)^4$, and
$\bar n_q\le45(2s+7)^4\lvert I_q\rvert$ as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(iii). With $\sqrt{\lvert I_q\rvert}\le
\lvert I_q\rvert$ and distinct islands giving distinct $y_q$,
\[
\bar T_u=\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\bar\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{\bar n_u}\sum_q
\sqrt{\bar n_q}\,e^{-\kappa(w_{uq}-2s-8)}\le c_2(\beta_W)F(y).
\]
\emph{Step 5: probabilities.} By Step 1 with two single blocks, at most
$11^4\lvert W\rvert$ blocks of $W^{+5}$ and at most $(2R+1)^4$ blocks
within distance $R$ of each,
\[
\mu_L(\mathcal G^c)\le11^4(2R+1)^4\lvert W\rvert(Mp)^2 .
\]
For $y\in W$, $\E[\mathbf 1_{y\in B}F(y)]$ is a sum over $y'$ with
$\dist(y,y')>R$ of $e^{-\kappa\dist(y,y')}$ times a sum over the connected
sets $C'\ni y'$ with $y\notin C'$ of $\lvert C'\rvert\mu_L\{y\in B,\,I(y')=C'\}$.
On that event $y$ and $I(y')$ lie in different islands, so $y$ is at
distance at least $2s+9\ge6$ from every subset of $I(y')$, and Step~2
with $T=\{y\}$, whose factor in Step~1 is $Mp$, bounds the sum over $C'$
by $Mp\,G_0$. The sum over $y'$ is at most $\sum_z
e^{-\kappa\lVert z\rVert_\infty}$ over $z\in\Z^4$ with $\lVert z
\rVert_\infty>R$, by the preimages of the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}(ii), which is at most $\sigma(\kappa)$
and, by $e^{-\kappa\lVert z\rVert_\infty}\le e^{-\kappa R/2}e^{-\kappa
\lVert z\rVert_\infty/2}$ there, at most $e^{-\kappa R/2}\sigma(\kappa/2)$.
So $\E[\mathbf 1_{y\in B}F(y)]\le Mp\,G_0\tau$, and by Step 4, Markov's
inequality and a union bound over $W$,
\begin{multline*}
\mu_L\bigl(\mathcal G\cap\{\bar T_u>\sigma\text{ for some }I_u\text{
meeting }W\}\bigr)\\
\le\frac{c_2(\beta_W)}\sigma\,\lvert W\rvert\,Mp\,G_0\tau .
\end{multline*}
\emph{Step 6: the coupling.} By Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}, $p\le e^{f(
\beta_W)}$ with $f$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}, which decreases
on $[96/\rho^2,\infty)$, so $p\le e^{f(\beta^*)}=q^*$. Since
$\bar\Lambda_2\ge99.0001\,\beta_W$, the logarithmic derivative of
$c_2(\beta)e^{f(\beta)}$ is at most $2/\beta-1/\beta+6/\beta-\rho^2/16$,
which is negative for $\beta\ge\beta^*$ because $\beta^*\rho^2/16=
\lvert\log q^*\rvert+6(\log\beta^*+C_0)>7$. Hence $c_2(\beta_W)p\le
c_2q^*$, and Step 5 gives the bound $\epsilon$ on the complement of the
event of (ii).

\emph{Step 7: the consequences.} Outside that event, $\varDelta_{ab}\le
\bar\varDelta_{ab}\le\bar T_a\le\sigma$, since $\bar\varDelta_{ab}$ is a term
of $\bar T_a$ with a factor at least one, and $S_a,S_b\le\sigma$, which
gives the first form of $\varDelta_*$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}. By
$\tanh t\le t$ and $\ell(q,q')\le w_{qq'}-2s-8$, the sum of
Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} at $q$ is at most $\frac14\bar T_q\le
\frac14\sigma$, so $\theta\le\sigma/4<1$, and the corollary with $T_a,T_b
\le\sigma$ gives the last display.

\emph{The numbers.} Here $H=6^4$, $M=11^4$ and $\lvert\log q^*\rvert=H(\log2
+2\log N_s)+1+4\log11+4\log6$, with $N_1=21^4-1=2^4\cdot5\cdot11\cdot13\cdot
17$ and $\log N_5=4\log37+\log(1-37^{-4})$, where $-x/(1-x)\le\log(1-x)\le
-x$. The logarithms of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold},
together with $\log\frac{13}{12}=2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{25}$,
$\log\frac{17}{16}=2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{33}$ and $\log\frac{37}{36}=
2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{73}$, give $\lvert\log q^*\rvert$ within
$10^{-2}$ of $32481.67$ for $s=1$ and of $38354.07$ for $s=5$. The function
$g(\beta)=\beta\rho^2/16-6(\log\beta+C_0)-\lvert\log q^*\rvert$ increases
for $\beta>96/\rho^2$, and at the ends of the two stated intervals it is
negative and positive, with margins above $0.5$. With $\log10=\log2+\log5$,
$\log_{10}(Mq^*)=(4\log11-\lvert\log q^*\rvert)/\log10$ lies within
$10^{-3}$ of $-14102.446$ for $s=1$ and of $-16652.797$ for $s=5$, and
$\log_{10}(eH)\le3.547$ gives $A\le A^*\le10^{-14098.8}$ at $s=1$. Since
$2eH2^{-H}\le10^{-300}$, $G_0\le HMq^*(1+10^{-300})$, and $\log_{10}H\le
3.1127$ gives the two bounds on $G_0$; with $\sigma(2\alpha_G)\le6.151\cdot
10^{15}$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}, $G_0\sigma(2\alpha_G)\le
10^{-14083.5}$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}, $\frac{1920}{\beta^*}\bar\Lambda_2(\beta^*)^2
r^2=1920\beta^*r^2(99.0001+4.65\cdot10^6/\beta^*)^2$, which increases with
$\beta^*$ and is therefore at most its value at the upper end of the
interval for $\beta^*$: at most $10^{16.2645}$ for $s=1$ and $10^{16.3356}$
for $s=5$. The remaining factors of $c_2$ at $\kappa=2\alpha_G=5\cdot
10^{-4}$ give $c_2\le10^{22.122}$ for $s=1$ and $c_2\le10^{23.140}$ for
$s=5$, and $c_2$ is smaller at $\kappa=\alpha_G$. For the sums $\sigma$,
write $x=1-v$; then $x(1+4x+x^2)=6-12v+7v^2-v^3$, the function
$(6-12v+7v^2)v^{-4}$ decreases for $v>0$, and $v\ge u=\kappa-\kappa^2/2$,
so the closed form of Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass} gives $\sigma(\kappa)
\le1+64(6-12u+7u^2)u^{-4}+16u^{-2}$, hence $\sigma(\alpha_G)\le9.831\cdot
10^{16}$ and $\sigma(\alpha_G/2)\le1.573\cdot10^{18}$.

In $\epsilon$, the first term has $\log_{10}(11^4(2R+1)^4(Mq^*)^2)$ at most
$-28194.76$ for $R=15$, $-28166.31$ for $R=2\cdot10^8$ and $-28165.11$ for
$R=4\cdot10^8$ at $s=1$, and $-33267.01$ for $R=2\cdot10^8$ at $s=5$. For
$R=15$, $\tau\le\sigma(2\alpha_G)$ and $Mq^*c_2G_0\tau\le10^{-28163.86}$.
For $R=2\cdot10^8$ with $\kappa=2\alpha_G$, and for $R=4\cdot10^8$ with
$\kappa=\alpha_G$, $\kappa R/2=5\cdot10^4$ and $e^{-5\cdot10^4}\le
10^{-21714}$, so $\tau\le10^{-21714}\sigma(\kappa/2)$ and the second term
is at most $10^{-48000}\lvert W\rvert$ for $\sigma\ge10^{-1000}$, which the
margins of the first term absorb.
\end{proof}

The bound is a union bound over the window and is linear in $\lvert W
\rvert$; for $\lvert W\rvert\le10^{28000}$ it is at most $10^{-166}$. Its
content lies in the windows where Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} does not
exclude islands: the probability that $W$ contains a bad block at all is at
most $\lvert W\rvert A\le10^{-14098.8}\lvert W\rvert$, so for $10^{14099}\le
\lvert W\rvert\le10^{28000}$ that theorem does not exclude bad blocks in
$W$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} shows that, outside probability $10^{-166}$,
every island they form is a cluster of diameter at most $5$, at distance
more than $2\cdot10^8$ from every other island, and meets the conditions
of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} and Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} with
$\sigma=10^{-1000}$. No coupling beyond the threshold $\beta^*$ of the joining distance $2s+8$
and no factor $\varGamma>1$ is needed: the
weighted volume $\sigma(2\alpha_G)=6.1\cdot10^{15}$ of the decay length is
beaten by $G_0\le10^{-14099.3}$. The bound is void for windows of more
than $10^{28166}$ blocks, and it is a statement about the labels
under $\mu_L$, not about the law of the labels near $I_u$ given that $I_u$
is an island; the covariance of two labels with the others averaged is
bounded in the mean over the coarse field in Sec.~\ref{ssec:labelcov}, and for
a fixed coarse field outside a set of small probability by
Proposition~\ref{prop:fixedgood}, but not uniformly in the coarse field.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_manyislands.png}
\caption{(a) Islands of bad blocks (red: the two islands $I_a$, $I_b$
compared; blue: other islands $I_q$) in a window whose remaining blocks are
good. The solid arc is the two-island bound $\varDelta_{ab}$ of
Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}; the dashed arcs are the bounds
$\varDelta_{uq}$ through which the other islands enter
$\varDelta_*$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}. (b) The bound
$\varDelta$ for two islands against the width $w$ of the good layer
between them, with $\Lambda_2$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo} at
$\beta_W=1.13\cdot10^{37}$; it falls below one at $w=99072$.}
\label{fig:manyislands}
\end{figure*}

\subsection{The covariance of the labels}\label{ssec:labelcov}

Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} compares two islands given the labels of all
the others, and Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} controls the island sums in
a window by a union bound. This subsection bounds the covariances with the
labels averaged, on the whole torus and with no condition on the size of a
window, in the mean over the coarse field. Three constructions do it. The
islands are grouped: the islands near an observable form one group, the
rest a second, and the mixed derivative of the kernel of
Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel} between the two groups is bounded by one
application of~\eqref{eq:layerbound}, with no Dobrushin condition on the
islands. Two independent copies of the labels are compared by an explicit
involution, which exchanges the labels of the group of one observable
between the copies; the weights of a configuration and of its image differ
by the cross-ratio of the two groups. And a group that reaches far from its
observable contains a chain of bad blocks in one copy or the other, whose
probability is paid by the separated rarity of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow}. For two functions of the labels near sets
$N_A$ and $N_B$ the covariance is at most $2\epsilon\lvert N_A\rvert\lvert
N_B\rvert$ times their oscillations, with $\epsilon$ the rarity of a bad
block defined below, since each sees a bad block; the
theorem multiplies this by a factor that decays at the rate $2\alpha_G$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} down to a floor of order $10^{-7011}$. For two
local observables of the field the covariance under $\mu^c$, in the mean
over $c$, decays at the same rate down to a floor of order $10^{-14062}$,
and as $e^{-\sqrt d/2}$ when the joining distance of the groups grows with
the distance.

\emph{Setting.} Throughout, the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} hold: $G=\SU(2)$, $s\ge1$, $2758\rho\le
