6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, $r=43\rho$, $\eta=92\rho$, $\beta_W\ge\beta^*$, on the
torus in the tree gauge, with $\Lambda$ the set of all blocks and no
exterior; hypotheses (a)--(c) of Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} then hold,
(c) being void. For a coarse field $c$ let $\mu^c$ be $\mu_L$ conditioned on
$V^\sharp=c$, through the coarea formula as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw}, let $P^c$ be the law of the labels under
$\mu^c$, and let $\E_c$ be the mean over the law of $V^\sharp$ under
$\mu_L$, so that $\E_c\mu^c=\mu_L$. A labelling $\omega$ assigns a label to
every block, $B(\omega)$ is its set of bad blocks, $\omega_X$ its
restriction to a set $X$ of blocks, and $Z^c(\omega)$ the weight of the
event that the labels are $\omega$, defined as $Z_{ij}$ in
Sec.~\ref{ssec:factorisation}, so that $P^c(\omega)=Z^c(\omega)/\sum
_{\omega'}Z^c(\omega')$. With $f$, $M$, $q^*$ of
Theorems~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} and~\ref{thm:islandwindow} put
\[
\epsilon=Me^{f(\beta_W)}\le Mq^*,\qquad g_R=\sqrt2\,(2R+1)^4\epsilon^{1/4},
\]
so that, by Steps~1 and~6 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow},
$\mu_L(T\subset B)\le\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert}$ for every set $T$ of blocks
pairwise at distance at least $6$. With $\bar\Lambda_2$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} put
\[
b_*=\frac{1920}{\beta_W}\bar\Lambda_2^2r^2,\qquad\nu_s=45(2s+9)^4 .
\]
For a set $Y$ of blocks, its \emph{components} are the classes of the
joining distance $2s+8$ and its \emph{$R$-clusters} those of the joining
distance $R\ge2s+8$; an $R$-cluster is a union of components. For disjoint
sets $X,X'$ of blocks put
\[
\varDelta(X,X')=b_*\nu_s\lvert X\rvert^{1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{y\in X'}
e^{-4\alpha_G(\dist(y,X)-2s-9)_+}\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
and for integers $R,t$ and $d>0$
\begin{gather*}
M_{d,t}=b_*\nu_se^{-2\alpha_G(d-t-2s-9)_+},\\
\varPhi_R=b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)\epsilon^{1/2}e^{-\alpha_G(R-4s-17)},
\end{gather*}
with $\sigma(\kappa)=\sum_{y\in\Z^4}e^{-\kappa\lVert y\rVert_\infty}$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass}; by the proof of its part (ii),
$\sum_ye^{-\kappa\dist(W,y)}\le\lvert W\rvert\sigma(\kappa)$ for every set
$W$ of blocks.

\begin{lemma}[two groups of islands]\label{lem:groupcross}
Let $Y$ be a set of blocks, $X$ a union of components of $Y$ and
$X'=Y\setminus X$. Let $D_X$ be the product of the sets $D_u$ of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:manyislands} over the components $I_u\subset X$, and $D_{X'}$
likewise. There are a smooth function $\tilde K:D_X\times D_{X'}\to(0,
\infty)$ and, for every labelling $\pi$ of $X$ and $\pi'$ of $X'$, finite
positive measures $a_\pi$ on $D_X$ and $b_{\pi'}$ on $D_{X'}$, such that
for all labellings $\omega$ with $B(\omega)\subset Y$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $Z^c(\omega)=\iint\tilde K(x,x')\,a_{\omega_X}(dx)\,b_{\omega_{X'}}
(dx')$;
\item for all $x_0,x_1\in D_X$ and $x'_0,x'_1\in D_{X'}$,
\[
\Bigl|\log\frac{\tilde K(x_1,x'_1)\tilde K(x_0,x'_0)}{\tilde K(x_1,x'_0)
\tilde K(x_0,x'_1)}\Bigr|\le\varDelta:=\min\{\varDelta(X,X'),\varDelta(X',
X)\};
\]
\item for $Z^c(\omega)>0$ and bounded measurable $F$ of the active links
based in $X$ and $H$ of those based in $X'$, there are measurable $f$ on
$D_X$, depending on $F$ and $\omega_X$ only, and $h$ on $D_{X'}$, depending
on $H$ and $\omega_{X'}$ only, with $\lvert f\rvert\le\lVert F\rVert$,
$\lvert h\rvert\le\lVert H\rVert$, $\E_{\mu^c}[FH\mid\omega]=\int fh\,
d\varPi_\omega$ and $\E_{\mu^c}[F\mid\omega]=\int f\,d\varPi_\omega$, where
$\varPi_\omega$ is the probability law proportional to $\tilde K\,a_{\omega
_X}\otimes b_{\omega_{X'}}$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for $\omega,\tilde\omega,\omega'$ of positive weight with
bad blocks in $Y$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item if $\tilde\omega$ agrees with $\omega$ on $X$, the conditional
expectations of $F$ given $\tilde\omega$ and given $\omega$ differ by at
most $2\lVert F\rVert\tanh(\varDelta/4)$;
\item $\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H\mid\omega)\rvert\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H
\rVert\tanh(\varDelta/4)$;
\item the labellings $\omega^\natural=(\omega'_X,\omega_{X'})$ and
$\omega'^\natural=(\omega_X,\omega'_{X'})$ have positive weight and
\[
e^{-\varDelta}\le\frac{Z^c(\omega^\natural)Z^c(\omega'^\natural)}
{Z^c(\omega)Z^c(\omega')}\le e^{\varDelta}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{The kernel.} Distinct components of $Y$ are at distance at least
$2s+9$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel} applies to the components $I_u$ of
$Y$, every block outside $Y$ being good in every labelling considered. Its
proof runs with any labelling of each $I_u$: the labels change only the
$u$-factors, so the product of the $K$-factors, and with it $\tilde K(x)=
\int_{D_z}e^{-\mathcal U(z;x)}dz$, does not depend on the labels of $Y$,
while the measure $\gamma_u$ obtained by integrating the $u$-factors over
$L_u$ and $p_u$ depends on the labels of $I_u$, on $c$ and on $\beta_W$
only. Put $a_\pi=\bigotimes_{I_u\subset X}\gamma_u$ and $b_{\pi'}=\bigotimes
_{I_u\subset X'}\gamma_u$ with the labels $\pi$, $\pi'$; this is (i). In the
same construction, given $x$ and $\omega$, the families $L_u\cup p_u$ are
independent over $u$, each with law proportional to the product of its
$u$-factors, and independent of $z$. The active links based in $X$ are at
$d_u=0$ for some $I_u\subset X$, hence in $L_u$; so $f(x)=\E[F\mid x,
\omega]$ is the integral of $F$ against the product of these laws over
$I_u\subset X$, a function of $x$ and $\omega_X$, and likewise $h$; this is
(iii).

\emph{The mixed derivative.} Let $h_X$, $h_{X'}$ be vectors in the
coordinates of $x\in D_X$ and $x'\in D_{X'}$ with $\lVert h_e\rVert\le2r$
for each link. No term of $\mathcal U$ depends on coordinates of two
components, by Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}(ii), so Lemma~\ref{lem:connected}
gives
\[
\partial_{h_X}\partial_{h_{X'}}\log\tilde K=\Cov_{\mu_{x,x'}}\bigl(
\partial_{h_X}\mathcal U,\partial_{h_{X'}}\mathcal U\bigr).
\]
Let $v=\nabla_z\partial_{h_X}\mathcal U$ and $v'=\nabla_z\partial_{h_{X'}}
\mathcal U$, supported on sets $S$ and $S'$ of $z$-links based at distance
at most $s+4$ from $X$, respectively $X'$. The supports of distinct
components lie in blocks at coarse distance at least $1$, so the
coordinates entering $v_e$ belong to one component, and Step~1 of the proof
of Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}, which applies to each component, bounds
$\sum_f\lVert\partial_e\partial_f\mathcal U\rVert$ over them by
$\beta_Wc_W+c_\psi\le\bar\Lambda_2$. Hence $\lVert v_e\rVert\le2r\bar
\Lambda_2$, and $\lVert v'_e\rVert\le2r\bar\Lambda_2$. Apply
\eqref{eq:layerbound}, with $\mathcal A=480/\beta_W$ and $\alpha=\alpha_G$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:manylayer}, to $\varphi(e)=-\dist(e,S)$, the fine distance
between link midpoints. A block carries $45$ non-path active links, so
$\lvert S\rvert\le\nu_s\lvert X\rvert$. A link $e\in S'$ is based in a
block $y$ with $\dist(y,y')\le s+4$ for some $y'\in X'$, and a link of $S$
in a block $y''$ with $\dist(y'',X)\le s+4$; then $\dist(y,y'')\ge\dist(y',
X)-2s-8$, and links based in blocks at coarse distance $D\ge1$ have
midpoints at fine distance at least $2D-2$, so $\dist(e,S)\ge2(\dist(y',X)
-2s-9)_+$. Summing over $y'$, the $(2s+9)^4$ blocks $y$ and their $45$
links,
\[
\begin{split}
\bigl\lvert\partial_{h_X}\partial_{h_{X'}}\log\tilde K\bigr\rvert&\le
\frac{480}{\beta_W}(2r\bar\Lambda_2)^2\bigl(\nu_s\lvert X\rvert\bigr)
^{1/2}\\
&\quad\times\Bigl(\nu_s\sum_{y'\in X'}e^{-4\alpha_G(\dist(y',X)-2s-9)_+}
\Bigr)^{1/2},
\end{split}
\]
which is $\varDelta(X,X')$; with $\varphi=-\dist(\cdot,S')$ the same
argument gives $\varDelta(X',X)$. The sets $D_X$, $D_{X'}$ are convex,
two of their points differ by at most $2r$ in each link, and the logarithm
of the cross-ratio is the integral of the mixed derivative over the unit
square; this is (ii).

\emph{The consequences.} Let $\mu'=k\mu/\mu(k)$ with $\sup k\le e^\kappa
\inf k$; the tilt paragraph of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov} gives
$\lVert\mu'-\mu\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\tanh(\kappa/4)$. (a) Under
$\varPi_\omega$ the law of $x$ has density proportional to $k_\omega(x)=
\int\tilde K(x,x')b_{\omega_{X'}}(dx')$ with respect to $a_{\omega_X}$, and
$a_{\tilde\omega_X}=a_{\omega_X}$, $f$ is the same for both. Integrating
(ii) against $b_{\tilde\omega_{X'}}\otimes b_{\omega_{X'}}$ shows that
$k_{\tilde\omega}/k_\omega$ has logarithmic oscillation at most
$\varDelta$, so the two laws differ by at most $\tanh(\varDelta/4)$ in total
variation, and $\operatorname{osc}f\le2\lVert F\rVert$. (b) Given $x$, the
law of $x'$ under $\varPi_\omega$ is proportional to $\tilde K(x,\cdot)
b_{\omega_{X'}}$, and by (ii) these laws differ by at most $\tanh(\varDelta
/4)$ for two values of $x$; so $m(x)=\E_{\varPi_\omega}[h\mid x]$ has
$\operatorname{osc}m\le2\lVert H\rVert\tanh(\varDelta/4)$. By (iii),
$\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H\mid\omega)=\Cov_{\varPi_\omega}(f,h)=\Cov_{\varPi_\omega}
(f,m)$, and a variance is at most a quarter of the squared oscillation
(Popoviciu~\cite{Pop35}), so $\lvert\Cov(f,m)\rvert\le\frac14
\operatorname{osc}f\operatorname{osc}m$. (c) The measures of $\omega$ and
$\omega'$ are nonzero since their weights are positive, and $\tilde K>0$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} with $a_{\omega_X},a_{\omega'_X}$ and
$b_{\omega_{X'}},b_{\omega'_{X'}}$ gives the bound.
\end{proof}

The second construction is a union bound over chains in two copies. Let
$Q^c=P^c\otimes P^c$ be the law of two independent labellings $\omega,
\omega'$ given $c$, and $\mathsf D=B(\omega)\cup B(\omega')$.

\begin{lemma}[chains in two copies]\label{lem:labelchains}
Let $N$ and $N'$ be sets of blocks, $R\ge6$ and $t\ge R$ integers with
$\dist(N,N')>t$ and $g_R\le\frac12$, and $\mathcal C$ the union of the
$R$-clusters of $\mathsf D\cup N\cup N'$ that meet $N$. Then
\[
\E_c\,Q^c\{\mathcal C\not\subset N^{+t}\}\le2\lvert N^{+R}\rvert
g_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor},
\]
and the same holds with $B(\omega)$ in place of $\mathsf D$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{A chain.} Let $\mathcal C\not\subset N^{+t}$. There is a path $y_0,
\dots,y_n$ in $\mathsf D\cup N\cup N'$ with steps at most $R$, $y_0\in N$ and
$\dist(y_n,N)>t$; let $i$ be its first index with $\dist(y_i,N)>t$. The
blocks $y_0,\dots,y_{i-1}$ are at distance at most $t$ from $N$, hence not
in $N'$, and if $j<i$ is the last index with $y_j\in N$, then $j<i-1$, since
$\dist(y_i,N)>t\ge R$. So $y_{j+1},\dots,y_{i-1}$ is a sequence of blocks of
$\mathsf D$ with steps at most $R$, beginning in $N^{+R}$ and ending at
distance more than $t-R$ from $N$. Choose such a sequence $z_1,\dots,z_m$ in
$\mathsf D$ with $m$ least. Then $\dist(z_k,z_l)>R$ for $\lvert k-l\rvert
\ge2$, since otherwise a shorter sequence exists, and $(m-1)R>t-2R$, so
$m\ge\lfloor t/R\rfloor$.

\emph{Two copies.} Let $T$ be the set of the $\lceil m/2\rceil$ blocks
$z_k$ with $k$ odd, pairwise at distance more than $R\ge6$. The event $T
\subset\mathsf D$ is the union over $T_1\subset T$ of $\{T_1\subset B(\omega),
\,T\setminus T_1\subset B(\omega')\}$, and for each $T_1$, since $P^c\le1$
and by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
with $T_2=T\setminus T_1$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\bigl[P^c(T_1\subset B)\,P^c(T_2\subset B)\bigr]\\
\le\bigl(\mu_L(T_1\subset B)\,\mu_L(T_2\subset B)\bigr)^{1/2}\le
\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}.
\end{multline*}
So $\E_cQ^c\{T\subset\mathsf D\}\le(2\epsilon^{1/2})^{\lceil m/2\rceil}
\le(\sqrt2\,\epsilon^{1/4})^m$, as $2\epsilon^{1/2}\le1$. There are at most
$\lvert N^{+R}\rvert(2R+1)^{4(m-1)}$ sequences of $m$ blocks with steps at
most $R$ beginning in $N^{+R}$, so
\begin{multline*}
\E_cQ^c\{\mathcal C\not\subset N^{+t}\}\le\lvert N^{+R}\rvert\sum_{m\ge
\lfloor t/R\rfloor}g_R^m\\
\le2\lvert N^{+R}\rvert g_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor}.
\end{multline*}
With $B(\omega)$ in place of $\mathsf D$ the event is smaller.
\end{proof}

The third ingredient is the mean of $\varDelta$ for a group confined near
its observable. Let $N$, $N'$, $R\ge2s+9$, $t\ge R$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains}, let $Y=\mathsf B\cup N\cup N'$ with $\mathsf B$
equal to $\mathsf D$ or to $B(\omega)$, let $\mathcal C$ be the union of
the $R$-clusters of $Y$ meeting $N$, and let $k$ be $2$ or $1$
accordingly. On the event $\mathcal C\subset N^{+t}$, every $y\in Y
\setminus\mathcal C$ lies in an $R$-cluster distinct from those of
$\mathcal C$, so $\dist(y,\mathcal C)>R\ge2s+9$, and $\dist(y,\mathcal C)
\ge\dist(y,N^{+t})$; a block of $N'$ has $\dist(y,\mathcal C)\ge\dist(N,N')
-t$. For a block $y\in\mathsf B\setminus\mathcal C$ the exponent
splits as
\begin{multline*}
4\alpha_G(\dist(y,\mathcal C)-2s-9)\\
\ge2\alpha_G(R-2s-8)+2\alpha_G(\dist(y,N^{+t})-2s-9),
\end{multline*}
and with $\sqrt{\sum_yu_y}\le\sum_y\sqrt{u_y}$,
\begin{multline*}
\Bigl(\sum_{y\in Y\setminus\mathcal C}e^{-4\alpha_G(\dist(y,\mathcal C)
-2s-9)_+}\Bigr)^{1/2}\\
\le\lvert N'\rvert^{1/2}e^{-2\alpha_G(\dist(N,N')-t-2s-9)_+}\\
+e^{-\alpha_G(R-2s-8)}\sum_{y\in\mathsf B}e^{-\alpha_G(\dist(y,N^{+t})-2s
-9)} .
\end{multline*}
The mean of the last sum over $\E_cQ^c$, or $\E_cP^c$, is at most $k
\epsilon e^{\alpha_G(2s+9)}\lvert N^{+t}\rvert\sigma(\alpha_G)$, since
$\E_cQ^c\{y\in\mathsf D\}\le2\mu_L(y\in B)\le2\epsilon$ and $\E_cP^c\{y\in
B\}\le\epsilon$. With $\lvert\mathcal C\rvert\le\lvert N^{+t}\rvert$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:groupmean}
\begin{split}
&\E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C\subset N^{+t}}\varDelta(\mathcal C,Y
\setminus\mathcal C)\bigr]\\
&\quad\le\lvert N^{+t}\rvert^{1/2}\lvert N'\rvert^{1/2}M_{d',t}+k
\epsilon^{1/2}\lvert N^{+t}\rvert^{3/2}\varPhi_R,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
with $\E$ the mean over $\E_cQ^c$ or $\E_cP^c$ and $d'=\dist(N,N')$.

\begin{theorem}[the label covariance]\label{thm:labelcov}
Let $N_A$, $N_B$ be sets of blocks at distance $d\ge6$, $\phi$ a function of
the labels of $N_A$ and $\psi$ one of the labels of $N_B$. Then
\[
\E_c\bigl\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\bigr\rvert\le2\epsilon\lvert N_A
\rvert\lvert N_B\rvert\operatorname{osc}\phi\operatorname{osc}\psi .
\]
If moreover $R\ge2s+9$ and $t\ge2R$ are integers with $d\ge t+6$ and
$g_R\le\frac12$, then, with $V=\lvert N_B^{+t}\rvert$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\bigl\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\bigr\rvert\le\operatorname{osc}\phi
\operatorname{osc}\psi\,\lvert N_A\rvert\lvert N_B\rvert\,\epsilon\\
\times\bigl(11^4V^{1/2}M_{d-5,t}+2V^{3/2}\varPhi_R+4(2R+1)^4Vg_R^{\lfloor
t/R\rfloor-2}\bigr).
\end{multline*}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $c$. Let $\omega_0$ be the labelling with every block good, and put
$\hat\phi(\omega)=\phi(\omega)-\phi(\omega_0)$ and $\hat\psi(\omega)=
\psi(\omega)-\psi(\omega_0)$. Then $\lvert\hat\phi\rvert\le
\operatorname{osc}\phi$, $\hat\phi(\omega)=0$ unless $B(\omega)\cap N_A\ne
\emptyset$, and likewise for $\hat\psi$ and $N_B$. Under $Q^c$,
$\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)=\Cov_{P^c}(\hat\phi,\hat\psi)=\E_{Q^c}G$ with
$G(\omega,\omega')=\hat\phi(\omega)(\hat\psi(\omega)-\hat\psi(\omega'))$,
and
\[
\lvert G\rvert\le\operatorname{osc}\phi\operatorname{osc}\psi\sum_{z_A\in
N_A,\,z_B\in N_B}J_{z_Az_B},
\]
where $J_{z_Az_B}=\mathbf 1[z_A,z_B\in B(\omega)]+\mathbf 1[z_A\in
B(\omega),\,z_B\in B(\omega')]$. As $\dist(z_A,z_B)\ge6$, the mean of
$J_{z_Az_B}$ over $\E_cQ^c$ is at most $\mu_L(z_A,z_B\in B)+\E_c[P^c(z_A
\in B)P^c(z_B\in B)]\le\epsilon^2+\epsilon\le2\epsilon$, by the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and $P^c\le1$ in the second term; this is the
first bound. For the second let $Y=\mathsf D\cup N_B$, $\mathcal C$ the
union of its $R$-clusters meeting $N_B$, $\mathcal G=\{\mathcal C\subset
N_B^{+t}\}$ and $\varDelta_B=\varDelta(\mathcal C,Y\setminus\mathcal C)$.

\emph{The exchange.} Define $\chi(\omega,\omega')=(\tilde\omega,\tilde
\omega')$ by $\tilde\omega=\omega'$ and $\tilde\omega'=\omega$ on
$\mathcal C$, and $\tilde\omega=\omega$, $\tilde\omega'=\omega'$ elsewhere.
On every block the pair of labels is kept or exchanged, so $\mathsf D$, $Y$,
$\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal G$ are the same for $(\omega,\omega')$ and its
image, and $\chi$ is an involution. By Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(c) with
$X=\mathcal C$, a union of components of $Y$, a pair of positive weight is
mapped to one of positive weight, with
\[
e^{-\varDelta_B}\le\frac{Q^c(\chi(\omega,\omega'))}{Q^c(\omega,
\omega')}\le e^{\varDelta_B}.
\]
On $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal C\cap N_A=\emptyset$, since $d>t$; so $\tilde
\omega=\omega$ on $N_A$ and $\tilde\omega=\omega'$, $\tilde\omega'=\omega$
on $N_B\subset\mathcal C$, and $G\circ\chi=-G$. Split $\E_{Q^c}[G
\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}]$ into the orbits of $\chi$. A fixed point has $G=0$.
An orbit $\{x,\chi x\}$ of two points contributes $(Q^c(x)-Q^c
(\chi x))G(x)$, and $\lvert1-\varrho\rvert\le(1+\varrho)\tanh(\varDelta
_B/2)$ for $\varrho\in[e^{-\varDelta_B},e^{\varDelta_B}]$. As $\varDelta_B$
and $\lvert G\rvert$ are constant on the orbit, with $\tanh u\le u$,
\[
\lvert\E_{Q^c}G\rvert\le\operatorname{osc}\phi\operatorname{osc}\psi
\sum_{z_A,z_B}\E_{Q^c}\bigl[J_{z_Az_B}\bigl(\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}
\varDelta_B+\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G^c}\bigr)\bigr].
\]
Fix $z_A\in N_A$ and $z_B\in N_B$; the two means are bounded in turn, after
the mean $\E_c$.

\emph{The far islands.} On $\mathcal G$, $\lvert\mathcal C\rvert\le V$ and
$Y\setminus\mathcal C\subset\mathsf D$, each of its blocks at distance more
than $R$ from $\mathcal C$, hence from $z_B$. By $\sqrt{\sum_yu_y}\le
\sum_y\sqrt{u_y}$,
\[
\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\varDelta_B\le b_*\nu_sV^{1/2}\sum_{y\in\mathsf D
\setminus\mathcal C}e^{-2\alpha_G(\dist(y,\mathcal C)-2s-9)_+}.
\]
The $11^4$ blocks $y$ at distance at most $5$ from $z_A$ have $\dist(y,
\mathcal C)\ge\dist(z_A,N_B^{+t})-5\ge d-t-5$, so their terms add up to at
most $11^4V^{1/2}M_{d-5,t}$, whose product with $J_{z_Az_B}$ has mean at
most $2\epsilon\cdot11^4V^{1/2}M_{d-5,t}$. For every other block $y$ with
$\dist(y,z_B)>R$ the blocks $z_A$, $z_B$, $y$ are pairwise at distance at
least $6$, and $J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1[y\in\mathsf D]$ is at most a sum of
four indicators of events $\{T_1\subset B(\omega),\,T_2\subset
B(\omega')\}$ with $T_1\cup T_2=\{z_A,z_B,y\}$; as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains} each has mean at most $\epsilon^{3/2}$. As in
the derivation of~\eqref{eq:groupmean}, $e^{-2\alpha_G(\dist(y,\mathcal C)
-2s-9)}\le e^{-\alpha_G(R-2s-8)}e^{-\alpha_G(\dist(y,N_B^{+t})-2s-9)}$, and
summing over $y$ with $\sigma(\alpha_G)$,
\[
\tfrac12\E_c\E_{Q^c}\bigl[J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\varDelta_B
\bigr]\le\epsilon\bigl(11^4V^{1/2}M_{d-5,t}+2V^{3/2}\varPhi_R\bigr).
\]

\emph{The chain.} On $\mathcal G^c$, the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains} with $N=N_B$ and $N'=\emptyset$ gives $m\ge
\lfloor t/R\rfloor$ and blocks $z_1,\dots,z_m$ of $\mathsf D$ with steps at
most $R$, $z_1\in N_B^{+R}$, $\dist(z_k,z_l)>R$ for $\lvert k-l\rvert\ge2$,
$\dist(z_m,N_B)>t-R$ and $m$ least. By minimality $\dist(z_k,N_B)\le t-R$
for $k<m$, so every $z_k$ is within $t$ of $N_B$ and at distance at least
$d-t\ge6$ from $z_A$. The blocks $z_k$ with $k$ odd are pairwise at distance
more than $R\ge11$, so at most one of them is within $5$ of $z_B$; removing
it, or else the last odd one, leaves a set $T$ of $\lceil m/2\rceil-1$
blocks with $\{z_A,z_B\}\cup T$ pairwise at distance at least $6$. Each of
the two terms of $J_{z_Az_B}$ times $\mathbf 1\{T\subset\mathsf D\}$ is a
sum over $T_1\subset T$ of indicators of events $\{z_A\in B(\omega),\,T_1
\subset B(\omega)\}$ with $z_B$ in one of the two copies and $T\setminus T_1
\subset B(\omega')$, so, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains},
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\E_{Q^c}\bigl[J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1\{T\subset\mathsf D\}\bigr]\\
\le2\epsilon(2\epsilon^{1/2})^{\lceil m/2\rceil-1}\le2\epsilon(\sqrt2\,
\epsilon^{1/4})^{m-2}.
\end{multline*}
With at most $V(2R+1)^{4(m-1)}$ sequences of length $m$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\E_{Q^c}\bigl[J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G^c}\bigr]\le2\epsilon
(2R+1)^4V\sum_{m\ge\lfloor t/R\rfloor}g_R^{m-2}\\
\le4\epsilon(2R+1)^4Vg_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor-2}.
\end{multline*}
Adding the two parts and summing over $z_A$ and $z_B$ gives the bound.
\end{proof}

The second bound is the first multiplied by half the factor in
parentheses, which with $V$ of order one is below $1$ for $d$ above about
$1.2\cdot10^5$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:fibrecovnumbers}); its floor
$2V^{3/2}\varPhi_R$ is of order $10^{-7011}$.

Comparing two copies along the clusters on which they may differ is the
idea of the disagreement percolation of van den Berg and
Maes~\cite{vdBM94}; here the two copies are independent, they are compared
by an exchange whose weight is the cross-ratio of
Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}, and the clusters are those of the union of the
two bad sets. For local observables of the field the
conditional covariance given the labels is added, and the labels enter
through conditional expectations, which change by
Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(a) when the labels far from the observable
change.

\begin{theorem}[the fibre covariance]\label{thm:fibrecov}
Let $N_A$, $N_B$ be sets of blocks at distance $d$, $F$ and $H$ bounded
measurable functions of the active links based in $N_A$ and in $N_B$, and
$R\ge2s+9$, $t\ge R$ integers with $t<d$ and $g_R\le\frac12$. Put $V=\max\{
\lvert N_A^{+t}\rvert,\lvert N_B^{+t}\rvert\}$. Then
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\bigl\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H)\bigr\rvert\\
\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert V\bigl(10g_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor}+
\tfrac94M_{d,t}+\tfrac{17}4\epsilon^{1/2}V^{1/2}\varPhi_R\bigr),
\end{multline*}
and $\Cov_{\mu_L}(F,H)$ differs from the covariance under $\mu_L$ of
$\E_{\mu^c}F$ and $\E_{\mu^c}H$, functions of $c$, by at most the same
bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $c$ and write $\varphi(\omega)=\E_{\mu^c}[F\mid\omega]$, $\psi(\omega)=
\E_{\mu^c}[H\mid\omega]$. Then
\[
\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H)=\E_{P^c}\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H\mid\omega)+\Cov_{P^c}(\varphi,
\psi).
\]
\emph{Given the labels.} Let $Y_1=B(\omega)\cup N_A\cup N_B$, $\mathcal C_1$
the union of its $R$-clusters meeting $N_A$, and $\mathcal G_1=\{\mathcal
C_1\subset N_A^{+t}\}$. On $\mathcal G_1$, $N_B\cap\mathcal C_1=\emptyset$
since $d>t$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(b) with $Y=Y_1$, $X=\mathcal C_1$
gives $\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H\mid\omega)\rvert\le\frac14\lVert F\rVert\lVert
H\rVert\varDelta(\mathcal C_1,Y_1\setminus\mathcal C_1)$; off
$\mathcal G_1$ the covariance is at most $\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains} and~\eqref{eq:groupmean} with $k=1$, $N=N_A$,
$N'=N_B$, and $\lvert N_A^{+R}\rvert,\lvert N_B\rvert\le V$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\E_{P^c}\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H\mid\omega)\rvert\\
\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert V\bigl(2g_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor}+\tfrac14
M_{d,t}+\tfrac14\epsilon^{1/2}V^{1/2}\varPhi_R\bigr).
\end{multline*}
\emph{The labels.} Let $Y=\mathsf D\cup N_A\cup N_B$, $\mathcal C_A$ and
$\mathcal C_B$ the unions of its $R$-clusters meeting $N_A$ and $N_B$,
$\mathcal G=\{\mathcal C_A\subset N_A^{+t},\,\mathcal C_B\subset N_B^{+t}\}$,
$\varDelta_A=\varDelta(\mathcal C_A,Y\setminus\mathcal C_A)$ and
$\varDelta_B=\varDelta(\mathcal C_B,Y\setminus\mathcal C_B)$. On $\mathcal
G$, $\mathcal C_A\cap\mathcal C_B=\emptyset$, since an $R$-cluster in
both would lie in $N_A^{+t}$ and contain a block of $N_B$. Let $G=
\varphi(\omega)(\psi(\omega)-\psi(\omega'))$, so that $\Cov_{P^c}(\varphi,
\psi)=\E_{Q^c}G$ and $\lvert G\rvert\le2\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert$, and
let $\chi$ exchange the labels on $\mathcal C_B$ as in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}; it preserves $Y$, $\mathcal C_A$, $\mathcal C_B$,
$\mathcal G$, $\varDelta_A$, $\varDelta_B$, and changes the weight by a
factor in $[e^{-\varDelta_B},e^{\varDelta_B}]$. On $\mathcal G$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(a) applied with $X=\mathcal C_A$ to $\omega$,
$\tilde\omega$, which agree on $\mathcal C_A$, and with $X=\mathcal C_B$ to
$\tilde\omega,\omega'$ and to $\tilde\omega',\omega$, which agree on
$\mathcal C_B$, gives
\begin{gather*}
\lvert\varphi(\tilde\omega)-\varphi(\omega)\rvert\le2\lVert F\rVert
\tanh(\varDelta_A/4),\\
\lvert\psi(\tilde\omega)-\psi(\omega')\rvert\le2\lVert H\rVert\tanh
(\varDelta_B/4),
\end{gather*}
and the same for $\psi(\tilde\omega')-\psi(\omega)$. Writing
\[
\begin{split}
G\circ\chi+G&=\bigl(\varphi(\tilde\omega)-\varphi(\omega)\bigr)\bigl(
\psi(\tilde\omega)-\psi(\tilde\omega')\bigr)\\
&\quad+\varphi(\omega)\bigl(\psi(\tilde\omega)-\psi(\omega')-\psi
(\tilde\omega')+\psi(\omega)\bigr)
\end{split}
\]
gives $\lvert G\circ\chi+G\rvert\le4\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert(\tanh
\frac{\varDelta_A}4+\tanh\frac{\varDelta_B}4)$. With $w_x=Q^c(x)+Q^c(\chi x)$ and $w'_x=Q^c(x)-
Q^c(\chi x)$, an orbit $\{x,\chi x\}$ of two points in $\mathcal G$
contributes
\[
\tfrac12w_x\bigl(G+G\circ\chi\bigr)(x)+\tfrac12w'_x\bigl(G-G\circ\chi
\bigr)(x),
\]
with $\lvert G-G\circ\chi\rvert\le4\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert$ and
$\lvert w'_x\rvert\le w_x\tanh(\varDelta_B/2)$, and a fixed point
contributes $\frac12Q^c(x)(G+G\circ\chi)(x)$. With $\tanh u\le u$,
\begin{multline*}
\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\varphi,\psi)\rvert\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert\bigl(
2Q^c(\mathcal G^c)\\
+\E_{Q^c}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\bigl(\tfrac12\varDelta_A+\tfrac32
\varDelta_B\bigr)\bigr]\bigr).
\end{multline*}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains} for $N_A$ and for $N_B$, and
\eqref{eq:groupmean} with $k=2$ for $(N,N')=(N_A,N_B)$ and $(N_B,N_A)$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\varphi,\psi)\rvert\\
\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert V\bigl(8g_R^{\lfloor t/R\rfloor}+2M_{d,t}
+4\epsilon^{1/2}V^{1/2}\varPhi_R\bigr).
\end{multline*}
Adding the two parts gives the bound. Finally $\Cov_{\mu_L}(F,H)=\E_c
\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H)+\Cov(\E_{\mu^c}F,\E_{\mu^c}H)$, the last covariance
under the law of $c$.
\end{proof}

The bound has three terms. The first is the chance that the group of an
observable reaches distance $t$; the second is the cross-ratio between the
two groups through the good layer, at the rate $2\alpha_G$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound}; the third is the cross-ratio between a group
and the islands at distance more than $R$ from it, in the mean, which is
of order $\epsilon$ and does not decay with $d$. The numbers follow.

\begin{corollary}[the covariances in numbers]\label{cor:fibrecovnumbers}
At $\rho=2.17\cdot10^{-16}$, with $s\in\{1,5\}$, $\beta_W\ge\beta^*$, and
$V$ the volume of Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} or~\ref{thm:fibrecov} for the
stated $t$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item for $d\ge6s+34$, with $R=2s+9$ and $t=R(\lceil d/(10^4R)\rceil+2)$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\rvert\le\operatorname{osc}\phi
\operatorname{osc}\psi\,\lvert N_A\rvert\lvert N_B\rvert\,\epsilon\\
\times\Bigl(\frac{\beta_W}{\beta^*}10^{c_s}V^{1/2}e^{-2\alpha_G(1-10^{-4})
d}\\
+4(4s+19)^4Ve^{-\lambda_sd}+10^{-f_s}V^{3/2}\Bigr),
\end{multline*}
with $c_1=26.26$, $\lambda_1=0.0736$, $f_1=7011.8$, $c_5=27.29$, $\lambda_5=
0.0503$, $f_5=8285.9$, and $V\le\lvert N_B\rvert(d/5000+12s+55)^4$;
\item for $d\ge2s+10$, with $R=2s+9$ and $t=R\lceil d/(10^4R)\rceil$,
\begin{multline*}
\E_c\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H)\rvert\le\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert\Bigl(
\frac{\beta_W}{\beta^*}10^{a_s}Ve^{-2\alpha_G(1-10^{-4})d}\\
+10^{-a'_s}V^{3/2}\Bigr),
\end{multline*}
with $a_1=22.75$, $a'_1=14062.6$, $a_5=23.77$, $a'_5=16611.8$, and $V\le
\max\{\lvert N_A\rvert,\lvert N_B\rvert\}(d/5000+4s+19)^4$;
\item for $10^8\le d\le10^{100}$, with $R=\lceil2000\sqrt d\rceil$ and
$t=\lfloor d/2\rfloor$,
\[
\E_c\lvert\Cov_{\mu^c}(F,H)\rvert\le10^{-1965}\frac{\beta_W}{\beta^*}
\lVert F\rVert\lVert H\rVert V^{3/2}e^{-\sqrt d/2},
\]
with $V\le\max\{\lvert N_A\rvert,\lvert N_B\rvert\}(d+1)^4$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Dependence on $\beta_W$.} By Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} and Step~6 of
the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow}, $f$ decreases on $[\beta^*,
\infty)$ and $f(\beta^*)=\log q^*$, so $\epsilon\le Mq^*$ and $g_R$ is at
most its value at $\beta^*$. The logarithmic derivative of $b_*=1920r^2
(99.0001\beta_W+4.65\cdot10^6)^2/\beta_W$ is at most $1/\beta_W$, so $b_*
\le(\beta_W/\beta^*)b_*(\beta^*)$. As $f'(\beta)=6/\beta-\rho^2/16$, the
logarithmic derivatives of $b_*\epsilon^{1/2}$ and $b_*\epsilon$ are at
most $4/\beta_W-\rho^2/32$ and $7/\beta_W-\rho^2/16$, both negative since
$\beta^*\rho^2/16>8$; so $\varPhi_R$ and $\epsilon^{1/2}\varPhi_R$ are at
most their values at $\beta^*$. At $\beta^*$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow}, $b_*\nu_s\le10^{22.0833}$ for $s=1$ and
$10^{23.1039}$ for $s=5$, $\sigma(\alpha_G)\le9.831\cdot10^{16}$, and
$-\log g_{2s+9}\ge8105.1$ for $s=1$ and $9571.0$ for $s=5$. Indeed, the
proof of that theorem gives $b_*(\beta^*)\le10^{16.2645}$ and $10^{16.3356}$,
$\sigma(\alpha_G)\le9.831\cdot10^{16}$, $\lvert\log q^*\rvert$ within
$10^{-2}$ of $32481.67$ and $38354.07$, and $\log_{10}(Mq^*)$ within
$10^{-3}$ of $-14102.446$ and $-16652.797$; here $\nu_1=45\cdot11^4$,
$\nu_5=45\cdot19^4$ with $\log19=\log18+2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{37}$,
and at $\epsilon=Mq^*$
\[
-\log g_R=\tfrac14\bigl(\lvert\log q^*\rvert-4\log11\bigr)-\tfrac12\log2-
4\log(2R+1),
\]
which at $2R+1=4s+19$, that is $23$ and $39=3\cdot13$, lies within
$10^{-2}$ of $8105.13$ and $9571.12$. Every number below is a decimal
logarithm of a product of these factors, computed with $\log10=\log2+
\log5$; and $b_*(\beta^*)\ge1920r^2\cdot99^2\beta^*>10^{16}$, so $10\le
\frac94b_*\nu_s$.

(i) Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}: $t\ge3R$, $t\le d/10^4+3R$ and $(6s+34)
(1-10^{-4})\ge6s+33$, so $d\ge t+6$; $d-5-t-2s-9\ge(1-10^{-4})d-8s-41$, so
$11^4M_{d-5,t}\le(\beta_W/\beta^*)10^{c_s}e^{-2\alpha_G(1-10^{-4})d}$ with
$10^{c_s}\ge11^4b_*(\beta^*)\nu_se^{2\alpha_G(8s+41)}$; $\lfloor t/R\rfloor
-2=\lceil d/(10^4R)\rceil$ and $-\log g_R/(10^4R)\ge\lambda_s$; $2\varPhi_R
\le10^{-f_s}$; and $2t+1\le d/5000+12s+55$. (ii)
Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrecov}: $R\le t\le d/10^4+R<d$ for $d\ge2s+10$, and
$d-t-2s-9\ge(1-10^{-4})d-2(2s+9)$. The chain term is at most $10e^{-
\lambda d/(10^4R)}$ with $\lambda=-\log g_R$, and $\lambda/(10^4R)\ge2
\alpha_G$ and $10\le\frac94b_*\nu_s$, so the first two terms are at most
$(\beta_W/\beta^*)\frac92b_*(\beta^*)\nu_se^{4\alpha_G(2s+9)}e^{-2\alpha_G
(1-10^{-4})d}V$; the third is $\frac{17}4b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)\epsilon
e^{\alpha_G(2s+8)}V^{3/2}\le10^{-a'_s}V^{3/2}$. (iii) For $d\ge10^8$, $t\ge
d/2-1\ge2000\sqrt d+1\ge R$, and $t/R\ge\sqrt d/4001\ge1$, so $\lfloor t/R
\rfloor\ge\sqrt d/8002$; $R\le2000\cdot10^{50}+1$, where $-\log g_R\ge
7623.9$ for $s=1$ and $9092.0$ for $s=5$. The third term carries
$e^{-\alpha_GR}\le e^{-\sqrt d/2}$, and $d-t-2s-9\ge d/2-2s-9$; the ratios
of the chain and main terms to $e^{-\sqrt d/2}$ decrease in $d$ on $[10^8,
\infty)$, and $V\le V^{3/2}$.

\emph{The numbers}, for $s=1$ and $s=5$. In (i),
\begin{gather*}
\log_{10}\bigl(11^4b_*\nu_se^{2\alpha_G(8s+41)}\bigr)\le26.2596,\ 27.2871,
\\
-\log g_R/(10^4R)\ge0.07368,\ 0.05037,\\
\log_{10}\bigl(2b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)(Mq^*)^{1/2}e^{\alpha_G(2s+8)}
\bigr)\\
\le-7011.84,\ -8285.99,
\end{gather*}
which give $c_s$, $\lambda_s$ and $f_s$. In (ii), $-\log g_R/(10^4R)\ge2
\alpha_G$ and
\begin{gather*}
\log_{10}\bigl(\tfrac92b_*\nu_se^{4\alpha_G(2s+9)}\bigr)\le22.742,\
23.766,\\
\log_{10}\bigl(\tfrac{17}4b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)Mq^*e^{\alpha_G(2s+8)}
\bigr)\\
\le-14062.73,\ -16612.06,
\end{gather*}
which give $a_s$ and $a'_s$. In (iii), at $2R+1\le4\cdot10^{53}+3$ the
display for $-\log g_R$ gives $\lambda=-\log g_R\ge7623.9$ and $9092.0$, so
that $\lambda/8002>\frac12$. The chain and main ratios are at most
\begin{gather*}
10e^{-(\lambda/8002-1/2)\sqrt d},\\
\tfrac94b_*\nu_se^{-2\alpha_G(d/2-2s-9)+\sqrt d/2};
\end{gather*}
the first decreases in $d$, and the second for $\sqrt d>1/(4\alpha_G)=
1000$. At $d=10^8$ the chain ratio is at most $10^{-1965.2}$ and
$10^{-2761}$, the main ratio at most $10^{-8663.4}$ and $10^{-8662.4}$, and
the coefficient $\frac{17}4b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)Mq^*e^{\alpha_G(4s+17)}$
of the third term at most $10^{-14062.7}$ and $10^{-16612}$.
\end{proof}

The groups make the Dobrushin condition on the islands unnecessary in these
bounds: two groups have one cross-ratio. Where that condition holds, as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow}(iii), part (ii) of
Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov} has a constructive proof, by the heat-bath sweep
of F\"ollmer~\cite{Fol82} under Dobrushin's matrix~\cite{Dob68,Dob70},
which needs neither the minimising coupling nor compactness.

\begin{lemma}[the sweep]\label{lem:sweep}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:islandcov}, with $f,g$ bounded measurable,
suppose that $D=\sum_{n\ge0}C^n$ converges. Let $T_qu(\xi)=\int u(\xi^\eta)
P_q(d\eta\mid\xi)$, let $q_1,q_2,\dots$ run through $\mathcal Q$
cyclically, $u_0=f$ and $u_k=T_{q_k}u_{k-1}$. Then
\begin{gather*}
\Cov_P(f,g)=\sum_{k\ge1}\E_P\bigl[\Cov_{q_k}(u_{k-1},g)\bigr],\\
\sum_{k:\,q_k=q}\delta_q(u_{k-1})\le\sum_{q'}\delta_{q'}(f)D_{q'q},
\end{gather*}
with $\Cov_q$ the covariance under $P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)$ in the coordinate
$q$; hence $\lvert\Cov_P(f,g)\rvert\le\frac14\sum_{q,q'}\delta_{q'}(f)
D_{q'q}\delta_q(g)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The law $P$ is invariant under $T_q$, and $T_qu$ does not depend on
the coordinate $\xi_q$; so $\E_P[(T_qu)g]=\E_P[(T_qu)(T_qg)]$ and $\E_P[ug]=\E_P[(T_qu)(T_qg)]+\E_P
\Cov_q(u,g)$, which gives $\Cov_P(u,g)-\Cov_P(T_qu,g)=\E_P\Cov_q(u,g)$.
For $q'\ne q$, changing $\xi_{q'}$ changes $T_qu$ by at most $\delta_{q'}
(u)+C_{qq'}\delta_q(u)$: the integrand by $\delta_{q'}(u)$, and the law
$P_q(\cdot\mid\xi)$ by $C_{qq'}$ in total variation, against a function of
oscillation $\delta_q(u)$. So the vector $v_k=(\delta_q(u_k))_q$ obeys
$v_k\le v_{k-1}-\tau_ke_{q_k}+\tau_kC_{q_k\cdot}$ with $\tau_k=(v_{k-1})
_{q_k}$, and since $D\ge0$ and $D-CD=I$, $v_kD\le v_{k-1}D-\tau_ke_{q_k}$.
Summing, the accumulated $\tau$ at each $q$ is at most $(v_0D)_q$, the
second claim. In particular $\sum_k\tau_k<\infty$; each $(v_n)_q$ is at
most the sum of the $\tau_k$ since the last visit to $q$, as $C\le1$, so
$v_n\to0$, $\operatorname{osc}u_n\le\sum_q(v_n)_q\to0$ and $\Cov_P(u_n,g)
\to0$. This gives the identity, and $\lvert\Cov_q(u,g)\rvert\le\frac14
\delta_q(u)\delta_q(g)$ by Popoviciu~\cite{Pop35} gives the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:labelcovopen}
Four things are not proved here. First, the bounds are means over the
coarse field. For a fixed $c$ the labels need not be rare: a coarse
plaquette with $\delta(c_P,I)>\eta$ makes its blocks bad with
$P^c$-probability one. The proofs use rarity only through $\E_cP^c(T\subset
B)=\mu_L(T\subset B)$ and its two-copy form in
Lemma~\ref{lem:labelchains}; a bound for every $c$, or uniform in an
exterior as (D) asks, is not given. Second, the floor. The chains are paid
for at the joining distance $R$, while the islands beyond $R$ enter
$\varDelta$ through $e^{-\alpha_GR}$, so with $R$ fixed the bound stops at
a floor, of order $\epsilon^{3/2}$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} and
$\epsilon$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrecov}, and with $R\propto\sqrt d$ it decays as $e^{-\sqrt d/2}$. Decay
at the rate $2\alpha_G$ without a floor needs control of $\log Z^c$ as a
function of the labels of three or more components: the mixed differences
of order $k\ge3$ of $\log Z^c$ over the labels of $k$ components, bounded
by $C^ke^{-2\alpha_G\ell}$ with $\ell$ the length of the shortest tree
joining them. The inputs give the differences of order two, and through
Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius} those of every order in terms of the diameter only;
those of
order three of $\log\tilde K$ are third cumulants of the layer law, which
\eqref{eq:layerbound} does not bound, and $\tilde K$ and $D_z$ depend on
the set $Y$ of components. Third, the covariance of $\E_{\mu^c}F$ and
$\E_{\mu^c}H$ as functions of $c$ is the multiscale part, item (iv) of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}. Fourth, the bounds are consistent with
Proposition~\ref{prop:hiddenbit}: in its mixture the labels are independent
given the hidden bit, which plays the role of $c$, so the covariance under
the fibre law vanishes and the covariance $q^2/16$ is that of the
conditional means; the theorems above use the cross-ratio of
Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}, not rarity alone.
\end{remark}

Remark~\ref{rem:labelcovopen} leaves open a covariance bound for the labels
for a fixed coarse field, uniform in the exterior, decaying at the rate
$2\alpha_G$ with no floor. The rest of this subsection determines what the
inputs used above give for one law of the labels. The proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} uses two properties of the laws $P^c$. For a law
$P$ on the labellings of $\Lambda$ and $0<\epsilon'<1$ consider:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[$(\mathrm R_{\epsilon'})$] $P(T\subset B)\le\epsilon'^{\lvert T
\rvert}$ for every nonempty set $T$ of blocks pairwise at distance at
least $6$;
\item[$(\mathrm X)$] for every set $Y$ of blocks, every union $X$ of
components of $Y$, $X'=Y\setminus X$, and all labellings $\omega,\omega'$
of positive probability with $B(\omega),B(\omega')\subset Y$, the
labellings $\omega^\natural=(\omega'_X,\omega_{X'})$ and $\omega'^\natural
=(\omega_X,\omega'_{X'})$ have positive probability and
\[
e^{-\varDelta}\le\frac{P(\omega^\natural)P(\omega'^\natural)}{P(\omega)
P(\omega')}\le e^{\varDelta},
\]
with $\varDelta=\min\{\varDelta(X,X'),\varDelta(X',X)\}$.
\end{itemize}
For every coarse field $c$ the law $P^c$ has $(\mathrm X)$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(c), and the law of the labels under $\mu_L$
has $(\mathrm R_\epsilon)$.

\begin{lemma}[one law]\label{lem:onelaw}
Let $P$ be a law on the labellings of $\Lambda$ with $(\mathrm X)$ and
$(\mathrm R_{\epsilon^{1/2}})$, and let $N_A,N_B,\phi,\psi$ be as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}. Then $\lvert\Cov_P(\phi,\psi)\rvert$ obeys both
bounds of Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}, with the same constants. In
particular this holds for every law with $(\mathrm X)$ and $(\mathrm
R_\epsilon)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Run the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} with $P^c$ replaced by $P$,
$Q^c$ by $Q=P\otimes P$, and the means $\E_c$ omitted. The exchange and the
orbit decomposition use $(\mathrm X)$ only. The mean over $c$ enters
through the probabilities, under $Q$, of events $\{T_1\subset B(\omega),
\,T_2\subset B(\omega')\}$ with $T=T_1\cup T_2$ pairwise at distance at
least $6$, which the proof bounds by $\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}$, and
through $\mu_L(z_A,z_B\in B)\le\epsilon^2$ in the first bound. Under $Q$
the first probability is $P(T_1\subset B)P(T_2\subset B)\le
\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}$ by $(\mathrm R_{\epsilon^{1/2}})$, with
$P(\emptyset\subset B)=1$; it covers the means of $J_{z_Az_B}$, at most
$2\epsilon$, of $J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1[y\in\mathsf D]$, at most $4
\epsilon^{3/2}$, and of $J_{z_Az_B}\mathbf 1\{T\subset\mathsf D\}$ along a
chain, at most $2\epsilon(2\epsilon^{1/2})^{\lvert T\rvert}$. In the first
bound the mean of $J_{z_Az_B}$ is at most $P(z_A,z_B\in B)+P(z_A\in B)P(z_B
\in B)\le2\epsilon$. Every other step is pointwise in the labellings.
Finally $\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert}\le\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[fixed coarse fields]\label{prop:fixedgood}
Let $\mathcal G_\Lambda$ be the set of coarse fields $c$ for which $P^c$
has $(\mathrm R_{\epsilon^{1/2}})$. Then
\[
\mu_L\{V^\sharp\notin\mathcal G_\Lambda\}\le(1+\epsilon^{1/2})^{\lvert
\Lambda\rvert}-1,
\]
which is at most $2\lvert\Lambda\rvert\epsilon^{1/2}$ when $\lvert\Lambda
\rvert\epsilon^{1/2}\le1$, and for every $c\in\mathcal G_\Lambda$ the
covariance $\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\rvert$ obeys both bounds of
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}. No coarse field with a coarse plaquette
$\delta(c_P,I)>\eta$ lies in $\mathcal G_\Lambda$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For a set $T$ of blocks, $\E_cP^c(T\subset B)=\mu_L(T\subset B)\le
\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert}$ when $T$ is pairwise at distance at least $6$,
so by Markov's inequality the law of $V^\sharp$ gives the set $\{c:
P^c(T\subset B)>\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}\}$ mass at most
$\epsilon^{\lvert T\rvert/2}$. The union over the nonempty sets $T\subset
\Lambda$ has mass at most $\sum_{T\ne\emptyset}\epsilon^{\lvert T
\rvert/2}=(1+\epsilon^{1/2})^{\lvert\Lambda\rvert}-1\le e^{\lvert\Lambda
\rvert\epsilon^{1/2}}-1$, and $e^x-1\le2x$ on $[0,1]$. For $c\in\mathcal
G_\Lambda$, $P^c$ has $(\mathrm X)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}(c), and
Lemma~\ref{lem:onelaw} applies. A coarse plaquette with $\delta(c_P,I)>
\eta$ makes its corner bad with $P^c$-probability one, and $1>
\epsilon^{1/2}$.
\end{proof}

The floor of Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} comes from the joining distance
$R$; with $R$ of order $\sqrt d$ it becomes a stretched exponential, as for
the fibre in Corollary~\ref{cor:fibrecovnumbers}(iii).

\begin{corollary}[the labels, stretched]\label{cor:labelstretched}
At $\rho=2.17\cdot10^{-16}$, with $s\in\{1,5\}$, $\beta_W\ge\beta^*$ and
$10^8\le d\le10^{100}$, both $\E_c\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\rvert$ and,
for every $c\in\mathcal G_\Lambda$, $\lvert\Cov_{P^c}(\phi,\psi)\rvert$
are at most
\[
\operatorname{osc}\phi\operatorname{osc}\psi\,\lvert N_A\rvert\lvert
N_B\rvert\,10^{-u_s}V^{3/2}e^{-\sqrt d/20},
\]
with $u_1=21114.2$, $u_5=24938.6$ and $V\le\lvert N_B\rvert(d+1)^4$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Take $R=\lceil200\sqrt d\rceil$ and $t=\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov}, or in Lemma~\ref{lem:onelaw}. For $d\ge10^8$,
$t\ge d/2-1\ge2R$, $d\ge t+6$, $2R+1\le401\sqrt d$ and $t/R\ge\sqrt d/401$,
so $\lfloor t/R\rfloor-2\ge\sqrt d/401-3>0$; $R\le200\cdot10^{50}+1$, where
$-\log g_R\ge7633.1$ for $s=1$ and $9101.2$ for $s=5$. The three terms of
the bracket, multiplied by the factor $\epsilon$ in front, are bounded as
follows. The far term $2V^{3/2}\varPhi_R$ carries $e^{-\alpha_GR}\le
e^{-\sqrt d/20}$, since $200\alpha_G=\frac1{20}$, with coefficient
$2b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)\epsilon^{1/2}e^{\alpha_G(4s+17)}$. The main term
has $d-5-t-2s-9\ge d/2-2s-14$, and its ratio to $e^{-\sqrt d/20}$,
$11^4b_*\nu_se^{2\alpha_G(2s+14)}e^{-\alpha_Gd+\sqrt d/20}$, decreases on
$[10^8,\infty)$. The chain term is at most $4\cdot401^4d^2Ve^{3\lambda}
e^{-\lambda\sqrt d/401}$ with $\lambda=-\log g_R$, and its ratio to
$e^{-\sqrt d/20}$ decreases on $[10^8,\infty)$ since $\lambda/401>\frac1
{20}+4\cdot10^{-4}$. By the monotonicity in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fibrecovnumbers}, $\epsilon b_*$, $\epsilon^{3/2}b_*$
and $g_R$ are at most their values at $\beta^*$. At $\beta^*$ and
$d=10^8$, the coefficient of the far term times $\epsilon$ is at most
$10^{-21114.22}$ for $s=1$ and $10^{-24938.64}$ for $s=5$, and the main
and chain ratios are below $10^{-24000}$ and $10^{-86000}$; with $V^{1/2},
V\le V^{3/2}$ and $2t+1\le d+1$ this gives the bound.

\emph{The numbers} come from the factors listed in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fibrecovnumbers}. The display for $-\log g_R$ there at
$2R+1\le4\cdot10^{52}+3$ gives $\lambda\ge7633.1$ and $9101.2$. With
$\epsilon\le Mq^*$, the decimal logarithm of $2b_*\nu_s\sigma(\alpha_G)
(Mq^*)^{3/2}e^{\alpha_G(4s+17)}$ is at most $-21114.28$ for $s=1$ and
$-24938.79$ for $s=5$; that of $11^4b_*\nu_se^{2\alpha_G(2s+14)}e^{-\alpha_G
d+\sqrt d/20}Mq^*$ at $d=10^8$ is at most $-24716$ and $-27265$; and the
chain ratio times $\epsilon$ is at most $4\cdot401^4d^2e^{-\lambda(\sqrt
d/401-3)+\sqrt d/20}Mq^*$, whose decimal logarithm at $d=10^8$ is at most
$-86581$ and $-103119$.
\end{proof}

The next theorem shows that no argument which uses only $(\mathrm X)$ and a
rarity bound does better: for a fixed coarse field nothing crosses a bad
component, and with rarity the decay is at best a stretched exponential.

\begin{theorem}[what rarity and the group cross-ratios give]
\label{thm:fixedobstruction}
Let $s\ge1$, $\alpha_G$ and $b_*\nu_s\ge1$ be as above, and let $d\ge2$ be
an integer, on a torus of side larger than $2d$; let $a$ and $b=a+de_1$ be
two blocks.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $J\ge0$ there is a law $P$ with $(\mathrm X)$, under which
the blocks $a+ie_1$, $0<i<d$, are bad with probability one, such that
\[
\Cov_P\bigl(\mathbf 1[a\in B],\mathbf 1[b\in B]\bigr)=\tfrac14\tanh
\tfrac J4 ;
\]
in it every second difference of $\log P$ between the labels of two sets
of blocks at distance at least $2s+9$, all other labels fixed, vanishes.
\item Let $0<\epsilon'\le e^{-3}$, $\varkappa=\log(e/\epsilon')$ and
$h_*=\lceil\varkappa/(2\alpha_G)\rceil$, and suppose $h_*\ge2s+9$. If
$d=m^2h_*$ with an integer $m\ge1$, there is a law $P$ with $(\mathrm X)$
and $(\mathrm R_{\epsilon'})$ such that
\begin{multline*}
\Cov_P\bigl(\mathbf 1[a\in B],\mathbf 1[b\in B]\bigr)\ge\tfrac12
e^{-(2m+1)\varkappa-2\alpha_Gm}\\
=\tfrac12e^{-\varkappa}\exp\bigl(-(2\varkappa+2\alpha_G)\sqrt{d/h_*}
\bigr).
\end{multline*}
In it the mixed difference of order $m+1$ of $\log P$ over the labels of
the blocks $a+jmh_*e_1$, $0\le j\le m$, equals $e^{-2\alpha_Gd/m}$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently no bound
\[
\lvert\Cov_P(\phi,\psi)\rvert\le C\operatorname{osc}\phi
\operatorname{osc}\psi\,\lvert N_A\rvert\,\lvert N_B\rvert\,e^{-\kappa d}
\]
with $C<\infty$ and $\kappa>0$ holds for all laws with $(\mathrm X)$ and
$(\mathrm R_{\epsilon'})$; with $\kappa=2\alpha_G$ and $C\epsilon'$ in place
of $C$ it fails at $d=9h_*$ for every $C<e^{3\varkappa-6\alpha_G}/(2e)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) Let $K=\{a+ie_1:0<i<d\}$, a set connected at distance one. Let $P$
give the labellings with $B=K\cup B_0$, $B_0\subset\{a,b\}$, the weights
$Z_{11}=Z_{00}=e^{J/2}$ and $Z_{10}=Z_{01}=1$, the indices being the
labels of $a$ and $b$, and every other labelling the weight zero; by
Corollary~\ref{cor:twolabels} the covariance is $\frac14\tanh(J/4)$. Let
$Y$, $X$, $\omega$, $\omega'$ be as in $(\mathrm X)$. Then $K\subset Y$,
and $a$ and $b$, when they lie in $Y$, lie in the component of $Y$ that
contains $K$, since they are at distance one from $K$. If $X$ contains
that component, $\omega^\natural$ and $\omega'^\natural$ agree with
$\omega'$ and $\omega$ at $a$ and $b$; otherwise they agree with $\omega$
and $\omega'$ there. Every other block has the same label in all four
labellings, so the ratio in $(\mathrm X)$ is one. Two sets at distance at
least $2s+9$ off which every block is good contain $K$ in one of them,
and $a$ and $b$, when bad, in the same one; so the label of only one of
them varies, and the second difference vanishes.

(ii) Put $h=mh_*$, $y_j=a+jhe_1$ for $0\le j\le m$, $S=\{y_0,\dots,y_m\}$,
$k=m+1$, $p=\epsilon'/e$ and $J=e^{-2\alpha_Gh}\le1$. Let $P$ give the
labelling with bad set $A\subset S$ the probability
\[
P(A)=\frac1N\,p^{\lvert A\rvert}(1-p)^{k-\lvert A\rvert}e^{J\mathbf 1[A
=S]},
\]
with $N=1+(e^J-1)p^k$, and every other labelling the probability zero.

\emph{Rarity.} For $T\subset S$ nonempty, $P(T\subset B)=(p^{\lvert T
\rvert}+(e^J-1)p^k)/N\le e^Jp^{\lvert T\rvert}\le e^{1-\lvert T\rvert}
\epsilon'^{\lvert T\rvert}\le\epsilon'^{\lvert T\rvert}$; for $T\not
\subset S$ it vanishes.

\emph{The cross-ratios.} With $\sigma_j=\mathbf 1[y_j\in B]$, $\log P=
\mathrm{const}+\lvert B\rvert\log\frac p{1-p}+J\prod_j\sigma_j$. In
$(\mathrm X)$ the bad sets of the four labellings lie in $S$, and
$\lvert B(\omega^\natural)\rvert+\lvert B(\omega'^\natural)\rvert=\lvert
B(\omega)\rvert+\lvert B(\omega')\rvert$. If $S\not\subset Y$, some $y_j$
is good in all four and the products vanish. If $S\subset X$ or $S\subset
X'$, the two products on each side are the same. Otherwise, with $x,x'$
the products over $S\cap X$ in $\omega,\omega'$ and $z,z'$ those over
$S\cap X'$, the logarithm of the ratio is $J(x'z+xz'-xz-x'z')=-J(x-x')
(z-z')$, of modulus at most $J$; and two consecutive blocks $y_j,y_{j+1}$
lie on different sides, at distance $h$, so that both $\varDelta(X,X')$
and $\varDelta(X',X)$ are at least $b_*\nu_se^{-2\alpha_G(h-2s-9)}\ge J$.

\emph{The covariance.} $P(a\in B)=(p+(e^J-1)p^k)/N$ and $P(a,b\in B)=(p^2
+(e^J-1)p^k)/N$, so
\[
\Cov_P\bigl(\mathbf 1[a\in B],\mathbf 1[b\in B]\bigr)=\frac{(e^J-1)p^k
(1-p)^2}{N^2}\ge\tfrac12Jp^k,
\]
since $e^J-1\ge J$, $p\le e^{-4}$ and $N\le1+2p^2$. As $2\alpha_Gh_*\le
\varkappa+2\alpha_G$, $J\ge e^{-m\varkappa-2\alpha_Gm}$, and $p^k=
e^{-(m+1)\varkappa}$; with $m=\sqrt{d/h_*}$ this is the bound. The mixed
difference of order $k$ over $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_m$ of the linear part
vanishes, as $k\ge2$, and that of $J\prod_j\sigma_j$ is $J=e^{-2\alpha_G
d/m}$.

\emph{The consequence.} For fixed $C$ and $\kappa>0$ the lower bound of
(ii) exceeds $Ce^{-\kappa d}$ for $d=m^2h_*$ and $m$ large. With $\kappa=
2\alpha_G$, $2\alpha_Gd\ge m^2\varkappa$ and $\epsilon'=e^{1-\varkappa}$,
so the ratio of the covariance to $C\epsilon'e^{-2\alpha_Gd}$ is at least
$e^{(m^2-2m)\varkappa-2\alpha_Gm-1}/(2C)$, which at $m=3$ exceeds one for
$C<e^{3\varkappa-6\alpha_G}/(2e)$.
\end{proof}

At $\epsilon'=10^{-14102.4}$, the bound on $\epsilon$ for $s=1$,
$\varkappa\in[32472.97,32472.98]$, $h_*=64945953$, and the law of (ii)
has covariance at least $\frac12e^{-\varkappa}e^{-8.06\sqrt d}$ at
$d=m^2h_*$; for $s=5$, $\epsilon'=10^{-16652.7}$, $h_*=76690518$ and the
exponent is $8.76\sqrt d$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:onelaw} every law with
$(\mathrm X)$ and $(\mathrm R_\epsilon)$ obeys the bound of
Corollary~\ref{cor:labelstretched}. Within this class the decay is
therefore a stretched exponential, with the coefficient of $\sqrt d$
between $\frac1{20}$ and $8.06$ for $s=1$; at $d=9h_*\le5.85\cdot10^8$ a
bound $C\epsilon e^{-2\alpha_Gd}$ already needs $C\ge10^{42307}$. The laws
of (ii) are made of one interaction among $m+1$ rare blocks at spacing
$d/m$, which the group cross-ratios charge only through the spacing; a
cluster expansion and a coupling that use only $(\mathrm X)$ and rarity
are both subject to (ii).

The pair comparison of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} is an input of
another kind: it bounds the second difference of two islands with the
labels of all the others fixed, in every such environment, and it controls
the differences of every order.

\begin{lemma}[differences of higher order]\label{lem:mobius}
Let the data and hypotheses be those of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands},
with the index set $\mathcal I=\mathcal K\cup\mathcal Q$, $\lvert\mathcal
K\rvert=k\ge2$, two patterns $\omega_u^0,\omega_u^1$ on $I_u$ for $u\in
\mathcal K$ and one pattern on $I_q$ for $q\in\mathcal Q$. For
$\varsigma\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal K}$ let $Z(\varsigma)$ be the weight of the
event that the labels of $\Lambda$ are $\omega_u^{\varsigma_u}$ on $I_u$,
$u\in\mathcal K$, the given patterns on the $I_q$ and good elsewhere, and
suppose $Z(\varsigma)>0$ for all $\varsigma$. Then
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{\varsigma}(-1)^{k-\lvert\varsigma\rvert}\log Z(\varsigma)
\Bigr|\le2^{k-2}\min_{u\ne v\in\mathcal K}\varDelta_*(u,v),
\]
with $\lvert\varsigma\rvert=\sum_u\varsigma_u$ and $\varDelta_*(u,v)$ the
quantity $\varDelta_*$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} for $a=u$, $b=v$
and the sets $I_w$, $w\in\mathcal I\setminus\{u,v\}$, in the role of
$\mathcal Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The numbers $\varDelta_{uv}$, $S_u$, $C$ and $D$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} depend on the sets $I_w$, on $\Lambda_2$
and on $\beta_W$, and not on the patterns, since $\tilde K$ and $\mathcal
U$ are the same in all sectors by Lemma~\ref{lem:manykernel}(i). Fix
$u\ne v$ and, for $\varsigma'\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal K\setminus\{u,v\}}$,
let $D(\varsigma')$ be the second difference $\log Z_{11}+\log Z_{00}-
\log Z_{10}-\log Z_{01}$ in $(\varsigma_u,\varsigma_v)$ with the other
indices equal to $\varsigma'$. These four weights are those of
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} with the sets $I_w$, $w\ne u,v$, carrying
the patterns $\omega_w^{\varsigma'_w}$, so $\lvert D(\varsigma')\rvert\le
\varDelta_*(u,v)$. The sum in the statement is $\sum_{\varsigma'}(-1)^{k-2-
\lvert\varsigma'\rvert}D(\varsigma')$, which has $2^{k-2}$ terms.
\end{proof}

Under the weighted Dobrushin condition of
Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} the right side is at most
$2^{k-2}(\varDelta_{uv}+e^{-2\vartheta\alpha_G\ell(u,v)}T_uT_v/(4(1-
\theta)))$ for the pair $u,v$ of largest $\ell(u,v)$, so the differences of
order $k$ decay with the diameter of the $k$ sets in the pseudometric
$\ell$. In the laws of Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(ii) the pair
$y_0,y_m$, with the blocks of $S$ between them bad, has second difference
$e^{-2\alpha_Gd/m}$ at distance $d$, so a pair bound that decays with the
distance as in Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains} excludes them.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:fixedcopen}
For a fixed coarse field the results above give the following.
Proposition~\ref{prop:fixedgood} gives the bounds of
Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} for every coarse field outside a set of
probability at most $2\lvert\Lambda\rvert\epsilon^{1/2}$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:labelstretched} decay as $e^{-\sqrt d/20}$ for
$10^8\le d\le10^{100}$, with no floor in that range. Decay at the rate
$2\alpha_G$ is not proved, for three reasons. First, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(ii) it does not follow from rarity and
the group cross-ratios of Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross}, which are all that
the proofs of Theorems~\ref{thm:labelcov} and~\ref{thm:fibrecov} use.
Second, Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius} bounds the differences of order $k$ by the
diameter of the $k$ sets, while a cluster expansion in the labels, through
the criterion of Koteck\'y and Preiss~\cite{KP86}, needs the length of
the shortest tree joining them, as in Remark~\ref{rem:labelcovopen}; with
the diameter the sum over $k$ islands in a ball of radius $D$ carries the
entropy $D^{4(k-1)}$, which the rarity pays only while $\epsilon D^4$ is
small, and the pair bound decays only where the weighted Dobrushin
condition holds. Third, uniformity in the coarse field and in the exterior
is excluded for these inputs by Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(i): for
a coarse field whose coarse plaquettes with $\delta(c_P,I)>\eta$ have
corners joining a neighbourhood of $N_A$ to one of $N_B$, the labels of
$N_A$ and $N_B$ adjoin one component that is bad for every labelling, and
neither Lemma~\ref{lem:groupcross} nor Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}
bounds anything across it. A bound uniform in the coarse field therefore
needs the response of the law across the interior of a bad component,
which no result here gives, and a bound at the rate $2\alpha_G$ for the
coarse fields of $\mathcal G_\Lambda$ needs the tree form of the
differences of order three and more. The statement of item (ii) of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains} is accordingly posed in the mean over the coarse
field or for the coarse fields of $\mathcal G_\Lambda$.
\end{remark}

The tree form named in Remarks~\ref{rem:labelcovopen}
and~\ref{rem:fixedcopen} asks for a bound $C_0C^ke^{-2\alpha_G\ell}$ on the
mixed differences of order $k\ge3$, with $\ell$ the length of the
shortest tree joining the $k$ sets. The next two propositions show that
it follows neither from the second differences in every environment,
which are all that Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius} uses, nor from the layer
bound~\eqref{eq:layerbound}, which is all that the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} uses of the layer law. The length of a tree
whose vertices are blocks is the sum of the distances of its edges.

\begin{proposition}[pair bounds give the diameter form]\label{prop:pairsonly}
Let $s\ge1$, $\alpha_G$ and $b_*\nu_s\ge1$ be as above, $0<\epsilon'<1$,
$3\le k\le16$, $D\ge2s+9$ an integer, and on a torus of side larger than
$2D$ let $S$ be a set of $k$ vertices of a cube $a+\{0,D\}^4$, so that
any two blocks of $S$ are at distance $D$. Put $J=e^{-2\alpha_G(D-2s-9)}$.
There is a law $P$ with $(\mathrm X)$ and $(\mathrm R_{\epsilon'})$ such
that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item every second difference of $\log P$ between the labels of two sets
of blocks at distance $t$, all other labels fixed, vanishes unless both
sets meet $S$, and then $t\le D$ and its modulus is at most $J\le
e^{-2\alpha_G(t-2s-9)}$;
\item the mixed difference of order $k$ of $\log P$ over the labels of the
blocks of $S$ equals $J$;
\item every tree whose vertices include $S$ has length at least $kD/2$.
\end{enumerate}
So the bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius} by the second differences of a
pair, in every environment, is attained up to its factor $2^{k-2}$, while a bound
$C_0C^ke^{-2\alpha_G\ell}$ fails for this law as soon as $\alpha_G(k-2)D>
\log(C_0C^k)-2\alpha_G(2s+9)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $p=\epsilon'/e$ and let $P$ give the labelling with bad set $A\subset
S$ the probability $N^{-1}p^{\lvert A\rvert}(1-p)^{k-\lvert A\rvert}e^{J
\mathbf 1[A=S]}$, with $N=1+(e^J-1)p^k$, and every other labelling the
probability zero; this is the law of the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(ii) on the set $S$. For $T\subset S$
nonempty, $P(T\subset B)=(p^{\lvert T\rvert}+(e^J-1)p^k)/N\le e^Jp^{\lvert
T\rvert}\le e^{1-\lvert T\rvert}\epsilon'^{\lvert T\rvert}\le\epsilon'^{
\lvert T\rvert}$, as $J\le1$, and for $T\not\subset S$ it vanishes; this
is $(\mathrm R_{\epsilon'})$. With $\sigma_y=\mathbf 1[y\in B]$, on the
labellings of positive probability $\log P=\mathrm{const}+\lvert B\rvert
\log\frac p{1-p}+J\prod_{y\in S}\sigma_y$. In $(\mathrm X)$ the
computation of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(ii) gives
the ratio $e^{-J(x-x')(z-z')}$, which is one unless $S$ meets both $X$ and
$X'$; then some $y\in S\cap X$ and $y'\in S\cap X'$ are at distance $D$, so
both $\varDelta(X,X')$ and $\varDelta(X',X)$ are at least $b_*\nu_se^{
-2\alpha_G(D-2s-9)}\ge J$. (i) The linear part has no second differences,
and the second difference of $J\prod_y\sigma_y$ between two sets is $J$
times the product of the differences of the two partial products and of
the fixed labels of the rest of $S$, so its modulus is at most $J$, and it
vanishes unless both sets meet $S$; then $t\le D$. (ii) The mixed
difference of order $k\ge2$ of the linear part vanishes, and that of
$J\prod_y\sigma_y$ is $J$. (iii) A closed walk around a tree of length
$\lambda$ that starts at a block of $S$ and traverses each edge twice has
length $2\lambda$ and visits every block of $S$. Cut it at the first visits of the $k$ blocks of $S$: it
falls into $k$ walks, each between two distinct blocks of $S$, so each of
length at least $D$, and $2\lambda\ge kD$. For the last assertion,
$J>C_0C^ke^{-\alpha_GkD}$ is the inequality stated, and
$\ell\ge kD/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[the layer bound and third cumulants]
\label{prop:layerthird}
Let $\alpha>0$, $D>0$, and give three sites $1,2,3$ the distances
$d(i,j)=D$ for $i\ne j$. For $x\in\R^3$ let $\mu_x$ be the probability
measure on $\R^3$ with density proportional to $e^{-U(z;x)}$,
\[
U(z;x)=\tfrac12\lvert z\rvert^2+J\sin z_1\sin z_2\sin z_3-x\cdot z,\qquad
J=\tfrac16e^{-\alpha D},
\]
and let $K(x)=\int e^{-U(z;x)}\,dz$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item for every $x$, every $\varphi$ with $\lvert\varphi(i)-\varphi(j)
\rvert\le d(i,j)$ and all smooth $F,H$ with bounded derivatives,
\[
\lvert\Cov_{\mu_x}(F,H)\rvert\le2\,\bigl\lVert e^{-\alpha\varphi}\nabla
F\bigr\rVert_{L^2(\mu_x)}\bigl\lVert e^{\alpha\varphi}\nabla H
\bigr\rVert_{L^2(\mu_x)},
\]
which is~\eqref{eq:layerbound} with $\mathcal A=2$ and the rate $\alpha$;
\item $\lvert\partial_{x_i}\partial_{x_j}\log K(x)\rvert=\lvert\Cov_{\mu_x}
(z_i,z_j)\rvert\le2e^{-\alpha D}$ for $i\ne j$ and every $x$;
\item $\partial_{x_1}\partial_{x_2}\partial_{x_3}\log K(0)$ is the third
cumulant of $z_1,z_2,z_3$ under $\mu_0$, of modulus at least
$\frac1{30}e^{-\alpha D}$, while every tree joining the three sites has
length at least $\frac32D$.
\end{enumerate}
So~\eqref{eq:layerbound}, at every $x$ and with the second derivatives of
$\log K$ decaying at the rate $\alpha$, gives no bound $Ce^{-\alpha\ell}$
on the third derivatives, with $\ell$ the length of the shortest joining
tree: here $C\ge\frac1{30}e^{\alpha D/2}$ for every $D$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Write $\operatorname{Hess}_zU=I+JM$, where the entries of $M$ are
$-\sin z_1\sin z_2\sin z_3$ on the diagonal and $\cos z_i\cos z_j\sin z_k$
off it, all of modulus at most one. With $w=e^{\alpha\varphi}$ the entries
of $wMw^{-1}$ have modulus at most $e^{\alpha D}$, so $\lVert J\,wMw^{-1}
\rVert\le3Je^{\alpha D}=\frac12$, and the same holds for $M$. The
potential is smooth with bounded derivatives of order at least two and
$\operatorname{Hess}_zU\ge\frac12$, and the weighted Helffer--Sj\"ostrand
representation in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(ii) applies:
$\operatorname{Re}\langle u,\mathcal A_wu\rangle\ge(1-\frac12)\lVert u
\rVert^2$, so $\lVert\mathcal A_w^{-1}\rVert\le2$ and (i) follows.
(ii) $\log K(x)-\log K(0)=\log\E_{\mu_0}e^{x\cdot z}$, so the derivatives of
$\log K$ are the joint cumulants of $z$ under $\mu_x$; the second ones are
covariances, and (i) with $F=z_i$, $H=z_j$ and $\varphi=-d(\cdot,i)$
gives $2e^{-\alpha D}$.
(iii) $U(\cdot;0)$ is invariant under $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(-z_1,-z_2)$ and
$(z_1,z_3)\mapsto(-z_1,-z_3)$, so $\E_{\mu_0}z_i=0$ and the third cumulant
is $\E_{\mu_0}z_1z_2z_3$. Let $\gamma_1$ be the standard Gaussian measure
on $\R$, $a_n=\int t\sin^nt\,d\gamma_1$ and $b_n=\int\sin^nt\,d\gamma_1$.
Expanding $e^{-J\sin z_1\sin z_2\sin z_3}$, which is legitimate since the
product is bounded,
\[
\E_{\mu_0}z_1z_2z_3=\frac{\sum_n(-J)^na_n^3/n!}{\sum_n(-J)^nb_n^3/n!} .
\]
By parity $a_n=0$ for even $n$ and $b_n=0$ for odd $n$; $b_0=1$ and
$b_n\ge0$; $\lvert a_n\rvert\le\int t^2d\gamma_1=1$ for $n\ge1$, since
$\lvert\sin t\rvert\le\min\{1,\lvert t\rvert\}$; and $a_1=\int\cos t\,
d\gamma_1=e^{-1/2}$ by Gaussian integration by parts. So the numerator has
modulus at least $Je^{-3/2}-(\sinh J-J)$ and the denominator lies in
$[1,\cosh J]$. As $(2i+1)!\ge6\,(2i-2)!$, $\sinh J-J\le\frac{J^3}6\cosh J$,
and with $J\le\frac16$, $\cosh J<1.014$ and $e^{-3/2}>0.2231$, as $e^{3/2}
<2.71829\cdot1.64873<4.482$,
\[
\lvert\E_{\mu_0}z_1z_2z_3\rvert\ge\frac{J(0.2231-0.0047)}{1.014}>
\frac J5=\frac{e^{-\alpha D}}{30}.
\]
The bound on trees is Proposition~\ref{prop:pairsonly}(iii) with $k=3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:treeform}
The tree form of the differences of order three and more is therefore
not proved, and Propositions~\ref{prop:pairsonly} and~\ref{prop:layerthird}
locate what it needs. In the law of Proposition~\ref{prop:layerthird} the
third cumulant is carried by the term $J\sin z_1\sin z_2\sin z_3$, whose
mixed third derivative couples three sites at mutual distance $D$ with
size $e^{-\alpha D}$. The differences of order three of $\log\tilde K$ are
third cumulants of the layer law (Remark~\ref{rem:labelcovopen}), and a
proof of their tree form needs two inputs that~\eqref{eq:layerbound} does
not contain: a bound in tree form on the mixed derivatives of order three
of $\mathcal U$ in the coordinates $z$ and in the island coordinates, and
a weighted representation of the third cumulants of $\mu_{x,y}$ through
the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand operator and these derivatives, valid on the box
$D_z$ with its walls. The proof of~\eqref{eq:layerbound} reaches the walls
through the approximations $H_n$ of the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(ii), whose derivatives of order three grow
with $n$, so that argument gives no bound on third cumulants uniform in
$n$. With both inputs the
differences of $\log\tilde K$ would still have to be carried to those of
$\log Z^c$ through the island weights, and uniformity in the coarse field
stays excluded by Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(i).
\end{remark}

For a fixed coarse field $c$ the blocks that are bad for every labelling
are the corners of the coarse plaquettes with $\delta(c_P,I)>\eta$. On them
no label restricts the active links, and $\mu^c$ there is the constrained
law of Sec.~\ref{ssec:smallfibres}, with the links outside as exterior. The
rest of this subsection determines what the chart estimates of that section
give for this law, in the $\SU(2)$ model and not in the class
$(\mathrm X)+(\mathrm R)$: a component on which the coarse field stays below
the scale of the chart is crossed at the rate $\alpha_G$, with no cost in
its length beyond the mass of the constrained law off the chart, and that
mass tends to one as the length grows at fixed $\beta_W$; above four times
the chart threshold of the coarse curvature no point of the fibre carries
a chart. The
mass off the chart is a ratio of two weights of the fibre, and the next
lemma records why its denominator has to be controlled.

\begin{lemma}[conditioned weights]\label{lem:condweights}
Let $\gamma$ be a finite measure, $D$, $G$, $T$ measurable sets with
$T\cap G=\emptyset$, $V$ a real function on $D$ that is bounded above on
$G\cap D$ and below on $T\cap D$, and $\nu=e^{-V}\mathbf 1_D\,\gamma$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $\gamma(G^c)\le\delta<\gamma(D)$, then $\nu(G)>0$ and
\[
\frac{\nu(T)}{\nu(G)}\le e^{\sup_{G\cap D}V-\inf_{T\cap D}V}\,
\frac{\delta}{\gamma(D)-\delta}.
\]
\item If $\gamma$ has no atoms, $\gamma(G)>0$ and $T=G^c$ with
$\gamma(T)>0$, then for every $M$ there is $D\supset T$ with
$\nu(T)/\nu(G)\ge M$ at $V=0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) The two weights obey
\begin{gather*}
\nu(T)\le e^{-\inf_{T\cap D}V}\gamma(T\cap D)\le e^{-\inf_{T\cap D}V}
\gamma(G^c),\\
\nu(G)\ge e^{-\sup_{G\cap D}V}\gamma(G\cap D)\ge e^{-\sup_{G\cap D}V}
\bigl(\gamma(D)-\gamma(G^c)\bigr),
\end{gather*}
and the last factor is positive. (ii) An
atomless measure takes every value between $0$ and $\gamma(G)$ on subsets
of $G$; take $D=T\cup G_\varepsilon$ with $G_\varepsilon\subset G$ and
$\gamma(G_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon=\gamma(T)/M$. Then $\nu(T)/\nu(G)=
\gamma(T)/\varepsilon=M$.
\end{proof}

A tail bound, the factor $e^{\sup V-\inf V}\delta$, therefore controls a
conditioned probability only together with a lower bound on the mass
$\gamma(D)$ of the conditioning set. For the fibres of the path map this
mass is computed: the reference measure is product Haar measure on
$G^{45\mathcal B}$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:pathZ} bounds $Z_\lambda(v)$ from
both sides. For the fibres of the cut-off average the reference measure
carries the coarea weights $\lvert\det D_gV\rvert^{-1}$, and these are not
bounded: in Proposition~\ref{prop:fold} the weights of the branches
$g_\pm(\lambda)$ tend to infinity as $\lambda\downarrow\gamma^*$ while the
Wilson action of every branch lies in $[0,12]$, and the law of the path
link tends to $\delta_{g^*}$ for every $\beta_W$. So no bound on the
conditioned probability of a branch in terms of the action alone holds
uniformly in the coarse field.

For $\SU(2)$ the constant $4+28\pi$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}
improves to $4$, up to a term of second order.

\begin{lemma}[the sharp witness]\label{lem:coarsewitnesssharp}
Let $G=\SU(2)$. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness},
\[
\delta(c_P,I)\le4\kappa+7700\kappa^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Three facts about $\SU(2)$ with the Hilbert--Schmidt norm are used.

(a) For $X,Y\in\g$, $\delta(e^Xe^Y,e^{X+Y})\le\lVert X\rVert\lVert Y
\rVert$. Indeed, with $g(t)=e^{-t(X+Y)}e^{tX}e^{tY}$, $g'(t)=e^{-t(X+Y)}
[e^{tX},Y]e^{tY}$ and $[e^{tX},Y]=\int_0^te^{uX}[X,Y]e^{(t-u)X}\,du$, so
$\lVert g'(t)\rVert\le t\lVert[X,Y]\rVert\le2t\lVert X\rVert\lVert Y
\rVert$, and $\delta(e^Xe^Y,e^{X+Y})=\delta(g(1),I)\le\int_0^1\lVert g'
\rVert$. Applying this three times, with bi-invariance of $\delta$ and the
triangle inequality,
\[
\delta\bigl(e^{X_1}e^{X_2}e^{X_3}e^{X_4},e^{X_1+X_2+X_3+X_4}\bigr)\le
\sum_{i<j}\lVert X_i\rVert\lVert X_j\rVert .
\]

(b) If $\delta(g,I)\le1$, then $\lVert\log g\rVert\le\delta(g,I)(1+\delta(g,
I)^2)$. Let $e^{\pm i\psi}$, $0\le\psi\le\pi$, be the eigenvalues of $g$ and
$t=\psi/2$. Then $\lVert\log g\rVert=2\sqrt2\,t$, $\delta(g,I)=2\sqrt2\sin
t$, and $\delta(g,I)\le1$ gives $t<\pi/2$. Since $t-\sin t\le t^3/6$ and
$t\le\frac\pi2\sin t$, $t\le\sin t+\frac{\pi^3}{48}\sin^3t\le\sin t\,(1+8
\sin^2t)$.

(c) If $X\in\g$ and $\lVert X\rVert<\sqrt2\pi$, then $\log e^X=X$, as the
eigenvalues $\pm i\psi$ of $X$ have $\sqrt2\psi=\lVert X\rVert<\sqrt2\pi$;
and $\delta(e^X,I)\le\lVert X\rVert$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}.

Let the sides $k=1,\dots,4$ of $P$ be the pairs $(y,\mu)$, $(y+e_\mu,\nu)$,
$(y+e_\nu,\mu)$, $(y,\nu)$, with path links $\ell_k$, and for $x\in B(y)$
let $P^k_x$ be the path of the pair $k$ from $x+o_k$, where $o_1=o_4=0$,
$o_2=2e_\mu$, $o_3=2e_\nu$. As in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}, $\delta(P^k_x,\ell_k)\le24\kappa<\frac12$,
so the cut-off of each side equals one, $Z^x_k=\log(\ell_k^{-1}P^k_x)$ is
defined, and by (b) $\lVert Z^x_k\rVert\le24\kappa(1+576\kappa^2)\le a=
24.001\kappa$. Then $c_k=\ell_ke^{\bar Z_k}$ with $\bar Z_k=\frac1{16}
\sum_xZ^x_k$ and $\lVert\bar Z_k\rVert\le a$.

The loop $H_x=P^1_xP^2_x(P^3_x)^{-1}(P^4_x)^{-1}$ is the holonomy around
the square of side two at $x$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, whose four fine
plaquettes have their vertices in the four corner blocks; as in the proof
of Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}, $\delta(H_x,I)\le4\kappa$. At $x=2y$ every
$P^k_x$ is $\ell_k$, so $\ell_P=\ell_1\ell_2\ell_3^{-1}\ell_4^{-1}=H_{2y}$
has $\delta(\ell_P,I)\le4\kappa$, and $Y=\log\ell_P$ has $\lVert Y\rVert\le
4.001\kappa$ by (b).

Let $g_1=\ell_1$, $g_2=\ell_1\ell_2$, $g_3=\ell_1\ell_2\ell_3^{-1}$, and for
$Z\in\g^4$
\begin{gather*}
\Psi(Z)=\ell_1e^{Z_1}\ell_2e^{Z_2}e^{-Z_3}\ell_3^{-1}e^{-Z_4}\ell_4^{-1},\\
\mathsf L(Z)=\operatorname{Ad}(g_1)Z_1+\operatorname{Ad}(g_2)(Z_2-Z_3)-
\operatorname{Ad}(g_3)Z_4 .
\end{gather*}
Moving the $\ell_k$ to the right,
\[
\Psi(Z)=e^{\operatorname{Ad}(g_1)Z_1}e^{\operatorname{Ad}(g_2)Z_2}e^{-
\operatorname{Ad}(g_2)Z_3}e^{-\operatorname{Ad}(g_3)Z_4}\ell_P,
\]
and $H_x=\Psi(Z^x)$, $c_P=\Psi(\bar Z)$.
The maps $\operatorname{Ad}(g_i)$ are isometries, so by (a), for $Z$ with
$\lVert Z_k\rVert\le a$,
\begin{gather*}
\delta\bigl(\Psi(Z),e^{\mathsf L(Z)}\ell_P\bigr)\le6a^2\le3457\kappa^2,\\
\delta\bigl(e^{\mathsf L(Z)}\ell_P,e^{\mathsf L(Z)+Y}\bigr)\le4a\cdot4.001
\kappa\le385\kappa^2 .
\end{gather*}
For every $x$ this gives $\delta(e^{\mathsf L(Z^x)+Y},I)\le4\kappa+3842
\kappa^2$; as $\lVert\mathsf L(Z^x)+Y\rVert\le4a+4.001\kappa<\sqrt2\pi$,
(c) and (b) give $\lVert\mathsf L(Z^x)+Y\rVert\le4\kappa+3843\kappa^2$,
since $(4\kappa+3842\kappa^2)^3\le\kappa^2$. The average over $x$ is
$\mathsf L(\bar Z)+Y$, so $\delta(e^{\mathsf L(\bar Z)+Y},I)\le\lVert
\mathsf L(\bar Z)+Y\rVert\le4\kappa+3843\kappa^2$, and
\[
\delta(c_P,I)\le(3457+385)\kappa^2+4\kappa+3843\kappa^2=4\kappa+7685
\kappa^2 .\qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

Proposition~\ref{prop:uniformflux} below shows that the constant $4$
cannot be lowered.

\begin{proposition}[coarse curvature and the chart]\label{prop:badchart}
Let $G=\SU(2)$ and let $c$ be a coarse field.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $V^\sharp(R(c))=c$. A plaquette $p$ of $R(c)$ in the plane
$\{\mu,\nu\}$ has $R(c)_p=I$ unless both coordinates $\mu$ and $\nu$ of
its corner are odd; then its corner lies in a block $y$ and $R(c)_p=c_P$,
with $P$ the coarse plaquette at $y$ in that plane.
\item Let $W$ be a set of blocks that contains the four corner blocks of
a coarse plaquette $P$ with $\delta(c_P,I)>2.418\cdot10^{-12}$. Then every
field $U$ with $V^\sharp_k(U)=c_k$ for the four sides $k$ of $P$ has a
plaquette with a vertex in a block of $W^+$ and $\delta(U_p,I)>6.044\cdot
10^{-13}$. Consequently no background $U$ of the fibre over $W$ satisfies
the hypothesis $4\cdot10^5c_3(\kappa+s)\le\frac1{195}$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}\textup{(iv)} with the constant $c_3=1.5\cdot
10^4\sqrt2$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants}, for any $s\ge0$,
and Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart}\textup{(iv)} and~\ref{thm:chartdecay}
apply at no point of that fibre.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Every path of the pair $k$ is the product of a link inside a block,
equal to $I$, and a private link of $k$, equal to $c_k$, so every path and
the path link equal $c_k$; in the formula $c_k=\ell_k\exp(\chi N)$ of the
proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound} every logarithm in $N$ vanishes, so
$V^\sharp_k(R(c))=c_k$. Let $p$ have corner $x$ and links $(x,\mu)$,
$(x+e_\mu,\nu)$, $(x+e_\nu,\mu)$, $(x,\nu)$. A link $(z,\mu)$ of $R(c)$ is
$I$ when $z_\mu$ is even, since it lies inside a block, and is $c_{y',\mu}$
when $z_\mu$ is odd, $y'$ the block of $z$. If $x_\mu$ is even, both
$\mu$-links of $p$ are $I$, and the two $\nu$-links start at $x$ and
$x+e_\mu$, which lie in one block and have the same coordinate $\nu$, so
they are equal and $R(c)_p=I$; likewise if $x_\nu$ is even. If both are
odd and $x\in B(y)$, the four links are $c_{y,\mu}$, $c_{y+e_\mu,\nu}$,
$c_{y+e_\nu,\mu}$, $c_{y,\nu}$, since $x+e_\mu\in B(y+e_\mu)$ and $x+e_\nu
\in B(y+e_\nu)$, and their product is $c_P$.

(ii) Put $\kappa=6.044\cdot10^{-13}\le10^{-8}$. If every plaquette with a
vertex in one of the blocks at distance at most one from the four corner
blocks had $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$, Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp}
would give $\delta(c_P,I)\le4\kappa+7700\kappa^2<2.4177\cdot10^{-12}$, as
$4\kappa=2.4176\cdot10^{-12}$ and $7700\kappa^2<3\cdot10^{-21}$. Those
blocks lie in $W^+$. A background with plaquettes up to $\kappa'>\kappa$ on
$W^+$ has $4\cdot10^5c_3\kappa'>4\cdot10^5c_3\kappa>\frac1{195}$, since
$195\cdot4\cdot10^5\cdot1.5\cdot10^4\sqrt2>1.6546\cdot10^{12}$ gives
$1/(195\cdot4\cdot10^5c_3)<6.044\cdot10^{-13}$.
\end{proof}

At $\rho=2.17\cdot10^{-16}$, $\eta=92\rho<2.0\cdot10^{-14}$. So the coarse
plaquettes that make a block bad for every labelling range over three
scales: up to $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, thirty times $\eta$, part (i) gives a
background with plaquettes below the chart threshold of
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} whenever the exterior near the
window agrees with $R(c)$; above $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$, part (ii) excludes
every background; in between, Proposition~\ref{prop:uniformflux} gives
backgrounds for some exteriors, and Proposition~\ref{prop:spread} gives
them for the exterior $R(c)$ of the coarse fields $c^\theta$ up to
$2.39\cdot10^{-12}$. Where a background exists, the constrained law of the
component decays across it at the rate
of the chart.

\begin{theorem}[a bad component on the chart]\label{thm:badcross}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\beta_W\ge2.3\cdot10^{17}$, let $W$ be a set of blocks
and $U$ a field with $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every plaquette with a
vertex in a block of $W^+$, and let $s>0$ with $s\le1/(6000c_3)$,
$\kappa+6s\le10^{-8}$ and $\kappa+s\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$. Let $\mu_W$ be the
constrained law on the fibre $F$ of $U$ over $W$, $r=s/32$, $\Phi$ and
$\Omega_r$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, and
\[
p=\mu_W\bigl(F\setminus\Phi(\Omega_r)\bigr).
\]
For sets $X_1,X_2\subset A_W$ and bounded smooth functions $\tilde F$,
$\tilde G$ of the links of $X_1$ and of $X_2$ whose left-invariant
gradients have norm at most $1$ in each link,
\begin{multline*}
\bigl\lvert\Cov_{\mu_W}(\tilde F,\tilde G)\bigr\rvert\le\frac{4.8\cdot
10^4}{\beta_W}\bigl(\lvert X_1\rvert\lvert X_2\rvert\bigr)^{1/2}e^{-\alpha_G
d(X_1,X_2)}\\
+6p\,\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert_\infty,
\end{multline*}
with $\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$ and $d$ the distance of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}. The bound does not depend on $W$, on the
exterior or on the coarse field beyond $\kappa$ and $p$, and the labels of
the blocks of $W$ enter neither its hypotheses nor the bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypotheses are those of Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}\textup{(iv)}: by
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants}, $\kappa+s\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$
gives $4\cdot10^5c_3(\kappa+s)\le\frac1{195}$, and $\lambda=\beta_W/4\ge
5.6\cdot10^{16}\ge60c_6$. Let $A=\Phi(\Omega_r)$ and $\mu_A=\mu_W(\cdot\mid
A)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}\textup{(iii)} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}, $\lvert\Cov_{\mu_A}(\tilde F,\tilde
G)\rvert$ is at most the first term, as $c_9/\lambda=4.8\cdot10^4/\beta_W$.
If $p=0$ this is the claim, and if $p=1$ the claim follows from
$\lvert\Cov\rvert\le\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert
_\infty$. Otherwise, with $\mu_{A^c}=\mu_W(\cdot\mid F\setminus A)$ and
$\mu_W=(1-p)\mu_A+p\mu_{A^c}$,
\[
\begin{split}
\Cov_{\mu_W}(\tilde F,\tilde G)={}&(1-p)\Cov_{\mu_A}(\tilde F,\tilde G)+
p\Cov_{\mu_{A^c}}(\tilde F,\tilde G)\\
&+p(1-p)\bigl(\mu_A\tilde F-\mu_{A^c}\tilde F\bigr)\bigl(\mu_A\tilde G-
\mu_{A^c}\tilde G\bigr),
\end{split}
\]
so the difference from $\Cov_{\mu_A}$ is at most $p\lVert\tilde F\rVert
_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert_\infty$ twice, from the first two terms, plus
$4p\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert_\infty$. Nothing in
Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart} and~\ref{thm:chartdecay} refers to the labels
of the blocks of $W$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:badcompopen}
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} bounds the response inside a bad component by
the chart, with no cost growing with its length except through $p$, and
leaves three things.
First, the mass $p$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:condweights} it is bounded by the
excess action off the chart times the reference mass off the chart,
divided by the reference mass of the chart in the fibre; the first factor
is a Peierls bound, the reference masses carry the coarea weights, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:fold} shows that these weights are not controlled by
the action. In the other direction Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass} bounds
$p$ from below: at fixed $\beta_W$ it tends to one as the component grows,
and it exceeds $1-e^{-5.5\lvert W\rvert}$ for $\beta_W\le10^{24}$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:offchartmass}). In the mean over the coarse field $\E_c$ the mass off the chart
is a probability under $\mu_L$; for a fixed coarse field it is the open
step of Remark~\ref{rem:smallfibreopen}(c) and Remark~\ref{rem:fibrechartopen}(a).
Second, the coarse fields above $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$, where by
Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}(ii) the chart applies at no point; there
the fibre law near the component is that of a large field, which
Proposition~\ref{prop:fold} shows to jump, and no estimate of this paper
bounds its response. A bound uniform in the coarse field needs that
regime. Third, the passage from $\mu_W$ to $\mu^c$ and to the labels. Under
$\mu^c$, given the links outside $A_W$, the averages of the pairs that
enter $W$ from outside are fixed as well, and they bind links of $A_W$;
and the labels adjoining a component are functions of links outside its
interior, so that their covariance across it is the cross-ratio of the
weight of the interior as a function of its two ends. For a good layer
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation} solves the path links of the entering
pairs by Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}, writes the weight through a kernel
on a domain that the ends do not move, and Lemma~\ref{lem:connected}
turns the cross-ratio into a covariance of the layer law. Both steps use
non-path links within $r$ of the reconstruction. For a bad component
Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage} moves the links that bind the entering
averages to the exterior, so that the constrained law of the reduced fibre
is the conditional law under $\mu^c$, and Corollary~\ref{cor:badcrossratio}
bounds the cross-ratio for ends that enter the action only; ends that
enter the averages, on which the labels depend, are not treated
(Remark~\ref{rem:badmassopen}).

The other two routes do not reach the interior of a component. A
single-link Dobrushin or disagreement-percolation bound needs row sums
below one, while the coefficient of Lemma~\ref{lem:fixedset} is
$\frac{\pi^2}8\beta_W$ for each link that shares a plaquette with the given
one, and on
the fibre the Kantorovich response of the path-link law to its non-path
links is infinite by Proposition~\ref{prop:fold}\textup{(iv)}; blocks
large enough to contract must carry the constraints of the cut-off
average, which is the chart of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross}. The tree form of
the mixed differences of $\log Z^c$ asked for in
Remark~\ref{rem:labelcovopen} concerns the labels of distinct components,
which are separated by good layers; a component bad for every labelling
lies inside one component together with the blocks it adjoins, so neither
that bound nor a cluster expansion built on it reaches the response across
