it. In the law of Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction}(i) the second
difference over the labels of $a$ and $b$, all other labels fixed, is $J$,
and a bound on it decaying with $\dist(a,b)$ is exactly the response
across the component.
\end{remark}

The bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} contains the mass $p$ of the
constrained law off the product chart $\Phi(\Omega_r)$, and that chart asks
every one of the $45\lvert W\rvert$ coordinates $\eta_e$, $e\in L'$, to lie
in a ball of radius $r$. On the chart the law has a density whose Hessian
is bounded above, so each coordinate leaves its ball with a conditional
probability bounded below, and $p$ grows with $\lvert W\rvert$. The next
lemma is the elementary estimate behind this.

\begin{lemma}[leaving a ball]\label{lem:ballexit}
Let $E$ be a Euclidean space, $r>0$, $B_t=\{x\in E:\lvert x\rvert\le t\}$,
and let $f$ be a real function of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of
$B_{2r}$ with $\lVert\Hess f(x)\rVert\le\Lambda$ for $x\in B_{2r}$. Then
\[
\int_{B_{2r}\setminus B_r}e^{-f}\,dx\ge\frac13e^{-5.5\Lambda r^2}
\int_{B_{2r}}e^{-f}\,dx .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose a unit vector $u$ with $\nabla f(0)\cdot u\le0$. For $x\in B_{2r}$,
$\nabla f(x)\cdot u\le\nabla f(0)\cdot u+\Lambda\lvert x\rvert\le\Lambda
\lvert x\rvert$, and for $x,x+v\in B_{2r}$, the segment between them lying
in the convex set $B_{2r}$, $f(x+v)\le f(x)+\nabla f(x)\cdot v+\frac12
\Lambda\lvert v\rvert^2$. Put $O=B_{2r}\setminus B_r$, $S_+=\{x\in B_r:x
\cdot u\ge0\}$ and $S_-=B_r\setminus S_+$.

For $x\in S_+$, $\lvert x+ru\rvert^2=\lvert x\rvert^2+2r\,x\cdot u+r^2$
lies in $[r^2,4r^2]$ and exceeds $r^2$ unless $x=0$, so the translation
$x\mapsto x+ru$ maps $S_+$ into $O$ up to a null set, and
$f(x+ru)\le f(x)+r\Lambda\lvert x\rvert+\frac12\Lambda r^2\le f(x)+
1.5\Lambda r^2$. Hence $\int_Oe^{-f}\ge e^{-1.5\Lambda r^2}\int_{S_+}
e^{-f}$. The reflection $R(x)=x-2(x\cdot u)u$ maps $S_-$ into $S_+$ and
preserves Lebesgue measure; for $x\in S_-$, $R(x)=x+tu$ with $t=2\lvert x
\cdot u\rvert\le2r$, so $f(R(x))\le f(x)+t\Lambda r+\frac12\Lambda t^2\le
f(x)+4\Lambda r^2$, and $\int_{S_+}e^{-f}\ge e^{-4\Lambda r^2}\int_{S_-}
e^{-f}$. Therefore
\[
\int_{B_r}e^{-f}\le\bigl(1+e^{4\Lambda r^2}\bigr)e^{1.5\Lambda r^2}
\int_Oe^{-f},
\]
and $\int_Oe^{-f}\big/\int_{B_{2r}}e^{-f}\ge(1+e^{1.5\Lambda r^2}+e^{5.5
\Lambda r^2})^{-1}\ge\frac13e^{-5.5\Lambda r^2}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[the mass off the chart]\label{thm:offchartmass}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross},
\begin{align*}
p&\ge1-\Bigl(1-\frac13e^{-2843.5\beta_Wr^2}\Bigr)^{45\lvert W\rvert}\\
&\ge1-\exp\bigl(-15\lvert W\rvert e^{-10^{-24}\beta_W}\bigr).
\end{align*}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $\mathrm{Box}_t$ for the product over $e\in L'$ of the balls
$\{\lVert\xi_e\rVert\le t\}$ in $\g$, so that $\Omega_t=S(\mathrm{Box}_t)$
in the notation of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}. Since $S(
\mathrm{Box}_{2r})\subset K_{30.2r}$ and $30.2r<s$, the paragraph on the
density in that proof, which uses Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart}\textup{(iii)}
on $K_s$ only, shows that the constrained law $\mu_W$ conditioned on $\Phi(
\Omega_{2r})$ has, in the coordinates $\xi\in\g^{L'}$, the density
proportional to $e^{-\bar H}$ on $\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$, with $\bar H$ smooth on
the preimage under $S$ of the interior of $K_s$, a neighbourhood of
$\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:weightednorms}\textup{(i)}, $\lVert\Hess\bar H\rVert\le
\lVert\Hess\bar H\rVert_{(\vartheta)}\le2068\lambda$ on $\mathrm{Box}_{2r}$,
with $\lambda=\beta_W/4$.

Let $a=\mu_W(\Phi(\Omega_{2r}))$. If $a=0$, then $p=1$. Otherwise let $\nu$
be the conditioned law in the coordinates $\xi$, enumerate $L'=\{e_1,\dots,
e_N\}$ with $N=45\lvert W\rvert$, and let $A_i=\{\lVert\xi_{e_i}\rVert\le
r\}$. Under $\nu$, given the coordinates other than $\xi_{e_i}$, the
coordinate $\xi_{e_i}$ has the density proportional to $e^{-f}$ on the
ball of radius $2r$ in $\g$, where $f$ is $\bar H$ with the other
coordinates fixed and $\lVert\Hess f\rVert\le2068\lambda$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:ballexit} with $\Lambda=2068\lambda$, the conditional
probability of $A_i$ is at most $1-q_0$, with
\[
q_0=\tfrac13e^{-5.5\cdot2068\lambda r^2}=\tfrac13e^{-2843.5\beta_Wr^2}.
\]
The events $A_{i+1},\dots,A_N$ are functions of the other coordinates, so
$\nu(A_i\cap\dots\cap A_N)\le(1-q_0)\,\nu(A_{i+1}\cap\dots\cap A_N)$, and by
induction $\nu(\mathrm{Box}_r)\le(1-q_0)^N$. As $\Phi$ is injective,
$\mu_W(\Phi(\Omega_r))=a\,\nu(\mathrm{Box}_r)\le(1-q_0)^N$, which is the
first bound. For the second, $1-q\le e^{-q}$, and $\kappa+s\le6.0\cdot
10^{-13}$ gives $r\le1.875\cdot10^{-14}$, so $2843.5r^2<10^{-24}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:offchartmass}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item if $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, then $p\ge1-e^{-5.5\lvert W\rvert}$; at
$\beta_W=2.3\cdot10^{17}$, $p\ge1-e^{-14.99\lvert W\rvert}$;
\item the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} is smaller than the trivial
bound $\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert_\infty$ only if
$\beta_W>10^{24}(4.40+\ln\lvert W\rvert)$;
\item for fixed $\beta_W$, $p\to1$ as $\lvert W\rvert\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
(i) For $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, $q_0\ge\frac13e^{-1}>0.1226$ and $45q_0>5.5$;
at $\beta_W=2.3\cdot10^{17}$, $q_0\ge\frac13(1-2.3\cdot10^{-7})$ and
$45q_0>14.99$. Use $(1-q_0)^N\le e^{-Nq_0}$. (ii) The bound contains $6p
\lVert\tilde F\rVert_\infty\lVert\tilde G\rVert_\infty$, so it is smaller
than the trivial bound only if $p<\frac16$. Then $e^{-45\lvert W\rvert
q_0}\ge1-p>\frac56$, so $15\lvert W\rvert e^{-2843.5\beta_Wr^2}<\ln\frac65<
0.1824$; as $2843.5r^2<10^{-24}$, this gives $10^{-24}\beta_W>\ln(15
\lvert W\rvert/0.1824)>4.40+\ln\lvert W\rvert$. (iii) follows from the
second bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass}.
\end{proof}

Fig.~\ref{fig:offchartmass} draws the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass} and the couplings at which Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} improves on the trivial bound.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_offchartmass.png}
\caption{The mass off the chart in a bad component $W$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass}). (a)~The lower bound
$1-\exp(-15\lvert W\rvert e^{-10^{-24}\beta_W})$ on $p$ over
$\beta_W/10^{24}$ and $\log_{10}\lvert W\rvert$. (b)~The curve
$\beta_W=10^{24}(4.40+\ln\lvert W\rvert)$, above which the bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} improves on the trivial one, and the region in
which the lower bound on $p$ exceeds $\frac12$.}
\label{fig:offchartmass}
\end{figure*}

So the absence of a cost in the length in Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} is
carried entirely by $p$: a product chart in all the coordinates of the
component, which the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand argument of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} uses, holds the whole component near the
background, and a component of $n$ blocks leaves it unless $\beta_Wr^2$
exceeds a multiple of $\ln n$. With the constants of
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} the radius $r$ is at most
$1.875\cdot10^{-14}$, so the threshold $2.3\cdot10^{17}$ of the theorem is
seven orders of magnitude below the coupling at which $p$ can be small for
a single block. In the other direction Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres} gives
$p\le\varepsilon_W(K,\lambda)$ on every fibre through a field whose
plaquettes near $W$ are at most $K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$, with $s\ge1.24\cdot10^5K$,
which needs $\lambda K^2$ larger than a multiple of $\lvert W\rvert\ln(n_P/
K)$; the necessary condition grows like $\ln\lvert W\rvert$ and the
sufficient one like $\lvert W\rvert$.

The fibres to which the theorem applies include arbitrarily long bad
components, and their coarse plaquettes come arbitrarily close to four
times the bound $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ on $\kappa+s$, which by
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp} no such fibre exceeds by more than
$7700\kappa^2$. Let $T_0=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)\in\g$, so that
$\delta(e^{\theta T_0},I)=2\sqrt2\lvert\sin(\theta/2)\rvert$ for real
$\theta$.

\begin{proposition}[a uniform field strength]\label{prop:uniformflux}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, let the side $2L$ of the periodic lattice have $L\ge4$
even, let $\mu\ne\nu$ be two directions and $0<f\le7\cdot10^{-9}$. Let
$g(t)=f\min\{t,2L-t\}$ for $t\in\{0,\dots,2L-1\}=\Z/2L\Z$, so that $g(t+1)-
g(t)=f$ for $0\le t\le L-1$ and $g(t+1)-g(t)=-f$ for $L\le t\le2L-1$, let $U^f$ have the links $U^f_{x,\mu}=e^{-g(x_\nu)T_0}$ and
all other links $I$, and let $\tilde U$ be its image in the tree gauge
under the gauge transformation that equals $I$ at the corner of every
block. Put $\kappa_f=2\sqrt2\sin(f/2)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Every plaquette has $\delta(\tilde U_p,I)\le\kappa_f$.
\item The coarse field $c=V^\sharp(\tilde U)$ takes values in $\{e^{\theta
T_0}\}$, and for every block $y$ with $0\le y_\nu\le L/2-2$ the coarse
plaquette $P$ at $y$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ has $c_P=e^{4fT_0}$, so
that
\[
\delta(c_P,I)=2\sqrt2\sin2f=4\cos\tfrac f2\cos f\;\kappa_f\ge4(1-f^2)
\kappa_f .
\]
\item For every set $W$ of blocks the fibre of $\tilde U$ over $W$ satisfies
the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} with $U=\tilde U$ and $\kappa=
\kappa_f$, for every $\beta_W\ge2.3\cdot10^{17}$ and every $s>0$ with $s\le1/(6000c_3)$, $\kappa_f+6s\le
10^{-8}$ and $\kappa_f+s\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, for every $t\in(0,2.39\cdot10^{-12}]$ there are a coarse
field with a coarse plaquette $P$ of $\delta(c_P,I)=t$ and, for every $W$,
an exterior whose fibre over $W$ satisfies the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} with $s=2.4\cdot10^{-15}$; and the constant $4$
of Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp} cannot be lowered.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Every link of $U^f$ lies in the torus $\{e^{\theta T_0}\}$, and we give
it the real angle $\theta_{x,\mu}=-g(x_\nu)$, or $0$. The real sum of a
plaquette at $x$, $\theta_1+\theta_2-\theta_3-\theta_4$ in the notation of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:smallfibres}, is $g(x_\nu+1)-g(x_\nu)=\pm f$ in the plane
$\{\mu,\nu\}$, and $0$ in every other plane, since a plaquette in the plane
$\{\mu,\rho\}$, $\rho\ne\nu$, has its two $\mu$-links at the same
coordinate $\nu$. The gauge transformation is $e^{\lambda_xT_0}$ with
$\lambda_x$ real, $0$ at the corners, and fixed along the tree of each
block by the condition that the real angles $\tilde\theta_{x,\rho}=
\theta_{x,\rho}+\lambda_x-\lambda_{x+e_\rho}$ of the tree links vanish. The
real sums of the plaquettes do not change, so every plaquette of $\tilde U$
is $e^{\pm fT_0}$ or $I$.

(ii) Let $k$ be a pair, $v=P_{2y}$ its path link and $v_x=v^{-1}P_x$. By
(i) and Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(i), which applies as $\kappa_f\le\sqrt2
f\le10^{-8}$, $\delta(v_x,I)\le24\kappa_f<\frac12$, so the cut-off equals one, and $v_x=e^{\varphi_xT_0}$ with
$\varphi_x=\tilde\theta(P_x)-\tilde\theta(v)$, where $\tilde\theta$ of a
path is the sum of the real angles along it. The principal logarithm of
$v_x$ is $\varphi'_xT_0$ with $\varphi'_x\equiv\varphi_x$ modulo $2\pi$.
As functions of $f\in[0,7\cdot10^{-9}]$, $\varphi_x$ is linear, since
$g$ and the gauge transformation are, and $\varphi'_x$ is continuous, since
$v_x$ stays within $24\kappa_f<1$ of $I$, where the principal logarithm is
continuous; their difference lies in $2\pi\Z$ and vanishes at $f=0$, so
$\varphi'_x=\varphi_x$. Hence
\[
c_k=v\exp\Bigl(\frac1{16}\sum_x\varphi_xT_0\Bigr)=\exp\Bigl(\frac1{16}
\sum_x\tilde\theta(P_x)\,T_0\Bigr).
\]
With the sides $k=1,\dots,4$ of $P$ as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}(i) and the sites $x\in B(y)$, $x+2e_\mu$,
$x+2e_\nu$ of the same offset,
\[
c_P=\exp\Bigl(\frac1{16}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\tilde\theta(\partial S_x)\,T_0
\Bigr),
\]
where $\partial S_x$ is the boundary of the square of side two at $x$ in
the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$. Its real angle is the sum of the real sums of its
four plaquettes, whose coordinates $\nu$ lie in $\{2y_\nu,2y_\nu+1,2y_\nu+
2\}\subset\{0,\dots,L-1\}$, so each is $f$ and $c_P=e^{4fT_0}$. Finally
$\sin2f=4\sin\frac f2\cos\frac f2\cos f$, and $\cos\frac f2\cos f\ge(1-
\frac{f^2}8)(1-\frac{f^2}2)\ge1-f^2$.

(iii) $\tilde U$ lies in its own fibre and has every plaquette at most
$\kappa_f$; the other hypotheses are the conditions on $\beta_W$ and $s$.

For the last statement let $f=\frac12\arcsin(t/(2\sqrt2))$, so that $2\sqrt2
\sin2f=t$ and $f<4.3\cdot10^{-13}$. Then $\kappa_f\le t/(4(1-f^2))<5.976
\cdot10^{-13}$, so $s=2.4\cdot10^{-15}$ satisfies the conditions of (iii),
as $1/(6000c_3)>7.8\cdot10^{-9}$. By (ii) the ratio $\delta(c_P,I)/\kappa_f$
tends to $4$ as $f\to0$, while $\kappa_f\le10^{-8}$ and every plaquette of $\tilde U$ is at most
$\kappa_f$.
\end{proof}

The blocks with $0\le y_\nu\le L/2-1$ are corners of the coarse plaquettes
of (ii), which exceed $\eta$ once $2\sqrt2\sin2f>\eta$, so they lie in one
component bad for every labelling, of $L^4/2$ blocks. On these fibres
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} applies for every $\lvert W\rvert$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:offchartmass} shows that its bound loses its content as
$\lvert W\rvert$ grows.

Under $\mu^c$ the links of a window are not distributed by $\mu_W$: the
averages of the pairs that enter $W$ from outside are fixed too, and they
contain links of $A_W$. These links can be moved to the exterior. Let
$I_W$ be the set of active links $(x,\mu)$ inside a block $B(y)$, $y\in W$,
with $y-e_\mu\notin W$, let $A^-_W=A_W\setminus I_W$, $L'^-=A^-_W\setminus
\{d_k\}$, and for a field $U$ let $F^-$ be the set of fields that agree with
$U$ off $A^-_W$ and have the same averages $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ as $U$ for
$y\in W$. The measure $\nu^-_c$ on $F^-$ and the constrained law $\mu^-_W=
e^{-\lambda Q^-}\nu^-_c/\nu^-_c(e^{-\lambda Q^-})$, with $Q^-$ the sum of
$\delta(U_p,I)^2$ over the plaquettes that contain a link of $A^-_W$, are
defined as $\nu_c$ and $\mu_F$ before~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}, with the
links of $I_W$ among the fixed links.

\begin{proposition}[the window under $\mu^c$]\label{prop:badpassage}
Let $G=\SU(2)$ and let $W$ be a set of blocks.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Every average $V^\sharp_{y',\mu}$ with $y'\notin W$ is a function of
the links off $A^-_W$. For $\E_c$-almost every $c$, the constrained law
$\mu^-_W$ on the fibre through a field is a version of the conditional law
under $\mu^c$ of the links of $A^-_W$ given the links off $A^-_W$.
\item Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart}, \ref{thm:chartdecay},
\ref{thm:offchart}\textup{(i)}, \ref{thm:badcross} and~\ref{thm:offchartmass}
and Propositions~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} and~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}
hold for $F^-$, $A^-_W$ and $L'^-$ in place of $F$, $A_W$ and $L'$, with the
same constants, and with $45\lvert W\rvert$ replaced by $\lvert L'^-\rvert
\ge28\lvert W\rvert$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) An inside link $(x,\mu)$ of a block $B(y)$ enters only the averages of
$(y,\mu)$, as the first link of the path from $x$, and of $(y-e_\mu,\mu)$,
as the second link of the path from $x-e_\mu$; a private link enters only
the average of its pair. So $V^\sharp_{y',\mu}$, $y'\notin W$, depends on
the links of $B(y')$ and the private links of $(y',\mu)$, which are not in
$A_W$, and on inside links of $B(y'+e_\mu)$, which lie in $I_W$ when
$y'+e_\mu\in W$. In the tree gauge the active links have density
proportional to $e^{-\beta_WS}$ with respect to product Haar measure $h$
(proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(ii)). Write the active links as $(E,z)$
with $z$ the links of $A^-_W$, and $C=(C_{\rm out},C_W)$ for the averages
of the pairs based off and in $W$, so that $C_{\rm out}$ is a function of
$E$. The construction of~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}, with the links of $I_W$
fixed, gives $h(dz)=\int\nu^-_{E,c_W}(dz)\,dh(c_W)$, so
\[
e^{-\beta_WS}h(dE)\,h(dz)=e^{-\beta_WS}h(dE)\int\nu^-_{E,c_W}(dz)\,
dh(c_W),
\]
and the conditional law of $z$ given $(E,C_W)$ is proportional to
$e^{-\beta_WS}\nu^-_{E,C_W}$, which is $\mu^-_W$, the plaquettes without a
link of $A^-_W$ giving a factor that does not depend on $z$. Since $C_{\rm
out}$ is a function of $E$, conditioning on $(E,C)$ is conditioning on
$(E,C_W)$, and by the tower property this is the conditional law under
$\mu^c$ given $E$, for almost every $c$.

(ii) Let $J:\g^{A^-_W}\to\g^{A_W}$ be extension by zero. The fibre $F^-$
is $F$ with the links of $I_W$ fixed, so $\xi$ is tangent to $F^-$ exactly
when $J\xi$ is tangent to $F$, and on $F^-$ the difference $Q-Q^-$ depends
only on links off $A^-_W$ and is constant. The window enters the proofs of
the listed results only through the following objects, and each has a
counterpart on $F^-$ with the same bound.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The derivative $DC_k=\tilde B_k+R_k$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(iv), with $\lVert R_k\rVert\le260\kappa$; on
$F^-$ it is $DC_kJ=\tilde B_kJ+R_kJ$, and $\lVert R_kJ\rVert\le\lVert R_k
\rVert$, $\lVert\tilde B_kJ\rVert\le\lVert\tilde B_k\rVert$.
\item The Gram matrix $\mathcal G=DC\,DC^*$. Its diagonal blocks are at
least $\frac18-227\kappa$ because the squared coefficients of $V_{y,\mu}$
on the eight private links of $(y,\mu)$ add up to $\frac18$; these links
lie in $A^-_W$, so $\tilde B_kJJ^*\tilde B_k^*\ge\frac18$ and the
perturbation $2\lVert\tilde B_kJ\rVert\,260\kappa+(260\kappa)^2\le227\kappa$
is the same. The upper bounds $\frac3{16}+227\kappa$ on the diagonal blocks
and $\frac1{32}+227\kappa$ on the two off-diagonal blocks of a row bound
sums of the norms of the contributions of single links, which only lose
terms. So $\mathcal G^-=DC\,JJ^*DC^*$ has the block bounds from which the
proofs of Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrechart} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicitdecay} derive $\mathcal G\ge\frac1{16}-700
\kappa$, $\lVert\mathcal G^{-1}\rVert\le17$ and the weighted norms of
$\mathcal G^{-1}$.
\item The derivative bounds with the constants $c_3$ and $c_6$ for $c_k$,
$Q$ and $j$, and $A=Dc(X)$: on vectors supported on $A^-_W$ they hold as
before, and $AJ$, $DC\,J$ have the same block sparsity.
\item The section: $(S^-\xi)_e=\xi_e$ for $e\in L'^-$ and $(S^-\xi)_{d_k}=
-B_{k,d_k}^{-1}\sum_{e\in A^-_W\setminus\{d_k\}}B_{k,e}\xi_e$, that is
$JS^-=SJ$. The path link $d_k$ lies in $A^-_W$ and enters only $V_k$, and
the bound $15.1$ is a sum of norms over $e$ that only loses terms.
\end{enumerate}
The function $\bar H$ and the matrices $P$, $\bar P$ on $F^-$ are defined
by the same formulas from $AJ$, $DC\,J$ and $S^-$, and their bounds are
derived in those proofs from (a)--(d) by the same computations. The
distance $d$ on $L'^-$ is the restriction of that on $L'$. The proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:offchart}(i) applies to fields that agree off $A^-_W$,
since these agree off $A_W$. Since $DC\,J$ is onto by (b), $F^-$ has
codimension $4\lvert W\rvert\dim G$ and $\dim T_U=\lvert L'^-\rvert\dim G$.
The $28\lvert W\rvert$ private links other than the path links lie in
$L'^-$.
\end{proof}

The weight of the interior as a function of two ends follows, for ends
that enter only the action.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:badcrossratio}
Let $G=\SU(2)$ and let $E_a$, $E_b$ be disjoint sets of links off $A^-_W$,
none of which enters an average $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ with $y\in W$, such that
no plaquette contains a link of $E_a$ and a link of $E_b$. Fix the other
links off $A^-_W$, let $a_0,a_1\in G^{E_a}$, $b_0,b_1\in G^{E_b}$, $X_e,
Y_e\in\g$ with $a_{1,e}=a_{0,e}e^{X_e}$, $b_{1,e}=b_{0,e}e^{Y_e}$, and
$x_a=\max_e\lVert X_e\rVert$, $x_b=\max_e\lVert Y_e\rVert$. Let $Z_{ij}=
\nu^-_c(e^{-\lambda Q^-})$ on the fibre with the links $a_i$ on $E_a$ and
$b_j$ on $E_b$, and let $N_a$, $N_b$ be the links of $A^-_W$ that share a
plaquette with a link of $E_a$, of $E_b$. Suppose that at the links
$a_0e^{\sigma X}$, $b_0e^{\tau Y}$, for all $\sigma,\tau\in[0,1]$, the
fibre satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} with fixed
$\kappa$ and $s$, and let $\bar p$ bound its mass off the chart. Then
\begin{multline*}
\Bigl\lvert\log\frac{Z_{11}Z_{00}}{Z_{10}Z_{01}}\Bigr\rvert\le3.9\cdot10^6
\beta_Wx_ax_b\bigl(\lvert N_a\rvert\lvert N_b\rvert\bigr)^{1/2}e^{-\alpha_G
d(N_a,N_b)}\\
+432\,\beta_W^2\,\bar p\,\lvert E_a\rvert\lvert E_b\rvert x_ax_b .
\end{multline*}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Neither the fibre $F^-$ nor $\nu^-_c$ depends on the links of $E_a\cup
E_b$, since these enter no constraint, so $Z(\sigma,\tau)=\nu^-_c(e^{-
\lambda Q^-})$ at the links $a_0e^{\sigma X}$, $b_0e^{\tau Y}$ is an integral
over a fixed space, and differentiating under the integral,
$\partial_\sigma\partial_\tau\log Z=\Cov(\phi_a,\phi_b)$ under $\mu^-_W$,
with $\phi_a=\partial_\sigma\lambda Q^-$ and $\phi_b=\partial_\tau\lambda
Q^-$, because no plaquette contains links of both sets, so that
$\partial_\sigma\partial_\tau Q^-=0$. The function $\phi_a$ depends on the
links of $N_a$. For a plaquette $p$, $\delta(U_p,I)^2=4-2\ReTr U_p$; moving
a link $e$ of $p$ along $X_e$ inserts $X_e$ between unitary factors, and
$\ReTr(VX)=\ReTr((V-I)X)$ for skew-Hermitian $X$, so the derivative is at
most $2\delta(U_p,I)\lVert X_e\rVert$, and the mixed derivative along $X_e$
and along a unit vector at another link of $p$ is at most $2\lVert X_e
\rVert$. A link lies in six plaquettes, and a plaquette with a link of
$A^-_W$ has at most three links of $E_a$; so the left-invariant gradient of
$\phi_a$ has norm at most $6\cdot3\cdot2\lambda x_a=36\lambda x_a$ in each
link. As $\delta(U_p,I)\le2\sqrt2$, summing over the links $e\in E_a$ and
the six plaquettes through each gives $\lVert\phi_a\rVert_\infty\le6\lvert
E_a\rvert\cdot2\cdot2\sqrt2\,\lambda x_a=24\sqrt2\lambda\lvert E_a\rvert
x_a$, and likewise for $\phi_b$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}(ii), Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} applied
to $\phi_a/(36\lambda x_a)$ and $\phi_b/(36\lambda x_b)$ gives
\[
\begin{split}
\lvert\Cov(\phi_a,\phi_b)\rvert\le{}&\frac{4.8\cdot10^4}{\beta_W}(36
\lambda)^2x_ax_b\\
&\times\bigl(\lvert N_a\rvert\lvert N_b\rvert\bigr)^{1/2}e^{-\alpha_G
d(N_a,N_b)}\\
&+6\bar p\,(24\sqrt2\lambda)^2\lvert E_a\rvert\lvert E_b\rvert x_ax_b,
\end{split}
\]
and with $\lambda=\beta_W/4$ the two coefficients are $81\cdot4.8\cdot10^4
\beta_W=3.888\cdot10^6\beta_W$ and $6\cdot1152\beta_W^2/16=432\beta_W^2$. Integrate over $(\sigma,\tau)\in[0,1]^2$.
\end{proof}

The first term decays at the rate $\alpha_G$ in the distance between the
ends, with no cost in the length of $W$; the second needs $\bar p$ small
against $\beta_W^{-2}$, which by Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass} requires
$\beta_Wr^2$ larger than a multiple of $\ln\beta_W+\ln\lvert W\rvert$.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:badmassopen}
What remains of the bad regions in item (ii) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{The mass off the chart.} Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass} shows
that no bound on $p$ uniform in the length of the component exists, for
any coarse field and exterior to which Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} applies,
and that $p$ is close to one for $\beta_W\le10^{24}$. A bound on the
response across a component uniform in its length therefore cannot pass
through a single product chart of the whole component; it needs charts
local in the component, around which the links far from the observables
may leave the chart, that is a decomposition of the fibre into small-field
and large-field regions with a convex chart on each small-field region.
Theorem~\ref{thm:localcharts} shows that charts fixed by the exterior of
their window put the window on the chart with conditional probability at
most $0.033^{\lvert W\rvert}$ for $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, so that in such a
decomposition the large-field region carries most of the mass. For fixed
$\lvert W\rvert$, a bound on $p$
for a fixed coarse field is Corollary~\ref{cor:calmfibres}, whose
condition grows linearly in $\lvert W\rvert$, against the logarithmic
necessary condition of Corollary~\ref{cor:offchartmass}(ii).
\item \emph{Larger coarse fields.} Above $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ no field of
the fibre carries a chart (Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}(ii)). Between
$6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ the fibres of
Proposition~\ref{prop:uniformflux} carry backgrounds. For the exterior
$R(c)$, whose plaquettes carry each coarse plaquette in one fine plaquette,
a background would have to spread the coarse curvature over the plaquettes
of the window, almost aligned and almost of equal size as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp}, while matching $R(c)$ off $A_W$.
The exact condition is that the fibre over $W$ of a field agreeing with
$R(c)$ off $A_W$ contain a field $U$ with $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every
plaquette with a vertex in a block of $W^+$, for some $\kappa<6.0\cdot
10^{-13}$; under it Theorems~\ref{thm:badcross} and~\ref{thm:offchartmass}
apply with every $s\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}-\kappa$. It holds for the coarse
fields $c^\theta$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:spread} up to $2.39\cdot
10^{-12}$; for opposite fluxes at adjacent coarse plaquettes no field with
values in a torus satisfies it above $1.8\cdot10^{-12}$; for a general
coarse field it is not decided.
\item \emph{Ends in the averages.} Corollary~\ref{cor:badcrossratio} needs
ends that enter no average of a pair of $W$. The links of $I_W$, and the
inside links of a block $y+e_\mu\notin W$ in the direction $\mu$ for
$y\in W$, enter those averages, and the labels of the blocks adjoining the
component depend on such links; moving them moves the fibre, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:insidefold} shows that off the chart the law then
jumps. On the chart the dependence is smooth. The exact missing
statement is the bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:badcrossratio} for ends $E_a$,
$E_b$ that contain such links, that is a bound on the mixed derivative of
$\log\nu^-_c(e^{-\lambda Q^-})$ in two links that move the constraints,
decaying in their distance. Lemma~\ref{lem:endpairs} places an end in one
pair factor of $\nu^-_c$, Proposition~\ref{prop:endfold} shows that this
factor jumps under small moves of the end at every value of the coarse
link, and Remark~\ref{rem:badendsopen} states the bound in the mean that is
missing.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

The three points of Remark~\ref{rem:badmassopen} are taken in turn. The
first concerns charts local in the component. Such a chart is attached to a
window $W$, a set of blocks inside the component, and is fixed by the field
outside the window; the next theorem bounds the conditional probability that
the window lies on it, uniformly in the window, the exterior and the coarse
field.

\begin{theorem}[local charts]\label{thm:localcharts}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\beta_W\ge2.3\cdot10^{17}$, let $c$ be a coarse field and
$W$ a set of blocks, and write $E$ for the links off $A^-_W$. Suppose that
for each $E$ a field $U(E)$ is given in the reduced fibre $F^-(E)$ over $W$
through $E$, with averages $c_k$ for the pairs based in $W$, such that $F^-(E)$
satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} at $U(E)$ with
constants $\kappa(E)$, $s(E)$, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}%
\textup{(ii)}, and let $\mathcal A$ be the event that the links of $A^-_W$
lie in the chart $\Phi_E(\Omega_{r(E)})$ of $F^-(E)$ at $U(E)$, $r(E)=s(E)/
32$, assumed measurable. Then for $\E_c$-almost every $c$
\[
\mu^c(\mathcal A)\le\exp\Bigl(-\frac{28}3\lvert W\rvert e^{-10^{-24}
\beta_W}\Bigr).
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, then $\mu^c(\mathcal A)\le e^{-3.433\lvert W
\rvert}<0.033^{\lvert W\rvert}$; at $\beta_W=2.3\cdot10^{17}$, $\mu^c(
\mathcal A)\le e^{-9.333\lvert W\rvert}$.
\item If $\beta_W\le10^{24}$ and $\mathcal A_1,\dots,\mathcal A_J$ are such
events, given by fields $U_1(E),\dots,U_J(E)$, then the union of the
$\mathcal A_j$ has $\mu^c$-probability at most $J\,e^{-3.433\lvert W\rvert}$.
\item If $\mu^c(\mathcal A\mid E)\ge\frac12$ on a set of values of $E$ of
positive probability, then $\beta_W>2.6\cdot10^{24}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}\textup{(i)}, for $\E_c$-almost every
$c$ the conditional law under $\mu^c$ of the links of $A^-_W$ given $E$ is
the constrained law $\mu^-_W$ on $F^-(E)$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}\textup{(ii)}, Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass}
holds on $F^-(E)$ with $45\lvert W\rvert$ replaced by $\lvert L'^-\rvert\ge
28\lvert W\rvert$, so that, with $q_0=\frac13e^{-2843.5\beta_Wr(E)^2}$,
\[
\begin{split}
\mu^c(\mathcal A\mid E)&=\mu^-_W\bigl(\Phi_E(\Omega_{r(E)})\bigr)\\
&\le(1-q_0)^{\lvert L'^-\rvert}\le e^{-28q_0\lvert W\rvert}.
\end{split}
\]
As $\kappa(E)+s(E)\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, $r(E)\le1.875\cdot10^{-14}$ and
$2843.5\,r(E)^2<10^{-24}$, so $q_0\ge\frac13e^{-10^{-24}\beta_W}$; taking
the mean over $E$ gives the bound. (i) For $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, $q_0\ge
\frac13e^{-1}>0.12262$ and $28\cdot0.12262>3.433$; as $e^3>20.08$ and
$e^{0.433}>1.54$, $e^{3.433}>30.9>1/0.033$. At $\beta_W=2.3\cdot10^{17}$,
$q_0\ge\frac13e^{-2.3\cdot10^{-7}}\ge\frac13(1-2.3\cdot10^{-7})$, and
$28q_0>9.333$. (ii) is the union bound. (iii) On that set $e^{-28q_0}\ge
e^{-28q_0\lvert W\rvert}\ge\frac12$, so $q_0\le\frac{\ln2}{28}$ and
$e^{-10^{-24}\beta_W}\le\frac{3\ln2}{28}$. As $\ln2<0.69315$, $\frac{28}{3
\ln2}>\frac{28}{2.07945}>13.465$, while $e^{2.6}<7.38906\cdot1.82212<
13.4638$; so $10^{-24}\beta_W>2.6$.
\end{proof}

The bound holds for every window, so it holds block by block: whatever the
exterior and the coarse field, a single block lies on a chart of this kind
with conditional probability below $0.033$ for $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, and
below $\frac12$ only if $\beta_W>2.6\cdot10^{24}$, and $J\le15$ charts for
each exterior cover it with probability below $\frac12$. A decomposition of
the fibre of a component into small-field regions, each carrying such a
chart, and a large-field region, as in Remark~\ref{rem:badmassopen}(a), has
the large-field region carrying all but at most $J\,0.033^{\lvert W'\rvert}$
of the conditional mass of each window $W'$. The cost per block of a bound
built on these charts is therefore not small at $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, and a
bound uniform in the length must control the response on the large-field
region, which is the regime of Proposition~\ref{prop:fold}. The theorem does
not cover charts whose background depends on the links of the window
itself, such as a background chosen nearest to the configuration from a
continuous family.

The second point is the existence of backgrounds for the exterior $R(c)$
between $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$. In the next
proposition the curvature of one coarse plaquette is spread over the fine
plaquettes of its four corner blocks, with every link in the torus $\{e^{
\varphi T_0}\}$. On such a field a link is given by a real angle, a
plaquette at $x$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ has the real sum $\varphi_{x,
\mu}+\varphi_{x+e_\mu,\nu}-\varphi_{x+e_\nu,\mu}-\varphi_{x,\nu}$, and a
path the sum of its two angles.

\begin{proposition}[spreading a coarse plaquette]\label{prop:spread}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, let the periodic lattice have side $2L$, let $\mu<\nu$ be two
directions, $0<\theta\le1.7\cdot10^{-12}$, and let $M\ge4$ and $L\ge M+6$ be
integers. Let $a(0)=0$, $a(1)=a(2)=a(3)=\theta$, $a(k)=\theta(M+3-k)/M$ for
$3\le k\le M+3$ and $a(k)=0$ for $M+3\le k\le L-1$, indices modulo $L$. Let
$c^\theta$ be the coarse field with $c^\theta_{y,\nu}=e^{a(y_\mu)T_0}$ for
$y_\nu=0$ and every other coarse link $I$, and $W_\theta=\{y:y_\mu,y_\nu
\in\{0,1\}\}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The coarse plaquettes of $c^\theta$ other than $I$ lie in the plane
$\{\mu,\nu\}$ at blocks with $y_\nu=0$: $c^\theta_P=e^{\theta T_0}$ for
$y_\mu=0$, so that $\delta(c^\theta_P,I)=t:=2\sqrt2\sin\frac\theta2$, and
$c^\theta_P=e^{-(\theta/M)T_0}$ for $3\le y_\mu\le M+2$, with $\delta(
c^\theta_P,I)\le\sqrt2\theta/M$. The set $W_\theta$ consists of the corner
blocks of the first.
\item Let $U^\theta$ be the field with the angles of
Table~\ref{tab:spread}\textup{(a)} on the links listed there, at every value
of the coordinates other than $\mu$ and $\nu$, and equal to $R(c^\theta)$
elsewhere. Then $U^\theta$ vanishes on the tree links, agrees with $R(
c^\theta)$ off $A_{W_\theta}$, has $V^\sharp_k(U^\theta)=c^\theta_k$ for
every pair $k$ based in $W_\theta$, and every plaquette has $\delta(
U^\theta_p,I)\le\kappa_\theta:=2\sqrt2\sin\frac\theta8$. So $U^\theta$ lies
in the fibre over $W_\theta$ of $R(c^\theta)$.
\item Let $U^{\theta,-}$ be the field with the angles of
Table~\ref{tab:spread}\textup{(b)}, and $R(c^\theta)$ elsewhere. Then
$U^{\theta,-}$ vanishes on the tree links, agrees with $R(c^\theta)$ off
$A^-_{W_\theta}$, has $V^\sharp_k(U^{\theta,-})=c^\theta_k$ for every pair
$k$, and every plaquette has $\delta(U^{\theta,-}_p,I)\le\kappa'_\theta:=
2\sqrt2\sin\frac\theta7$. So for every set $W\supset W_\theta$, $U^{\theta,
-}$ lies in the reduced fibre over $W$ of $R(c^\theta)$, and in its fibre.
\item Let $U$ be any field with values in the torus $\{e^{\varphi T_0}\}$,
$y$ a block, $W'=\{y+ie_\mu+je_\nu:0\le i\le2,\ 0\le j\le1\}$, and suppose
that $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa\le10^{-8}$ for every plaquette with a vertex in
a block of $W'^+$. Write $U_p=e^{a_pT_0}$ with $a_p\in(-\pi,\pi]$, and let
$S_x$ be the four plaquettes of the square of side two at $x$ in the plane
$\{\mu,\nu\}$. Then the coarse plaquettes $P$ at $y$ and $P'$ at $y+e_\mu$
in that plane of $c=V^\sharp(U)$ satisfy
\[
c_P=\exp\Bigl(\frac1{16}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\sum_{p\in S_x}a_p\,T_0\Bigr),
\]
$c_{P'}$ is given by the same formula with $B(y+e_\mu)$ in place of $B(y)$,
and if $c_{P'}=c_P^{-1}$, then $\delta(c_P,I)\le3\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, for every $t\in(0,2.39\cdot10^{-12}]$, with $\theta=2\arcsin
(t/(2\sqrt2))$, the fibre over $W_\theta$ of $R(c^\theta)$ contains a field
at which it satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} with
$s=2.4\cdot10^{-15}$; and for every $t\in(0,2.09\cdot10^{-12}]$ and every
$W\supset W_\theta$, the reduced fibre over $W$ of $R(c^\theta)$ contains a
field at which it satisfies them, in the sense of
Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}\textup{(ii)}, with the same $s$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) A coarse plaquette at $y$ in a plane $\{\rho,\sigma\}$ is $c_{y,\rho}
c_{y+e_\rho,\sigma}c_{y+e_\sigma,\rho}^{-1}c_{y,\sigma}^{-1}$. Only the
links in the direction $\nu$ with $y_\nu=0$ differ from $I$, and two links
in the direction $\nu$ based at blocks that differ in a coordinate other
than $\mu$ and $\nu$ are equal; so only the plaquettes in the plane $\{\mu,
\nu\}$ at $y_\nu=0$ can differ from $I$, and there $c^\theta_P=e^{(a(y_\mu
+1)-a(y_\mu))T_0}$. The increments of $a$ are $\theta$ at $y_\mu=0$,
$-\theta/M$ for $3\le y_\mu\le M+2$, and $0$ otherwise, also at $y_\mu=
L-1$, where $a(L-1)=a(0)=0$ as $L-1\ge M+3$. Finally $2\sqrt2\sin x\le2
\sqrt2x$.

(ii), (iii) We write $\varphi$ for the angles of the field in question and
$\varphi^R$ for those of $R(c^\theta)$, all real. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}\textup{(i)} and its proof, $\varphi^R$ is
$0$ on every link in the direction $\mu$ and on every link in the
direction $\nu$ except $(x,\nu)$ with $x_\nu=1$, where it is $a(y_\mu)$,
$x\in B(y)$, and all sixteen paths of a pair $(y,\rho)$ have the angle
$\vartheta_{y,\rho}$ of $c^\theta_{y,\rho}$, which is $a(y_\mu)$ or $0$.

\emph{Links.} The field differs from $R(c^\theta)$ only on the links of the
table with an entry different from that of $R(c^\theta)$, and the entries
do not depend on the other two coordinates. These are links $(x,\nu)$ with
$x_\nu=1$ and $0\le x_\mu\le3$, which have $o_\nu=1$ and are private links
of pairs based in $W_\theta$, and links $(x,\mu)$ with $0\le x_\mu,x_\nu
\le3$, which are private links of such pairs when $x_\mu$ is odd; when
$x_\mu$ is even the entry is nonzero only for $x_\nu$ odd, and then $o_\nu
=1$ with $\nu>\mu$, so the link is an active link inside a block of
$W_\theta$, not a tree link. In (b) the links with $x_\mu$ even have $x_\mu
=2$, in a block $y$ with $y-e_\mu\in W_\theta$, so they are not in
$I_{W_\theta}$. Hence $U^\theta$ agrees with $R(c^\theta)$ off
$A_{W_\theta}$ and $U^{\theta,-}$ off $A^-_{W_\theta}$, and both vanish on
the tree links. For $W\supset W_\theta$, $A^-_{W_\theta}\subset A^-_W$: a
link of $A_{W_\theta}$ in the direction $\rho$ that lies in $I_W$ is inside
a block $y\in W_\theta$ with $y-e_\rho\notin W$, hence $y-e_\rho\notin
W_\theta$, and so lies in $I_{W_\theta}$.

\emph{Averages.} Let $D_x=\varphi(P_x)-\vartheta_{y,\rho}$ for the paths
$P_x$ of a pair $(y,\rho)$. Every entry differs from that of $R(c^\theta)$
by at most $\frac27\theta$, so $\lvert\varphi(P_x)-\varphi(P_{2y})\rvert\le
\frac87\theta$ and $\delta(P_x,P_{2y})=2\sqrt2\sin\frac{\lvert\varphi(P_x)-
\varphi(P_{2y})\rvert}2<4\theta<\frac12$. The cut-off of~\eqref{eq:cutoff}
equals one, $\rho_G=1$, and as these differences are less than $\pi$ the
principal logarithm of $P_{2y}^{-1}P_x$ is $(\varphi(P_x)-\varphi(P_{2y}))
T_0$. So
\[
V^\sharp_{y,\rho}=\exp\Bigl(\Bigl(\vartheta_{y,\rho}+\frac1{16}\sum_{x\in
B(y)}D_x\Bigr)T_0\Bigr),
\]
and $V^\sharp_{y,\rho}=c^\theta_{y,\rho}$ when $\sum_xD_x=0$. For $\rho
\notin\{\mu,\nu\}$ every $D_x$ vanishes. For $\rho=\nu$, $D_x\ne0$ needs a
link $(x',\nu)$ with $x'_\nu=1$ on the path, so only the pairs with $y_\nu
=0$ are concerned, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}\textup{(iii)} $\sum_xD_x
=8(d(2y_\mu)+d(2y_\mu+1))$, $d(m)$ the deviation of the link $(x,\nu)$ with
$x_\mu=m$, $x_\nu=1$. The deviations are $-\frac14,\frac14,-\frac14,\frac14$
in (a) and $-\frac17,\frac17,-\frac27,\frac27$ in (b) for $m=0,1,2,3$, and
$0$ otherwise, so the sums vanish. For $\rho=\mu$, let $X(m)$ be the sum of
the deviations of the two links $(x,\mu)$ with $x_\mu=m$ and $x_\nu\in\{2
y_\nu,2y_\nu+1\}$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}\textup{(iii)}, $\sum_xD_x=
4\bigl(X(2y_\mu)+2X(2y_\mu+1)+X(2y_\mu+2)\bigr)$. For $y_\nu\in\{0,1\}$ and
$m=-1,\dots,4$, $X(m)$ is $0,-\frac14,\frac14,-\frac14,\frac18,0$ in (a)
and $0,0,\frac17,-\frac27,\frac17,0$ in (b), and $X(m)=0$ for other $m$ or
$y_\nu$. The combination vanishes for $y_\mu\in\{0,1\}$ in (a), and for
every $y$ in (b).

\emph{Plaquettes.} A plaquette in a plane other than $\{\mu,\nu\}$ has two
parallel links that differ only in a coordinate other than $\mu$ and $\nu$
and two links in a direction other than $\mu$ and $\nu$; the first two
have equal angles and the other two the angle $0$, so its real sum is $0$.
In the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ the real sum at $x$ is read off the table; the
table lists every plaquette that contains a link at which the field differs
from $R(c^\theta)$, and all other plaquettes are those of $R(c^\theta)$, whose real sums are $0$ or
$a(y_\mu+1)-a(y_\mu)\in\{0,-\theta/M\}$ with $\lvert\theta/M\rvert\le\frac
\theta4$, by Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}\textup{(i)}. So every real sum
has modulus at most $\frac\theta4$ in (a) and $\frac{2\theta}7$ in (b), and
$\delta(U_p,I)=2\sqrt2\sin\frac{\lvert\cdot\rvert}2$ gives the bounds.

(iv) For a pair $k$ based in $W'$ let $v=P_{2y}$ be its path link. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}\textup{(i)}, $\delta(v^{-1}P_x,I)\le24\kappa<
\frac12$, so the cut-off is one and $c_k=v\exp(\frac1{16}\sum_x\psi_x
T_0)$, where $v^{-1}P_x=e^{\psi_xT_0}$ with $\psi_x\in(-\pi,\pi]$ and
$\lvert\psi_x\rvert\le27\kappa$, since $2\sqrt2\sin\frac{\lvert\psi\rvert}2
\ge\frac{2\sqrt2}\pi\lvert\psi\rvert$. Choose real angles $\varphi_k$ of the
path links. Then $c_k=e^{\gamma_kT_0}$ with $\gamma_k=\varphi_k+\frac1{16}
\sum_x\psi_x$, and with the sides $k=1,\dots,4$ of $P$ and signs $\epsilon_k
=1,1,-1,-1$, $c_P=e^{\Theta T_0}$ with
\[
\Theta=\sum_k\epsilon_k\gamma_k=\frac1{16}\sum_{x\in B(y)}\Theta_x,\qquad
\Theta_x=\sum_k\epsilon_k\bigl(\varphi_k+\psi^{(k)}_{x_k}\bigr),
\]
where $x_k\in\{x,x+2e_\mu,x+2e_\nu,x\}$ is the site of the same offset as
$x$ in the block of side $k$. The term $\varphi_k+\psi^{(k)}_{x_k}$ is an
angle of the path $P^{(k)}_{x_k}$, and on the torus the product of the four
paths around the square of side two at $x$ is the product of the four
plaquettes of $S_x$, so $\Theta_x\equiv\sigma_x:=\sum_{p\in S_x}a_p$ modulo
$2\pi$. Now $\lvert a_p\rvert\le1.12\kappa$, since $2\sqrt2\sin\frac{\lvert
a\rvert}2\ge\frac{2\sqrt2}\pi\lvert a\rvert$, so $\lvert(\Theta_x-\sigma_x)-
(\Theta_{2y}-\sigma_{2y})\rvert\le4\cdot27\kappa+8\cdot1.12\kappa<2\pi$, as
$\psi^{(k)}_{2y}=0$. Hence $\Theta_x-\sigma_x$ is the same multiple of $2\pi
$ for all $x$, and $\Theta$ differs from $\frac1{16}\sum_x\sigma_x$ by a
multiple of $2\pi$, which gives the formula for $c_P$; the same holds for
$P'$. Let $\Theta_P$, $\Theta_{P'}$ be the two exponents. A plaquette at the
corner $z$, $z_\mu=2y_\mu+i$ and $z_\nu=2y_\nu+j$, lies in $S_x$ for
$n(i)n(j)$ sites $x$ of $B(y)$ with the coordinates of $z$ other than $\mu$
and $\nu$, and for $n(i-2)n(j)$ sites of $B(y+e_\mu)$, where $n(0)=n(2)=1$,
$n(1)=2$ and $n=0$ otherwise. So
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_P-\Theta_{P'}&=\frac1{16}\sum_zw_za_{p_z},\\
\sum_z\lvert w_z\rvert&=(1+2+0+2+1)(1+2+1)\cdot4=96,
\end{split}
\]
the factor $4$ counting the offsets in the other two directions. If
$c_{P'}=c_P^{-1}$, then $\Theta_P+\Theta_{P'}\in2\pi\Z$, and as $\lvert
\Theta_P\rvert,\lvert\Theta_{P'}\rvert\le4\cdot1.12\kappa<\pi$ it vanishes.
So $2\lvert\Theta_P\rvert\le6\alpha$ with $\alpha=\max\lvert a_p\rvert$, and
as $\sin3x\le3\sin x$ for $0\le x\le\frac\pi6$,
\[
\delta(c_P,I)=2\sqrt2\sin\frac{\lvert\Theta_P\rvert}2\le2\sqrt2\sin\frac{
3\alpha}2\le3\cdot2\sqrt2\sin\frac\alpha2\le3\kappa .
\]

For the last statement, $\sin x\ge x(1-x^2/6)$ gives $\theta<1.7\cdot10^{-
12}$ for $t\le2.39\cdot10^{-12}$. In (ii), $\sin\frac\theta2=4\sin\frac
\theta8\cos\frac\theta8\cos\frac\theta4$, so $\kappa_\theta=t/(4\cos\frac
\theta8\cos\frac\theta4)\le t/(4(1-\theta^2))<5.976\cdot10^{-13}$. In (iii),
$t\ge\sqrt2\theta(1-\theta^2/24)$, so $\kappa'_\theta\le\frac{2\sqrt2}7
\theta\le\frac27t(1+\theta^2/12)<5.972\cdot10^{-13}$ for $t\le2.09\cdot
10^{-12}$. Every plaquette is below $\kappa_\theta\le10^{-8}$, respectively
$\kappa'_\theta$, so the plaquette condition holds on $W^+$ for every $W$;
and $s=2.4\cdot10^{-15}$ satisfies $s\le1/(6000c_3)$, $\kappa+6s\le10^{-8}$
and $\kappa+s\le6.0\cdot10^{-13}$.
\end{proof}

The fields of (ii) and (iii) spread the coarse curvature $\theta$ over the
plaquettes of the corner blocks with the largest real sum $\frac\theta4$ and
$\frac{2\theta}7$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp} no field does
better than $\frac\theta4$ up to a term of order $\theta^2$, so (ii) is
sharp up to that term. The gap between $2.39\cdot10^{-12}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ is the
rounding of the chart threshold $6.044\cdot10^{-13}$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart}\textup{(ii)} to $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross}: for every threshold $\kappa_*$ in place of
$6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, (ii) gives a background whenever $\delta(c_P,I)<4
\kappa_*(1-\theta^2)$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitnesssharp} excludes one above
$4\kappa_*+7700\kappa_*^2$. Part (iv) shows that the factor depends on the
neighbouring coarse plaquettes: for a coarse field with opposite fluxes at
two adjacent coarse plaquettes and $\delta(c_P,I)>1.8\cdot10^{-12}$, no
field with values in a torus has every plaquette near the six blocks below
$6.0\cdot10^{-13}$.

The third point is the ends that enter the averages. They meet the fibre
measure in one factor.

\begin{lemma}[ends and pairs]\label{lem:endpairs}
Let $W$ be a set of blocks and $e$ an active link off $A^-_W$ that enters an
average $V^\sharp_{y,\rho}$ with $y\in W$. Then $e=(x,\rho)$ with $x_\rho$
even, and either
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $x\in B(y)$, $y-e_\rho\notin W$, $e\in I_W$, and $e$ is the first link
of the path $P_x$, whose second link is the private link $(x+e_\rho,\rho)$
of $(y,\rho)$; or
\item $x\in B(y+e_\rho)$, $y+e_\rho\notin W$, and $e$ is the second link of
$P_{x-e_\rho}$, whose first link is the private link $(x-e_\rho,\rho)$ of
$(y,\rho)$.
\end{enumerate}
In either case $(y,\rho)$ is the only pair based in $W$ whose average
contains $e$, $e$ lies on one of its sixteen paths, and among the factors of
$\nu^-_c$ over the pairs based in $W$ only the factor of $(y,\rho)$ depends
on $e$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A private link enters only the average of its own pair, and the private
links of pairs based in $W$ lie in $A^-_W$; so $e$ is an inside link
$(x,\rho)$, $x_\rho$ even, of a block $B(y')$. As in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage}\textup{(i)}, it enters only the averages
of $(y',\rho)$, as the first link of $P_x$, and of $(y'-e_\rho,\rho)$, as the
second link of $P_{x-e_\rho}$. If $y'\in W$, then $e\in A_W\setminus A^-_W=
I_W$, so $y'-e_\rho\notin W$ and $y=y'$, which is (a). If $y'\notin W$, the
pair is $(y'-e_\rho,\rho)$, which is (b). The other link of the path has
offset $1$ in the direction $\rho$ and joins $B(y)$ to $B(y+e_\rho)$, so it
is a private link of $(y,\rho)$. Given the inside links and the links off
$A^-_W$, the averages of the pairs based in $W$ depend on disjoint sets of
private links, and $\nu^-_c$ is the product of the Haar measure of the
inside links in $A^-_W$ and of one factor for each pair, built from its
average as before~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}; only the factor of $(y,\rho)$
contains $e$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[an end at the fold]\label{prop:endfold}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\mu\le2$, let $W$ be a set of blocks, $y\in W$ with $y-e_\mu
\notin W$, $k=(y,\mu)$, and $c_k\in\SU(2)$. There are values of the links of
the pair $k$ and of the links inside $B(y)$ and $B(y+e_\mu)$, with an
active inside link $u_b$ of $B(y)$ in the direction $\mu$, which lies in
$I_W$ and is an end of case \textup{(a)} of Lemma~\ref{lem:endpairs}, moved
along a one-parameter family $u_b(t)$, such that for every $\beta_W\ge0$,
every value of the other links and every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $t<0<t'$
with $d(u_b(t),u_b(t'))<\varepsilon$ and
\[
W_1^\delta\bigl(\pi^{(t)},\pi^{(t')}\bigr)\ge0.126 ,
\]
where $\pi^{(t)}$ is the law~\eqref{eq:pathlaw} of the path link of $k$
given its seven non-path links, at the value $c_k$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take the configuration of Proposition~\ref{prop:insidefold}, at the value
$c_{\gamma^*}$, with its moved link $u_b(t)$, and let $h=c_kc_{\gamma^*}^{-1
}$. Let $\Gamma_h$ multiply every private link of $k$ on the left by $h$ and
conjugate every link of $B(y)$ in the direction $\mu$ by $h$; it fixes the
tree links, which are $I$. A path of $k$ from a site with $o_\mu=0$ is $u\ell$,
with $u$ in $B(y)$ and $\ell$ private, and $(huh^{-1})(h\ell)=hu\ell$; a path
from a site with $o_\mu=1$ is $\ell w$, with $w$ in $B(y+e_\mu)$, and becomes
$h\ell w$. So $\Gamma_h$ multiplies every path of $k$ on the left by $h$, the
distances $\delta(P_x,P_{2y})$ and the logarithms in~\eqref{eq:cutoff} do
not change, and $V^\sharp_k\circ\Gamma_h=hV^\sharp_k$. As a function of
the path link $g$, the preimages of $c_k$ after $\Gamma_h$ are the points
$hg$ with $g$ a preimage of $c_{\gamma^*}$ before, and since left
translation is an isometry of the bi-invariant metric, $\lvert\det D_gV
\rvert$ is the same at $hg$ as at $g$. The action $S(g;\cdot)$ of the path
link is a sum of nonnegative multiples of $\delta(U_p,I)^2\le8$ over the
plaquettes through it, so $0\le S\le S_{\max}$ with $S_{\max}$ independent
of the configuration. Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:insidefold}, for
$0<\lvert t\rvert<\tau$ the preimages are $hg_L(t)$, whose weight is at most
$1/\lvert\det D_gV(g_L(t))\rvert$, which tends to $1/\lvert\det D_gV(
g_L^*)\rvert<\infty$, and for $t<0$ also $hg_\pm(t)$, whose weights are at
least $e^{-\beta_WS_{\max}}/\lvert f'(q_\pm(t);t)\rvert\to\infty$ as
$t\uparrow0$, with the function $f$ of the proof of that proposition. As
there, $\pi^{(t)}\to\delta_{hg^*}$ as $t\uparrow0$ and $\pi^{(t)}\to
\delta_{hg_L^*}$ as $t\downarrow0$, and $\delta(hg^*,hg_L^*)=\delta(g^*,
g_L^*)\ge0.1268$. Kantorovich duality with $\delta(\cdot,hg^*)$ gives the
bound, and $d(hu_b(t)h^{-1},hu_b(t')h^{-1})=d(u_b(t),u_b(t'))$. The link
$u_b$ lies in $B(y)$, has $o_\mu=0$, is active, and $y-e_\mu\notin W$, so it
lies in $I_W$.
\end{proof}

By Lemma~\ref{lem:endpairs} the dependence of the weight of the interior on
an end is that of one pair factor, and by Proposition~\ref{prop:endfold}
that factor, conditioned on the non-path links, jumps under arbitrarily
small moves of the end at every value of the coarse link and every
$\beta_W$. In the same configuration the normalisation $Z$ of~\eqref{eq:pathlaw} is
bounded for small $t>0$ and tends to infinity as $t\uparrow0$, so the
derivative of $\log Z$ in the end, at fixed non-path links, is not
bounded.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:badendsopen}
What remains of the three points.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Length.} By Theorem~\ref{thm:localcharts}, charts fixed by the
exterior of their window carry less than half of the conditional mass of
each block for $\beta_W\le2.6\cdot10^{24}$, and less than $0.033$ of it for
$\beta_W\le10^{24}$. A bound uniform in the length needs the response on the
large-field region of the fibre, or charts whose background moves with the
window links, together with a bound on the mass of their union; neither is
available.
\item \emph{Coarse fields.} For the coarse fields $c^\theta$ the exterior
$R(c)$ carries a background up to $2.39\cdot10^{-12}$, and the reduced fibre
up to $2.09\cdot10^{-12}$ for every window containing the component
(Proposition~\ref{prop:spread}). For a general coarse field between $6.0
\cdot10^{-13}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ with exterior $R(c)$, and for the
reduced fibre between $2.09\cdot10^{-12}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$, the
existence of a background is not decided; by
Proposition~\ref{prop:spread}\textup{(iv)} a background with values in a
torus does not exist above $1.8\cdot10^{-12}$ for opposite fluxes at
adjacent coarse plaquettes.
\item \emph{Ends.} A bound of the form of
Corollary~\ref{cor:badcrossratio} for ends in the averages cannot hold at
fixed non-path links, by Proposition~\ref{prop:endfold}. The missing input
is a bound, uniform in $c_k$, on the derivative in an end of the logarithm
of its pair factor after integration over the seven non-path links, where
the coarea formula keeps the normalisation finite, together with its
locality in the distance between two ends.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\subsection{The one-step error in gauge-invariant form}\label{ssec:relstep}

Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth} requires the one-step error to be a
relative bound by a gauge-invariant form. This subsection constructs such a
bound at the trivial background on a box of blocks, from an absolute bound
on the gauge complement taken as a hypothesis. The error of the covariant
Hessian of a gauge-invariant induced action vanishes on the coarse gauge
directions and is at most a multiple $\varepsilon'$ of the coarse Wilson
form. On a box of side $n$, $\varepsilon'$ is of order $n^2$ times the
absolute error, and this order cannot be improved.

\emph{Setting.} On the coarse lattice of side $L$ let $W=\{y:a_\nu\le y_\nu
\le a_\nu+n-1\}$ be a box of $n^4$ blocks, $n+2\le L$, $K=\{(y,\mu):y\in
W\}$ and $W^\circ=\{y\in W:y-e_\mu\in W\text{ for every }\mu\}$. As in
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, the links off $A_W$ are fixed and the averages
of the pairs that enter $W$ from outside are integrated. For $w\in\g^K$ put
$|w|^2=\sum_k\lVert w_k\rVert^2$, let $Q_1(w)$ be the coarse plaquette form
of $w$ extended by zero off $K$, and put
\[
S_W(w)=\inf\bigl\{Q(X):X\in\g^{A_W},\ V_k(X)=w_k\ (k\in K)\bigr\}.
\]
At $U=I$, $2\lambda Q_1$ is the Hessian at $I$ of the coarse Wilson action
$\lambda Q_1$ with the links off $K$ fixed. $2\lambda S_W$ is the Hessian of
the Gaussian block-spin step, the minimum of the Hessian $2\lambda Q$ of
the fine action at given averages. The \emph{coarse gauge group} $\Gamma_W=
G^{W^\circ}$ acts on $G^K$ by $(h\cdot V)_{y,\mu}=h_yV_{y,\mu}h_{y+e_\mu
}^{-1}$, with $h_y=I$ for $y\notin W^\circ$. This is the action on the
cut-off averages of the fine gauge transformations that are constant on
blocks and equal to $I$ off the blocks of $W^\circ$. These transformations
preserve the tree gauge by Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(ii), and they fix the
links off $A_W$: a link with base in a block $y'\notin W$ ends in $y'$ or
$y'+e_\mu$, and neither lies in $W^\circ$. They also preserve the Wilson
action and Haar measure, and the cut-off average is covariant
(Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}). For $V_0\in G^K$ and $\eta\in\g^{W^\circ}$,
extended by zero, put
\[
(d_{V_0}\eta)_{y,\mu}=\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,y,\mu}^{-1})\eta_y-
\eta_{y+e_\mu},
\]
let $\mathcal O_{V_0}=d_{V_0}(\g^{W^\circ})$ be the gauge directions at
$V_0$ and $\Pi_{V_0}$ the orthogonal projection of $\g^K$ onto $\mathcal
O_{V_0}^\perp$. At $V_0=I$ write $d$, $\mathcal O$ and $\Pi$.

\begin{lemma}[the window off the gauge directions]\label{lem:windowgap}
Let $W$ be the box above.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The map $d$ is injective on $\g^{W^\circ}$, and $\mathcal O=\ker
Q_1=\ker S_W$.
\item For every $w\in\g^K$, $|\Pi w|^2\le C_n\,Q_1(w)$ with
\[
C_n=1+\frac1{4\sin^2(\pi/2n)}\le1+\frac{n^2}4 .
\]
\item $c_*Q_1\le S_W\le4Q_1$ on $\g^K$, with $c_*=(1+\sqrt{21/8})^{-2}>
0.1456$.
\item There is $w\in\mathcal O^\perp\setminus\{0\}$ with $|w|^2=C_n^-Q_1
(w)$, where $C_n^-=(12\sin^2(\pi/(2n+2)))^{-1}\ge(n+1)^2/(3\pi^2)$.
\item If $W$ is the whole coarse torus, the fields that are constant in each
direction lie in $\mathcal O^\perp\cap\ker Q_1\cap\ker S_W$, so no
bound of the form \textup{(ii)} holds.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\Lambda=\prod_\nu[a_\nu,a_\nu+n]$, with boundary $\partial\Lambda$.
The interior sites of $\Lambda$ form $W^\circ$. Call $(y,\mu)\in K$
\emph{inner} if $y_\nu>a_\nu$ for every $\nu\ne\mu$, and a \emph{face link}
otherwise. The inner links are the links of $\Lambda$ not contained in
$\partial\Lambda$; call a plaquette of $\Lambda$ not contained in $\partial
\Lambda$ inner. The links of $\partial\Lambda$ that are not face links have
base outside $W$, so they are fixed, and $w$ vanishes on them.

(ii) The cochain complex of $\Lambda$ relative to $\partial\Lambda$, with
values in $\g$, has the interior sites, inner links and inner plaquettes as
cells of degrees $0,1,2$. On these, $d_0=d$, and $d_1$ is the curvature on
the inner plaquettes of a field on the inner links extended by zero. This
complex is the fourfold tensor product of the complex of $[0,n]$ relative
to its endpoints. In that complex $C^0=\R^{n-1}$, $C^1=\R^n$ and $d$ is the
difference operator. With the product inner products, the Laplacian $\Delta
=dd^*+d^*d$ of the product is the sum of the Laplacians of the factors. On
$C^0$, $d^*d$ is the Dirichlet Laplacian, with eigenvalues $4\sin^2(\pi j/
2n)$ for $1\le j\le n-1$. On $C^1$, $dd^*$ has the same nonzero eigenvalues
and one zero eigenvalue. A $1$-cochain of $\Lambda$ is a sum of products
with exactly one factor of degree one, so $\Delta_1\ge\gamma_n=12\sin^2(\pi
/2n)$. On $\ker d_0^*=\mathcal O^\perp$ this gives $\lvert d_1u\rvert^2\ge
\gamma_n|u|^2$.

Write $w=u+f$, with $u$ on the inner links and $f$ on the face links. Since
$\mathcal O$ lies on the inner links, $\Pi w=\Pi u+f$ and $|\Pi w|^2=|\Pi
u|^2+|f|^2$. Let $f_k\ne0$ at a face link $k=(y,\mu)$, and let $\nu\ne\mu$
be the least direction with $y_\nu=a_\nu$. The plaquette at $y-e_\nu$ in
the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ has $k$ as its only link in $K$, since its other
three links have base outside $W$. So its curvature is $\pm f_k$, and
distinct face links give distinct such plaquettes, none of them inner.
Consider next an inner plaquette $P$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ at $z$.
It has $z_\rho>a_\rho$ for $\rho\notin\{\mu,\nu\}$, so its face links are
among $(z,\mu)$, if $z_\nu=a_\nu$, and $(z,\nu)$, if $z_\mu=a_\mu$. Thus
$P$ contains at most two face links, and a face link lies in at most one
inner plaquette. Hence $(d_1u)_P^2\le3\bigl((dw)_P^2+\sum_{k\in P}f_k^2
\bigr)$, where the sum runs over the face links of $P$. Since $d_1\Pi u=
d_1u$,
\[
\begin{split}
|\Pi w|^2&\le\gamma_n^{-1}\lvert d_1u\rvert^2+|f|^2\\
&\le\frac3{\gamma_n}\Bigl(\sum_{P\text{ inner}}(dw)_P^2+|f|^2\Bigr)+|f|^2
\le C_nQ_1(w),
\end{split}
\]
because the inner plaquettes and the plaquettes of the face links are
distinct terms of $Q_1(w)$. Finally $\sin x\ge2x/\pi$ on $[0,\pi/2]$ gives
$C_n\le1+n^2/4$.

(iii) Let $X\in\g^{A_W}$ with $V(X)=w$ on $K$. Extended by zero, $X$
vanishes on the tree links, and its averages are $w$ on $K$, zero on the
coarse links with both blocks outside $W$, and $v'_{y-e_\mu,\mu}=
S^\mu_y/16$ on a pair entering $y\in W$ from $y-e_\mu\notin W$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(iii). By Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(i),
$Q_1(w+v')\le Q(X)$. The sum $S^\mu_y$ has at most seven active links, and
every link inside a block enters one such sum. So $\sum|v'|^2\le\frac7{256}
I\le\frac7{32}Q(X)$, by the bound $I\le8Q_{\rm in}$ in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap}, which uses only the tree links. A coarse
plaquette contains at most two entering pairs, since $(z,\mu)$ and $(z+e_\mu
,\nu)$ cannot both enter, nor can $(z,\nu)$ and $(z+e_\nu,\mu)$. A coarse link
lies in six plaquettes, so $Q_1(v')\le12\sum|v'|^2\le\frac{21}8Q(X)$. By the
triangle inequality for $Q_1^{1/2}$, $Q_1(w)^{1/2}\le(1+\sqrt{21/8})Q(X)^{
1/2}$, and the infimum over $X$ gives $S_W\ge c_*Q_1$. For the upper
bound, the field $\varphi^*(w)$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(ii),
with $w$ extended by zero, lies in $\g^{A_W}$, has averages $w$ on $K$ and
$Q(\varphi^*(w))=4Q_1(w)$.

(i) If $d\eta=0$, follow the links of direction $0$ from $y\in W^\circ$ to
the first site outside $W^\circ$, where $\eta$ vanishes; so $\eta_y=0$.
Extended by zero, $d\eta$ is exact on the whole lattice, so $Q_1(d\eta)=
0$, and $\ker Q_1\subset\mathcal O$ by (ii). The fine field $\varphi=d(\eta
\circ b)$, with $b(x)$ the block of $x$, vanishes on the tree links and has
$Q(\varphi)=0$. It has $V(\varphi)=d\eta$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(ii).
It lies in $\g^{A_W}$, since a link on which it is nonzero meets a block of
$W^\circ$ and so has base in $W$. Hence $S_W(d\eta)=0$, and $\ker S_W
\subset\ker Q_1$ by (iii).

(iv) Let $f$ be the product of sines on $\{a_\nu,\dots,a_\nu+n-1\}^3$,
$\nu=1,2,3$, whose eigenvalue for the Dirichlet Laplacian of the cube is
$12\sin^2(\pi/(2n+2))$. Let $w_{y,0}=f(y_1,y_2,y_3)Z$ for a unit $Z\in\g$,
and $w=0$ in the other directions. The sum over $y_0$ telescopes, so $\ip w
{d\eta}=0$ for every $\eta$. The curvature of a plaquette in the plane
$\{0,\nu\}$ is a difference of $f$ along $e_\nu$, the plaquettes in the other
planes vanish, and for each of the $n$ values of $y_0$ the sum is the
Dirichlet form of $f$. Hence $Q_1(w)/|w|^2=12\sin^2(\pi/(2n+2))\le3\pi^2/
(n+1)^2$.

(v) Then $W^\circ=W$ and every coarse link is in $K$. A constant field has
$dw=0$, and $\ip w{d\eta}=\sum_y\sum_\mu\ip{w_\mu}{\eta_y-\eta_{y+e_\mu}}=
0$. The field $\varphi^*(w)$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(ii) has
$Q=4Q_1(w)=0$, so $S_W(w)=0$.
\end{proof}


The gauge directions at a background $V_0$ near $I$ are close to those at
$I$, and the flat form keeps its gap off them.

\begin{lemma}[the window at a curved background]\label{lem:curvedwindow}
Let $V_0\in G^K$ with $\lVert\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,k}^{-1})-1\rVert\le
\theta$ for every $k\in K$, and put $s_n=2\sin(\pi/2n)$. If $\theta<s_n$,
then every $w\in\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$ satisfies
\[
|w-\Pi w|\le\frac\theta{s_n}\,|w|,\qquad
|w|^2\le\Bigl(1-\frac\theta{s_n}\Bigr)^{-2}C_n\,Q_1(w).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $d_{V_0}=d+R$ with $(R\eta)_{y,\mu}=(\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,y,\mu}^{-1})
-1)\eta_y$. Every site of $W^\circ$ is the base of the four links $(y,\mu)$,
all in $K$, so $|R\eta|^2\le4\theta^2|\eta|^2$ and $\lVert R^*\rVert\le
2\theta$. The form $|d\eta|^2$ is the Dirichlet form of the box $\Lambda$ of
the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap} relative to its boundary, the sum of
four one-dimensional Dirichlet Laplacians, so $d^*d\ge4s_n^2$ and
$\lVert d(d^*d)^{-1}\rVert=\lVert(d^*d)^{-1/2}\rVert\le(2s_n)^{-1}$. For
$w\perp\mathcal O_{V_0}$ we have $d_{V_0}^*w=0$, that is $d^*w=-R^*w$, and
$w-\Pi w=d(d^*d)^{-1}d^*w=-d(d^*d)^{-1}R^*w$. Hence $|w-\Pi w|\le
\theta|w|/s_n$, so $|w|\le(1-\theta/s_n)^{-1}|\Pi w|$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(ii) gives the second bound.
\end{proof}

For a smooth function $f$ near $V_0\in G^K$ write $\Hess f(0)$ and $\nabla_k
f(0)$ for the Hessian and the gradient in the coordinates $\omega\mapsto f(
V_0e^\omega)$, $e^\omega=(e^{\omega_k})_k$.

\begin{lemma}[invariant functions and the slice]\label{lem:invariantslice}
Let $f$ be smooth and $\Gamma_W$-invariant near $V_0\in G^K$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $w\in\g^K$ and $\eta\in\g^{W^\circ}$, with $a_k=\operatorname{Ad}
(V_{0,k}^{-1})\eta_y$ and $b_k=\eta_{y+e_\mu}$ at $k=(y,\mu)$,
\[
\Hess f(0)[w,d_{V_0}\eta]=\frac12\sum_k\ip{\nabla_kf(0)}{[w_k,a_k+b_k]}.
\]
\item $d_{V_0}$ is injective, and $\Upsilon(s,\eta)=e^\eta\cdot(V_0e^s)$, on
$\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp\times\g^{W^\circ}$, is a diffeomorphism from a
neighbourhood of $0$ onto a neighbourhood of $V_0$, with $f(\Upsilon(s,
\eta))=f(V_0e^s)$. The \emph{covariant Hessian}
\[
\mathcal Hf(w,w')=\Hess(f\circ\Upsilon)(0)\bigl[D\Upsilon(0)^{-1}w,
D\Upsilon(0)^{-1}w'\bigr]
\]
equals $\Hess f(0)[\Pi_{V_0}w,\Pi_{V_0}w']$. It vanishes if $w$ or $w'$
lies in $\mathcal O_{V_0}$, and it equals $\Hess f(0)$ if $\nabla f(0)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) For the action of $e^{t\eta}$,
\[
(e^{t\eta}\cdot V_0e^\omega)_k=V_{0,k}e^{\omega_k}e^{t\operatorname{Ad}(
e^{-\omega_k})a_k}e^{-tb_k},
\]
and $\frac d{dt}\log(e^\omega e^{t\xi})|_{t=0}=\Phi(\operatorname{ad}_
\omega)\xi$ with $\Phi(z)=z/(1-e^{-z})$. So the orbit through $V_0e^\omega$
has the tangent
\[
\zeta(\omega)_k=\Phi(\operatorname{ad}_{\omega_k})\bigl(\operatorname{Ad}
(e^{-\omega_k})a_k-b_k\bigr),
\]
with $\zeta(0)=d_{V_0}\eta$ and $D\zeta(0)w=-\frac12([w_k,a_k+b_k])_k$. Invariance gives $Df(\omega)
[\zeta(\omega)]=0$ near $0$. Differentiating along $w$ at $0$ gives $\Hess
f(0)[w,\zeta(0)]=-Df(0)[D\zeta(0)w]$.

(ii) Injectivity follows as in Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(i), with $\eta_y=
\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,k})\eta_{y+e_\mu}$ along the links $k$ of direction
$0$. $D\Upsilon(0)(\sigma,\eta)=\sigma+d_{V_0}\eta$ is an isomorphism, and
the inverse function theorem applies. Invariance gives $f\circ\Upsilon(s,
\eta)=f(V_0e^s)$, whose Hessian at $0$ is $\Hess f(0)$ on the $s$-variables
and zero in $\eta$. Since $D\Upsilon(0)^{-1}w=(\Pi_{V_0}w,\eta)$ with
$d_{V_0}\eta=w-\Pi_{V_0}w$, the formula follows. If $\nabla f(0)=0$, (i)
shows that $\Hess f(0)$ vanishes on $\g^K\times\mathcal O_{V_0}$, so
$\Hess f(0)[w,w']=\Hess f(0)[\Pi_{V_0}w,\Pi_{V_0}w']$.
\end{proof}

At a point that is not critical, $\Hess f(0)$ does not vanish on the gauge
directions. The Hessian in exponential coordinates of an invariant
function, and with it any absolute bound on it, is therefore not
gauge-invariant; $\mathcal Hf$ is the gauge-invariant object. Let $j(\omega)=
\det\bigl((1-e^{-\operatorname{ad}_\omega})/\operatorname{ad}_\omega\bigr)$
be the density of Haar measure in exponential coordinates. Since $\operatorname
{ad}_\omega$ is skew, $\log j(\omega)=\frac1{24}\Tr(\operatorname{ad}_\omega
^2)+O(\lVert\omega\rVert^4)$. Put
\[
\delta_G=\frac1{12}\sup_{\lVert x\rVert=1}\lvert\Tr(\operatorname{ad}_x^2)
\rvert\le\frac{\dim G}3,
\]
which is $\frac13$ for $\SU(2)$, where $\lVert\operatorname{ad}_x\rVert_{HS}
=2\lVert x\rVert$.

\begin{proposition}[relative one-step bound]\label{prop:relstep}
Let $U=I$, so that $V_0=I$. Let $A$ be smooth near $0\in\g^K$ and suppose
that, for some $\varepsilon\ge0$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess A(0)[\sigma,\sigma]-2\lambda S_W(\sigma)\bigr\rvert\le
\lambda\varepsilon|\sigma|^2\quad\text{for }\sigma\in\mathcal O^\perp.
\tag{H}
\]
Let $A^{\rm gi}$ be the $\Gamma_W$-invariant function with $A^{\rm gi}
(\Upsilon(s,\eta))=A(s)+\sum_k\log j(s_k)$, and let $E=\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}-
2\lambda S_W$ as bilinear forms. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $E(w,g)=0$ for every $w\in\g^K$ and $g\in\mathcal O$;
\item for every $w\in\g^K$,
\[
\begin{split}
\lvert E(w,w)\rvert&\le(\lambda\varepsilon+\delta_G)|\Pi w|^2\le
(\lambda\varepsilon+\delta_G)C_nQ_1(w)\\
&\le\varepsilon'\cdot2\lambda S_W(w),\qquad\varepsilon'=\Bigl(\varepsilon+
\frac{\delta_G}\lambda\Bigr)\frac{C_n}{2c_*},
\end{split}
\]
so that $(1-\varepsilon')\,2\lambda S_W\le\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}\le(1+
\varepsilon')\,2\lambda S_W$;
\item the factor $C_n$ is necessary up to a constant. The
$\Gamma_W$-invariant $F$ with $F(\Upsilon(s,\eta))=\lambda S_W(s)+\frac12
\lambda\varepsilon|s|^2$ has $\Hess F(0)=2\lambda S_W+\lambda\varepsilon
|\cdot|^2$ on $\mathcal O^\perp$ and $\mathcal HF-2\lambda S_W=\lambda
\varepsilon|\Pi\cdot|^2$. At the field $w$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}\textup{(iv)} this is at least $\frac18
\varepsilon C_n^-\cdot2\lambda S_W(w)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) $\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}(w,g)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii).
$S_W$ is positive semidefinite with $g\in\ker S_W$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(i), so $S_W(w,g)=0$ by Cauchy--Schwarz.
(ii) By Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii), $\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}(w,w)$ is the
Hessian at $0$ of $s\mapsto A(s)+\sum_k\log j(s_k)$ at $\Pi w$, that is,
$\Hess A(0)[\Pi w,\Pi w]+\frac1{12}\sum_k\Tr(\operatorname{ad}_{(\Pi w)_k}
^2)$. Also $S_W(w)=S_W(\Pi w)$, by (i). Hypothesis (H) at $\sigma=\Pi w$
gives the first inequality. Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(ii) gives the second,
and Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iii), $Q_1\le S_W/c_*$, gives the third.
(iii) The Hessian of $s\mapsto\lambda S_W(s)+\frac12\lambda\varepsilon|s|^
2$ is $2\lambda S_W+\lambda\varepsilon|\cdot|^2$. That $w$ lies in
$\mathcal O^\perp$ and has $|w|^2=C_n^-Q_1(w)\ge\frac14C_n^-S_W(w)$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iii).
\end{proof}

\emph{Loop remainders.} Hypothesis (H) is an absolute bound, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep}(iii) shows that it costs the factor $C_n$. A
remainder built from Wilson loops that are filled by plaquettes obeys a
relative bound instead, at every flat background, and then $C_n$ falls on
the Haar term alone. Let $G\subset\U(N)$, with $\ip XY=-\Tr(XY)$ on $\g$,
and put
\[
s(g)=1-\frac1N\ReTr g=\frac1{2N}\lVert I-g\rVert_{HS}^2\qquad(g\in\U(N)),
\]
which is invariant under conjugation and inversion. For a coarse path $C$
let $V_C$ be its holonomy, the ordered product of its links. An
\emph{ordered filling} of a closed path $C$ is an identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:filling}
V_C=\prod_{j=1}^{A_C}h_jV_{p_j}^{\epsilon_j}h_j^{-1},\qquad\epsilon_j=\pm1,
\end{equation}
valid for every field, in which each $h_j$ is the holonomy of a path and
$V_{p_j}$ the holonomy around a plaquette $p_j$ read from one of its
corners. Let $m_{Cp}$ be the number of $j$ with $p_j=p$. This is the lattice
form of the non-abelian Stokes theorem of Brali\'c~\cite{Bra80}.\footnote{In
words: the holonomy of a loop is a product of plaquette holonomies, each
carried to the base point along a path. The order of the factors matters,
the field does not.}

\begin{lemma}[filled loops]\label{lem:loopfill}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $g_1,\dots,g_A\in\U(N)$,
\[
s(g_1\cdots g_A)\le A\sum_{j=1}^As(g_j).
\]
\item Every closed path of length $\ell$ in $\Z^4$ has an ordered filling
by at most $\ell(\ell-1)/2$ plaquettes, all in the smallest box that
contains the path.
\item If $C$ has an ordered filling, then $s(V_C)\le A_C\sum_pm_{Cp}\,
s(V_p)$ for every field $V$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Since $I-g_1\cdots g_A=\sum_jg_1\cdots g_{j-1}(I-g_j)$ and the
Hilbert--Schmidt norm is unitarily invariant,
\[
\lVert I-g_1\cdots g_A\rVert_{HS}\le\sum_j\lVert I-g_j\rVert_{HS}.
\]
Square, apply Cauchy--Schwarz and divide by $2N$.

(ii) Write $C$ as a word of unit steps from its base point. Suppose two
consecutive steps $u$, from $x$ to $x+e$, and $v$, from $x+e$ to $x+e+f$,
point in different directions, with $e,f\in\{\pm e_\mu\}$. Let $v'$ be the
step from $x$ to $x+f$ and $u'$ the step from $x+f$ to $x+e+f$. The loop
$uv(u')^{-1}(v')^{-1}$ is the boundary of a plaquette $p$ read from its
corner $x$, so $V_uV_v=V_p^{\pm1}V_{v'}V_{u'}$. If $P$ is the part of $C$
before $u$ and $C'$ is $C$ with $uv$ replaced by $v'u'$, then
\[
V_C=\bigl(V_PV_p^{\pm1}V_P^{-1}\bigr)V_{C'}.
\]
Each exchange of two adjacent steps of different directions therefore puts
one factor of the form~\eqref{eq:filling} in front. Sort the steps by
their direction in this way, keeping the order of the steps of one
direction. The number of exchanges is the number of pairs of steps out of
order, at most $\ell(\ell-1)/2$. The sorted path is a succession of runs
along single lines. Since $C$ is closed, each run returns to its starting
point, and a closed path on a line has holonomy $I$: it contains a step
followed by its reverse, which cancel. So $V_C$ is the product of the
factors. The new corner $x+f$ has each coordinate equal to the coordinate
of $x$ or of $x+e+f$, so every path in the process, and every plaquette,
stays in the smallest box containing $C$.

(iii) Apply (i) to~\eqref{eq:filling}; conjugation and inversion do not
change $s$.
\end{proof}

At $V_0\in G^K$, with the links off $K$ fixed, write $D_pw=\frac d{dt}
V_p(V_0e^{tw})|_{t=0}$ for the derivative of the holonomy of $p$. If $V_0$
is flat on $p$, that is $V_{0,p}=I$, then $D_pw\in\g$, and changing the
corner from which $p$ is read conjugates $D_pw$ and leaves $\lVert D_pw
\rVert$ unchanged. At $V_0=I$, $D_pw=\pm(dw)_p$, so $\sum_p\lVert D_pw
\rVert^2=Q_1(w)$.

\begin{proposition}[loop remainders at flat backgrounds]\label{prop:flatloops}
Let $R(V)=\sum_Cr_C\,s(V_C)$, a sum over closed coarse paths $C$, each with a
chosen ordered filling, such that
\[
\mathcal L=\sup_p\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert A_Cm_{Cp}<\infty
\]
and the series converges with its first two derivatives near $V_0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\lvert R(V)\rvert\le\mathcal L\sum_ps(V_p)$ for every field $V$,
including large fields.
\item If $V_0$ is flat on every plaquette of the fillings, then $\nabla R(0)
=0$ and, in the coordinates $V_0e^\omega$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess R(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le\frac{\mathcal L}N\sum_p\lVert D_pw
\rVert^2\qquad(w\in\g^K).
\]
\item Under (ii), $\Hess R(0)[w,d_{V_0}\eta]=0$ for every $w$ and every
$\eta\in\g^{W^\circ}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) By Lemma~\ref{lem:loopfill}(iii),
\[
\lvert R(V)\rvert\le\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert A_C\sum_pm_{Cp}s(V_p),
\]
and the order of the nonnegative sums may be exchanged.

(ii) For a $C^2$ path $g(t)$ in $\U(N)$ with $g(0)=I$, differentiating
$s(g)=\frac1{2N}\lVert I-g\rVert_{HS}^2$ twice gives
\[
\frac d{dt}s(g(t))\Big|_0=0,\qquad\frac{d^2}{dt^2}s(g(t))\Big|_0=\frac1N
\lVert\dot g(0)\rVert_{HS}^2.
\]
Along $V(t)=V_0e^{tw}$ every factor of~\eqref{eq:filling} equals $I$ at
$t=0$, so $V_C(0)=I$, and the derivative of the product is the sum of the
derivatives of the factors. Since $V_{p_j}(0)=I$, the derivatives of $h_j$
and of $h_j^{-1}$ cancel, and
\[
\dot V_C(0)=\sum_{j=1}^{A_C}\epsilon_j\,h_j(0)\,D_{p_j}w\,h_j(0)^{-1}.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{split}
\frac{d^2}{dt^2}s(V_C(t))\Big|_0&=\frac1N\lVert\dot V_C(0)\rVert^2\le
\frac1N\Bigl(\sum_j\lVert D_{p_j}w\rVert\Bigr)^2\\
&\le\frac{A_C}N\sum_pm_{Cp}\lVert D_pw\rVert^2.
\end{split}
\]
In the coordinates $\omega$ the path is the line
$\omega=tw$, so this second derivative is $\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]$, and the
first derivative vanishes. Summing with the weights $\lvert r_C\rvert$ gives
(ii).

(iii) $R$ is $\Gamma_W$-invariant: a gauge transformation conjugates $V_C$
by its value at the base point. Since $\nabla R(0)=0$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(i) gives (iii).
\end{proof}

The flat backgrounds include the pure gauges $V_{0,y,\mu}=g_yg_{y+e_\mu}
^{-1}$, whose links may be far from $I$.

\begin{corollary}[one step with a loop remainder]\label{cor:loopstep}
Let $U=I$, so that $V_0=I$, and let $A=A_0+R$ near $0$, where $\Hess A_0(0)
[\sigma,\sigma]=2\lambda S_W(\sigma)$ for $\sigma\in\mathcal O^\perp$ and
$R$ is as in Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}, with all its paths and
fillings in the box $\Lambda$, and $\mathcal L\le N\lambda\varepsilon$.
Then the error $E$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} vanishes on $\g^K\times
\mathcal O$ and
\[
\begin{split}
\lvert E(w,w)\rvert&\le\lambda\varepsilon Q_1(w)+\delta_G\lvert\Pi w
\rvert^2\le\varepsilon''\cdot2\lambda S_W(w),\\
\varepsilon''&=\Bigl(\varepsilon+\frac{\delta_GC_n}\lambda\Bigr)
\frac1{2c_*}.
\end{split}
\]
For $\SU(2)$, $\lambda=10^{100}$ and $\varepsilon=1.63\cdot10^{-9}$,
$\varepsilon''\le5.60\cdot10^{-9}$ for $n\le10^{40}$ and $\varepsilon''\le
0.1$ for $n\le9.2\cdot10^{49}$, against $n\le8455$ under (H).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Part (i) of Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} does not use (H). As in its
part (ii),
\[
E(w,w)=\Hess R(0)[\Pi w,\Pi w]+\frac1{12}\sum_k\Tr\bigl(\operatorname
{ad}_{(\Pi w)_k}^2\bigr),
\]
since the term of $A_0$ is $2\lambda S_W(\Pi w)=2\lambda S_W(w)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}(ii) at $V_0=I$ bounds
the first term by $\lambda\varepsilon Q_1(\Pi w)$, and $Q_1(\Pi w)=Q_1(w)$
because $Q_1$ is positive semidefinite and vanishes on $\mathcal O$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(i)). The second term is at most $\delta_G|\Pi
w|^2\le\delta_GC_nQ_1(w)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(ii), and $Q_1\le
S_W/c_*$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iii). The numbers follow from $2c_*>
0.29131$ and $C_n\le\frac54+n^2/\pi^2$.
\end{proof}

Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep}(iii) and Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep} do not
conflict. The function $F$ there has the error $\frac12\lambda\varepsilon
|\sigma|^2$ in the slice variable, a sum over links that is not a function
of loops. The Hessian of a loop remainder at a flat background is a sum of
squares of combinations of the curvature derivatives $D_pw$, so $Q_1$
itself controls it.

\begin{remark}[what the loop bound does not give]\label{rem:valueshessians}
The bound has three limits.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Winding loops.} On the whole coarse torus of side $L$, a loop
winding around the torus has no filling. Take the field with $V_{y,\mu}=I$
for $\mu\ne0$ and
\[
V_{y,0}=g=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(e^{i\pi/2L},e^{-i\pi/2L}\bigr)\in\SU(2).
\]
Every plaquette holonomy is $I$, while the loop along direction $0$ has
holonomy $g^L=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$, and $s(g^L)=1$. No bound of $s(V_C)$ by a
multiple of the plaquette action holds for it. In the box $\Lambda$ every
closed path has a filling, by Lemma~\ref{lem:loopfill}(ii).
\item \emph{Values are not Hessians.} For $\SU(2)$, $m\in4\mathbb N$ and
$g(\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta})$, the function
$R_m(g(\theta))=\epsilon(1-\cos\theta)\cos(m\theta)$ is a class function,
smooth because $\cos(m\theta)=T_m(\frac12\Tr g)$ with $T_m$ the Chebyshev
polynomial. It satisfies $\lvert R_m\rvert\le\epsilon s$ everywhere, while
\[
\frac{d^2}{d\theta^2}R_m(g(\theta))\Big|_{\theta=\pi/2}=-\epsilon m^2,
\]
since $\cos\frac{m\pi}2=1$ and $\sin\frac{m\pi}2=0$. Composed with one
plaquette holonomy it is a gauge-invariant action term with a relative
bound on its values and an unbounded Hessian at a background where that
plaquette has holonomy $g(\pi/2)$. A relative bound on the values of the
remainder therefore gives no Hessian bound at curved backgrounds; part (ii)
of Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops} uses flatness through $V_C(0)=I$.
\item \emph{The representation.} The induced action is not shown here to be
a series of filled loops with small $\mathcal L$. Its determinants and
coarea factors are not of this form as they stand, and the Haar term
$\delta_G$ keeps the factor $C_n$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\emph{Curved backgrounds.} Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}(ii) uses
flatness through $V_C(0)=I$, and Remark~\ref{rem:valueshessians}(b) shows
that a bound on values cannot replace it. A bound on the coefficients can.
At a background whose plaquettes lie within $\kappa$ of $I$, the Hessian of
a loop remainder is bounded by a covariant plaquette form plus a Euclidean
term of order $\kappa$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}). On the window
the Euclidean term costs a factor of order $\kappa n^2$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv}), and this order is attained
(Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}). Measured by the action of the
background on the window, the loss is of order $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ for
every $n$, and this order is attained as well
(Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}, Corollary~\ref{cor:actionsharp}).
Norms of matrices in $\U(N)$ are operator norms in this part.

For a path $\gamma$ and $w\in\g^K$, extended by zero, let
\[
Z_\gamma(w)=\frac d{dt}\Big|_{t=0}V_\gamma(V_0)^{-1}V_\gamma(V_0e^{tw})
\in\g
\]
be the derivative of its holonomy at $V_0$, trivialised on the left. If
$\gamma$ makes the steps $k_1,\dots,k_\ell$ with orientations $\epsilon_i
=\pm1$, then $(V_ke^{tw_k})^{-1}=V_k^{-1}e^{-t\operatorname{Ad}(V_k)w_k}$
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pathexp}
V_\gamma(V_0e^{tw})=V_\gamma(V_0)\,e^{tY_1}\cdots e^{tY_\ell},\qquad
Z_\gamma(w)=\sum_iY_i,
\end{equation}
where $Y_i=\operatorname{Ad}(s_i^{-1})w_{k_i}$ if $\epsilon_i=1$, $Y_i=
-\operatorname{Ad}(s_i^{-1}V_{0,k_i})w_{k_i}$ if $\epsilon_i=-1$, and
$s_i$ is the holonomy at $V_0$ of the part of $\gamma$ after its $i$-th
step. In particular $\lVert Y_i\rVert=\lVert w_{k_i}\rVert$. For a
plaquette $p$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, $\mu<\nu$, with base point $x$,
$Z_p$ is taken along $(x,\mu)$, $(x+e_\mu,\nu)$, $(x+e_\nu,\mu)^{-1}$,
$(x,\nu)^{-1}$, and
\[
Q^{V_0}(w)=\sum_p\lVert Z_p(w)\rVert^2
\]
is the \emph{covariant plaquette form} at $V_0$. If $V_{0,p}=I$, then
$Z_p(w)=D_pw$; in particular $Q^I=Q_1$. A filling~\eqref{eq:filling} is in
\emph{normal form} if every $V_{p_j}$ is read from the base point of $p_j$
in this order. Reading $p$ from another corner, or in the other direction,
conjugates $V_p$ by the holonomy of at most two of its links and may invert
it, so every ordered filling is brought to normal form by lengthening each
$h_j$ by at most two links. For a closed path $C$ with a filling in normal
form let $\ell_C$ be its length, $n_{Ck}$ the number of its steps along the
link $k$, $T_C=\sum_j\ell(h_j)$ the total length of the paths $h_j$, and
$t_{Ck}$ the number of their steps along $k$.

\begin{lemma}[a filled loop at a curved background]\label{lem:curvedloop}
Let $C$ be a closed path with an ordered filling in normal form, and let
$\lVert I-V_{0,p_j}\rVert\le\kappa$ for every $j$. In the coordinates
$V_0e^\omega$, for every $w\in\g^K$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item with $Z_C=Z_C(w)$,
\[
\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]=-\frac1N\ReTr\Bigl(V_C(V_0)\Bigl(Z_C^2+\sum_{i<i'}
[Y_i,Y_{i'}]\Bigr)\Bigr);
\]
\item $\lVert Z_C\rVert\le\sum_j\lVert Z_{p_j}\rVert+2\kappa\sum_j\lVert
Z_{h_j}\rVert$;
\item the second derivative differs from $\frac1N\lVert Z_C\rVert^2$ by
\[
\begin{split}
\Bigl\lvert\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]&-\frac1N\lVert Z_C\rVert^2\Bigr\rvert\\
&\le\frac{A_C\kappa}N\Bigl(\lVert Z_C\rVert^2+\ell_C\sum_kn_{Ck}\lVert w_k
\rVert^2\Bigr);
\end{split}
\]
\item with $a_C=(1+\kappa)(1+A_C\kappa)$,
\[
\begin{split}
\bigl\lvert\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert&\le\frac{a_CA_C}N\sum_pm_{Cp}
\lVert Z_p\rVert^2\\
&\quad+\frac\kappa N\sum_k\bigl(A_C\ell_Cn_{Ck}+4a_CT_Ct_{Ck}\bigr)
\lVert w_k\rVert^2 .
\end{split}
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) By~\eqref{eq:pathexp}, $V_C(V_0e^{tw})=V_C(V_0)E(t)$ with $E(t)=
e^{tY_1}\cdots e^{tY_\ell}$, so $E(0)=I$ and
