\[
E''(0)=\sum_iY_i^2+2\sum_{i<i'}Y_iY_{i'}=Z_C^2+\sum_{i<i'}[Y_i,Y_{i'}].
\]
Differentiate $s(g)=1-\frac1N\ReTr g$ twice.

(ii) The identity~\eqref{eq:filling} holds for every field, so it may be
differentiated. Let $Z(g)$ denote the left-trivialised derivative of a
holonomy~$g$. Then $Z(h^{-1})=-\operatorname{Ad}(h)Z(h)$ and
\[
Z(G_1\cdots G_A)=\sum_j\operatorname{Ad}\bigl((G_{j+1}\cdots G_A)^{-1}
\bigr)Z(G_j).
\]
For $G=hVh^{-1}$ these give
\[
Z(G)=\operatorname{Ad}(h)Z(V)+\operatorname{Ad}(h)\bigl(\operatorname{Ad}
(V^{-1})-1\bigr)Z(h).
\]
Take $G_j=h_jV_{p_j}^{\epsilon_j}h_j^{-1}$. Then $\lVert Z(V_{p_j}^{
\epsilon_j})\rVert=\lVert Z_{p_j}\rVert$, and $\lVert\operatorname{Ad}(g)
-1\rVert\le2\lVert I-g\rVert$ for unitary $g$, since $\operatorname{Ad}(g)
x-x=(g-I)xg^{-1}+x(g^{-1}-I)$. As $\operatorname{Ad}$ is isometric, (ii)
follows.

(iii) Put $M=V_C(V_0)-I$. Each factor of~\eqref{eq:filling} has $\lVert I
-G_j\rVert=\lVert I-V_{0,p_j}\rVert\le\kappa$, so the telescoping sum in
the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:loopfill}(i) gives $\lVert M\rVert\le A_C
\kappa$. Since $-\Tr Z_C^2=\lVert Z_C\rVert^2$ and $\Tr[Y,Y']=0$, part (i)
gives
\[
\begin{split}
\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]&-\frac1N\lVert Z_C\rVert^2\\
&=-\frac1N\ReTr\Bigl(M\Bigl(Z_C^2+\sum_{i<i'}[Y_i,Y_{i'}]\Bigr)\Bigr).
\end{split}
\]
With $\lvert\Tr(MX)\rvert\le\lVert M\rVert\,\lVert X\rVert_1$, $\lVert
Z_C^2\rVert_1=\lVert Z_C\rVert^2$, $\lVert[Y,Y']\rVert_1\le2\lVert Y\rVert
\lVert Y'\rVert$ and
\[
2\sum_{i<i'}\lVert Y_i\rVert\lVert Y_{i'}\rVert\le\Bigl(\sum_i\lVert
w_{k_i}\rVert\Bigr)^2\le\ell_C\sum_kn_{Ck}\lVert w_k\rVert^2,
\]
(iii) follows.

(iv) By (ii) and $(a+b)^2\le(1+\kappa)a^2+(1+\kappa^{-1})b^2$,
\[
\lVert Z_C\rVert^2\le(1+\kappa)A_C\sum_pm_{Cp}\lVert Z_p\rVert^2+4\kappa
(1+\kappa)\Bigl(\sum_j\lVert Z_{h_j}\rVert\Bigr)^2,
\]
and $\bigl(\sum_j\lVert Z_{h_j}\rVert\bigr)^2\le\bigl(\sum_kt_{Ck}\lVert
w_k\rVert\bigr)^2\le T_C\sum_kt_{Ck}\lVert w_k\rVert^2$; for $\kappa=0$ the
first bound follows from (ii) directly. Insert this in (iii).
\end{proof}

The Euclidean term is converted with the gap of $Q^{V_0}$ off the gauge
directions, which depends on the curvature alone.

\begin{lemma}[the window at small curvature]\label{lem:smallcurv}
Let $\Lambda'=\prod_\nu[a_\nu-1,a_\nu+n]$, and suppose that $\lVert I-
V_{0,p}\rVert\le\kappa$ for every plaquette $p$ with its corners in
$\Lambda'$, the links off $K$ included. Put $\delta=3(n+1)\kappa$ and
$\varrho_0=C_n^{1/2}/(1-2\delta/s_n)$, and suppose $2\delta<s_n$ and
$\gamma_\kappa=\sqrt{432}\,\delta\varrho_0<1$. Then
\[
|u|^2\le\varrho_n(\kappa)^2\,Q^{V_0}(u)\quad(u\in\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp),
\qquad\varrho_n(\kappa)=\frac{\varrho_0}{1-\gamma_\kappa}.
\]
If $\kappa(n+2)^2\le10^{-2}$, the hypotheses hold and $\varrho_n(\kappa)^2
\le2.31\,C_n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A gauge transformation $g\in G^{\Lambda'}$ acts on the links of $\Lambda'$
by $(gV)_{y,\mu}=g_yV_{y,\mu}g_{y+e_\mu}^{-1}$. Let $(Tw)_{y,\mu}=
\operatorname{Ad}(g_{y+e_\mu})w_{y,\mu}$, an isometry of $\g^K$. Then
$(gV_0)e^{Tw}=g(V_0e^w)$, so $Z_p$ at $gV_0$ in the direction $Tw$ is
$\operatorname{Ad}(g_x)Z_p(w)$, $x$ the base point of $p$, and $Q^{gV_0}(Tw)
=Q^{V_0}(w)$. Also $d_{gV_0}(\operatorname{Ad}(g)\eta)=Td_{V_0}\eta$, so $T$
maps $\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$ onto $\mathcal O_{gV_0}^\perp$, and the
plaquette holonomies are conjugated. The statement for $gV_0$ therefore
gives it for $V_0$.

The links $(x,\mu)$ of $\Lambda'$ with $x_\nu=a_\nu-1$ for every $\nu<\mu$
form a spanning tree of $\Lambda'$, so $g$ can be chosen with $gV_0=I$ on
them; write $V_0$ for $gV_0$. Let $(x,\mu)$ be another link of $\Lambda'$,
and $\nu<\mu$ the least direction with $x_\nu\ge a_\nu$. The plaquette $p$
in the plane $\{\nu,\mu\}$ with base point $x-e_\nu$ has its corners in
$\Lambda'$, and its two links of direction $\nu$ lie in the tree, since
their coordinates below $\nu$ are those of $x$. So $V_{0,p}=V_{0,x,\mu}
V_{0,x-e_\nu,\mu}^{-1}$ and $\lVert I-V_{0,x,\mu}\rVert\le\kappa+\lVert I-
V_{0,x-e_\nu,\mu}\rVert$. Induction on $\sum_{\nu<\mu}(x_\nu-a_\nu+1)\le\mu
(n+1)$ gives $\lVert I-V_{0,k}\rVert\le\delta$ for every link $k$ of
$\Lambda'$.

Then $\lVert\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,k}^{-1})-1\rVert\le2\delta<s_n$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedwindow} gives $|u|\le\varrho_0Q_1(u)^{1/2}$ on
$\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$. By~\eqref{eq:pathexp}, $Z_p(u)-(du)_p=\sum_i\pm
(\operatorname{Ad}(g_i)-1)u_{k_i}$, where $g_i$ is a holonomy of three, two,
two and one links of $p$ for $i=1,\dots,4$. Hence $\lVert Z_p(u)-(du)_p
\rVert\le2\delta(3b_1+2b_2+2b_3+b_4)$ with $b_i=\lVert u_{k_i}\rVert$, and
its square is at most $72\delta^2\sum_ib_i^2$. A link lies in six
plaquettes, so
\[
\begin{split}
Q_1(u)^{1/2}&\le Q^{V_0}(u)^{1/2}+\sqrt{432}\,\delta|u|,\\
|u|&\le\varrho_0Q^{V_0}(u)^{1/2}+\gamma_\kappa|u|.
\end{split}
\]
For the numbers, $s_n\ge2/n$ and $C_n\le1+n^2/4\le(n+2)^2/4$ give $2\delta
/s_n\le3n(n+1)\kappa\le0.03$ and $\gamma_\kappa\le\frac{3\sqrt{432}}{2(1-
0.03)}\kappa(n+2)^2\le0.3215$, so $\varrho_n(\kappa)^2\le C_n/(0.97^2
\cdot0.6785^2)\le2.31\,C_n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[loop remainders at curved backgrounds]
\label{prop:curvedloops}
Let $R(V)=\sum_Cr_C\,s(V_C)$, with fillings in normal form, converge with
its first two derivatives near $V_0$. Let $\lVert I-V_{0,p}\rVert\le
\kappa$ for every plaquette of the fillings, and put $a_C=(1+\kappa)(1+
A_C\kappa)$,
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal L_\kappa&=\sup_p\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert\,a_CA_Cm_{Cp},\\
\mathcal M_\kappa&=\sup_k\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert\bigl(A_C\ell_Cn_{Ck}+4a_C
T_Ct_{Ck}\bigr).
\end{split}
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $w\in\g^K$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess R(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le\frac{\mathcal L_\kappa}N
Q^{V_0}(w)+\frac{\kappa\mathcal M_\kappa}N|w|^2.
\]
\item $R$ is $\Gamma_W$-invariant, and $\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)\rvert\le
\frac{\mathcal L_\kappa}NQ^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}w)+\frac{\kappa\mathcal
M_\kappa}N\lvert\Pi_{V_0}w\rvert^2$.
\item Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv},
\[
\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)\rvert\le\frac{\mathcal L_\kappa+\kappa\varrho_n
(\kappa)^2\mathcal M_\kappa}N\,Q^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}w),
\]
and if $\kappa(n+2)^2\le10^{-2}$ the factor is at most $(\mathcal L_\kappa
+0.58\,\kappa(n+2)^2\mathcal M_\kappa)/N$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Sum Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedloop}(iv) with the weights $\lvert r_C\rvert$
and exchange the nonnegative sums. (ii) A gauge transformation in
$\Gamma_W$ fixes the links off $K$ and conjugates $V_C$, so $R$ is
invariant, and Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii) gives $\mathcal HR(w,w)=
\Hess R(0)[\Pi_{V_0}w,\Pi_{V_0}w]$. (iii) Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv} at $u=
\Pi_{V_0}w$, with $2.31\,C_n\le0.58(n+2)^2$.
\end{proof}

The background $V_0$ need not be a critical point of $R$ or of the induced
action: the gradient terms of Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(i) are removed
by the projection, and the bound holds uniformly on the set of fields with
plaquettes within $\kappa$ of $I$, without third derivatives. At $\kappa=0$,
$\mathcal L_0=\mathcal L$ and (i) is Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}(ii).
For the plaquette sum $R=r\sum_ps(V_p)$, $\mathcal L_\kappa=(1+\kappa)^2
\lvert r\rvert$ and $\mathcal M_\kappa=24\lvert r\rvert$, so (iii) gives
the factor $(1+\kappa)^2+14\kappa(n+2)^2$ times $\lvert r\rvert/N$. At
$V_0=I$, $Q^I\circ\Pi=Q_1\le S_W/c_*$. At a curved background the Gaussian
reference is $2\lambda S^U_W\circ\Pi_{V_0}$
(Remark~\ref{rem:relstepinputs}(d)), and its comparison with $Q^{V_0}\circ
\Pi_{V_0}$ is not proved here. The order $\kappa n^2$ of the loss in (iii)
cannot be improved.

\begin{proposition}[the loss $\kappa n^2$ is attained]
\label{prop:curvedsharp}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $a_\nu=1$, $X_j=i\sigma_j/\sqrt2$, $0<\alpha\le\pi/4$ and
$\varsigma=\pm1$. On the links of $\Lambda'$ let $V_{0,x,0}=A=\cos\alpha+
i\sigma_1\sin\alpha$, $V_{0,x,1}=B=\cos\alpha+\varsigma i\sigma_2\sin
\alpha$ and $V_{0,x,2}=V_{0,x,3}=I$. The plaquettes in the plane $\{0,1\}$
have holonomy $ABA^{-1}B^{-1}$, with $\lVert I-ABA^{-1}B^{-1}\rVert=2\sin^2
\alpha=\kappa$, and the others have holonomy $I$. Let $\phi(j)=\sin(\pi j/
(n+1))$ for $1\le j\le n$, $\phi(j)=0$ otherwise, and for $y\in W$
\[
u_{y,0}=\phi(y_1)\phi(y_2)\phi(y_3)X_1,\qquad u_{y,1}=\phi(y_0)\phi(y_2)
\phi(y_3)X_2,
\]
with $u=0$ on the other links. Let $P=\sum_ps(V_p)$ over the plaquettes of
$\Lambda'$. Then $u\in\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$, $\mathcal HP(u,u)=\Hess
P(0)[u,u]$, and for $n\ge9$ and $\sin^2\alpha\le10^{-2}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item if $\varsigma=1$ and $\kappa(n+1)^2\le2$, then $\mathcal HP(u,u)\ge
\bigl(1+0.037\,\kappa(n+1)^2\bigr)\frac12Q^{V_0}(u)$;
\item if $\varsigma=-1$ and $\kappa(n+1)^2\ge31$, then $\mathcal HP(u,u)<0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $s=\sin\alpha$, $c=\cos\alpha$, $x=\pi/(2n+2)$ and $\Psi=((n+1)/2)^2$.
Then $\sum_j\phi(j)^2=(n+1)/2$, $\sum_j\phi(j)\phi(j+1)=\cos(2x)(n+1)/2$
and $\sum_j\phi(j)=\cot x$.

$\operatorname{Ad}(A)$ is the rotation by $2\alpha$ about $X_1$ and
$\operatorname{Ad}(B)$ the rotation by $2\varsigma\alpha$ about $X_2$; in
particular $\operatorname{Ad}(A)X_1=X_1$ and $\operatorname{Ad}(B)X_2=X_2$.
The adjoint of $d_{V_0}$ is $(d_{V_0}^*u)_y=\sum_\mu(\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,
y,\mu})u_{y,\mu}-u_{y-e_\mu,\mu})$, so for $y\in W^\circ$
\[
(d_{V_0}^*u)_y=(u_{y,0}-u_{y-e_0,0})+(u_{y,1}-u_{y-e_1,1})=0,
\]
because $u_{\cdot,0}$ does not depend on $y_0$ nor $u_{\cdot,1}$ on $y_1$ in
$W$. So $\Pi_{V_0}u=u$, and $\mathcal HP(u,u)=\Hess P(0)[u,u]$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii). The real part of the commutator
$ABA^{-1}B^{-1}$ of unit quaternions with orthogonal axes is $1-2s^4$, so
its eigenvalues $e^{\pm i\vartheta}$ have $1-\cos\vartheta=2s^4$ and
$\lVert I-ABA^{-1}B^{-1}\rVert=(2-2\cos\vartheta)^{1/2}=2s^2$.

In the plane $\{0,\nu\}$, $\nu\ge2$, with coefficients $f,f'$ of $u$ on
$(z,0)$, $(z+e_\nu,0)$, the holonomy along $V_0e^{tu}$ is $Ae^{t(f-f')X_1}
A^{-1}$. So $Z_p=(du)_p$, and the Hessian of $s(V_p)$ is $\frac12(f-f')^2=
\frac12\lVert(du)_p\rVert^2$. The same holds in the planes $\{1,\nu\}$, and
$u$ vanishes in the plane $\{2,3\}$. In the plane $\{0,1\}$ let $f$, $g'$,
$f'$, $g$ be the coefficients of $u$ on $(z,0)$, $(z+e_0,1)$, $(z+e_1,0)$,
$(z,1)$, and $F=f+f'$, $G=g+g'$. By~\eqref{eq:pathexp},
\[
\begin{gathered}
Y_1=f\operatorname{Ad}(BAB^{-1})X_1,\quad Y_2=g'\operatorname{Ad}(BA)X_2,\\
Y_3=-f'\operatorname{Ad}(B)X_1,\quad Y_4=-gX_2 .
\end{gathered}
\]
In the basis $X_1,X_2,X_3$, with $c_2=\cos2\alpha$, $s_2=\sin2\alpha$, these
are $f(c_2^2+c_2s_2^2,-\varsigma s_2^2,\varsigma s_2c_2(1-c_2))$, $g'(
\varsigma s_2^2,c_2,-s_2c_2)$, $-f'(c_2,0,\varsigma s_2)$ and $-g(0,1,0)$.
Their inner products give
\[
\lVert Z_p\rVert^2=(f-f')^2+(g-g')^2+4s^2(ff'+gg')+8\varsigma s^2c^2fg .
\]
Write $ABA^{-1}B^{-1}=(1-2s^4)I+\hat C$ with $\hat C\in\g$; its
coordinates are $2\sqrt2s^2(sc,-\varsigma sc,-\varsigma c^2)$. Since $Z^2=
-\frac12\lVert Z\rVert^2I$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedloop}(i) gives
\[
\Hess s(V_p)(0)[u,u]=\bigl(\tfrac12-s^4\bigr)\lVert Z_p\rVert^2+\tfrac12
\Bigl\langle\hat C,\sum_{i<i'}[Y_i,Y_{i'}]\Bigr\rangle,
\]
and the six triple products $\ip{\hat C}{[Y_i,Y_{i'}]}=-\sqrt2\det(\hat C,
Y_i,Y_{i'})$ add up to
\[
\begin{split}
\Hess s(V_p)(0)[u,u]&=\tfrac12\lVert Z_p\rVert^2-s^4(F^2+G^2)\\
&\quad+2\varsigma s^2c^2(FG-2fg).
\end{split}
\]
Both are identities between polynomials in $c$, $s$, $f$, $f'$, $g$, $g'$
modulo $c^2+s^2=1$.

Over the plaquettes of the plane $\{0,1\}$, $\sum ff'=\sum gg'=\frac12n(n+1)
\cos(2x)\Psi$, $\sum fg=\cot^2x\,\Psi$, $\sum FG=\sigma^2\Psi$ with $\sigma
=\sum_{j=1}^n(\phi(j)+\phi(j+1))=2\cot x-\sin2x$, and $\sum(F^2+G^2)=4n(n+1)
\cos^2x\,\Psi$. Also $|u|^2=n(n+1)\Psi$, and as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iv), $Q_1(u)=12\sin^2x\,|u|^2$. Hence
\[
\begin{split}
Q^{V_0}(u)&=Q_1(u)+\Psi s^2\bigl(4n(n+1)\cos2x\\
&\quad+8\varsigma c^2\cot^2x\bigr),\\
\Hess P(0)[u,u]&=\tfrac12Q^{V_0}(u)-4s^4n(n+1)\cos^2x\,\Psi\\
&\quad+2\varsigma s^2c^2(\sigma^2-2\cot^2x)\Psi .
\end{split}
\]
From $\tan x\ge x$ and $\cos x\ge1-x^2/2$, $x^{-2}-1\le\cot^2x\le x^{-2}$;
and $\sigma^2-2\cot^2x=2\cot^2x-8\cos^2x+\sin^22x\ge2x^{-2}-10$. Also
$\frac12Q_1(u)=6\sin^2x\,n(n+1)\Psi\le\frac32\pi^2\Psi$. Put $t=s^2(n+1)^2
=\frac12\kappa(n+1)^2$, so that $s^2x^{-2}=4t/\pi^2$, and use $n\ge9$ and
$s^2\le10^{-2}$.

(i) Here
\[
\begin{split}
&\Hess P(0)[u,u]-\tfrac12Q^{V_0}(u)\\
&\qquad\ge\Psi t\Bigl(c^2\Bigl(\frac{16}{\pi^2}-\frac{20}{(n+1)^2}\Bigr)
-4s^2\Bigr)\ge1.3669\,\Psi t,\\
&\tfrac12Q^{V_0}(u)\le\Psi\Bigl(\frac{3\pi^2}2+t\Bigl(2+\frac{16}{\pi^2}
\Bigr)\Bigr)\le18.43\,\Psi
\end{split}
\]
for $t\le1$. The ratio is at least $0.0741\,t\ge0.037\,\kappa(n+1)^2$.

(ii) Here, dropping the term in $s^4$,
\[
\begin{split}
\Hess P(0)[u,u]&\le\Psi\Bigl(\frac{3\pi^2}2+t\Bigl(2-\frac{32c^2}{\pi^2}
\Bigr)+24s^2c^2\Bigr)\\
&\le\Psi\Bigl(\frac{3\pi^2}2-0.9698\,t\Bigr),
\end{split}
\]
which is negative for $2t\ge31$. The constants follow from $c^2\ge0.99$,
$s^2\le t/100$ and $9.8696<\pi^2<9.8697$: in (i), $0.99(1.62112-0.2)-0.04\ge
1.3669$ and $14.805+3.622\le18.43$; in (ii), $2-31.68/9.8697+0.24\le
-0.9698$ and $14.805/0.9698<15.27$.
\end{proof}

For $R=rP$ with $r>0$, part (i) gives $\mathcal HR(u,u)\ge(1+0.037\,\kappa
(n+1)^2)\frac{\mathcal L}NQ^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}u)$, against the factor $(1+
\kappa)^2+14\kappa(n+2)^2$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(iii):
the loss is of order $\kappa n^2$ in both. Part (ii) says more. Once
$\kappa(n+1)^2\ge31$, the covariant Hessian of the coarse plaquette action
has a negative direction off the gauge directions, so it obeys no
comparison with a positive semidefinite gauge-invariant form there (Fig.~\ref{fig:curvedsharp}). This is
the lattice form of the unstable mode of Nielsen and Olesen~\cite{NO78} in
a constant chromomagnetic field. The comparison asked for in
Remark~\ref{rem:relstepinputs}(d) must therefore lose a multiple of $\kappa
\lvert\cdot\rvert^2$, and on a window of side $n$ it is a relative bound
only while $\kappa n^2$ is small.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_curvedsharp.png}
\caption{The ratio of the covariant Hessian of the plaquette action to half
the covariant plaquette form at the field $u$ and the background of
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}, from the closed forms in its proof.
(a) The ratio over the window side $n$ and $\kappa(n+1)^2$, for the two
orientations $\varsigma=\pm1$. (b) The section $n=63$: for $\varsigma=+1$
the ratio exceeds one, above the bound of part (i), dashed; for
$\varsigma=-1$ it changes sign near $\kappa(n+1)^2=23$, below the
threshold $31$ of part (ii).}
\label{fig:curvedsharp}
\end{figure*}

\emph{Curvature in the action.} The loss $\kappa n^2$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(iii) comes from the supremum $\kappa$ of
the curvature and from the gap $C_n$ of the window in $\ell^2$. In four
dimensions the Euclidean term can be paid instead with the $\ell^2$ norm of
the curvature, the square root of the Wilson action of the background, and
an $\ell^4$ bound on the field, which holds on the window with a constant
independent of $n$. For a plaquette $p$ write $\kappa_p=\lVert I-V_{0,p}
\rVert$, the operator norm, which does not depend on the corner from which
$p$ is read or on its orientation, and put
\[
\lVert\kappa\rVert_2=\Bigl(\sum_p\kappa_p^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\le\Bigl(2N\sum_p
s(V_{0,p})\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
the sums over the plaquettes with their corners in the box $\Lambda'=
\prod_\nu[a_\nu-1,a_\nu+n]$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv}; the inequality is
$\kappa_p\le\lVert I-V_{0,p}\rVert_{HS}$. For $w\in\g^K$ put $\lvert w
\rvert_4=(\sum_k\lVert w_k\rVert^4)^{1/4}$. As in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}, a link $(y,\mu)\in K$ is inner when $y_\nu>a_\nu$
for every $\nu\ne\mu$, and a face link otherwise.

The $\ell^4$ bound rests on an inequality of Gagliardo type. For finite
sets $X_1,\dots,X_d$, $d\ge2$, and $x\in\prod_iX_i$, let $\hat x_i$ be $x$
with its $i$-th coordinate removed. If $F_i\ge0$ are functions of $\hat
x_i$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gagliardo}
\sum_x\prod_{i=1}^dF_i(\hat x_i)^{\frac1{d-1}}\le\prod_{i=1}^d\Bigl(
\sum_{\hat x_i}F_i(\hat x_i)\Bigr)^{\frac1{d-1}}.
\end{equation}
For $d=2$ both sides equal $\sum F_1\sum F_2$. For $d\ge3$, sum first over
$x_d$, on which $F_d$ does not depend. H\"older's inequality with $d-1$
factors bounds $\sum_{x_d}\prod_{i<d}F_i^{1/(d-1)}$ by $\prod_{i<d}
G_i^{1/(d-1)}$, where $G_i=\sum_{x_d}F_i$ does not depend on $x_i$ or
$x_d$. H\"older's inequality with the exponents $d-1$ and $(d-1)/(d-2)$ in
the remaining variables, and~\eqref{eq:gagliardo} for $d-1$ applied to the
$G_i$, give the claim, since $\sum G_i=\sum F_i$.

\begin{lemma}[a Sobolev inequality on the window]\label{lem:windowsobolev}
Let $n\ge2$, fix $\mu$, and let $B_\mu$ be the set of $y$ with $a_\mu\le
y_\mu\le a_\mu+n-1$ and $a_\nu+1\le y_\nu\le a_\nu+n-1$ for $\nu\ne\mu$. For
$f\colon B_\mu\to[0,\infty)$, extended by zero, let $E_\mu(f)$ be the sum
of $(f(y+e_\nu)-f(y))^2$ over the pairs $(y,y+e_\nu)$, $\nu\ne\mu$, that
meet $B_\mu$, and over the pairs $(y,y+e_\mu)$ in $B_\mu$. Then
\[
\Bigl(\sum_yf(y)^4\Bigr)^{1/2}\le c_S\,E_\mu(f),\qquad c_S=\Bigl(\frac{27}
{32}\Bigr)^{1/2}<0.9186 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put $g=f^3$, $\Phi=(\sum f^4)^{1/2}$, $a_\nu^2$ for the part of
$E_\mu(f)$ in the direction $\nu$, and $b=a_\mu$. In a direction $\nu\ne
\mu$ a line of $B_\mu$ has $n-1$ points and $g$ vanishes at its two ends
outside $B_\mu$. Summing the differences of $g$ from either end gives $g(y)
\le F_\nu(\hat y_\nu)=\frac12h_\nu(\hat y_\nu)$, where $h_\nu$ is the sum of
$\lvert g(z+e_\nu)-g(z)\rvert$ over the $n$ pairs of the line. In the
direction $\mu$ a line has $n$ points, and $g(y)\le g(z)+h_\mu$ for every
$z$ on it, where $h_\mu$ is the sum over its $n-1$ pairs; averaging over
$z$ gives $g(y)\le F_\mu(\hat y_\mu)=\frac1n\sum_zg(z)+h_\mu(\hat y_\mu)$.

For $s,t\ge0$, $\lvert s^3-t^3\rvert\le\frac32\lvert s-t\rvert(s^2+t^2)$,
and each point of a line is an end of at most two of its pairs. By
Cauchy--Schwarz and $(s^2+t^2)^2\le2(s^4+t^4)$, the sum of $\lvert g(z+e_
\nu)-g(z)\rvert$ over all pairs in the direction $\nu$ is at most
\[
\frac32a_\nu\Bigl(\sum2\bigl(f(z)^4+f(z+e_\nu)^4\bigr)\Bigr)^{1/2}\le3a_\nu
\Phi .
\]
Fix $\nu_0\ne\mu$. The Dirichlet Laplacian on a line of $n-1$ points has
least eigenvalue $4\sin^2(\pi/2n)\ge4/n^2$, so $\sum f^2\le\frac{n^2}4
a_{\nu_0}^2$, and $\frac1n\sum g\le\frac1n(\sum f^2)^{1/2}\Phi\le\frac12
a_{\nu_0}\Phi$. Hence $\sum F_\nu\le\frac32a_\nu\Phi$ for $\nu\ne\mu$ and
$\sum F_\mu\le(\frac12a_{\nu_0}+3b)\Phi$. Since $f^4=g^{4/3}\le\prod_\rho
F_\rho^{1/3}$, \eqref{eq:gagliardo} with $d=4$ gives
\[
\Phi^2\le\Phi^{4/3}\Bigl(\frac{27}8\,a_{\nu_0}a_{\nu_1}a_{\nu_2}\bigl(
\tfrac12a_{\nu_0}+3b\bigr)\Bigr)^{1/3},
\]
where $\{\nu_0,\nu_1,\nu_2\}$ are the directions other than $\mu$. Let $E=
E_\mu(f)$. Then $a_{\nu_0}^2a_{\nu_1}a_{\nu_2}\le\frac12a_{\nu_0}^2(a_{\nu_1}^2
+a_{\nu_2}^2)\le\frac18E^2$ and $a_{\nu_0}a_{\nu_1}a_{\nu_2}b\le(E/4)^2$, so
$\Phi^2\le\frac{27}8(\frac1{16}+\frac3{16})E^2=\frac{27}{32}E^2$.
\end{proof}

For $v\in\g^K$ and $x$ with $(x,\mu)\in K$, let
\[
(D_\nu v_\mu)(x)=v_{x+e_\nu,\mu}-\operatorname{Ad}\bigl(V_{0,x+e_\mu,\nu}^{
-1}\bigr)v_{x,\mu},
\]
with $v$ extended by zero off $K$. The term $v_{x,\mu}$ is the coordinate
of $V_{0,x,\mu}e^{v_{x,\mu}}$ and transforms at $x+e_\mu$, so $D_\nu v_\mu$
compares two values at $x+e_\mu+e_\nu$; it is the covariant difference of
$v_\mu$ in the direction $\nu$. Since $\operatorname{Ad}$ is isometric,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kato}
\bigl\lvert\lVert v_{x+e_\nu,\mu}\rVert-\lVert v_{x,\mu}\rVert\bigr\rvert
\le\lVert(D_\nu v_\mu)(x)\rVert .
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[the covariant Gaffney inequality]\label{lem:covgaffney}
Let $n\ge2$ and let $v\in\g^K$ vanish on the face links. Let $E_\mu$ be as
in Lemma~\ref{lem:windowsobolev}, $f_\mu(y)=\lVert v_{y,\mu}\rVert$, and for
$k=(y,\mu)$ let $c_k=\sum_{\nu\ne\mu}\kappa_{p(y;\mu,\nu)}$ if $y\in
W^\circ$ and $c_k=0$ otherwise, where $p(y;\mu,\nu)$ is the plaquette at
$y$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$. Then
\[
\sum_\mu E_\mu(f_\mu)\le\sum_{P\text{ inner}}\lVert Z_P(v)\rVert^2+\lvert
d_{V_0}^*v\rvert^2+2\sum_kc_k\lVert v_k\rVert^2,
\]
and $\sum_kc_k^2\le6\lVert\kappa\rVert_2^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The support of $v$ is $\bigcup_\mu B_\mu\times\{\mu\}$. For $\nu\ne\mu$ the
pairs $(x,x+e_\nu)$ of $E_\mu$ are those with $x$ the base of an inner
plaquette in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, and the pairs $(y-e_\mu,y)$ of
$E_\mu$ in the direction $\mu$ are those with $y\in W^\circ$. By
\eqref{eq:kato}, $\sum_\mu E_\mu(f_\mu)$ is at most the covariant energy
$\mathcal E(v)$, the sum of $\lVert(D_\nu v_\mu)(x)\rVert^2$ over the same
pairs.

Let $P$ be the plaquette at $x$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$, $\mu<\nu$, with
links $k_1=(x,\mu)$, $k_2=(x+e_\mu,\nu)$, $k_3=(x+e_\nu,\mu)$, $k_4=(x,
\nu)$, and write $V_i=V_{0,k_i}$. By~\eqref{eq:pathexp},
\[
Z_P(v)=\operatorname{Ad}(V_4V_3)\bigl(\operatorname{Ad}(V_2^{-1})v_{k_1}+
v_{k_2}-v_{k_3}-\operatorname{Ad}(V_3^{-1})v_{k_4}\bigr),
\]
so $\lVert Z_P(v)\rVert=\lVert(D_\nu v_\mu)(x)-(D_\mu v_\nu)(x)\rVert$.
Also $(d_{V_0}^*v)_y=\sum_\mu\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,y,\mu})(D_\mu v_\mu)(y-
e_\mu)$ for $y\in W^\circ$. Expanding the squares,
\[
\sum_{P\text{ inner}}\lVert Z_P(v)\rVert^2+\lvert d_{V_0}^*v\rvert^2=
\mathcal E(v)+2\sum_{\mu<\nu}(\Sigma_{\mu\nu}-\Sigma'_{\mu\nu}),
\]
where, with $a(x)=v_{x,\mu}$, $b(x)=v_{x,\nu}$, $\alpha_y=\operatorname
{Ad}(V_{0,y,\mu})$ and $\beta_y=\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,y,\nu})$,
\[
\begin{split}
\Sigma_{\mu\nu}&=\sum_{y\in W^\circ}\bigl\langle\alpha_ya(y)-a(y-e_\mu),
\beta_yb(y)-b(y-e_\nu)\bigr\rangle,\\
\Sigma'_{\mu\nu}&=\sum_{P\text{ inner}}\bigl\langle(D_\nu v_\mu)(x),(D_\mu
v_\nu)(x)\bigr\rangle .
\end{split}
\]
Each sum has four terms per index. Since $\alpha_{x+e_\nu}=\operatorname
{Ad}(V_3)$ and $\beta_{x+e_\mu}=\operatorname{Ad}(V_2)$, three terms of
$\Sigma$ equal three terms of $\Sigma'$, with the same signs:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ip{\alpha_ya(y)}{b(y-e_\nu)}&=\ip{a(x+e_\nu)}{\alpha_y^{-1}b(x)},\\
\ip{a(y-e_\mu)}{\beta_yb(y)}&=\ip{\beta_y^{-1}a(x)}{b(x+e_\mu)},\\
\ip{a(y-e_\mu)}{b(y-e_\nu)}&=\ip{a(x+e_\nu)}{b(x+e_\mu)},
\end{aligned}
\]
at $y=x+e_\nu$, $y=x+e_\mu$ and $y=x+e_\mu+e_\nu$ respectively. Each of these terms vanishes unless both
its links are inner,
and two inner links in these positions force $y\in W^\circ$ and $P$
inner. For instance $(y,\mu)$ and $(y-e_\nu,\nu)$ inner give $a_\rho<
y_\rho<a_\rho+n$ for $\rho\notin\{\mu,\nu\}$ from either link, $y_\nu\ge
a_\nu+1$ and $y_\nu\le a_\nu+n-1$ from the first, and $a_\mu<y_\mu<a_\mu+
n$ from the second. So these three kinds of terms cancel, and what remains
is
\[
\Sigma_{\mu\nu}-\Sigma'_{\mu\nu}=\sum_{x\in W^\circ}\bigl\langle\bigl(
\operatorname{Ad}(V_4^{-1}V_1)-\operatorname{Ad}(V_3V_2^{-1})\bigr)a(x),
b(x)\bigr\rangle .
\]
Here $(V_3V_2^{-1})^{-1}V_4^{-1}V_1=V_1^{-1}V_{0,P}V_1$, so the operator
has norm $\lVert\operatorname{Ad}(V_1^{-1}V_{0,P}V_1)-1\rVert\le2\kappa_P$,
and $2\lvert\Sigma_{\mu\nu}-\Sigma'_{\mu\nu}\rvert\le2\sum_{x\in W^\circ}
\kappa_P(\lVert a(x)\rVert^2+\lVert b(x)\rVert^2)$. Summed over $\mu<\nu$
this is $2\sum_kc_k\lVert v_k\rVert^2$. Finally $c_k^2\le3\sum_{\nu\ne\mu}
\kappa_{p(y;\mu,\nu)}^2$, and the plaquette $p(y;\mu,\nu)$ enters $c_k$ for
the two links $(y,\mu)$, $(y,\nu)$, so $\sum_kc_k^2\le6\lVert\kappa
\rVert_2^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[the window in $\ell^4$]\label{lem:windowlfour}
Let $n\ge1$, $\theta=\frac92\lVert\kappa\rVert_2<1$ and $u\in\mathcal
O_{V_0}^\perp$. Then
\[
\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le\Bigl(1+\frac{3c_S}{1-\theta}\Bigr)Q^{V_0}(u).
\]
In particular $\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le c_4Q^{V_0}(u)$ with $c_4=1+\frac94
\sqrt6<6.512$ if $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $u=v+f$ with $v$ on the inner links and $f$ on the face links. If
$n=1$ there are no inner links, and $\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le|u|^2=|f|^2\le
Q^{V_0}(u)$ by the face-link plaquettes below. Let $n\ge2$. A link $(y,\mu)$
on which some $d_{V_0}\eta$ is nonzero has $y\in W^\circ$ or $y+e_\mu\in
W^\circ$, and is inner, so $\mathcal O_{V_0}$ lies on the inner links,
$v\perp\mathcal O_{V_0}$ and $d_{V_0}^*v=0$.

As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(ii), each face link $k$ is the
only link in $K$ of a plaquette that is not inner, distinct for distinct
$k$, and for it $\lVert Z_p(u)\rVert=\lVert f_k\rVert$ by~\eqref{eq:pathexp}.
An inner plaquette $P$ contains at most two face links, and a face link
lies in at most one inner plaquette, so $\lVert Z_P(v)\rVert^2\le3(\lVert
Z_P(u)\rVert^2+\sum_{k\in P}\lVert f_k\rVert^2)$, the sum over the face
links of $P$. With $A=\sum_{P\text{ inner}}\lVert Z_P(u)\rVert^2$ and $B=
|f|^2$, this gives $\sum_{P\text{ inner}}\lVert Z_P(v)\rVert^2\le3(A+B)$ and
$A+B\le Q^{V_0}(u)$.

Let $\Phi_\mu=(\sum_y\lVert v_{y,\mu}\rVert^4)^{1/2}$. Then $\lvert v\rvert_
4^2=(\sum_\mu\Phi_\mu^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_\mu\Phi_\mu$, and
Lemmas~\ref{lem:windowsobolev} and~\ref{lem:covgaffney}, with Cauchy--Schwarz
in $\sum_kc_k\lVert v_k\rVert^2$, give
\[
\lvert v\rvert_4^2\le c_S\bigl(3(A+B)+2\sqrt6\,\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\lvert
v\rvert_4^2\bigr).
\]
Since $2\sqrt6\,c_S=\frac92$, $(1-\theta)\lvert v\rvert_4^2\le3c_S(A+B)$.
The supports of $v$ and $f$ are disjoint, so $\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le\lvert v
\rvert_4^2+\lvert f\rvert_4^2$, and $\lvert f\rvert_4^2\le|f|^2=B$. Hence
$\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le\frac{3c_S}{1-\theta}(A+B)+B$. For $\theta\le\frac12$,
$6c_S=\frac94\sqrt6<5.512$.
\end{proof}

For a closed path $C$ with a filling in normal form, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedloop}, let $\kappa_C=\sum_pm_{Cp}\kappa_p$ and $a_C=
(1+\kappa_C)^2$, let $\ell(h_j)$ be the length of the path $h_j$ and
$t_{jk}$ the number of its steps along $k$. For a loop sum $R=\sum_Cr_C\,
s(V_C)$ put
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal L^\sharp&=\sup_p\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert a_CA_Cm_{Cp},\\
\mathcal K(k,p)&=\sum_C\lvert r_C\rvert\Bigl(m_{Cp}\ell_Cn_{Ck}+4a_C\sum_{j
:p_j=p}\ell(h_j)t_{jk}\Bigr),\\
\mathcal N&=\Bigl(\sup_k\sum_p\mathcal K(k,p)\Bigr)^{1/2}\Bigl(\sup_p\sum
_k\mathcal K(k,p)\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\end{split}
\]

\begin{proposition}[loop remainders in the action]\label{prop:actionloops}
Let $R(V)=\sum_Cr_C\,s(V_C)$, with paths and fillings in normal form in
$\Lambda'$, converge with its first two derivatives near $V_0$, with
$\mathcal L^\sharp,\mathcal N<\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $w\in\g^K$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess R(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le\frac{\mathcal L^\sharp}NQ^{V_0}
(w)+\frac{\mathcal N\lVert\kappa\rVert_2}N\lvert w\rvert_4^2 .
\]
\item If $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$, then for every $w\in\g^K$
\[
\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)\rvert\le\frac{\mathcal L^\sharp+c_4\mathcal N
\lVert\kappa\rVert_2}N\,Q^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}w).
\]
\item For the plaquette sum $R=r\sum_ps(V_p)$ over the plaquettes with
their corners in $\Lambda'$, $\mathcal L^\sharp\le\lvert r\rvert(1+\kappa_\infty)
^2$ with $\kappa_\infty=\max_p\kappa_p$, and $\mathcal N=8\sqrt6\lvert r
\rvert$. If $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$, the factor in \textup{(ii)}
is at most $(1+130\lVert\kappa\rVert_2)\lvert r\rvert/N$, for every $n$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Let $C$ be one of the paths and $G_j=h_jV_{p_j}^{\epsilon_j}h_j^{-1}$
the factors of its filling at $V_0$, with $\lVert I-G_j\rVert=
\kappa_{p_j}$. The telescoping sum in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:loopfill}(i) gives $\lVert I-V_C(V_0)\rVert\le\kappa_C$, and
the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedloop}(iii) with this bound gives
\[
\begin{split}
\Bigl\lvert\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]&-\frac1N\lVert Z_C\rVert^2\Bigr\rvert\\
&\le\frac{\kappa_C}N\Bigl(\lVert Z_C\rVert^2+\ell_C\sum_kn_{Ck}\lVert w_k
\rVert^2\Bigr).
\end{split}
\]
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedloop}(ii) gives
\[
\lVert Z_C\rVert\le\sum_j\lVert Z_{p_j}\rVert+2\sum_j\kappa_{p_j}\lVert
Z_{h_j}\rVert .
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, $\bigl(\sum_j\lVert Z_{p_j}\rVert\bigr)^2\le A_C
\sum_pm_{Cp}\lVert Z_p\rVert^2$. The norm $\lVert Z_{h_j}\rVert$ is at
most the sum of $\lVert w_k\rVert$ over the steps of $h_j$,
by~\eqref{eq:pathexp}, so
\[
\begin{split}
\Bigl(\sum_j\kappa_{p_j}\lVert Z_{h_j}\rVert\Bigr)^2&\le\kappa_C\sum_j
\kappa_{p_j}\lVert Z_{h_j}\rVert^2\\
&\le\kappa_C\sum_j\kappa_{p_j}\ell(h_j)\sum_kt_{jk}\lVert w_k\rVert^2 .
\end{split}
\]
With $(s+t)^2\le(1+\kappa_C)s^2+(1+\kappa_C^{-1})t^2$, and directly if
$\kappa_C=0$,
\[
\begin{split}
\lVert Z_C\rVert^2&\le(1+\kappa_C)A_C\sum_pm_{Cp}\lVert Z_p\rVert^2\\
&\quad+4(1+\kappa_C)\sum_j\kappa_{p_j}\ell(h_j)\sum_kt_{jk}\lVert w_k
\rVert^2 .
\end{split}
\]
Hence
\[
N\bigl\lvert\Hess s(V_C)(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le a_CA_C\sum_pm_{Cp}\lVert
Z_p\rVert^2+\sum_k\beta^C_k\lVert w_k\rVert^2,
\]
where
\[
\beta^C_k=\sum_p\kappa_p\Bigl(m_{Cp}\ell_Cn_{Ck}+4a_C\sum_{j:p_j=p}\ell
(h_j)t_{jk}\Bigr).
\]
Summing with the weights $\lvert r_C\rvert$,
\[
N\bigl\lvert\Hess R(0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le\mathcal L^\sharp Q^{V_0}(w)+
\sum_k\beta_k\lVert w_k\rVert^2,
\]
with $\beta_k=\sum_p\mathcal K(k,p)\kappa_p$. By Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\beta_k^2\le\sum_p\mathcal K(k,p)\sum_p\mathcal K(k,p)\kappa_p^2,
\]
so $\sum_k\beta_k^2\le\mathcal N^2\lVert\kappa\rVert_2^2$, and the last
sum is at most $\mathcal N\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\lvert w\rvert_4^2$.

(ii) As in Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(ii), $\mathcal HR(w,w)$ is
the Hessian of $R$ at $0$ in the direction $\Pi_{V_0}w$. This field lies in
$\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:windowlfour} applies to it.

(iii) Here every path is a plaquette $p$ read from its base point, with
$A_C=1$, $m_{Cp}=1$, $\ell_C=4$, $n_{Ck}=1$ for the four links $k$ of $p$
and no paths $h_j$. So $\mathcal K(k,p)=4\lvert r\rvert$ if $k\in p$ and
$0$ otherwise. A link lies in six plaquettes and a plaquette has four
links, so $\mathcal N=(24\cdot16)^{1/2}\lvert r\rvert=8\sqrt6\lvert r\rvert$.
Since $\kappa_\infty\le\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$, $(1+\kappa_\infty)
^2\le1+\frac{19}9\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$, and $8\sqrt6\,c_4=8\sqrt6+108<
127.6$.
\end{proof}

Since $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2^2\le6(n+1)^2(n+2)^2\kappa_\infty^2$, the
hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv} with $\kappa_\infty(n+2)^2\le
10^{-2}$ gives $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le0.025$, and part (iii) then gives a
factor $1+O(\kappa_\infty n^2)$, the order of
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(iii) with a larger constant. When the
curvature is concentrated the factor does not grow with $n$. If $V_0=I$
except on one link $k_0\in K$, where $V_{0,k_0}=g$, then the six plaquettes
of $k_0$ have $\kappa_p=\lVert I-g\rVert$ and the others are flat, so
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_2=\sqrt6\lVert I-g\rVert$. Part (iii) gives the factor
$1+319\lVert I-g\rVert$ on every window that contains $k_0$, against
$(1+\kappa)^2+14\kappa(n+2)^2$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(iii).
The order of the loss in the action cannot be improved, and the
hypothesis that the action of the background on the window is small cannot
be dropped.

\begin{corollary}[the loss is attained in the action]\label{cor:actionsharp}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, and let $V_0$, $u$ and $P$ be as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}. Then $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2=\kappa(n+1)
(n+2)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $n\ge9$, $\varsigma=1$ and $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le2$, then
$\mathcal HP(u,u)\ge(1+0.0336\lVert\kappa\rVert_2)\frac12Q^{V_0}(u)$.
\item For every $n\ge39$ there is a background with $\lVert\kappa
\rVert_2\le31.8$ at which $\mathcal HP$ is negative at $u\in\mathcal
O_{V_0}^\perp$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The plaquettes with their corners in $\Lambda'=[0,n+1]^4$ in the plane
$\{0,1\}$ have bases with $x_0,x_1\in[0,n]$ and $x_2,x_3\in[0,n+1]$, so
there are $(n+1)^2(n+2)^2$ of them, each with $\kappa_p=\kappa$, and the
others are flat. (i) Here $\kappa\le2/110$, so $\sin^2\alpha=\kappa/2\le
10^{-2}$, and $\kappa(n+1)^2=\lVert\kappa\rVert_2(n+1)/(n+2)\le2$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}(i) gives the factor $1+0.037\,\kappa(n+
1)^2\ge1+0.037\cdot\frac{10}{11}\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$. (ii) Take $\varsigma=
-1$ and $\sin^2\alpha=15.5/(n+1)^2\le15.5/1600<10^{-2}$, so that $\kappa(n+
1)^2=31$; Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}(ii) applies, and $\lVert\kappa
\rVert_2=31(n+2)/(n+1)\le31\cdot\frac{41}{40}<31.8$.
\end{proof}

So the threshold of the unstable mode is a bound on the action of the
background on the window, independent of $n$, and the condition
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops} is
necessary up to the constant. The calm windows of
Corollary~\ref{cor:calmexterior} satisfy both forms of the condition,
because their curvature is scaled with the size of the window.

\begin{corollary}[calm windows]\label{cor:actioncalm}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $0<K\le10^{-8}$, let $W$ be a box of $n^4$ blocks, $n_P$ as
in Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre} and $\kappa_f=K/(4\sqrt{n_P})$. Let $U$
be a fine field with $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa_f$ for every fine plaquette
$p$ with a vertex in a block at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most two from
$W$, and let $V_0$ be its cut-off averages on the links of $\Lambda'$. Then
$\kappa_p\le2.683K/n^2$ for every coarse plaquette with its corners in
$\Lambda'$, so that
\[
\kappa_\infty(n+2)^2\le24.2\,K,\qquad\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le39.5\,K.
\]
In particular Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}\textup{(iii)} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}\textup{(ii)} hold on $W$ with a factor
$\mathcal L_\kappa+14.1K\mathcal M_\kappa$, respectively $\mathcal L^\sharp
+257.3K\mathcal N$, for every $n$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A coarse plaquette $P$ with its corners in $\Lambda'$ has its four blocks
at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most one from $W$, and the blocks at distance
at most one from these are at distance at most two from $W$. So
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness} applies with $\kappa_f\le10^{-8}$ and gives
$\kappa_P\le\delta(V_{0,P},I)\le92\kappa_f=23K/\sqrt{n_P}$. As in the proof
of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmrare}, $n_P\ge73.5\lvert W\rvert=73.5\,n^4$,
and $\sqrt{73.5}>8.573$, $23/8.573<2.683$. Then $(n+2)^2/n^2\le9$ gives
$24.15K$, and $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\sqrt6(n+1)(n+2)\kappa_\infty$ with
$(n+1)(n+2)/n^2\le6$ gives $\sqrt6\cdot6\cdot2.683K<39.44K$. Both bounds are
far below the hypotheses $\kappa_\infty(n+2)^2\le10^{-2}$ and $\lVert
\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$. The factors follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}(iii), $0.58\cdot24.2<14.1$, and from
$c_4\cdot39.5<257.3$.
\end{proof}

On calm windows the loss $\kappa n^2$ is therefore already of order $K$,
uniformly in $n$, and the bound in the action adds no strength there. Its
use lies in the hypothesis and in the count of windows. The action is
additive over windows, and the sup norm scaled by $n^2$ is not.

\begin{corollary}[windows that fail]\label{cor:actioncount}
Let the coarse torus have side $L=mn$ with $m,n\ge2$, tiled by the boxes
$W_i=a_i+[0,n-1]^4$, $a_i\in n\Z^4$, with the boxes $\Lambda'_i$, and let
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_{2,i}$ be $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ on $\Lambda'_i$. For
every coarse field $V_0$ and $\eta>0$,
\[
\#\{i:\lVert\kappa\rVert_{2,i}>\eta\}\le\frac{32N}{\eta^2}\sum_Ps(V_{0,P}),
\]
the sum over all coarse plaquettes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
In each coordinate a plaquette occupies one value $x$ or two values $x,x+1$,
and lies in $[a-1,a+n]$ only if $a$ is among $n+2$ consecutive integers.
For $n\ge2$ these contain at most two multiples of $n$, and $L\ge2n\ge n+2$
keeps them distinct modulo $L$. So a plaquette has its corners in at most
$2^4$ of the boxes $\Lambda'_i$, and $\sum_i\lVert\kappa\rVert_{2,i}^2\le
16\sum_P\kappa_P^2\le32N\sum_Ps(V_{0,P})$.
\end{proof}

With $\eta=\frac19$, all but $2592N\sum_Ps(V_{0,P})$ windows of the tiling
satisfy Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}(ii) with a factor at most
$\mathcal L^\sharp+0.73\mathcal N$, whatever $n$. The supremum condition
counts differently. Let $V_0=I$ except on the link $a_i+(0,e_0)$ of each
$W_i$, where $V_0=g$ with $\lVert I-g\rVert=2\eta'(n+2)^{-2}$. Links of
distinct windows differ by at least $n\ge2$ in a coordinate and share no
plaquette, so every window has $\kappa_\infty(n+2)^2=2\eta'>\eta'$, while
$\sum_P\kappa_P^2=24m^4\eta'^2(n+2)^{-4}$. A curved plaquette with its
corners in $\Lambda'_i$ contains a curved link whose base, a corner, lies in
$\Lambda'_i$; the coordinates of that base minus $a_i$ lie in $\{0,n\}$, so
there are at most $16$ such links and $\lVert\kappa\rVert_{2,i}\le
\sqrt{96}\,\lVert I-g\rVert=8\sqrt6\,\eta'(n+2)^{-2}$. All $m^4$ windows
fail the condition $\kappa_\infty(n+2)^2\le\eta'$, and none fails
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_{2,i}\le\frac19$ once $(n+2)^2\ge72\sqrt6\,\eta'$.

\begin{remark}[what the iteration needs]\label{rem:actioniteration}
The one-step factors $1+130\lVert\kappa^{(j)}\rVert_2$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}(iii) at the backgrounds of the scales
$j=1,2,\dots$ have a bounded product exactly when $\sum_j\lVert\kappa^{(j)}
\rVert_2<\infty$. On calm windows at the levels $K_j$ this holds if $\sum_j
K_j<\infty$, by Corollary~\ref{cor:actioncalm}. Three inputs are not
proved here. First, Corollary~\ref{cor:actioncalm} uses the supremum form of
Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}; a bound of the coarse action $\sum_P\kappa_P
^2$ by the fine action near the window, with a constant at most one, would
let the action bound $Q_W\le\frac34\kappa^2$ of the calm completions
(Corollary~\ref{cor:calmexterior}) pass from scale to scale, and it is not
proved. Second, the comparison of the Gaussian reference $S^U_W\circ\Pi_{
V_0}$ with $Q^{V_0}\circ\Pi_{V_0}$ of Remark~\ref{rem:relstepinputs}(d)
remains open. Third, the Haar term keeps the factor $C_n$ in every loop
representation (Proposition~\ref{prop:loopsums}(iv)), since it is a
multiple of $|\Pi_{V_0}w|^2$ and not of $\lvert\Pi_{V_0}w\rvert_4^2$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowlfour} does not remove it.
\end{remark}

The loop representation itself is the remaining question. For $\SU(2)$ the
class of loop sums is closed under products and dense, while a loop sum
has no a priori bound on its weights.

\begin{proposition}[loop sums for $\SU(2)$]\label{prop:loopsums}
Let $G=\SU(2)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Let $C,C'$ be closed paths based at $x,x'$, $\gamma$ a path from $x$
to $x'$, and $C\vee C'$, $C\vee C'^{-1}$ the closed paths $C\gamma C'
\gamma^{-1}$ and $C\gamma C'^{-1}\gamma^{-1}$. Then
\[
s(V_C)s(V_{C'})=s(V_C)+s(V_{C'})-\tfrac12s(V_{C\vee C'})-\tfrac12s(V_{C
\vee C'^{-1}}),
\]
and ordered fillings of $C$ and $C'$ give ordered fillings of $C\vee C'^{
\pm1}$ with $A_C+A_{C'}$ plaquettes and multiplicities $m_{Cp}+m_{C'p}$.
\item On a box $\Lambda'$ with all its links variable, every continuous
function invariant under the gauge group $G^{\Lambda'}$ is a uniform limit
of functions $c+\sum_Cr_Cs(V_C)$, finite sums over closed paths in
$\Lambda'$.
\item Let $\varphi$ be a class function with $\varphi(\operatorname{diag}
(e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}))=\sum_{m\ge0}c_m\cos m\theta$ and $\sum_mm^2
\lvert c_m\rvert<\infty$, and $C$ a closed path with an ordered filling.
Then
\[
\varphi(V_C)=\varphi(I)-\sum_{m\ge1}c_m\,s(V_{C^m}),
\]
where $C^m$ is $C$ traversed $m$ times with $m$ copies of its filling. Its
contribution to $\mathcal L$ is $\sum_mm^2\lvert c_m\rvert\,\sup_pA_Cm_{Cp}$.
The function $R_m$ of Remark~\ref{rem:valueshessians}(b) on one plaquette
has $\mathcal L=(2m^2+1)\epsilon$, although $\lvert R_m\rvert\le\epsilon s$.
\item If $R$ is a loop sum as in Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}, with
paths and fillings in $\Lambda$, and $\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)+\sigma\lvert
\Pi w\rvert^2\rvert\le\tau Q_1(w)$ at $V_0=I$ for every $w$, with $\sigma,
\tau\ge0$, then $\mathcal L\ge N(\sigma C_n^--\tau)$. The Haar term is
$-\frac13\lvert\Pi w\rvert^2$ for $\SU(2)$, so a loop sum that contains it
has $\mathcal L\ge2(\frac{(n+1)^2}{9\pi^2}-\tau)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) For $g,h\in\SU(2)$, $h+h^{-1}=(\Tr h)I$, so $\Tr g\Tr h=\Tr gh+\Tr
gh^{-1}$. Apply it to $g=V_C$ and $h=V_\gamma V_{C'}V_\gamma^{-1}$, whose
traces are real, and substitute $\Tr=2(1-s)$. The product of the fillings
of $V_C$ and of $V_\gamma V_{C'}^{\pm1}V_\gamma^{-1}$, the latter
conjugated by $V_\gamma$ and for $V_{C'}^{-1}$ inverted and reversed, is a
filling of $C\vee C'^{\pm1}$.

(ii) Each orbit of $G^{\Lambda'}$ meets the fields equal to $I$ on the
spanning tree $\tau$ of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv}, in an orbit
of the constant gauge transformations. Fix a site $o$. For a link $k\notin
\tau$ let $C_k$ run from $o$ along $\tau$ to the start of $k$, along $k$,
and back along $\tau$; at such fields $V_{C_k}=V_k$. Let $V,V'$ be two such
fields with $s(V_C)=s(V'_C)$ for every closed path $C$. Every word in the
$V_k$ is the holonomy of a closed path based at $o$, and the trace is real
on $\SU(2)$, so the unitary representations $\rho,\rho'$ of the free group
on $\{k\notin\tau\}$ with $\rho(k)=V_k$, $\rho'(k)=V'_k$ have the same
character. They are direct sums of irreducible representations. If $E_1,
\dots,E_r$ are the pairwise inequivalent irreducible summands of $\rho
\oplus\rho'$, the theorems of Burnside and Jacobson give an element of the
group algebra acting as the identity on $E_i$ and as zero on $E_j$, $j\ne
i$; its trace under $\rho$ and under $\rho'$ is $\dim E_i$ times the
multiplicity of $E_i$. So $\rho$ and $\rho'$ are equivalent. The unitary
factor $U$ of the polar decomposition of an intertwiner intertwines, and
$U(\det U)^{-1/2}\in\SU(2)$, as a constant gauge transformation, maps $V$ to
$V'$. Thus the functions $s(V_C)$ separate the orbits. With the constants
they span an algebra by (i), and the Stone--Weierstrass theorem on the
compact space of orbits gives (ii). This is the lattice form of the
reconstruction theorem of Giles~\cite{Gil81}.

(iii) At $g=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta})$, $s(g^m)=1-\cos
m\theta$, so $\varphi(g)=\sum_mc_m-\sum_{m\ge1}c_ms(g^m)$; both sides are
class functions, and $V_{C^m}=V_C^m$. The repeated filling has $mA_C$
factors and multiplicities $m\,m_{Cp}$. The derivatives of $s(g^m)$ of
orders one and two are of order $m$ and $m^2$, so the series converges with
two derivatives. For $R_m$, $(1-\cos\theta)\cos m\theta=\cos m\theta-\frac
12\cos(m+1)\theta-\frac12\cos(m-1)\theta$, so $R_m(V_p)=-\epsilon s(V_p^m)+
\frac\epsilon2s(V_p^{m+1})+\frac\epsilon2s(V_p^{m-1})$, and $\mathcal L=
\epsilon(m^2+\frac12(m+1)^2+\frac12(m-1)^2)$.

(iv) Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii) and part~(ii) of
Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops} give $\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)\rvert\le
\frac{\mathcal L}NQ_1(\Pi w)=\frac{\mathcal L}NQ_1(w)$. At the field $w$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iv), $\Pi w=w$ and $|w|^2=C_n^-Q_1(w)$, so $\sigma
C_n^-Q_1(w)\le(\frac{\mathcal L}N+\tau)Q_1(w)$. For $\SU(2)$, $\frac1{12}\Tr
(\operatorname{ad}_x^2)=-\frac13\lVert x\rVert^2$, and $C_n^-\ge(n+1)^2/(3
\pi^2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[what the representation leaves open]\label{rem:loopsopen}
Proposition~\ref{prop:loopsums}(ii) represents every invariant function by
loop sums in the sense of uniform approximation only. That controls
neither the values relative to $\sum_ps(V_p)$ nor the Hessians, and the
weights $\mathcal L_\kappa$, $\mathcal M_\kappa$ of the approximants may
diverge. They belong to a representation and not to the function: by
conjugation invariance $s(V_{\gamma C\gamma^{-1}})=s(V_C)$ while $T$ and
$t$ grow with $\gamma$, and $\mathcal M_\kappa$ can be taken as an infimum
over representations. That the exact induced action of one step, at strong
or at weak coupling, is a loop sum with finite $\mathcal L_\kappa$ and
$\mathcal M_\kappa$ is not proved. It would follow from a convergent
expansion of the induced action in polynomials in Wilson loops whose
weights beat the growth in part (i), where a product of $k$ loop functions
becomes $2^{k-1}$ loop functions whose fillings have the sum of the
areas. The character expansion at strong coupling and the expansion of
Ba{\l}aban~\cite{Bal89b} at weak coupling are of this kind, and neither
is carried out here for the cut-off averages. For $\SU(N)$, $N\ge3$, the
identity in (i) has no analogue linear in traces, and products of traces
would have to be admitted. Part (iv) shows that $C_n$ stays on the Haar
term in any loop representation, as in Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep}.
\end{remark}


\emph{The induced action.} Let $e^{-A(\omega)}$ be the density in $\omega$
of the cut-off averages of a window under the Wilson measure restricted by a
cut-off. The small-field restriction is an example: it is a soft box in the
coordinates of the chart of Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, which is not
$\Gamma_W$-invariant. Then $e^{-A^{\rm gi}}$ is the density with respect to
Haar measure on $G^K$ of the averages under the measure whose cut-off on
the fibre over $\Upsilon(s,\eta)$ is the transport by the block-constant
gauge transformation $e^\eta$ of the cut-off on the fibre over $e^s$. The
transport maps fibre to fibre (Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}) and preserves the
Wilson weight and Haar measure, so the fibre integrals agree. On the slice
$\mathcal O^\perp$ the two cut-offs coincide. A cut-off defined through
gauge-invariant quantities gives $A^{\rm gi}=A+\sum_k\log j$ everywhere.

\begin{remark}[inputs and what is missing]\label{rem:relstepinputs}
Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} rests on one input and leaves the following
open.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Input.} The bound (H) on the Hessian of the induced action at
one point is an absolute bound, of the kind by which
Theorems~\ref{thm:smallfibre} and~\ref{thm:fibrechart} control the
non-Gaussian terms, and only its restriction to $\mathcal O^\perp$ is used.
It is not proved in this paper. Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep} replaces it
by a loop representation of the remainder, under which $C_n$ falls on the
Haar term alone. As an illustration that no result uses, for $\SU(2)$,
$\lambda=10^{100}$ and $\varepsilon=1.63\cdot10^{-9}$, interval arithmetic
gives $\varepsilon'\le8.40\cdot10^{-9}$ at $n=2$, $1.52\cdot10^{-8}$ at
$n=4$, $1.52\cdot10^{-7}$ at $n=16$ and $5.95\cdot10^{-4}$ at $n=1024$, and
$\varepsilon'\le0.1$ for every $n\le8455$.
\item \emph{The cut-off.} The construction replaces a non-invariant cut-off
off the slice by its gauge transport. Ba{\l}aban defines the small-field
regions by gauge-invariant conditions on
plaquettes~\cite{Bal85a,Bal89b,Dim13}. For such a cut-off the transport is
not needed.
\item \emph{Points that are not critical.} $\mathcal H$ is taken at one
point. An iteration needs the bound as a function on a neighbourhood. There
the gradient terms of Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(i) and the third
derivatives enter, and Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} says nothing about
them. Ba{\l}aban expands around the minimiser of the action with given
averages, the background field, at which the first-order terms
vanish~\cite{Bal84a,Dim13}.
\item \emph{Curved backgrounds.} Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice} holds at
every $V_0$. The Gaussian reference $S^U_W(w)=\inf\{Q_U(X):BX=w\}$ need not
vanish on $\mathcal O_{V_0}$, where $B$ is the derivative of the cut-off
averages at $U$. The fine gauge variation $X_\eta$ of $e^\eta$ has $BX_\eta=
d_{V_0}\eta$ and $D_p(X_\eta)=(1-\operatorname{Ad}U_p)\eta_{y(p)}$, with
$y(p)$ the block of the base of $p$. Hence $S^U_W(d_{V_0}\eta)\le384
\kappa^2|\eta|^2$ when $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$, where $96$ plaquettes have
their base in a block. The reference for an invariant action is $S^U_W\circ
\Pi_{V_0}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:curvedwindow} its gap on $\mathcal
O_{V_0}^\perp$ follows from a comparison $S^U_W\ge c_1Q_1-c_2\kappa|\cdot|^2$
there, with the gap $c_1(1-\theta/s_n)^2C_n^{-1}-c_2\kappa$; that comparison
is not proved here.
\item \emph{The action.} The induced action is not a plaquette action. Its
Hessian is compared with $2\lambda S_W$, not with $2\lambda Q_1$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} does not apply to it as it stands at the next
scale. The large fields, which Ba{\l}aban treats separately~\cite{Bal89b},
are removed by the cut-off and not estimated.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[relative errors over scales]\label{rem:relscales}
The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:formstability} uses only the order of
forms, so it holds for positive semidefinite forms. A bound $(1\pm
\varepsilon')\,2\lambda S_W$ on the covariant Hessian therefore passes to
the block infimum of the next step with factor one.
Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth} does not apply to it. That proposition
concerns an error bounded by the Euclidean form, which does not vanish on
$\mathcal O$. The block infimum turns that error into a term at least
$4\lambda\varepsilon(1+2724\kappa)^{-1}|w|^2$, also where $S_W$ vanishes.

The two statements agree. A window of side $n$ in blocks of one scale has
side $n/2$ in the blocks of the next, and $C_n/C_{n/2}\to4$. Converting an
absolute error at one scale costs the factor $C_n$. Carrying it one step as
an absolute error multiplies it by at least four, after which converting
costs $C_{n/2}$. Both routes have the same order, and the factor four of
Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth} is the loss of the gap of the window.

With windows of side $n_k=n_12^{1-k}$ at the scales $k=1,\dots,K$,
$\sum_kC_{n_k}\le K+n_1^2/3$, so
\[
\sum_k\varepsilon'_k\le\sup_k\Bigl(\varepsilon_k+\frac{\delta_G}{\lambda_k}
\Bigr)\frac{K+n_1^2/3}{2c_*}.
\]
The part $n_1^2/3$ is the conversion cost. It is the absolute error carried
to the last scale, $4^{K-1}\approx n_1^2$, so it is finite for a fixed
window but not uniform in the volume. Removing it needs a gauge-invariant
localisation of the one-step bound, which is part of
Ba{\l}aban's analysis~\cite{Bal89b}. For a remainder that is a sum of
gauge-invariant terms on boxes, Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat} gives that
localisation, with the gap of each box in place of $C_n$, and by
Proposition~\ref{prop:chartlocal} the factor $C_n$ of the Haar term comes
from stating the hypothesis on the chart density. For a remainder that is a series of filled
Wilson loops, Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep} removes it from $\varepsilon_k$
and leaves it on the Haar term $\delta_G/\lambda_k$. The part $K$ is marginal. The Haar term $\delta_G/\lambda_k$ is of order
$g_k^2$, and $\sum_kg_k^2$ diverges logarithmically along the one-loop
coupling by Remark~\ref{rem:constrainedopen}(c). The order $g^2$ of the
one-step error must therefore be absorbed into the running coupling and the
normalisation of the field. Only a remainder of order $g^4$ can be carried
as $\varepsilon'_k$. For $n_1=2^{12}$, $K=13$, $\varepsilon_k=1.63\cdot
10^{-9}$ and $\lambda_k=10^{100}$, the values of $C_{n_k}$ give $\sum_k
\varepsilon'_k\le0.0127$, against $4^{12}\varepsilon_1\le0.028$ for the absolute
error of the first scale carried to the last. No effective action is constructed here beyond the first
scale, and item~(iv) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains} remains open.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Every compact simple group}\label{ssec:groups13}

The constructions of this section were written for $\SU(2)$. This
subsection records which of them hold for a general group, and with which
constants. Let $G$ be a compact connected group whose Lie algebra $\g$ is
simple, with a faithful unitary representation in which $G\subset\U(N)$,
the metric $\ip XY=-\Tr(XY)$ on $\g$, the least Ricci curvature $\kappa_G$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:groups}, $d=\dim G$ and $K=\kappa_G/(d-1)$. The
distance $\delta(g,h)=\lVert g-h\rVert$ is the Hilbert--Schmidt distance,
$d(g,h)$ the geodesic distance of $G$, the Wilson weight is
$\exp(-\beta_W\sum_ps_p)$ with
\[
s_p=1-\tfrac1N\ReTr U_p=\frac{\delta(U_p,I)^2}{2N},\qquad\beta_W=N^2\beta,
\]
which is the normalisation of this section for $N=2$, and $\rho_G$ is the
radius of Sec.~\ref{sec:blocks}. Put $I_d(x)=\int_0^x\sin^{d-1}u\,du$.

\begin{lemma}[spectral constants]\label{lem:adspread}
Let $X,Y\in\g$ and $U\in G$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The operator $\operatorname{ad}X$ on $\g$ is skew, with spectrum
in $i[-\sqrt2\lVert X\rVert,\sqrt2\lVert X\rVert]$.
\item $-\Tr\bigl((\operatorname{ad}X)^2\bigr)=4\kappa_G\lVert X\rVert^2$;
in particular $\delta_G=\kappa_G/3$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep}.
\item With $s(V)=1-\frac1N\ReTr V$, the derivative of $s(Ue^{tX})$ at
$t=0$ has modulus at most $\lVert X\rVert/\sqrt N$; on $\U(N)$,
$\delta(g,h)\le2\sqrt N$.
\item Let $j$ be the density of Haar measure in exponential coordinates,
\[
j(X)=\det\bigl((1-e^{-\operatorname{ad}X})/\operatorname{ad}X\bigr).
\]
If $\lVert X\rVert\le10^{-3}$, then
\[
\lvert\partial_Y\log j(X)\rvert\le\tfrac{\kappa_G}3(1+10^{-6})\lVert X
\rVert\lVert Y\rVert .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Invariance of the trace makes $\operatorname{ad}X$ skew. On $\mathfrak
u(N)$, in a basis in which $X=\operatorname{diag}(i\lambda_1,\dots,
i\lambda_N)$, $\operatorname{ad}X$ has eigenvalues $i(\lambda_j-
\lambda_k)$, and $\g$ is an invariant subspace; $(\lambda_j-\lambda_k)^2\le
2(\lambda_j^2+\lambda_k^2)\le2\lVert X\rVert^2$.
(ii) $\Ric(X,X)=-\frac14\Tr((\operatorname{ad}X)^2)$ is an
$\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant symmetric form. Since $\g\otimes\C$ is
simple, the adjoint representation is irreducible over $\C$ and every
invariant symmetric form is a multiple of $\ip\cdot\cdot$, so $\Ric=
\kappa_G\ip\cdot\cdot$. Then $\delta_G=\frac1{12}\cdot4\kappa_G$.
(iii) The derivative is $-\frac1N\ReTr(UX)$. Since $\overline{\Tr(UX)}=
-\Tr(U^*X)$, $\ReTr(UX)=\frac12\Tr((U-U^*)X)$, and $\lVert U-U^*\rVert^2=
4\sum_j\sin^2\theta_j\le4N$ for the eigenangles $\theta_j$ of $U$. The
diameter bound is $\lVert g-h\rVert^2=2N-2\ReTr(g^*h)\le4N$.
(iv) $\Tr\operatorname{ad}X=0$, so $\log j(X)=\Tr\Phi(\operatorname{ad}
X)$ with $\Phi(z)=\log(\sinh(z/2)/(z/2))$, and $\partial_Y\log j(X)=
\Tr(\Phi'(\operatorname{ad}X)\operatorname{ad}Y)$. For real $y$,
$\Phi'(iy)=i(\frac1y-\frac12\cot\frac y2)$ and $0\le\frac1y-\frac12\cot
\frac y2\le\frac y{12}(1+\frac{y^2}{50})$ for $0\le y\le1$; by (i) the
spectral radius of $\operatorname{ad}X$ is at most $\sqrt2\cdot10^{-3}$,
so $\lVert\Phi'(\operatorname{ad}X)\rVert_{HS}\le\frac1{12}(1+10^{-6})
\lVert\operatorname{ad}X\rVert_{HS}$, and (ii) together with the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives the bound.
\end{proof}

For $\SU(2)$ the spectrum in (i) is $\{0,\pm i\sqrt2\lVert X\rVert\}$, and
the estimates of Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound}, Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside},
Lemma~\ref{lem:goodsidedensity} and Step~4 of Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo}
that use the spectrum of an operator $\operatorname{ad}W$ use only that it
lies in $i[-\sqrt2\lVert W\rVert,\sqrt2\lVert W\rVert]$: the bounds
$\lVert L_X\rVert\le\theta/\sin\theta$, $\lVert E_Y\rVert\le1$,
$\lVert\varpi(\operatorname{ad}W)^{-1}\rVert\le m(\theta)$, the
divided-difference bounds and $\kappa_0<0.8935$ hold for $G$ unchanged.
The Hilbert--Schmidt norm $\lVert\operatorname{ad}W\rVert_{HS}=2\lVert W
\rVert$ becomes $2\sqrt{\kappa_G}\lVert W\rVert$, a trace over $\g$ is
bounded by $d$ times the operator norm instead of $3$ times it, and the
pair $(\lVert X\rVert/\sqrt2,2\sqrt2)$ of (iii) becomes $(\lVert X\rVert/
\sqrt N,2\sqrt N)$.

\begin{lemma}[the logarithm radius of a stabiliser]\label{lem:tensorlog}
Let $t$ be a tensor in $(\C^N)^{\otimes a}\otimes(\C^{N*})^{\otimes b}$
with $m=a+b\ge1$, and let $G$ be the identity component of the stabiliser
of $t$ in $\U(N)$. If $g\in G$ and $\delta(g,I)<2\sin\frac\pi{2m}$, the
principal logarithm of $g$ lies in $\g$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $e^{i\theta_j}$, $|\theta_j|\le\pi$, be the eigenvalues of $g$ and
$X=\log g$. Since $4\sin^2(\theta_j/2)\le\delta(g,I)^2<4\sin^2\frac\pi
{2m}$, every $|\theta_j|<\pi/m$. The induced action of $e^{sX}$ on the
tensor space is $e^{sD}$, where the derivation $D$ induced by $X$ is
skew-Hermitian with eigenvalues $i$ times sums of $m$ terms $\pm\theta_j$,
so its spectrum lies in $i(-\pi,\pi)$. Decompose $t=\sum_\mu t_\mu$ over the
eigenspaces of $D$. From $e^Dt=t$, $e^{i\mu}t_\mu=t_\mu$ with $|\mu|<\pi$,
so $t_\mu=0$ for $\mu\ne0$ and $Dt=0$. The one-parameter group $e^{sX}$
then fixes $t$ and lies in its identity component $G$, so $X\in\g$.
\end{proof}

$\SO(N)$ and $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$ are the identity components of the
stabilisers of a symmetric and of a skew form, $m=2$ and $2\sin\frac\pi4
>1$, so $\rho_G=1$. $G_2\subset\U(7)$, $F_4\subset\U(26)$, $E_6\subset
\U(27)$ and $E_8\subset\U(248)$ are the identity components of the
stabilisers of tensors of degree at most three: the three-form of the
octonions, the quadratic and cubic invariants of the traceless exceptional
Jordan algebra, its cubic determinant, and the Lie bracket~\cite{Bae02}.
Each $\rho_G<1$ is admissible for them, for instance $\rho_G=0.99$.
$E_7\subset\U(56)$ is the identity component of the stabiliser of the
symplectic and the quartic form of the Freudenthal triple
system~\cite{Bae02}, $m=4$, so $\rho_G=0.76<2\sin\frac\pi8$ is admissible.
For $\SU(N)$, $\rho_G=\min\{1,5/\sqrt N\}$.

\begin{lemma}[small balls]\label{lem:haarball}
For $r>0$, the Haar measure of $\{g\in G:d(g,I)\le r\}$ is at least
$I_d(\sqrt Kr)/I_d(\pi)$, with equality for $\SU(2)$. If $\sqrt Kr\le
\frac14$, it is at least $(\frac{95}{96})^{d-1}(\sqrt Kr)^d/(d\,I_d(\pi))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The Ricci curvature is at least $(d-1)K$, so the diameter is at most
$\pi/\sqrt K$ by Myers' theorem, and the relative volume comparison of
Bishop and Gromov~\cite{Pet16} bounds the ratio of the volume of the ball
of radius $r$ to that of the ball of radius $\pi/\sqrt K$, which is $G$,
from below by the same ratio on the sphere of curvature $K$ and dimension
$d$, $I_d(\sqrt Kr)/I_d(\pi)$. For $\SU(2)$ the group is that sphere,
of radius $\sqrt2$. The second bound follows from $\sin u\ge u(1-u^2/6)
\ge\frac{95}{96}u$ on $[0,\frac14]$.
\end{proof}

Lemma~\ref{lem:haarball} takes the place of the angle density $\frac2\pi
\sin^2\theta$ used in Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ}. With it, put
\begin{multline*}
C_0(G)=\frac12+\frac23\Bigl(\log\bigl(d\,I_d(\pi)\bigr)\\
+\frac d2\log\frac{16}{KN}-(d-1)\log\frac{95}{96}\Bigr).
\end{multline*}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:wilsonZG}
For $\beta_W\ge KN$, the normalising constant of the Wilson measure of $G$
on $\Lambda_L$ satisfies
\[
-\log Z_L\le6L^4\Bigl(\frac d3\log\beta_W+C_0(G)\Bigr),
\]
and $\E S\le6L^4(\frac d3\log\beta_W+C_0(G))/\beta_W$. If $KN\le16$, then
$C_0(G)>0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put $r=\sqrt N/(4\sqrt{\beta_W})$, so that $\sqrt Kr\le\frac14$. If every
link is within geodesic distance $r$ of $I$, every plaquette has
$\delta(U_p,I)\le d(U_p,I)\le4r$ and $s_p\le8r^2/N=1/(2\beta_W)$, so
$\beta_WS\le3L^4$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:haarball} the $4L^4$ links do so
with probability at least
\[
\Bigl(\bigl(\tfrac{95}{96}\bigr)^{d-1}\bigl(\tfrac{KN}{16\beta_W}
\bigr)^{d/2}\big/\bigl(d\,I_d(\pi)\bigr)\Bigr)^{4L^4},
\]
which gives the first bound; the second follows from the concavity of
$-\log Z_L$ in the coupling, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ}. The integrals
satisfy $I_dI_{d+1}=2\pi/d$, by induction from $I_{d+2}=\frac d{d+1}I_d$,
and $I_d\ge I_{d+1}$, so $d\,I_d(\pi)\ge\sqrt{2\pi d}>1$; the other terms
of $C_0(G)$ are nonnegative when $KN\le16$.
\end{proof}

For $\SU(2)$, $C_0(G)=4.32001$, below the constant $4.90817$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ}. For $\SU(N)$, $KN=N^2/(2(N^2-2))\le1$; for every
group of Table~\ref{tab:groups}, $KN\le1$, so the lemma holds at every
$\beta_W\ge1$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:defectsG}
For $\beta_W\ge KN$, $0<\rho\le1$ and every set $A$ of unit cubes,
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} and Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters} hold for
the Wilson measure of $G$ with
\[
q^G_\rho(\beta_W)=\min\Bigl\{1,\exp\Bigl(2d\log\beta_W+6C_0(G)-
\frac{\beta_W\rho^2}{8N}\Bigr)\Bigr\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reflection in a hyperplane through sites preserves Haar measure on $G$ and
maps $\ReTr U_p$ to $\ReTr U_p$ or $\ReTr U_p^{-1}=\ReTr U_p$, so the
chessboard estimate holds as in Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}. A bad
plaquette has $s_p>\rho^2/(2N)$, and if every cube is bad there are at
least $L^4/4$ bad plaquettes, so $S\ge\rho^2L^4/(8N)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZG}
bounds $Z_L$. The corollary uses only the product bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Section~\ref{sec:islands} for a compact simple group]
\label{thm:groups13}
Let $G\subset\U(N)$ be as above, with $\kappa_G\le2500$ in~(iii).
Replace $\SU(2)$ by $G$, the hypothesis $\rho\le10^{-8}$ by $\rho\le
10^{-8}\rho_G$, and $C_0$, $q_\rho$ by $C_0(G)$, $q^G_\rho$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Lemmas~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}, \ref{lem:branchbound},
\ref{lem:coverage}, \ref{lem:scalewitness}, Theorems~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}
and~\ref{thm:islandscales}~\textup{(i)}, \textup{(ii)} hold with
\[
f_G(\beta)=2d\log\beta+6C_0(G)-\frac{\beta\rho^2}{8N}
\]
in place of $f$ (and $\rho_0$ in place of $\rho$ at scale $j$), and with
$\beta^*>16dN/\rho^2$ in place of $\beta^*>96/\rho^2$. The numbers $M$,
$H$, $\varDelta$, $M_j$, $H_j$ and $\log q^*$ do not depend on $G$, and
\[
\beta^*_G=\frac{8N\lvert\log q^*\rvert}{\rho^2}(1+\epsilon_G),\quad
\epsilon_G=\frac{2d\log\beta^*_G+6C_0(G)}{\lvert\log q^*\rvert}.
\]
\item Theorems~\ref{thm:fibrechart}, \ref{thm:chartdecay},
Propositions~\ref{prop:explicitconstants} and~\ref{prop:explicitdecay}
hold as stated, since they are stated for every compact $G\subset\U(r)$:
$c_3=\max\{1.5\cdot10^4\sqrt N,d\}$, $c_6=6.81\cdot10^5d\,c_3^2$,
$\alpha_G=2.5\cdot10^{-4}$.
\item Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} holds with $\lambda=\beta_W/(2N)$,
hypothesis~(b) read as $\beta_W\ge480Nc_6$, and $\mathcal A=120/\lambda=
240N/\beta_W$. Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands} holds with
\[
\varDelta=\frac{960N}{\beta_W}\Lambda_2^2r^2\sqrt{n_xn_y}\,e^{-2\alpha_G
(w-2s-8)},
\]
and its hypothesis~(a) holds for $\rho\le1/(2758\cdot7.8\cdot10^7c_3)$.
\item Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo} holds with $\frac2Nc_W$ and $\frac d3
c_\psi$ in place of $c_W$ and $c_\psi$; under hypotheses (a) and (c) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound},
\[
\Lambda_2\le\frac{198.0002}N\beta_W+\frac{4.65\cdot10^6}3d .
\]
\item Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} holds with the density bounds
$(1+\kappa_0)^{-d}$ and $(1-\kappa_0)^{-d}$, and with radius
$\rho_G/32$ when $\rho_G<1$; Lemma~\ref{lem:sitelaw} holds with the
Jacobian bound $\sigma_0^d$; Lemma~\ref{lem:goodsidedensity} holds with
$64.94\cdot\frac d3\sqrt{\kappa_G}$ and $32.47\cdot\frac d3\sqrt
{\kappa_G}$; Theorem~\ref{thm:site} holds with $24n_p\beta_W$,
$197\beta_W+a_G$ and $87\beta_W+b_G$, where
\begin{gather*}
a_G=1558.56\,\sqrt N\,\tfrac d3\sqrt{\kappa_G}+1.1986,\\
b_G=779.28\,\sqrt N\,\tfrac d3\sqrt{\kappa_G}+0.5993 .
\end{gather*}
\item Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands}, Corollary~\ref{cor:islandchains},
Proposition~\ref{prop:islandmass} and Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} hold
with the threshold $\beta^*_G$ of~(i), the condition $2758\rho\le1/(7.8
\cdot10^7c_3)$, $\frac{960N}{\beta_W}$ in place of $\frac{1920}{\beta_W}$,
and $\bar\Lambda_2=\frac{198.0002}N\beta_W+\frac{4.65\cdot10^6}3d$.
\item The statements of Subsections~\ref{ssec:counting}
to~\ref{ssec:spectralweight}, other than
Proposition~\ref{prop:blockresponse}, of
Subsection~\ref{ssec:manyislands} and of Subsection~\ref{ssec:relstep}
hold for $G$ as stated, with $\delta_G=\kappa_G/3$.
\end{enumerate}
For $\SU(3)$, $d=8$, $N=3$, $\kappa_G=\frac32$, $\rho_G=1$, $C_0(G)\in
[10.44720,10.44721]$, $f_G(\beta)=16\log\beta+6C_0(G)-\beta\rho^2/24$, and
\begin{gather*}
\beta^*(10^{-8},1)\in[5.268,5.270]\cdot10^{21},\\
\beta^*(10^{-8},5)\in[8.230,8.232]\cdot10^{21},\\
\beta^*(10^{-9},1)\in[5.285,5.287]\cdot10^{23},\\
\beta^*(10^{-9},5)\in[8.247,8.249]\cdot10^{23},\\
\beta^*(10^{-8},5,10^{30})\in[2.971,2.973]\cdot10^{22},
\end{gather*}
with $0.026<\epsilon_G<0.045$ in the first four. At scale $j$, for $s=5$ and
$\rho=10^{-8}$, $\beta^*_1\in[4.367,4.368]\cdot10^{23}$, $\beta^*_2\in
[6.990,6.992]\cdot10^{24}$, $\beta^*_3\in[1.785,1.787]\cdot10^{26}$ and
$16^{-j}\beta^*_j\le4.38\cdot10^{22}$ for $1\le j\le12$. In~(iii) for
$\SU(3)$, $c_3\le25980.8$, $c_6\le3.678\cdot10^{15}$, (b) holds for
$\beta_W\ge5.30\cdot10^{18}$, (a) for $\rho\le1.789\cdot10^{-16}$, and at
$\rho=1.78\cdot10^{-16}$ the threshold with the joining distance $2s+8$
lies in $[2.569,2.571]\cdot10^{37}$ for $s=1$ and in $[3.014,3.016]\cdot
10^{37}$ for $s=5$, where (b) holds; $\Lambda_2\le66.0001\beta_W+1.24\cdot
10^7$, and the constant $c_2$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} at $s=1$,
$\vartheta=0$ is at most $10^{22.14}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) The witness paragraph of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}
uses Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}, which is stated for every $G$ with
$\kappa\le10^{-8}\rho_G$; Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, a statement on $\U(N)$;
and $d(g,h)\le(1+10^{-12})\delta(g,h)$ for $\delta(g,h)\le10^{-6}$,
which holds on $G$ because there $\delta\le\rho_G$, the principal
logarithm of $g^{-1}h$ lies in $\g$ and $d(g,h)=\lVert\log(g^{-1}h)
\rVert$. In Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness} the constants are those of
Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound} and the triangle inequality. In
Lemma~\ref{lem:branchbound} the cut-off is nonzero only where $\max_x
\delta(v_x,I)<\rho_G$, so the logarithms lie in $\g$, and the contraction
bound uses the spectrum of $\operatorname{ad}X$ only through
Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(i). Lemmas~\ref{lem:coverage}
and~\ref{lem:scalewitness} count cubes; Theorem~\ref{thm:defectscales},
used in the latter, is stated for every $G$. The threshold paragraph
applies to $f_G$, which is concave with maximum $2d\log(16dN/\rho^2)+6C_0
(G)-2d>0>\log q^*$ at $16dN/\rho^2$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZG} and
$\rho\le10^{-8}$. The identity for $\epsilon_G$ is $f_G(\beta^*_G)=\log
q^*$.
(ii) There is nothing to prove.
(iii) In the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} the Wilson action
enters as $\lambda\lVert\cdot\rVert^2$ with $\lambda=\beta_W/(2N)$, the
dimension enters through $\lVert A_v\rVert_1\le2d\,c_3\lVert x_v
\rVert_1$ and $\lVert A_a\rVert_2^2\le2d\,c_3^2\lVert\bar P\rVert^2\lvert
a\rvert^2$, which are absorbed in $c_6$, and the Haar part is the
logarithmic gradient of $j$ at $\lVert X_e\rVert\le10^{-3}$, at most
$\frac{\kappa_G}3(1+10^{-6})10^{-3}\le0.84$ per unit of $\lVert x_v
\rVert_1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(iv) and $\kappa_G\le2500$. The rest
of the proof is a statement about the chart constants of~(ii). The
corollary is Proposition~\ref{prop:layercross} with $4\mathcal A=960N/
\beta_W$, and $\eta+62r=2758\rho$.
(iv) The Wilson term of a plaquette is $\beta_W(1-\frac1N\ReTr U_p)$, so
every bound of~\eqref{eq:wilsonmixed} carries $\frac1N$ in place of
$\frac12$; Steps 2 to 6 use the spectrum of $\operatorname{ad}W$ through
Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(i) only. In Step~7, $\lvert\Tr A\rvert\le d
\lVert A\rVert$ on $\g$ replaces $\lvert\Tr A\rvert\le3\lVert A\rVert$.
(v) In the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} the density of a
linear map $T$ with $\lVert T-I\rVert\le\kappa_0$ on $\g$ lies between
$(1-\kappa_0)^d$ and $(1+\kappa_0)^d$; the cut-off is inactive below
$\rho_G/2$, which gives the radius $\rho_G/32$. Lemma~\ref{lem:privatesubmersion}
is stated with $\rho_G$, and $JJ^*\ge\sigma_0^2$ on the $d$-dimensional
$\g$ gives $\sqrt{\det JJ^*}\ge\sigma_0^d$. In the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:goodsidedensity}, $\operatorname{tr}(T^{-1}\dot T)$ is at
most $d\lVert T^{-1}\rVert\lVert\dot T\rVert$ and $\lVert\operatorname{ad}
W\rVert_{HS}=2\sqrt{\kappa_G}\lVert W\rVert$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(ii),
while the spectra lie in the segments used there by
Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(i). In the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:site} the
oscillation of a site function is at most $24\cdot2\sqrt N$ and
$\lvert\dot s_p\rvert\le v/\sqrt N$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(iii), so
the first term is at most $24\sqrt N\sup\lvert\partial_t\log h_t\rvert$;
the factors $\sqrt N$ cancel in the Wilson part, which gives $24n_p\beta_W$,
$24\cdot8.1916\,\beta_W<197\beta_W$ and $24\cdot6\cdot0.5993\,\beta_W<
87\beta_W$, and remain in the density part, which gives $a_G$ and $b_G$.
For $\SU(2)$, $a_G<2206$ and $b_G<1103$, the constants of the theorem.
(vi) These statements use the preceding ones through the constants
listed, and the threshold through $q^G$.
(vii) These statements concern the label variables, the coupling of
labels, the island combinatorics and the quadratic forms of a box. The
group enters them only through the results of Sec.~\ref{sec:blocks},
stated for every $G$, through the constants of~(iii) and~(iv), and
through $\delta_G$ in Subsection~\ref{ssec:relstep}, which is
$\kappa_G/3$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:adspread}(ii).

\emph{The numbers for $\SU(3)$.} Here $K=\kappa_G/7=\frac3{14}$, $KN=
\frac9{14}$ and $I_8(\pi)=\int_0^\pi\sin^7u\,du=\frac{32}{35}$, so $d\,I_d
(\pi)=\frac{256}{35}$, and the factorisations $\frac{256}{35}(\frac{224}9)^4
(\frac{96}{95})^7=2^{63}3^{-1}5^{-8}7^3\,19^{-7}$ and $7^2=2\cdot5^2\cdot
\frac{49}{50}$, $19=2^5\cdot3\cdot5^{-1}\cdot\frac{95}{96}$ give
\begin{multline*}
C_0(G)=\tfrac12+\tfrac23\bigl(\tfrac{59}2\log2-8\log3+2\log5\\
-\tfrac32\log\tfrac{50}{49}+7\log\tfrac{96}{95}\bigr).
\end{multline*}
The logarithms of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}, with
$\log\frac{50}{49}=2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{99}$ and $\log\frac{96}{95}
=2\operatorname{artanh}\frac1{191}$, give $C_0(G)$ within $10^{-7}$ of
$10.4472096$. The function $g_G(\beta)=\beta\rho^2/24-16\log\beta-6C_0(G)-
\lvert\log q^*\rvert-H\log\varGamma$ increases for $\beta>384/\rho^2$, and
$\beta^*$ is its largest zero. With $\lvert\log q^*\rvert$ within $10^{-3}$
of $21090.194$ and $33424.872$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}), at the
ends of each of the five stated intervals $g_G$ is negative and positive,
with margins above $2$, so that $\log\beta$ to two decimals decides the
signs; $\epsilon_G=(16\log\beta^*_G+6C_0(G))/\lvert\log q^*\rvert$
increases with $\beta^*_G$, and its values at the ends of the first four
intervals lie between $0.02603$ and $0.04442$. At scale $j$, $\rho_0=\rho/
(c\,4^j)$ with $c=1.01\cdot1.023$ and $24c^2\le25.6215417$, and
$\lvert\log q^*_j\rvert$ is as in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandscales}: within $10^{-3}$ of $105605.899$ and
$105608.929$ for $j=1,2$, and at most $169144.64+4j\log2$ for $j\ge3$. The
same sign check, with margins above $11$, gives the three intervals for
$\beta^*_1$, $\beta^*_2$, $\beta^*_3$. For $b>384c^2/\rho^2$,
\begin{multline*}
g_{G,j}(16^jb)=\frac{b\rho^2}{24c^2}-16\log b-6C_0(G)\\
-\bigl(\lvert\log q^*_j\rvert+64j\log2\bigr),
\end{multline*}
and at $b=4.38\cdot10^{22}$ the first term is at least $170949.9$, the next
two at most $834.15$ and $62.684$, and the bracket, for $j\le12$, at most
$105697.7$ when $j\le2$ and $169144.64+68j\log2\le169710.3$ when $j\ge3$;
so $g_{G,j}(16^jb)>0$ and $16^{-j}\beta^*_j\le4.38\cdot10^{22}$. In~(iii),
$c_3=1.5\cdot10^4\sqrt3\le25980.8$, $c_6=6.81\cdot10^5\cdot8\cdot6.75\cdot
10^8=3.6774\cdot10^{15}$, $480\cdot3\cdot c_6=5.295456\cdot10^{18}$ and
$2758\cdot7.8\cdot10^7\cdot25980.8\le5.5891\cdot10^{15}$, which give (b)
and (a). For the joining distance $2s+8$, $\lvert\log q^*\rvert$ lies
within $10^{-2}$ of $32481.67$ for $s=1$ and of $38354.07$ for $s=5$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow}), and the sign check at $\rho=1.78\cdot
10^{-16}$, with margins above $7$, gives the two intervals. In~(iv),
$\frac{198.0002}3\le66.0001$ and $\frac{4.65\cdot10^6\cdot8}3=1.24\cdot
10^7$. Finally, with $960N=2880$, $r=43\rho$ and $\kappa=2\alpha_G=5\cdot
10^{-4}$,
\[
c_2=2880\,\beta^*r^2\Bigl(66.0001+\frac{1.24\cdot10^7}{\beta^*}\Bigr)^2
\cdot45\cdot14^2\cdot9^2e^{0.008},
\]
which increases with $\beta^*$ and is at most $10^{22.134}$ at $\beta^*=
2.571\cdot10^{37}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:groups13}
Four parts of this section do not transfer. Subsection~\ref{ssec:witnessradius}
(Lemma~\ref{lem:ladder}, Propositions~\ref{prop:smallframessharp}
and~\ref{prop:constantcurvature}, Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide}) measures
frames by the angle of a unit quaternion; on $\SU(N)$, $N\ge3$, the
operator-norm angle is subadditive and conjugation invariant, and the
constants of the subsection have not been computed for it. Proposition~\ref{prop:fold}
uses every preimage of the average on $\SU(2)$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:blockresponse} is a computation with unit
quaternions. The examples of
Propositions~\ref{prop:roughbackground}, \ref{prop:nonconvex}
and~\ref{prop:branches} are stated on $\SU(2)$ and are not claimed for
other groups.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:groups13blocks}
For $\SU(3)$ the plaquette blocks reach $\beta_W\le0.52$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:su3blocks}), in place of $0.348$ for $\SU(2)$. For
other groups the block constant~\eqref{eq:blockconst3} needs the
modulus $\Lambda(r)$ of~\eqref{eq:alpha}, a gap of the one-link measure
and bounds on the Hessian of $\log Z$, and none of them has been
certified. The modulus that holds for every $G$ does not suffice: the
one-link measure $\nu_b$ satisfies the Bakry--\'Emery condition with
constant $\kappa_G-\lVert b\rVert_{\rm op}\ge\kappa_G-r$, so
$\Lambda(r)\le1/(\kappa_G-r)$; with this bound the right side
of~\eqref{eq:alpha} is below one only for $N\beta<\kappa_G/18$, and,
since $K_3\ge s\ge\Lambda(r)$, every value of $\alpha_3$ computed from it
is at least $10N\beta/(\kappa_G-6N\beta)$, below one only for $N\beta<
\kappa_G/16$. Both ranges lie inside $N\beta<2\kappa_G/29$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:groups}.
\end{remark}

\subsection{One step of the block map: the large fields}\label{ssec:lfstep}

This subsection carries out, for $G=\SU(2)$, the large-field part of one
step of the block map $U\mapsto c=V^\sharp(U)$ on the whole torus. It proves
three things. A set of rough blocks is suppressed by $e^{-\lambda\kappa^2}$
per block, either absolutely or in the mean. The weight of a coarse field
is an exact sum over large-field regions of kernels with this suppression.
The coarse action lies between $\lambda/(1.65\cdot10^6)$ and
$8\lambda$ times the coarse curvature, up to a volume term. It also states
which bound the next step would need, and how far
Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide} supplies it. The small-field part and its
locality are the subject of item~(iv) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains} and are
not treated here. The lattice counts and the numerical constants are
proved by hand. The one exception is the value of the coupling $(M_W)_{AB}$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}, which is computed in
Remark~\ref{rem:sfgaussvalue} and used by no proof; the statements that the
calm weight is not local are conditional on $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$.

Throughout, $\Lambda_L$ is the torus of side $L=2^m\ge32$ in the tree gauge,
$T$ is the coarse torus of the blocks $B(y)$, $|T|=L^4/16$, $\lambda=\beta_W/4$,
so that the Wilson weight is $e^{-\lambda Q}$ with $Q=\sum_p\delta(U_p,I)^2$,
and $\nu_c$ is the fibre measure of Sec.~\ref{ssec:largefields} with $W=T$.
For a coarse field $c$ write $c_P$ for the holonomy of a coarse plaquette
and $Q_1(c)=\sum_P\delta(c_P,I)^2$.

\begin{definition}\label{def:lfrough}
The plaquette at $x$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ is \emph{owned} by the block
containing $x$; $\Pi(y)$ is the set of plaquettes owned by $y$, and
$\Pi(X)=\bigcup_{y\in X}\Pi(y)$. For $\kappa>0$ a block $y$ is \emph{calm}
if $\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa$ for every $p\in\Pi(y)$, and \emph{rough}
otherwise; $R(U)$ is the set of rough blocks. For a block $y$ let $I_y$ be
the $17$ active links inside $B(y)$, $P_{y,\mu}$ the eight private links of
the pair $(y,\mu)$, and $\varXi_y=(I_y,P_{y,0},\dots,P_{y,3})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:lfowned}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Every plaquette has exactly one owner, and $|\Pi(y)|=96$.
\item Every $p\in\Pi(y)$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ contains an active link
with base in $B(y)$, and each of its links has its base in $B(y)$,
$B(y+e_\mu)$ or $B(y+e_\nu)$.
\item The variables $\varXi_y$, $y\in T$, are the active links, each once.
The factor $f_y=\exp(-\lambda\sum_{p\in\Pi(y)}\delta(U_p,I)^2)$ and the
indicator $r_y$ of $\{y\text{ rough}\}$ are functions of $\varXi_y$ and
$\varXi_{y+e_\mu}$, $0\le\mu\le3$, and $e^{-\lambda Q}=\prod_yf_y$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) A plaquette has one corner, and each of the $16$ sites of a block is
the corner of six plaquettes. (ii) Let $o$ be the offset of the corner $x$.
If $o_\mu=1$ the link $(x,\mu)$ leaves $B(y)$ and is private, and likewise
if $o_\nu=1$. If $o_\mu=o_\nu=0$ the four vertices lie in $B(y)$ and the
plaquette is a cycle in the block, which the fifteen tree links, a tree by
Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(i), cannot contain; so one of its links, all
based in $B(y)$, is active. The links of $p$ are based at $x$, $x+e_\mu$ and
$x+e_\nu$. (iii) A link based in $B(y)$ is a tree link, an active link inside
$B(y)$, or a private link of a pair $(y,\mu)$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(i); the rest follows from (ii).
\end{proof}

A computer enumeration of the $96$ plaquettes of a block agrees with (i)
and (ii); the proof does not use it.

\paragraph*{Suppression.}
For a set $X$ of blocks let $A_X$, $Q_X$, $\nu^X_c$, $\pi_E$ and $Q_*(E)$ be
as in Sec.~\ref{ssec:largefields} with $W=X$, so that $\nu^X_c$ lives on the
fibre of $X$ with the links off $A_X$ fixed.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:lfsuppression}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\kappa>0$, $\lambda>0$ and let $X$ be a set of blocks.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $c$ and every choice of the links off $A_X$,
\[
\int\mathbf 1\{X\subset R(U)\}\,e^{-\lambda Q_X}\,d\nu^X_c\le M^{4|X|}
e^{-\lambda\kappa^2|X|},
\]
with $M<2.3621\cdot10^4$ the constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity}.
\item Let $\kappa\le1$ and $0<\tau\le1$. If the exterior $E$ of $X$ has
$Q_*(E)\le(1-\tau)\kappa^2|X|$, then
\[
\pi_E\{X\subset R\}\le\Bigl(\frac{5.9\cdot10^{14}}{(\tau\kappa^2)^3}
\Bigr)^{49|X|}e^{-3\lambda\tau\kappa^2|X|/4}.
\]
\item If $\beta_W\ge1$ and $\kappa\le1$, then $\mu_L\{X\subset R\}\le
(16\,q_\kappa(\beta_W))^{|X|}$, with $q_\kappa$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On $\{X\subset R\}$ each block of $X$ owns a plaquette with $\delta(U_p,I)
>\kappa$; these plaquettes are distinct and, by Lemma~\ref{lem:lfowned}(ii),
contain links of $A_X$. Hence $Q_X>\kappa^2|X|$ there.

(i) The integrand is at most $e^{-\lambda\kappa^2|X|}$, and $\nu^X_c$ has
mass at most $M^{4|X|}$ by~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}.

(ii) With $t=\tau\kappa^2|X|$, $\{X\subset R\}\subset\{Q_X>Q_*(E)+t\}$. The
proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:fibrecompare} uses $t\le1$ only to have
$\rho=t/(90.6\,n_P)<1.5\cdot10^{-4}$. Each of the $49|X|$ links of $A_X$
lies in six plaquettes and a plaquette contains at most four of them, so
$n_P\ge73.5|X|$ and $\rho\le\tau\kappa^2/6659<1.51\cdot10^{-4}$, which
still gives $16\sqrt2\rho+16\rho^2<22.63\rho$. The proof therefore gives
the bound $(14\cdot90.6^3n_P^3/t^3)^{49|X|}e^{-3\lambda t/4}$, and $n_P\le
384|X|$ with $14\cdot90.6^3\cdot384^3<5.9\cdot10^{14}$.

(iii) The plaquette at $x$ lies in the unit cube $\mathcal C_x$, so a rough
block $y$ lies in $\bigcup_{x\in B(y)}B_x$. Expanding the intersection over
$y\in X$ of these unions gives at most $16^{|X|}$ intersections $\bigcap_{y
\in X}B_{x(y)}$ with $x(y)\in B(y)$, each over $|X|$ distinct cubes, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} bounds each by $q_\kappa^{|X|}$.
\end{proof}

Part (i) is uniform in the exterior and in $c$, but it is an absolute
bound: it does not compare rough with calm completions. The comparison (ii)
needs its hypothesis. For the frustrated exterior described after
Corollary~\ref{cor:defectscales}, a plaquette through the link $e$ is bad
with conditional probability tending to one. No conditional bound uniform in
the exterior holds.

\paragraph*{Coarse curvature.}
For a coarse plaquette $P$ let $N(P)$ be the fine plaquettes with a vertex in
one of the $144$ blocks at $\ell^\infty$ distance at most one from the four
