blocks of $P$, the witness region of Lemma~\ref{lem:coarsewitness}, and let
$N_{\rm ov}$ be the largest number of witness regions that contain one fine
plaquette. Then $N_{\rm ov}=1441$, and $2310$ witness regions meet
$\Pi(y)$. Indeed, let $P$ have the blocks $z$, $z+e_\mu$, $z+e_\nu$,
$z+e_\mu+e_\nu$, with $B(z)=2z+\{0,1\}^4$. The $144$ blocks fill the box of
fine sites $w$ with $w_i-2z_i\in[-2,5]$ for $i\in\{\mu,\nu\}$ and
$w_i-2z_i\in[-2,3]$ otherwise, and the plaquette at $x$ in the plane
$\{\alpha,\beta\}$ has a vertex in it exactly when, for each $i$, $x_i$ lies
in the $i$-th interval, enlarged by one site to the left when $i\in\{\alpha,
\beta\}$. For fixed $x$ the number of admissible $z_i$ is $4$ for
$i\in\{\mu,\nu\}$ and $3$ otherwise, plus one when $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$
and $x_i$ is odd. With $x_\alpha,x_\beta$ odd the six planes $\{\mu,\nu\}$
give $5\cdot5\cdot3\cdot3$, four times $5\cdot4\cdot4\cdot3$ and
$4^4$, which sum to $225+960+256=1441$, and no parity gives more. For the
second count take $y=0$: the plaquettes of $\Pi(0)$ have corners in
$\{0,1\}^4$ and any plane. For each $i$ the admissible $z_i$ are those with
$z_i\in[-2,1]$ for $i\in\{\mu,\nu\}$ and $z_i\in[-1,1]$ otherwise, and
$z_i=2$, which needs $x_i=1$ and $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$; so $z$ is admissible
exactly when at most two coordinates equal $2$. Of the $5\cdot5\cdot4\cdot4
=400$ points of the enlarged box, $8+6+1=15$ have three or four
coordinates equal to $2$, and the six planes give $6\cdot385=2310$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:lfcoarseenergy}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $C_E=8/\kappa_c^2<1140.26$ and $C_*=1441\,C_E<1.6432\cdot
10^6$. For every field $U$ in the tree gauge, $c=V^\sharp(U)$ and every
coarse plaquette $P$,
\[
\delta(c_P,I)^2\le C_E\max_{p\in N(P)}\delta(U_p,I)^2 ,
\]
and if $\kappa<\kappa_c$ and $\delta(c_P,I)>16.003\,\kappa$, some $p\in N(P)$
has $\delta(U_p,I)>\kappa$. Consequently $Q_1(c)\le C_*\,Q(U)$, and
\[
Q_1^{>}(c):=\sum_{\delta(c_P,I)>16.003\kappa}\delta(c_P,I)^2\le C_*
\sum_{\delta(U_p,I)>\kappa}\delta(U_p,I)^2 .
\]
In particular $Q(U)\ge r^2/1140.26$ whenever some coarse plaquette has
$\delta(c_P,I)\ge r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $m$ be the maximum over $N(P)$. If $m<\kappa_c$, then
Proposition~\ref{prop:smallframessharp}(iv), applied with every $\kappa\in
(m,\kappa_c)$, gives $\delta(c_P,I)\le16.003\,m$, and $16.003^2<256.1<C_E$.
If $m\ge\kappa_c$, then $\delta(c_P,I)\le2\sqrt2$, the diameter of
$\SU(2)$, so $\delta(c_P,I)^2\le8\le C_Em^2$. The second statement is the
same proposition. Summing $\delta(c_P,I)^2\le C_E\sum_{p\in N(P)}\delta(U_p,
I)^2$ over $P$ counts each fine plaquette at most $N_{\rm ov}$ times; for
$Q_1^{>}$ keep in each sum only the plaquettes above $\kappa$, among which
the maximum lies.
\end{proof}

The last statement is the first step of Proposition~\ref{prop:torusenergy}
for $\SU(2)$, with $1140.26$ in place of $1154$; it is a bound for one step
only.

\paragraph*{The coarse action.}
Since $h=\int\nu_c\,dh(c)$, the law of $c=V^\sharp(U)$ under the Wilson
measure is $Z_L^{-1}e^{-A_1(c)}\,dh(c)$ with
\[
e^{-A_1(c)}=Z(c)=\nu_c\bigl(e^{-\lambda Q}\bigr).
\]
Let $S_1(c)=\inf_{F_c}Q$. In the reconstruction $R(c)$ of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:pathblocks}, with $c_{y,\mu}$ on the private links of
$(y,\mu)$ and $I$ on the links inside the blocks, every path of $V^\sharp_
{y,\mu}$ has holonomy $c_{y,\mu}$. So $v_x=I$ at every site, $R(c)$ is
regular, and $V^\sharp(R(c))=c$. A plaquette at $x$ in the plane
$\{\mu,\nu\}$ of $R(c)$ is $c_P$ when $o_\mu=o_\nu=1$ and $I$ otherwise,
so $Q(R(c))=4Q_1(c)$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:lfaction}
Let $G=\SU(2)$. For every coarse field $c$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $A_1(c)\ge\lambda S_1(c)-4|T|\log M$, and $S_1(c)\ge Q_1(c)/C_*$;
\item for $\lambda\ge100$, $\eta>0$ and every regular $U\in F_c$,
$A_1(c)\le(1+\eta)\lambda Q(U)+c_1(\lambda,\eta)|T|$, where
\begin{multline*}
c_1(\lambda,\eta)=12\log1.957+45\log14\\
+67.5\bigl(1+\log(11520(1+\eta^{-1})\lambda)\bigr);
\end{multline*}
in particular $A_1(c)\le8\lambda Q_1(c)+c_1(\lambda,1)|T|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) $Z(c)\le\nu_c(F_c)e^{-\lambda S_1(c)}$ and $\nu_c(F_c)\le M^{4|T|}$ by
\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}; then Lemma~\ref{lem:lfcoarseenergy}.

(ii) Let $\rho^2=135/(2\cdot96\cdot8100(1+\eta^{-1})\lambda)$, so $\rho\le
9.32\cdot10^{-4}$ and $46\rho<0.043$. The proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:everyfibre} with $W=T$ uses $t\le1$ only through this
bound on $46\rho$. It gives a set $\Gamma(D)\subset F_c$ with $\nu_c(\Gamma(D))
\ge1.957^{-12|T|}(\rho^3/14)^{45|T|}$ on which each of the $n_P=96|T|$
plaquettes moves by at most $90\rho$. There $\delta(U'_p,I)\le\delta(U_p,
I)+90\rho$, so
\[
Q(U')\le(1+\eta)Q(U)+(1+\eta^{-1})\,96|T|\,8100\rho^2 .
\]
Hence $A_1(c)\le(1+\eta)\lambda Q(U)+|T|g(\rho)$ with $g(\rho)=(1+
\eta^{-1})777600\lambda\rho^2+135\log\rho^{-1}+12\log1.957+45\log14$, and
the chosen $\rho$ minimises $g$, with value $c_1(\lambda,\eta)$. For the
last statement take $U=R(c)$ and $\eta=1$.
\end{proof}

So the coarse action is $\lambda$ times a quantity between $Q_1/C_*$ and
$8Q_1$, up to $O(\log\lambda)$ per block; the volume term $67.5\log\lambda$
is the Gaussian count of the $135$ real fluctuation coordinates of a block.
Neither constant is near one. For example $c_1(10^{12},1)<2737.5$ and
$4\log M<40.35$.

\paragraph*{The large-field representation.}
Write $s_y=1-r_y$. For $X\subset T$ let $X_1,\dots,X_n$ be its components
for $\ell^\infty$ adjacency of blocks, so that distinct components are at
$\ell^\infty$ distance at least two. For a set $Y$ of blocks let
$\partial^-Y$ be the set of blocks $z\notin Y$ with $z+e_\mu\in Y$ for
some $\mu$; a block of $\partial^-X_i$ lies off $X$. By the definition of
$\nu_c$,
\[
\nu_c(d\varXi)=\prod_yh(dI_y)\prod_{y,\mu}\nu^{y,\mu}_{c}(dP_{y,\mu}\mid
I_y,I_{y+e_\mu}),
\]
where $\nu^{y,\mu}_c$ is the measure of~\eqref{eq:densityformula} on the
private links of the pair, of mass at most $M$.

Let $\partial^=X$ be the set of blocks $w\notin
X\cup\partial^-X$ with $w+e_\mu+e_\nu\in X$ for some $\mu\ne\nu$, and put
$\hat X=X\cup\partial^-X\cup\partial^=X$. Let $\mathcal P_X$ be the set of
pairs from $X$ together with the pairs $(z,\mu)$ with $z\notin X$ and
$z+e_\mu\in X$, and let $\mathcal V_X$ be the links inside the blocks of
$X$ together with the private links of the pairs of $\mathcal P_X$: these
are the variables that the kernel of $X$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}
integrates.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:sfkernel}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The factors $f_y$ and $r_y$ are functions of $I_y$, of the
$P_{y,\mu}$, and of $I_{y+e_\nu}$ and $P_{y+e_\nu,\mu}$ for $\mu\ne\nu$.
The average $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}$ is a function of $P_{y,\mu}$, $I_y$ and
$I_{y+e_\mu}$.
\item The factor $f_w$ involves a link of $\mathcal V_X$ if and only if
$w\in\hat X$.
\item Let the components $X_i$ of $X$ be at $\ell^\infty$ distance at least
two. Then $\hat X$ is the disjoint union of the $\hat X_i$, each block of
$\hat X_i$ lies within $\ell^\infty$ distance one of $X_i$, and for $j\ne i$
no factor $f_w$ or $r_w$ with $w\in\hat X_i$ involves a link of
$\mathcal V_{X_j}$.
\item Every plaquette that contains a link of $\mathcal V_X$ is owned by a
block of $\hat X$ and has a vertex in a block of $X$. There are at most
$216|X|$ such plaquettes, every plaquette of $\Pi(X)$ is one of them, and
$|\mathcal P_X|\le8|X|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Let $p$ be the plaquette at $x\in B(y)$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:lfowned}(ii) its links are based in $B(y)$, $B(y+e_\mu)$ or
$B(y+e_\nu)$. The one based in $B(y+e_\nu)$ is $(x+e_\nu,\mu)$, whose offset
in the direction $\mu$ is that of $x$: it is a link inside $B(y+e_\nu)$
or a tree link if $o_\mu=0$, and a private link of $(y+e_\nu,\mu)$ if
$o_\mu=1$. The links based in $B(y)$ are inside $B(y)$ or private to pairs
from $y$. The average is the mean over the paths $(x,\mu),(x+e_\mu,\mu)$,
$x\in B(y)$, of Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(iii). (ii) By (i), $f_w$ involves
a variable of $\varXi_y$ with $y\in X$ if and only if $w=y$ or $w+e_\nu=y$,
that is $w\in X\cup\partial^-X$. It involves a private link of a pair
$(z,\mu)$ with $z\notin X$, $z+e_\mu\in X$ if and only if $w=z$ or
$w=z-e_\nu$ with $\nu\ne\mu$; the first gives $w\in\partial^-X$ and the
second $w+e_\mu+e_\nu\in X$. (iii) Every block of $\hat X_i$ has the form $x$, $x-e_\mu$ or $x-e_\mu
-e_\nu$ with $x\in X_i$, so it lies within distance one of $X_i$, and a
block of $\hat X_i\cap\hat X_j$ would give blocks of $X_i$ and $X_j$ at
distance at most one. For the same reason a block of $\partial^-X_i$ or
$\partial^=X_i$ lies in no $X_j$ and in no $\partial^-X_j$, so $\hat X=
\bigcup_i\hat X_i$. By (ii) for $X_j$, a factor that involves a link of
$\mathcal V_{X_j}$ belongs to a block of $\hat X_j$, which is not in
$\hat X_i$. (iv)
A link of $\mathcal V_X$ is based in a block of $X$, or is a private link
$(x,\mu)$ of a pair $(z,\mu)$ with $z+e_\mu\in X$, which ends at $x+e_\mu\in
B(z+e_\mu)$. The owner of a plaquette that contains it involves it, so it
lies in $\hat X$ by (ii). Since $\mathcal V_X\subset\bigcup_{x\in X}\mathcal
V_{\{x\}}$, the count is at most $|X|$ times the number of plaquettes with
a vertex in one block $B(y)=2y+\{0,1\}^4$. The plaquette at $c$ in the plane
$\{\alpha,\beta\}$ has a vertex in $B(y)$ exactly when $c_i-2y_i\in\{0,1\}$
for $i\notin\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and $c_i-2y_i\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for
$i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, so there are $6\cdot2^2\cdot3^2=216$ of them. There are $4|X|$ pairs from $X$, and
$(z,\mu)\mapsto(z+e_\mu,\mu)$ is injective on the others. The plaquettes of
$\Pi(X)$ contain an active link with base in a block of $X$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:lfowned}(ii).
\end{proof}

A computer enumeration agrees with (i), and with (ii)--(iv) for $300$
random $\ell^\infty$-connected sets of up to seven blocks and for $300$
random pairs of such sets at distance at least two; the proof does not use it.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:lfmarkov}
Let $G=\SU(2)$ and $\kappa>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For every $c$, $Z(c)=\sum_{X\subset T}Z_X(c)$ with
\[
Z_X(c)=\int\nu^{\rm out}_{c,X}(d\varXi)\prod_{y\notin\hat X}
f_ys_y\prod_iK_{X_i}(c;\varXi),
\]
with $\hat X=\bigcup_i\hat X_i$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}.
Here $\nu^{\rm out}_{c,X}$ is the product of the factors of $\nu_c$ for
the links inside the blocks off $X$ and for the pairs with both blocks off
$X$. The kernel $K_{X_i}$ is the integral of $\prod_{y\in X_i}f_yr_y
\prod_{z\in\hat X_i\setminus X_i}f_zs_z$ against the factors of $\nu_c$ for the
links inside $X_i$, the pairs from $X_i$ and the pairs $(z,\mu)$ with $z\in
\partial^-X_i$ and $z+e_\mu\in X_i$. It depends on the integration variable
of $\nu^{\rm out}_{c,X}$ only through the blocks at $\ell^\infty$ distance
one from $X_i$. No two kernels share a factor or an integration
variable; two kernels may share boundary arguments, the inside links of
a block between them, which the common outer integral integrates.
\item For $\kappa<\kappa_c$, uniformly in the outer variables,
\[
0\le K_{X_i}\le M^{8|X_i|}\exp\Bigl(-\lambda\max\Bigl\{\kappa^2|X_i|,
\frac{Q^{(i)}(c)}{C_*}\Bigr\}\Bigr),
\]
where $Q^{(i)}(c)$ is the sum of $\delta(c_P,I)^2>(16.003\kappa)^2$ over
the coarse plaquettes $P$ with $\emptyset\ne N(P)\cap\Pi(X)\subset\Pi(X_i)$.
\item With $N_\lambda=e^{-c_1(\lambda,1)}$, $K_{X_i}\le N_\lambda^{|X_i|}
e^{-a(\lambda,\kappa)|X_i|}$, where
\[
a(\lambda,\kappa)=\lambda\kappa^2-8\log M-c_1(\lambda,1),
\]
and $Z(c)\ge N_\lambda^{|T|}e^{-8\lambda Q_1(c)}$ for $\lambda\ge100$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) Expand $\prod_y(f_yr_y+f_ys_y)$ and group the terms by $X=\{y:r_y\}$;
then apply Fubini to the nonnegative integrands. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:lfowned}(iii), $f_y$ and $r_y$ involve $\varXi_y$ and
$\varXi_{y+e_\mu}$, and $\nu^{y,\mu}_c$ involves $P_{y,\mu}$, $I_y$ and
$I_{y+e_\mu}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(ii) and~(iii), the factors
that involve a variable integrated by the kernel of $X_i$ are those of the
blocks of $\hat X_i$, and none of them involves a variable integrated by
the kernel of $X_j$, $j\ne i$. The measure of a pair into $X_i$ involves
its private links and the inside links of its two blocks, and a pair is
into or from at most one component.
(ii) The measures in $K_{X_i}$ have mass at most $M$ for each of the
$4|X_i|$ pairs from $X_i$ and the at most $4|X_i|$ pairs into it, and $h$
is a probability. The integrand is at most $e^{-\lambda Q_{\Pi(X_i)}}$
and vanishes unless every block of $X_i$ is rough. Then $Q_{\Pi(X_i)}>
\kappa^2|X_i|$, and every fine plaquette above $\kappa$ is owned by a rough
block. So for the $P$ counted in $Q^{(i)}$ the plaquettes above $\kappa$
in $N(P)$ lie in $\Pi(X_i)$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:lfcoarseenergy} gives
$Q^{(i)}(c)\le C_*Q_{\Pi(X_i)}$.
(iii) The first bound is (ii) with the definition of $a$; the second is
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}(ii) with $U=R(c)$.
\end{proof}

The representation is exact, and every kernel carries $e^{-\lambda\kappa^2}$
per block, uniformly in its boundary values and in $c$. When the coarse
field is curved its kernel also carries $e^{-\lambda Q^{(i)}/C_*}$. The
small-field factor $\prod f_ys_y$, however, is not a product of local
factors once the outer variables are integrated. The comparison of a kernel
with the calm weight $S_{X_i}$, the same integral with $s_y$ in place of
$r_y$ on $X_i$, would give the relative activities $K_{X_i}/S_{X_i}$. It
fails where $S_{X_i}=0<K_{X_i}$, that is, where the boundary values admit
no calm completion; Theorem~\ref{thm:lfsuppression}(ii) bounds the ratio
only under its hypothesis.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:lfkp}
Call two nonempty $\ell^\infty$-connected sets of blocks compatible when
their $\ell^\infty$ distance is at least two, and let $w$ be activities
with $|w(X)|\le e^{-9|X|}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The criterion of Koteck\'y and Preiss~\cite{KP86} holds with $a(X)=
|X|/10$. So $\log\sum\prod_iw(X_i)$, the sum over families of pairwise
compatible sets, is the absolutely convergent sum of the connected
clusters. The clusters incompatible with a given block contribute at most
$1/10$ in absolute value, and the logarithm is at most $|T|/10$ in modulus.
\item The rate of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(iii) satisfies $a(\lambda,
\kappa)\ge9$ for $\lambda\ge\max\{\lambda^*(\kappa),100\}$, with $\beta^*=
4\lambda^*$ given below.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\hline
$\kappa$ & $\beta^*$ & $\lambda^*\kappa^2$\\
\hline
$0.08$ & $1.13125\cdot10^{6}$ & $1810$\\
$10^{-2}$ & $8.404\cdot10^{7}$ & $2101$\\
$10^{-4}$ & $1.0964\cdot10^{12}$ & $2741$\\
$10^{-8}$ & $1.604\cdot10^{20}$ & $4010$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) A connected set of $n$ blocks through a given block is recovered from
a walk of length $2(n-1)$ around a spanning tree, with $80$ neighbours at
each step, as in Corollary~\ref{cor:defectclusters}; so there are at most
$6400^{n-1}$. A set incompatible with $X$ contains one of the at most
$81|X|$ blocks within distance one of $X$. Hence
\[
\sum_{X'\not\sim X}|w(X')|e^{|X'|/10}\le81|X|\frac u{1-6400u},
\]
with $u=e^{-8.9}$. Since $8.9>\log7290=\log2+6\log3+\log5$, $u<1/7290$,
and the right side, which increases with $u$, is below $81|X|/(7290-6400)
<0.092|X|<|X|/10$. This is the hypothesis of the theorem of Koteck\'y and
Preiss, whose conclusion is the statement.

(ii) Write $L_p=\log p$. With its tail bounded geometrically, the series
$\log\frac{1+x}{1-x}=2\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{x^{2k+1}}{2k+1}$ at $x=\frac13$,
$\frac15$, $\frac19$ and $\frac1{99}$ gives $\log2$, $\log\frac32$,
$\log\frac54$ and $\log\frac{50}{49}$ to within $10^{-10}$, hence
\begin{gather*}
0.69314718<L_2<0.69314719,\\
1.09861228<L_3<1.09861229,\\
1.60943791<L_5<1.60943792,\\
1.94591014<L_7<1.94591015,
\end{gather*}
and $\log10=L_2+L_5$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity}, $\log M<\log(2.4
\cdot10^4)=6L_2+L_3+3L_5$, and $\log1.957<\log1.96=2L_7-2L_5$. With
$\log14=L_2+L_7$ and $\log23040=9L_2+2L_3+L_5$, for $\lambda\ge100$
\[
8\log M+c_1(\lambda,1)\le K_0+67.5\log\lambda,
\]
where $K_0=67.5+700.5L_2+143L_3+67.5L_5+69L_7<953.06$. Put $t=\lambda
\kappa^2$. Then $a(\lambda,\kappa)\ge t-67.5\log t-K_0-67.5\log
\kappa^{-2}$, whose right side increases with $t$ for $t>67.5$. So $a\ge9$
for $\lambda\ge\max\{\lambda^*,100\}$ once $t^*=\lambda^*\kappa^2$
satisfies
\[
t^*-67.5\log t^*\ge962.06+67.5\log\kappa^{-2}.
\]
In the four rows of the table $\log\kappa^{-2}$ equals $4L_5-2L_2$,
$4\log10$, $8\log10$ and $16\log10$, and, by $\log(1+x)\le x$, $\log t^*$
is at most $\log1800+\frac1{180}$, $\log2100+\frac1{2100}$, $\log2744$ and
$\log4000+\frac1{400}$, with $1800=2^33^25^2$, $2100=2^2\cdot3\cdot5^2
\cdot7$, $2744=2^37^3$ and $4000=2^55^3$. With these bounds the left side
exceeds the right by more than $0.6$ in each row.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp} applies to the large fields once the small-field
part is in local form. Then each region costs its kernel divided by the
calm weight of the same region, and $a\ge9$ beats the entropy of connected
regions if that calm weight is at least $N_\lambda$ per block. This lower
bound on the calm weight with boundary values is not proved. It is the
small-field cluster expansion of item~(iv) of Sec.~\ref{ssec:remains}, and
it must have the relative and local form required by
Propositions~\ref{prop:formstability} and~\ref{prop:massgrowth} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}.

\paragraph*{The small-field part.}
The rest of this subsection treats the factor $\prod f_ys_y$. It proves
three things. First, a kernel is at most $e^{-a_2|X|}$ times the
calm weight of its region whenever the boundary values admit a completion
that is calm at a smaller threshold $\kappa'$. Second, the large-field sum
is exactly the calm weight times a mean, under the calm law, of products of
these ratios, and the polymer sums of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp} bound it once
the ratios are small. Third, to leading order in $\lambda$ the logarithm of
the calm weight is $-\lambda$ times the Gaussian block-spin form, so that
the calm weight is a product of local factors to within $e^{\pm
o(\lambda)}$ only if this form does not couple distant coarse links; its
coefficient at two coarse links three blocks apart is a rational number
$(M_W)_{AB}$, which a computation not used in the proofs finds nonzero.
What remains open is stated at the end.

\emph{The calm weight.} Fix $X\ne\emptyset$ and the outer variables of
$K_X$. Let $\lambda_X$ be the measure of $K_X$, the product of $h$ on the
links inside the blocks of $X$ and of the measures $\nu^k_c$ of the pairs
$k\in\mathcal P_X$, of mass at most $M^{8|X|}$. The \emph{calm weight} is
\[
S_X=\int\prod_{y\in\hat X}f_ys_y\,d\lambda_X ,
\]
the integral of $K_X$ with $s_y$ in place of $r_y$ on $X$. A plaquette of
$\Pi(\hat X)$ is \emph{moved} if it contains a link of $\mathcal V_X$ and
\emph{fixed} otherwise; $Q^{\rm mov}_X$ and $Q^{\rm fix}_X$ are the sums of
$\delta(U_p,I)^2$ over the moved and the fixed plaquettes, and $Q^{\rm fix}
_X$ is a function of the outer variables. A \emph{completion} is a value of
$\mathcal V_X$ at which the averages of the pairs of $\mathcal P_X$ equal
$c$. Put
\begin{multline*}
c_2(\lambda,\eta)=24\log1.957+73\log14\\
+109.5\bigl(1+\log(15979(1+\eta^{-1})\lambda)\bigr).
\end{multline*}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfcalm}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $0<\kappa'<\kappa$, $\eta>0$, and $\lambda\ge100$ with
$\lambda(\kappa-\kappa')^2\ge1$. Suppose that the fixed plaquettes of
$\Pi(\hat X)$ are at most $\kappa$, which holds whenever $K_X>0$, and that
there is a completion $U^0$ with
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\delta(v_x,I)\le\frac14$ at every site of every pair of $\mathcal
P_X$;
\item $\delta(U^0_p,I)\le\kappa'$ for every moved plaquette.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
S_X\ge e^{-c_2(\lambda,\eta)|X|}e^{-\lambda Q^{\rm fix}_X}e^{-(1+\eta)
\lambda Q^{\rm mov}_X(U^0)},
\]
and
\begin{multline*}
\frac{K_X}{S_X}\le\exp\Bigl(-\bigl(\lambda\kappa^2-8\log M-c_2(\lambda,\eta)
\bigr)|X|\\
+(1+\eta)\lambda Q^{\rm mov}_X(U^0)\Bigr)\le e^{-a_2|X|},
\end{multline*}
where $a_2(\lambda,\kappa)=\lambda\kappa^2\bigl(1-216(1+\eta)\kappa'^2/
\kappa^2\bigr)-8\log M-c_2(\lambda,\eta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $\rho^2=1/(15978.08(1+\eta^{-1})\lambda)$. Then $\rho\le7.92\cdot
10^{-4}$, and $90\rho\le0.712\lambda^{-1/2}<\kappa-\kappa'$. Let $L'$ be the
links of $\mathcal V_X$ other than the path links of the pairs of
$\mathcal P_X$, $17|X|+7|\mathcal P_X|\le73|X|$ in number, and $D$ the set
of $z\in G^{L'}$ with $d(z_e,U^0_e)\le\rho$ for every $e\in L'$. For $z\in
D$ and a pair $k$, each site $v_x$ of $k$ is $\ell^{-1}$ times a product
of at most two links of $L'$ and outer links, $\ell$ the path link. As in
the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:calmfibre}, with $R=44\rho$ the sites lie
within $46\rho<0.043$ of their values at $U^0$, so $\delta(v_x,I)<\frac12$
by (a), the cut-off equals one, and the contraction argument of that proof
solves each path link in the ball of radius $R$ about its value at $U^0$.
This gives an injective map $\Gamma$ from $D$ into the completions, near
whose image the averages are smooth with $\lvert\det\partial_{d_k}V^\sharp
_k\rvert\le1.957^3$. The coarea form of $\nu^k_c$ stated
after~\eqref{eq:fibrevolume}, applied to each pair of $\mathcal P_X$ with
the inside links of its blocks given, shows that $\lambda_X$ restricted to
$\Gamma(D)$ is the image of $h^{\otimes L'}$ on $D$ divided by
$\prod_k\lvert\det\partial_{d_k}V^\sharp_k\rvert$. Hence
\[
\lambda_X\bigl(\Gamma(D)\bigr)\ge1.957^{-3|\mathcal P_X|}\Bigl(\frac{\rho^3}
{14}\Bigr)^{|L'|}\ge1.957^{-24|X|}\Bigl(\frac{\rho^3}{14}\Bigr)^{73|X|}.
\]
A plaquette has at most two path links, so on $\Gamma(D)$ each moved
plaquette moves by at most $90\rho$, as in that proof, and stays at most
$\kappa'+90\rho<\kappa$; the fixed ones are at most $\kappa$. Every block of
$\hat X$ is therefore calm on $\Gamma(D)$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(iv),
\[
Q^{\rm mov}_X\le(1+\eta)Q^{\rm mov}_X(U^0)+(1+\eta^{-1})\,8100\rho^2\cdot
216|X| .
\]
So $S_X\ge e^{-g|X|}e^{-\lambda Q^{\rm fix}_X}e^{-(1+\eta)\lambda Q^{\rm
mov}_X(U^0)}$ with $g=24\log1.957+73\log14+219\log\rho^{-1}+(1+\eta^{-1})
1749600\lambda\rho^2$. With the chosen $\rho$ the last term is $109.5$
and $g\le c_2(\lambda,\eta)$, as $2\cdot216\cdot8100/219<15978.09$.

The integrand of $K_X$ is at most $e^{-\lambda Q^{\rm fix}_X}e^{-\lambda
Q^{\rm mov}_X}$ and vanishes unless every block of $X$ is rough. Then each
block of $X$ owns a plaquette above $\kappa$, these are distinct, and they
are moved by Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(iv), so $Q^{\rm mov}_X>\kappa^2|X|$.
With $\lambda_X$ of mass at most $M^{8|X|}$, $K_X\le M^{8|X|}e^{-\lambda
Q^{\rm fix}_X}e^{-\lambda\kappa^2|X|}$. Dividing gives the first bound, and
(b) with Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(iv) gives $Q^{\rm mov}_X(U^0)\le216
\kappa'^2|X|$.
\end{proof}

So the calm weight with given boundary values is at least $e^{-c_2}$ per
block, times the Gaussian factor of the completion, whenever the
boundary values admit a completion calm at $\kappa'$; the constant $c_2$
takes the place of $c_1$ because $K_X$ integrates up to $73$ rather than
$45$ links per block. With $\kappa'=\kappa/30$ and $\eta=1$,
$a_2=0.52\lambda\kappa^2-8\log M-c_2(\lambda,1)$, and $a_2\ge9$, the rate
that Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp} needs, holds for $\lambda\ge\lambda^{**}(\kappa)$,
with $\beta^{**}=4\lambda^{**}$ as follows:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\hline
$\kappa$ & $\beta^{**}$ & $\lambda^{**}\kappa^2$\\
\hline
$0.08$ & $3.6625\cdot10^{6}$ & $5860$\\
$10^{-2}$ & $2.7064\cdot10^{8}$ & $6766$\\
$10^{-4}$ & $3.504\cdot10^{12}$ & $8760$\\
$10^{-8}$ & $5.0872\cdot10^{20}$ & $12718$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Indeed, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(ii), now with $2\cdot
15979<32000=2^85^3$, $8\log M+c_2(\lambda,1)\le K_2+109.5\log\lambda$ for
$\lambda\ge100$, where $K_2=109.5+997L_2+8L_3+304.5L_5+121L_7<1534.89$, and
$0.52t-109.5\log t$ increases for $t>211$. In the four rows, with $t=
\lambda^{**}\kappa^2$, $\log t$ is at most $\log5832+\frac7{1458}$,
$\log6750+\frac8{3375}$, $\log8750+\frac1{875}$ and $\log12600+
\frac{59}{6300}$, where $5832=2^33^6$, $6750=2\cdot3^35^3$, $8750=2\cdot
5^47$ and $12600=2^33^25^27$, and $0.52t-109.5\log t$ exceeds $1543.89+
109.5\log\kappa^{-2}$ by more than $0.14$.
At these couplings $\rho\le(\kappa-\kappa')/90$ and $\rho\le7.92\cdot10^{-4}$.
The same construction bounds the calm weight of the whole torus.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:sfcoarse}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $0<\kappa'<\kappa<\kappa_c$, $\eta>0$ and $\lambda\ge100$
with $\lambda(\kappa-\kappa')^2\ge1$, and let $Z_\emptyset(c)=\nu_c(\prod_y
f_ys_y)$ be the calm weight of $c$. If $\delta(c_P,I)\le\kappa'$ for every
coarse plaquette, then
\[
Z_\emptyset(c)\ge e^{-c_1(\lambda,\eta)|T|}e^{-4(1+\eta)\lambda Q_1(c)},
\]
in particular $Z_\emptyset(c)\ge N_\lambda^{|T|}e^{-8\lambda Q_1(c)}$. If
$\delta(c_P,I)>16.003\kappa$ for some $P$, then $Z_\emptyset(c)=0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The plaquettes of the regular field $R(c)$ are the $c_P$ and $I$. In the
proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}(ii) with $U=R(c)$, $\rho\le(11520
\lambda)^{-1/2}$, so the plaquettes move by at most $90\rho<\kappa-\kappa'$
on $\Gamma(D)$, every block is calm there, and the bound of that proof holds
for $Z_\emptyset$. If $\delta(c_P,I)>16.003\kappa$, every field of $F_c$
has a plaquette above $\kappa$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:lfcoarseenergy}, so
$\prod_ys_y=0$ on $F_c$.
\end{proof}

So the class of coarse fields for which the calm weight can serve as a
reference lies between the fields with all coarse plaquettes at most
$\kappa'$ and those with all at most $16.003\kappa$. For $Z_\emptyset(c)>0$
let $\mu^\circ_c=Z_\emptyset(c)^{-1}\prod_yf_ys_y\,\nu_c$ be the calm law,
and for each $X$ and each value of its outer variables with $S_X>0$ let
$\rho_X=K_X/S_X$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:sfrelative}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\kappa>0$ and $Z_\emptyset(c)>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $Z(c)=Z_\emptyset(c)\,\varXi(c)+Z_\perp(c)$, where
\[
\varXi(c)=\sum_{X\subset T}\E_{\mu^\circ_c}\Bigl[\prod_i\rho_{X_i}\Bigr],
\]
the $X_i$ being the components of $X$, $\rho_{X_i}$ is defined
$\mu^\circ_c$-almost surely, and $Z_\perp(c)\ge0$ is the sum over $X$ of
the integrals of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(i), in the form of
Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(iii), restricted to the outer variables at which
some $S_{X_i}$ vanishes.
\item Suppose that for every nonempty $\ell^\infty$-connected $X$,
$\rho_X\le e^{-9|X|}$ holds $\mu^\circ_c$-almost surely. Then $\varXi(c)=
\E_{\mu^\circ_c}[e^{\varLambda}]$, where $\varLambda$ is the sum of the
connected clusters of the activities $\rho_X$ given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(i). Each cluster depends on the field only within
distance one of its support, the clusters incompatible with a given block
add up to at most $1/10$, $0\le\varLambda\le|T|/10$, and
\[
A_1(c)=-\log Z_\emptyset(c)-\log\E_{\mu^\circ_c}\bigl[e^{\varLambda}\bigr]
-\log\Bigl(1+\frac{Z_\perp(c)}{Z_\emptyset(c)\varXi(c)}\Bigr),
\]
with $0\le\log\E_{\mu^\circ_c}[e^{\varLambda}]\le|T|/10$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Fix $X$. The integrand $\prod_yf_ys_y$ of $Z_\emptyset$ factorises as
the integrand of $Z_X$ does in Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(iii), with
$s_y$ in place of $r_y$ on $X$, so by Fubini the law of the outer variables
of $X$ under $\mu^\circ_c$ is $Z_\emptyset^{-1}\varPhi_X\prod_iS_{X_i}\,
\nu^{\rm out}_{c,X}$, with $\varPhi_X$ the outer product. This law gives no
mass to $\{S_{X_i}=0\}$, and
\[
Z_X=\int\nu^{\rm out}_{c,X}\varPhi_X\prod_iK_{X_i}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{\text
{all }S_{X_i}>0\}+\mathbf 1\{\text{some }S_{X_i}=0\}\bigr).
\]
The first part is $Z_\emptyset\,\E_{\mu^\circ_c}[\prod_i\rho_{X_i}]$; sum
over $X$. (ii) For a field $U$ let $\rho_X(U)$ be $\rho_X$ at the outer
variables of $X$ in $U$. On a set of full $\mu^\circ_c$-measure all these
finitely many values are at most $e^{-9|X|}$, and there
$\sum_X\prod_i\rho_{X_i}(U)=e^{\varLambda(U)}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(i),
with the stated bounds; $\varLambda\ge0$ because the sum contains the
empty family and $\rho\ge0$. The mean of $\prod_i\rho_{X_i}$ is the same
whether taken on the outer variables of $X$ or on the field, which gives
$\varXi=\E[e^\varLambda]$, and $A_1=-\log Z$.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm} gives the hypothesis of (ii) at every field $U$
that is regular near $X$ and whose moved plaquettes are at most $\kappa'=
\kappa/30$, with $U$ itself as the completion. It does not give it at the
calm fields with a plaquette near $X$ between $\kappa'$ and $\kappa$, and
it says nothing about $Z_\perp$.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:sfshell}
The comparison of $K_X$ with $S_X$ needs a margin between the threshold of
the boundary values and that of the kernel, because a completion must stay
calm when it is moved by $90\rho$ and because its energy $Q^{\rm mov}_X$
must be small against $\kappa^2|X|$. For a calm field with plaquettes
near $X$ in the shell $(\kappa',\kappa]$, the moved energy of every
completion can be of order $216\kappa^2|X|$, and then the bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm} on $K_X/S_X$ exceeds one. Putting the blocks of
the shell into the large-field region removes them from the calm law, but
their kernels then carry only $e^{-\lambda\kappa'^2}$, and the comparison
moves to a smaller threshold $\kappa''<\kappa'$ with a new shell
$(\kappa'',\kappa']$. A bound on the calm law of the shell, uniform in $c$
and in the exterior, would end this regress; it is not proved.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:sfscale}
The decoupling of $\log\E_{\mu^\circ_c}[e^\varLambda]$ in $c$ and the
bound on the shell both ask for decorrelation of the calm law. Its
structure is as follows. By Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(i), $\nu_c$ is
$\prod_yh(dI_y)$ times the pair kernels $\nu^{y,\mu}_c(dP_{y,\mu}\mid I_y,
I_{y+e_\mu})$, each supported on $\{V^\sharp_{y,\mu}=c_{y,\mu}\}$ with mass
the density of Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity} at $c_{y,\mu}$, a function of
$I_y$ and $I_{y+e_\mu}$. So $\mu^\circ_c$ is a Gibbs measure for the
variables $\varXi_y$ of the blocks, with the factors $f_ys_y$, which by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}(i) couple $\varXi_y$ to $\varXi_{y+e_\nu}$, and the
pair kernels, which couple $I_y$ to $I_{y+e_\mu}$; all couplings have range
one. Large $\lambda$ does not make this a high-temperature system. In the
linearised law, the Gaussian measure proportional to $e^{-\lambda
Q(\varphi)}$ on an affine fibre $\{V(\varphi)=\gamma\}$ of real fields, the
conditional law of the variables of one block given the others is
Gaussian with a mean that is an affine function of the others independent
of $\lambda$, and a covariance equal to $\lambda^{-1}$ times a matrix
independent of $\lambda$. Hence the interdependence coefficients of
Dobrushin's condition for the Wasserstein distance, which for Gaussian laws
with equal covariances are the norms of the derivatives of these means,
do not depend on $\lambda$. Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}(iii) has the same
scaling: for functions $\lambda g_1$ and $\lambda g_2$ with $g_1$, $g_2$ as
there, it gives $c_9\lambda|X_1||X_2|e^{-\alpha_Gd(X_1,X_2)}$, which is
below one only for $d(X_1,X_2)\ge\alpha_G^{-1}\log(c_9\lambda|X_1||X_2|)$;
the logarithm of a calm weight is of this form to leading order, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss} below. The input that (ii) of
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative} needs for locality in $c$ is the decay of
the truncated correlations of all orders of the cluster terms of
$\varLambda$ under $\mu^\circ_c$, for every $c$ in the class of
Corollary~\ref{cor:sfcoarse}, the analogue for the calm law of the
differences of order three and more in Remark~\ref{rem:labelcovopen}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay}, \eqref{eq:layerbound} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound} give covariances of order two only.
\end{remark}

\emph{The Gaussian part of the calm weight.} Let $W$ be a finite set of
blocks and fix every link off $A_W$ to $I$. With the notation of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:largefields}, let $F_c$ be the fibre of $c=(c_k)_{k\in
W\times\{0,\dots,3\}}$, $\nu_c$ its measure, $Q_W$ the sum over the $n_P$
plaquettes that contain a link of $A_W$, and
\[
Z^\circ_W(c)=\int\prod_p\mathbf 1\{\delta(U_p,I)\le\kappa\}\,e^{-\lambda
Q_W}\,d\nu_c ,
\]
the product over the same $n_P$ plaquettes, the calm weight of $W$. For
real $\gamma\in\R^{W\times\{0,\dots,3\}}$ let
\[
q_W(\gamma)=\min\Bigl\{\sum_p(d\varphi)_p^2:\varphi\in\R^{A_W},\ V_k
(\varphi)=\gamma_k\ \text{for all }k\Bigr\},
\]
with $\varphi=0$ off $A_W$ and $V_k$ the linear average of
Definition~\ref{def:blockgauge}. The constraints are onto, since the path
link of $k$ enters $V_k$ alone, with coefficient $\frac18$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap} makes $\sum_p(d\varphi)_p^2$ positive definite on
$\{V(\varphi)=0\}$, so $q_W(\gamma)=\gamma^{\rm T}M_W\gamma$ for a positive
semidefinite matrix $M_W$. For $\g$-valued $w$, $\sum_aq_W(w^a)$ over the
components in an orthonormal basis of $\g$ is the form $S_W$ of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:relstep}, the minimum of the fine Hessian at given averages,
when $W$ is a box.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfgauss}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\kappa>0$, $W=\{0,e_0,2e_0,3e_0\}$, $A=(0,1)$ and
$B=(3e_0,1)$, $\tau\in\g$ with $\lVert\tau\rVert=1$, and for $\varepsilon>0$
and $s,t\in\{0,1\}$ let $c^{st}_\varepsilon$ equal $e^{\varepsilon s\tau}$
on $A$, $e^{\varepsilon t\tau}$ on $B$ and $I$ on the other coarse links of
$W$. Write $\Delta F=\sum_{s,t}(-1)^{s+t}F(c^{st}_\varepsilon)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $(M_W)_{AB}$ is a rational number.
\item There is $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for $0<\varepsilon\le
\varepsilon_0$
\[
\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty}\frac1\lambda\bigl\lvert\Delta\log Z^\circ_W
\bigr\rvert\ge\varepsilon^2\lvert(M_W)_{AB}\rvert .
\]
\item For such $\varepsilon$ there is $\lambda_0$ such that for $\lambda\ge
\lambda_0$ and every family of real functions $\phi_j$ on $G^{W\times
\{0,\dots,3\}}$, each of which does not depend on $c_A$ or does not depend
on $c_B$,
\[
\max_{s,t}\Bigl\lvert\log Z^\circ_W(c^{st}_\varepsilon)-\sum_j\phi_j
(c^{st}_\varepsilon)\Bigr\rvert\ge\frac{\lambda\varepsilon^2\lvert(M_W)_{AB}
\rvert}{5}.
\]
In particular, if $(M_W)_{AB}$ is not zero and $\lambda$ exceeds
$\max\{\lambda_0,2/(\varepsilon^2|(M_W)_{AB}|)\}$, then at these four
coarse fields $Z^\circ_W$ is not of the form
\[
\prod_{y\in W}\phi_y(c)\sum\prod_iw(X_i),
\]
with $\phi_y>0$ a function of the $c_{y',\mu}$
with $\ell^\infty(y',y)\le1$ and activities $|w(X)|\le e^{-9|X|}$ on the
connected subsets of $W$, compatible as in Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) The minimiser of $q_W(\gamma)$ solves the linear system of its
Lagrange conditions, which has $196$ unknowns, $16$ multipliers and the
$605$ plaquettes, and $(M_W)_{AB}=\varphi_A^{\rm T}G\varphi_B$ with
$\varphi_k$ the minimiser for $\gamma=e_k$ and $G$ the matrix of
$\sum_p(d\varphi)_p^2$. The system has rational coefficients and a unique
solution, so $\varphi_A$, $\varphi_B$ and $(M_W)_{AB}$ are rational.

(ii) All constants $C$ below depend on $W$ only. \emph{Two-sided bounds.}
Since $\nu_c(F_c)\le M^{4|W|}$, $Z^\circ_W(c)\le M^{16}e^{-\lambda
q(c)}$ with $q(c)=\inf_{F_c}Q_W$. If $U\in F_c$ is regular with all $n_P$
plaquettes at most $\kappa-90\rho$, $\rho\le9.32\cdot10^{-4}$, the
construction of the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:everyfibre} gives
\[
Z^\circ_W(c)\ge1.957^{-48}\Bigl(\frac{\rho^3}{14}\Bigr)^{180}e^{-\lambda
((1+\eta)Q_W(U)+(1+\eta^{-1})8100\rho^2n_P)} .
\]
Take $\eta=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $\rho=\lambda^{-1}$. Then
\[
q(c)\le\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty}\frac{-\log Z^\circ_W(c)}\lambda\le
\limsup_{\lambda\to\infty}\frac{-\log Z^\circ_W(c)}\lambda\le Q_W(U).
\]
\emph{Expansion of $q$.} Write fields near $I$ as $U=e^X$, $X\in\g^{A_W}$,
$|X|=\max_e\lVert X_e\rVert$, and let $\gamma^{st}=(s\,\delta_{kA}+t\,
\delta_{kB})_k\tau$, so that $c^{st}_\varepsilon=e^{\varepsilon\gamma^{st}}$
and the form $q^{\rm lin}(\gamma)=\sum_aq_W(\gamma^a)$ has $q^{\rm lin}
(\gamma^{st})=s(M_W)_{AA}+2st(M_W)_{AB}+t(M_W)_{BB}$. Near $I$ every cut-off
equals one and $V^\sharp$ and $Q_W$ are real analytic. By the formula for
the derivative in Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(iv) at $U=I$, and by the
Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff formula with $\delta(e^Y,I)^2=\lVert Y\rVert^2+
O(\lVert Y\rVert^4)$,
\[
\log V^\sharp_k(e^X)=V_k(X)+O(|X|^2),
\]
\[
Q_W(e^X)=\sum_p\lVert(dX)_p\rVert^2+O(|X|^3).
\]
The path link $d_k$ enters $V^\sharp_k$ alone, with derivative $\frac18$
at $I$, so the implicit function theorem solves $V^\sharp(e^X)=c$ for the
path links near $I$. \emph{Upper bound.} Let $X^*$ be the minimiser of
$q^{\rm lin}(\varepsilon\gamma^{st})$, $|X^*|\le C\varepsilon$, and change
its path links by $O(\varepsilon^2)$ so that $U_\varepsilon=e^X\in F_c$,
$c=c^{st}_\varepsilon$. Then $Q_W(U_\varepsilon)\le\varepsilon^2q^{\rm lin}
(\gamma^{st})+C\varepsilon^3$, $U_\varepsilon$ is regular, and its
plaquettes are at most $C\varepsilon$. \emph{Lower bound.} Let $U\in F_c$
with $Q_W(U)\le q(c)+\varepsilon^3\le C\varepsilon^2$. Every plaquette with
a vertex in a block of $W^+$ is one of the $n_P$, at most $C\varepsilon$, or
consists of links off $A_W$ and equals $I$. For $\varepsilon$ small
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(i) puts the active links inside the blocks
within $C\varepsilon$ of $I$ and the links leaving $B(y)$ in the direction
$\mu$ within $C\varepsilon$ of the path link $v$, and by (iv) of that
lemma $c_k=ve^{N}$ with $\lVert N\rVert\le C\varepsilon$, so $v$ is within
$C\varepsilon$ of $I$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, $U=e^X$ with $|X|\le
C\varepsilon$. Then $V(X)=\varepsilon\gamma^{st}+R$ with $|R|\le C
\varepsilon^2$, and since $q^{\rm lin}(a+b)\ge q^{\rm lin}(a)+2\langle a,
(M_W\otimes1)b\rangle$,
\[
Q_W(U)\ge q^{\rm lin}(\varepsilon\gamma^{st}+R)-C\varepsilon^3\ge
\varepsilon^2q^{\rm lin}(\gamma^{st})-C\varepsilon^3 .
\]
So $|q(c^{st}_\varepsilon)-\varepsilon^2q^{\rm lin}(\gamma^{st})|\le C
\varepsilon^3$, and for $\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_1$, where $\varepsilon_1$ depends on
$\kappa$ and $W$, the field $U_\varepsilon$ is admissible in the two-sided
bound.
Hence every limit point of $-\lambda^{-1}\Delta\log Z^\circ_W$ lies within
$4C\varepsilon^3$ of $\Delta(\varepsilon^2q^{\rm lin})=2\varepsilon^2(M_W)
_{AB}$, and $\varepsilon_0=\min\{\varepsilon_1,|(M_W)_{AB}|/(4C)\}$ gives
(ii) if $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$; otherwise (ii) holds with $\varepsilon_0=
\varepsilon_1$, its right side being zero.

(iii) $\Delta\phi_j=0$ for every $j$, since a function that does not depend
on $c_A$ takes the same value at $c^{1t}$ and $c^{0t}$, and likewise for
$c_B$. So $\lvert\Delta\log Z^\circ_W\rvert=\lvert\Delta E\rvert\le4\max
\lvert E\rvert$ for the difference $E$, and by (ii) $\lvert\Delta\log
Z^\circ_W\rvert\ge\frac45\lambda\varepsilon^2|(M_W)_{AB}|$ for $\lambda\ge
\lambda_0$. A factor $\phi_y$ that depends on $c_A$ and on $c_B$ would have
$\ell^\infty(y,0)\le1$ and $\ell^\infty(y,3e_0)\le1$, which is impossible.
The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(i) applies to the connected subsets of
$W$ and bounds the logarithm of the polymer sum by $|W|/10$ in modulus;
$Z^\circ_W>0$ by the lower bound. A representation of this form would
therefore give $\lambda\varepsilon^2|(M_W)_{AB}|/5\le2/5$, that is,
$\lambda\le2/(\varepsilon^2|(M_W)_{AB}|)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[a computation, not used by any result]\label{rem:sfgaussvalue}
Solving the system of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}(i) in exact
rational arithmetic gives $(M_W)_{AB}=-0.035264626\ldots$, so that the
hypothesis $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$ of the last assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}(iii) holds by this computation; no proof in
this paper uses it, and no hand proof of $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$ is given. For the
rows $W_n=\{0,\dots,(n-1)e_0\}$ and the end links $A=(0,1)$, $B=((n-1)e_0,
1)$, the same computation gives $(M_{W_n})_{AA}=20.0796\ldots$ for $n\ge4$
and
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lllllll}
\hline
$n$ & $2$ & $3$ & $4$ & $5$ & $6$ & $7$\\
\hline
$10^{n-2}(M_{W_n})_{AB}$ & $-3.32$ & $3.35$ & $-3.53$ & $3.88$
& $-4.47$ & $5.40$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
so in this computation the coupling decays by a factor between $8$ and
$10$ per block and does not vanish.
\end{remark}

By the argument of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}, a product of factors of
finite range $r$ reproduces the calm weight of $W_n$, $n-1>2r$, only up to
an error of order $\lambda\varepsilon^2|(M_{W_n})_{AB}|$. To leading order in
$\lambda$ the calm weight is $e^{-\lambda q}$ with $q$ the Gaussian
block-spin form, whose kernel decays at a rate independent of $\lambda$
with amplitude proportional to $\lambda$. A local expansion of the
small-field part therefore has to keep this form and expand around it, as
the Gaussian small-field expansion of Ba{\l}aban does; a product of
factors of range one times a polymer sum with activities $e^{-9|X|}$,
which is the form (H1) below asks for, fails for the calm weight of $W$
at every $\lambda>\max\{\lambda_0,2/(\varepsilon^2|(M_W)_{AB}|)\}$ when
$(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$, by Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}(iii).

So the small-field part of one step stands as follows. The kernels are
local, with the second layer $\partial^=X$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel}). The calm weight of a region with boundary
values is at least $e^{-c_2}$ per block times the Gaussian factor of a
completion calm at $\kappa'$, and the relative activity is then at most
$e^{-a_2|X|}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm}). The large-field sum is exactly
$Z_\emptyset\varXi+Z_\perp$, and under the uniform bound on the relative
activities the large fields change $A_1$ by at most $|T|/10$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}). Not proved are that bound at calm
fields with plaquettes in the shell $(\kappa',\kappa]$
(Remark~\ref{rem:sfshell}), a bound on $Z_\perp$, and the locality of
$-\log Z_\emptyset(c)$ and of $\log\E_{\mu^\circ_c}[e^\varLambda]$ in $c$.
For the first of these the form of the answer is fixed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}: to leading order it is the Gaussian block-spin
form with amplitude $\lambda$, and, if $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$, no product of
local factors.

\paragraph*{Locality, the shell and the remainder.}
The three questions left open above are taken up in turn. For the locality
of the calm weight, the form $e^{-\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\log c)}$ times a
polymer sum with local activities is impossible at $\lambda>0.548$, because
the calm weight is invariant under coarse gauge transformations and the
Gaussian block-spin form of $\log c$ is not; the linearised propagator with
the block-spin constraint decays at an explicit rate, which is the input that
an expansion around a gauge-invariant leading term would use. For the shell,
in the linearisation of the model the relative activities are not bounded
under the calm law, at any $\lambda$ and $\kappa$. For the remainder,
$Z_\perp(I)>0$ for $\SU(2)$ at every $\lambda$ and every $\kappa\le
10^{-8}$, and $Z_\perp$ is bounded in the mean over $c$ by the probability
of a rough block.

For a gauge field $g\in G^T$ on the coarse torus put $(c^g)_{y,\mu}=g_y
c_{y,\mu}g_{y+e_\mu}^{-1}$. The \emph{Gaussian block-spin form of the torus}
is $q_T(\gamma)=\min\{Q(\varphi):V(\varphi)=\gamma\}$ for real $\gamma$ on
the coarse links, the minimum over real fields on the active links of
$\Lambda_L$; for $\g$-valued $w$ put $q^{\rm lin}(w)=\sum_aq_T(w^a)$, with
the components in the orthonormal basis $\tau_a=i\sigma_a/\sqrt2$ of
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$. As for $q_W$, $q_T$ is a positive semidefinite quadratic
form, by Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap} on the periodic lattice.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:sfgaugeinv}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\kappa>0$ and $g\in G^T$. Then $Z(c^g)=Z(c)$ and
$Z_\emptyset(c^g)=Z_\emptyset(c)$ for every $c$, and $q_T(\gamma+d\chi)=
q_T(\gamma)$ for real $\gamma$ and $\chi$, where $(d\chi)_{y,\mu}=\chi_y-
\chi_{y+e_\mu}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\Phi$ be the fine gauge transformation equal to $g_y$ at every site of
$B(y)$. It fixes the tree links, so it preserves the tree gauge, and it
preserves $Q$, every indicator $s_y$ and $r_y$, and product Haar measure.
The cut-off average is covariant (Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}), so $\Phi$ maps
$F_c$ onto $F_{c^g}$. In the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:averagedensity} for the
pair $(y,\mu)$, $\Phi$ replaces the path link $\ell_0$ by $g_y\ell_0
g_{y+e_\mu}^{-1}$, the links inside $B(y)$ by their conjugates by $g_y$ and
those of $B(y+e_\mu)$ by their conjugates by $g_{y+e_\mu}$, so every site
$v_x$ is conjugated by $g_{y+e_\mu}$. The regions $R_0$, $R_1$, $R_2$, which
are defined by the norms $\delta(v_x,I)$, are therefore preserved, the
coordinates $h_a$ are conjugated, which preserves Haar measure, and the
derivative of $V^\sharp$ is conjugated by $\operatorname{Ad}(g_y)$, so
$\lvert\det DV^\sharp\rvert$ is unchanged. Hence the image of $\nu_c$ under
$\Phi$ is $\nu_{c^g}$, and $Z=\nu_c(e^{-\lambda Q})$ and $Z_\emptyset=\nu_c(
\prod_yf_ys_y)$ are invariant. For $q_T$, Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(ii) with
$h$ equal to $\chi_y$ on $B(y)$ maps $\{V=\gamma\}$ onto $\{V=\gamma+d\chi\}$
and preserves $Q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfgaugeobst}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\lambda>0$, $\kappa>0$, and let $F$ be $Z$ or $Z_\emptyset$.
Let $y$ be a block, $z=y+e_0$, $0<\phi\le\pi/2$, and let $g_y=\exp(\sqrt2
\phi\tau_1)$, $g_z=\exp(\sqrt2\phi\tau_2)$ and $g_w=I$ otherwise. Suppose that
at $c=I$ and at $c=I^g$
\[
F(c)=e^{-\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\log c)-E|T|}\prod_y\phi_y(c)\sum\prod_iw(X_i;c),
\]
where $\log$ is the principal logarithm on each coarse link, $E$ is a
constant, each $\phi_y>0$ is invariant under coarse gauge transformations,
and the sum runs over the families of pairwise compatible connected sets as
in Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}, with activities $|w(X;c)|\le e^{-9|X|}$ that
depend on $c$ only through the $c_{w',\mu}$ with $\ell^\infty(w',X)\le1$.
Then
$\lambda\le8.1/|\eta(\phi)|^2\le4.05/\sin^4\phi$, where $\cos\psi=\cos^2\phi$,
$0<\psi\le\pi/2$, and
\[
|\eta(\phi)|^2=4\Bigl(\frac{\psi\sin\phi\cos\phi}{\sin\psi}-\phi\Bigr)^2
+\frac{2\psi^2\sin^4\phi}{\sin^2\psi}.
\] At $\phi=\pi/2$,
$|\eta|^2=3\pi^2/2$ and $\lambda\le5.4/\pi^2<0.5472$. The field $I^g$ is
flat, $\delta((I^g)_P,I)=0$ for every coarse plaquette, and its links have
$\delta(c_k,I)\le2\sin\phi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $g_y=a+b\cdot i\sigma$ as unit quaternions. The links of $c=I^g$ are
$g_y$ on $(y,\mu)$, $\mu\ne0$, and $g_y^{-1}$ on $(y-e_\mu,\mu)$; $g_z$
on $(z,\mu)$ and $g_z^{-1}$ on $(z-e_\mu,\mu)$, $\mu\ne0$; $g_z$ on
$(z,0)$, $g_y^{-1}$ on $(y-e_0,0)$, and $g_yg_z^{-1}$ on $k=(y,0)$; $I$
elsewhere. Their bases form the set $S$ of the nine blocks $y-e_0$, $y$, $z$,
$y-e_\mu$ and $z-e_\mu$ ($\mu=1,2,3$). With $\chi$ equal to $\log g_y=\sqrt2\phi\tau_1$
at $y$, $\log g_z=\sqrt2\phi\tau_2$ at $z$ and $0$ elsewhere,
$\log(I^g)=d\chi+\eta\,\delta_k$ with $\eta=\log(g_yg_z^{-1})-\chi_y+\chi_z$.
The quaternion of $g_yg_z^{-1}$ is $\cos^2\phi+(\sin\phi\cos\phi,-\sin\phi
\cos\phi,\sin^2\phi)\cdot i\sigma$, whose principal logarithm is $\sqrt2\psi$
times the unit vector of its vector part, in the coordinates of the
$\tau_a$; this gives $|\eta|^2$, and at $\phi=\pi/2$, $g_y=i\sigma_1$,
$g_z=i\sigma_2$, $g_yg_z^{-1}=i\sigma_3$ and $\eta=\frac\pi{\sqrt2}(-\tau_1+
\tau_2+\tau_3)$. As $\psi\ge\sin\psi$, the second term of $|\eta|^2$ is at
least $2\sin^4\phi$; and $5.4/\pi^2<0.5472$ since $\pi^2>9.8696$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:sfgaugeinv} and since $q^{\rm lin}$ is a
sum of positive semidefinite forms, $q^{\rm lin}(\log I^g)=q^{\rm lin}(\eta
\delta_k)$. By the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(i), which
applies on the torus, $q_T\ge Q_1$, and $\delta_k$ lies in six coarse
plaquettes, so $q^{\rm lin}(\eta\delta_k)\ge6|\eta|^2$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:sfgaugeinv}, $F(I^g)=F(I)$, and the $\phi_y$ and $E$
cancel, so $\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\eta\delta_k)=\log\Sigma(I^g)-\log
\Sigma(I)$ with $\Sigma$ the polymer sum. By Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(i),
$\log\Sigma$ is the sum of the connected clusters, a cluster depends on $c$
only through the links with base within distance one of its support, and the
clusters incompatible with a given block add up to at most $\frac1{10}$ in
modulus. A cluster whose support does not meet the set $N_1(S)$ of blocks
within distance one of $S$ takes the same value at $I$ and $I^g$; a cluster
that meets it is incompatible with a block of $N_1(S)$. Count $N_1(S)$ by the
level $a$ of a block $w=y+ae_0+s$, $s$ spatial. The blocks of $S$ have $s=0$
at level $-1$ and $s\in D=\{0,-e_1,-e_2,-e_3\}$ at levels $0$ and $1$, and
the spatial points within distance one of $D$ are the $27$ points of
$\{-1,0,1\}^3$ and the $3\cdot9$ points with one coordinate $-2$ and the
others in $\{-1,0,1\}$. So level $-2$ contributes the $27$ points within
distance one of $s=0$, each of the levels $-1$, $0$, $1$, $2$ contributes
$54$, and $|N_1(S)|\le27+4\cdot54=243$. Hence $6\lambda|\eta|^2\le2\cdot243/10=48.6$. The
plaquettes of $I^g$ are conjugates of those of $I$, and $\delta(g_yg_z^{-1},
I)=2\sin\phi$ is the largest link.
\end{proof}

The following values are evaluations of the closed form for $|\eta(\phi)|^2$,
rounded to the digits shown, those of the last column upwards. The
conclusions below use only the row $\phi=\pi/2$, whose entries are exact,
and the bound $4.05/\sin^4\phi$.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{llll}
\hline
$\phi$ & $|\eta(\phi)|^2$ & $\max_k\delta(c_k,I)$ & $\lambda\le$\\
\hline
$\pi/2$ & $14.8044$ & $2$ & $0.5472$\\
$0.5$ & $0.13191$ & $0.9589$ & $61.41$\\
$0.1$ & $2.0044\cdot10^{-4}$ & $0.1997$ & $4.0411\cdot10^4$\\
$0.05$ & $1.2507\cdot10^{-5}$ & $0.09996$ & $6.4765\cdot10^5$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
So at every $\kappa$ the representation fails for $\lambda>0.5472$ at a flat
coarse field, and, among coarse fields with links within $0.1$ of $I$, for
$\lambda>6.5\cdot10^5$: at $\phi=0.05$ the links are within $2\sin\phi<0.1$
of $I$, and $\sin\phi>\phi-\phi^3/6>0.04997$, so $\lambda\le4.05/
0.04997^4<6.5\cdot10^5$. This is below $\lambda^{**}(0.08)<9.16\cdot10^5$.
The defect is the failure of $\log$ to intertwine the coarse gauge action:
$q^{\rm lin}(\log c)$ is invariant only under gauge transformations that
commute with $c$. A representation of the required kind needs a leading term
invariant under the coarse gauge group, such as $\lambda S_1(c)$ with $S_1(c)
=\inf_{F_c}Q$; by Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss} it is not local if $(M_W)_{AB}
\ne0$, and its Hessian
at $c=I$ is $2\lambda$ times the form $q^{\rm lin}$. Whether
$Z_\emptyset(c)e^{\lambda S_1(c)}$, or the same with another invariant form
of this Hessian, is a polymer sum with local activities is not decided here.

\emph{The block-spin propagator.} The expansion of such a form around a
minimiser uses the propagator of the fine field with the block-spin
constraint. In the linearisation it decays at a rate that the following
theorem makes explicit. For a pair $k=(y,\mu)$ label its eight private links
by $a\in\{0,1\}^3$, the offsets in the three directions $\nu\ne\mu$, and for
$w\in\{0,1\}^3\setminus\{0\}$ put $\xi_{k,w}=8^{-1/2}\sum_a(-1)^{a\cdot w}
\varphi_{k,a}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(iii), on $\{V=0\}$ the mean of
the eight is $m_k=-\frac1{16}(S^\mu_y+S^\mu_{y+e_\mu})$, so
\[
\varphi_{k,a}=8^{-1/2}\sum_w(-1)^{a\cdot w}\xi_{k,w}+m_k ,
\]
and the coordinates $v=(\varphi_e)_{e\text{ inside}}\oplus(\xi_{k,w})$,
with $17$ inside links and $28$ Walsh coordinates per block, define a linear
bijection $P:v\mapsto\varphi$ onto $\{V=0\}$. Let $H$ be the matrix of
$v\mapsto Q(Pv)$, and for a coordinate, a fine link or a coarse link let
its block be the block of its base. Write $d(\cdot,\cdot)$ for the
$\ell^\infty$ distance of the blocks on the coarse torus. Let $L_0$ map
$\gamma$ to the field equal to $\gamma_k$ on the eight private links of $k$
and to zero elsewhere, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(ii), and let
$A$ and $B$ be the matrices of $Q(L_0\gamma)=\gamma^{\rm T}A\gamma$ and of the
cross term, so that $Q(L_0\gamma+Pv)=\gamma^{\rm T}A\gamma+2\gamma^{\rm T}Bv
+v^{\rm T}Hv$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfprop}
On the periodic lattice of side $L\ge32$ let
\[
\bar S=168+42\sqrt2,\qquad\bar b=168+336\sqrt2,\qquad p_1=\frac7{2\sqrt2}+
\frac78,
\]
so that $\bar S<227.40$ and $\bar b<643.18$, and for $\alpha>0$ let
$c_\alpha=\frac1{52}-(\cosh3\alpha-1)\bar S$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $H_{ij}=0$ for $d(i,j)\ge4$, the sum $\sum_j|H_{ij}|$ is at most $\bar
S$ for every $i$, and $v^{\rm T}Hv\ge\frac1{52}|v|^2$ for every $v$.
\item If $0<\alpha\le\frac1{250}$, then $c_\alpha>0$ and $|(H^{-1})_{ij}|\le
c_\alpha^{-1}e^{-\alpha d(i,j)}$ for all coordinates $i$ and $j$.
\item For real $\gamma$ the Gaussian probability measure proportional to
$e^{-\lambda Q(\varphi)}$ on the affine space $\{V(\varphi)=\gamma\}$ of fields
in the tree gauge has as mean the minimiser $\varphi^*(\gamma)=L_0\gamma-
PH^{-1}B^{\rm T}\gamma$ of $q_T(\gamma)$ and as covariance $C=(2\lambda)^{-1}
PH^{-1}P^{\rm T}$, and for $0<\alpha\le\frac1{250}$
\[
|C_{ee'}|\le\frac{e^{2\alpha}p_1^2}{2\lambda c_\alpha}e^{-\alpha d(e,e')}.
\]
\item $q_T(\gamma)=\gamma^{\rm T}M\gamma$ with $M=A-BH^{-1}B^{\rm T}$; the
rows of $A$ and $B$ have $\ell^1$ norms at most $192$ and $\bar b$,
$A_{kk'}=0$ for $d(k,k')\ge2$ and $B_{ki}=0$ for $d(k,i)\ge3$; and for
$d(k,k')\ge2$ and $0<\alpha\le\frac1{250}$, $|M_{kk'}|\le e^{4\alpha}\bar b^2
c_\alpha^{-1}e^{-\alpha d(k,k')}$.
\end{enumerate}
At $\alpha=\frac1{500}$, $c_\alpha>0.0151$, and the three constants are
below $66.3$, $746.2/(2\lambda)$ and $2.762\cdot10^7$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) Write $e_i$ for the coordinate vectors of $v$. For an inside link
$e=(x,\mu)$ of $B(b)$ the coordinate enters only $S^\mu_b$, so by the
formula for $m_k$ the field $Pe_e$ is $1$ on $e$ and $-\frac1{16}$ on the
eight private links of each of the pairs $(b,\mu)$ and $(b-e_\mu,\mu)$; its
$\ell^1$ norm is $2$. For a Walsh coordinate $\xi_{k,w}$, $k=(b,\mu)$, the
field is $\pm8^{-1/2}$ on the eight private links of $k$, of $\ell^1$ norm
$2\sqrt2$. In both cases the links have base in $b$ or $b-e_\mu$. A row of
$P$ at an inside link has the single entry $1$; at a private link of a pair
$(b,\mu)$ it has $7$ Walsh entries $\pm8^{-1/2}$ and the $2(8-2^\mu)$ active
links of $S^\mu_b$ and $S^\mu_{b+e_\mu}$ with $-\frac1{16}$, so its $\ell^1$
norm is at most $p_1$, the value at $\mu=0$. A plaquette has four links and
a link lies in six plaquettes, so $\sum_p|(dPe_i)_p|\le6\cdot2\sqrt2$ and
$\sum_j|(dPe_j)_p|\le\sum_{l\in p}\sum_j|P_{lj}|\le4p_1$. As $H_{ij}=
\sum_p(dPe_i)_p(dPe_j)_p$,
\[
\sum_j|H_{ij}|\le\sum_p|(dPe_i)_p|\sum_j|(dPe_j)_p|\le48\sqrt2\,p_1=\bar S .
\]
If $H_{ij}\ne0$, a plaquette contains a link of $Pe_i$ and a link of $Pe_j$;
the bases of two links of a plaquette lie in blocks at distance at most one,
and the links of $Pe_i$ have base within distance one of the block of $i$,
so $d(i,j)\le3$. Finally $v^{\rm T}Hv=Q(Pv)\ge\frac1{52}\lvert Pv\rvert^2$
by Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap}, whose proof uses only the plaquettes inside
a block and those joining two neighbouring blocks and holds verbatim on
the periodic lattice,
and $\lvert Pv\rvert^2=\sum_{\rm inside}\varphi_e^2+\sum_k(\sum_w\xi_{k,w}^2+
8m_k^2)\ge|v|^2$, since the characters $a\mapsto(-1)^{a\cdot w}$, $w\ne0$,
are orthogonal and orthogonal to the constants.

(ii) Since $\cosh u-1=\sum_{m\ge1}u^{2m}/(2m)!\le\frac{u^2}2\cosh u$, so
that $\cosh u\le(1-\frac{u^2}2)^{-1}$ for $u^2<2$, at $\alpha=\frac1{250}$
one has $(\cosh3\alpha-1)\bar S\le\frac{0.012^2}2\cdot1.0001\cdot227.40<
0.01638<\frac1{52}$, and $c_\alpha$ decreases in
$\alpha$. Fix $j$, put $f_i=d(i,j)$ and $H_\alpha=e^{\alpha f}He^{-\alpha f}$.
For real $v$, by the symmetry of $H$,
\begin{align*}
v^{\rm T}H_\alpha v&=\sum_{i,l}H_{il}\cosh\bigl(\alpha(f_i-f_l)\bigr)v_iv_l\\
&=v^{\rm T}Hv+\sum_{1\le d(i,l)\le3}H_{il}\bigl(\cosh(\alpha(f_i-f_l))-1
\bigr)v_iv_l ,
\end{align*}
since $f_i=f_l$ when $d(i,l)=0$ and $H_{il}=0$ when $d(i,l)\ge4$. As $|f_i-
f_l|\le d(i,l)\le3$, the last sum is at most $(\cosh3\alpha-1)\bar S|v|^2$
in modulus, by the Schur test for the symmetric matrix of its coefficients
and (i). So $|H_\alpha v|\ge c_\alpha|v|$, $H_\alpha$ is invertible with
$\lVert H_\alpha^{-1}\rVert\le c_\alpha^{-1}$, and its entry $(i,j)$ is
$e^{\alpha d(i,j)}(H^{-1})_{ij}$.

(iii) $V(L_0\gamma)=\gamma$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(ii), so the
fields with $V=\gamma$ are the $L_0\gamma+Pv$, and the exponent is the
quadratic form above in $v$; completing the square gives the mean and the
covariance $(2\lambda H)^{-1}$ of $v$. By (i) a row of $P$ has $\ell^1$ norm
at most $p_1$, and $P_{ei}\ne0$ only if the block of $i$ is the block of $e$
or its neighbour in the direction of $e$, so the coordinates $i$, $l$ that
enter $C_{ee'}$ have $d(i,l)\ge d(e,e')-2$. Then apply (ii).

(iv) Minimising over $v$ gives $M$. The field $L_0\delta_k$ is $1$ on the
eight private links of $k$, which have base in the block of $k$ and belong
to no other pair, so $\sum_p|(dL_0\delta_k)_p|\le48$ and $\sum_{k'}|(dL_0
\delta_{k'})_p|\le4$. As in (i), $A_{kk'}=\sum_p(dL_0\delta_k)_p(dL_0
\delta_{k'})_p$ and $B_{ki}=\sum_p(dL_0\delta_k)_p(dPe_i)_p$ give the row
bounds $48\cdot4=192$ and $48\cdot4p_1=\bar b$ and the ranges one and two.
Then $|(BH^{-1}B^{\rm T})_{kk'}|\le\sum_{i,l}|B_{ki}||(H^{-1})_{il}||B_{k'l}|$
with $d(i,l)\ge d(k,k')-4$, and (ii) gives the bound.

At $\alpha=\frac1{500}$, $(\cosh3\alpha-1)\bar S\le\frac{0.006^2}2\cdot
1.0001\cdot227.40<0.004094$, so $c_\alpha>\frac1{52}-0.004094>0.0151$; with
$p_1^2=\frac{49}8+\frac{49}{8\sqrt2}+\frac{49}{64}<11.222$, $e^{0.004}<
1.00402$, $e^{0.008}<1.00807$ (from $e^u\le(1-u)^{-1}$) and $\bar b^2<
413{,}681$ the constants follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
A computation on the lattice of side $12$, which no statement here uses,
gives the entries of $H$, $A$ and $B$: all three have range one, the
largest sum of $|H_{ij}|$ over $d(i,j)=1$ is $S_1=20.45495\ldots$, and the
rows of $A$ and $B$ have $\ell^1$ norms at most $96$ and $77.456$. With these
values the argument of (ii), with $\cosh\alpha$ in place of $\cosh3\alpha$
and $S_1$ in place of $\bar S$ and with the constant $\frac{537}{5000}$ of
Remark~\ref{rem:blockgapsharp} in place of $\frac1{52}$, gives decay for
$\alpha<0.10243$, and at
$\alpha=0.08$ constants $23.87$, $314.3/(2\lambda)$ and $1.680\cdot10^5$.
Both rates are far from the decay of $(M_{W_n})_{AB}$ by a factor $8$ to
$10$ per block, which corresponds to $\alpha\approx2.1$; the loss comes from
bounding the off-diagonal part of $H$ by its row sums.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:sfbalaban}
Ba{\l}aban's renormalisation group for lattice gauge
theories~\cite{Bal84a,Bal85a,Bal85b,Bal85c,Bal87,Bal88,Bal89b} expands the
small-field part around the minimiser of the action at given block
averages: he treats this variational problem and the background fields it
defines in~\cite{Bal85c}, the propagators in such a background
in~\cite{Bal85b}, and the generation of the effective actions in a small
field approximation and their cluster expansions in~\cite{Bal87,Bal88}.
They are cited for the method only. His averaging operations are not
the cut-off average $V^\sharp$, and no proof here uses his results.
By Theorems~\ref{thm:sfgauss} and~\ref{thm:sfgaugeobst} the small-field
part of the present step calls for the same structure: a leading term of
amplitude $\lambda$, nonlocal if $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$, which cannot be
$\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\log c)$, and an expansion around it. Theorem~\ref{thm:sfprop} is the linear propagator bound of such
an expansion at the trivial background; the background field of $V^\sharp$
and the expansion around it are not carried out.
\end{remark}

\emph{The shell in the linearised model.} In the \emph{linear model} the
links are real: $\varphi$ is a real field on the active links of the torus,
$Q(\varphi)=\sum_p(d\varphi)_p^2$, a block $y$ is calm when $|(d\varphi)_p|
\le\kappa$ for every $p\in\Pi(y)$, the coarse field is $\gamma=V(\varphi)$,
and the fibre $\{V=\gamma\}$ carries Lebesgue measure in the coordinates
given by the values on the links other than the path links. The
statements of Lemma~\ref{lem:sfkernel} concern only which links a factor
involves, and hold verbatim. For $X=\{y\}$ and $\gamma=0$, the free links
of $\mathcal V_X$, the links of $\mathcal V_X$ other than the path links of
the pairs of $\mathcal P_X$, are coordinates $u\in\R^{73}$ of the
completions of given outer variables $o$, the remaining links. Let
$S^{\rm lin}_X(o)$ and $K^{\rm lin}_X(o)$ be the integrals over $u$ of
$\prod_{w\in\hat X}f_ws_w$ and of $f_yr_y\prod_{w\in\hat X\setminus X}f_ws_w$,
with $f_w=\exp(-\lambda\sum_{p\in\Pi(w)}(d\varphi)_p^2)$. The calm law is
proportional to $\prod_wf_ws_w$ on $\{V=0\}$. As in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}, the law of $o$ under it has density
proportional to $\varPhi_X(o)S^{\rm lin}_X(o)$ with respect to Lebesgue
measure in the free outer links, $\varPhi_X=\prod_{w\notin\hat X}f_ws_w$, and
$\rho^{\rm lin}_X=K^{\rm lin}_X/S^{\rm lin}_X$ is defined almost surely.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfshelllin}
In the linear model on a torus of coarse side at least $8$, with $\gamma=0$,
$X=\{y\}$, every $\kappa>0$ and every $\lambda>0$, the ratio $\rho^{\rm lin}
_X$ is not essentially bounded under the calm law: for every $R$ the calm law
gives positive probability to $\{\rho^{\rm lin}_X>R\}$. In particular the
hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(ii) fails in the linear
model at every $\lambda$ and $\kappa$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map $\varphi\mapsto\kappa\varphi$ replaces $\kappa$ by $1$ and $\lambda$
by $\lambda\kappa^2$, so let $\kappa=1$. Let $x=2y+(1,1,1,0)$. The three
faces of the unit cube at $x$ in the directions $0$, $1$, $2$ that contain
$x$ are owned by $y$; write $F_1$, $F_2$, $F_3$ for $d\varphi$ on the faces
in the planes $\{0,1\}$, $\{0,2\}$, $\{1,2\}$. Every link of the cube lies in
two of its faces with opposite signs, so
\[
F_1-F_2+F_3=(d\varphi)_{x+e_2,01}-(d\varphi)_{x+e_1,02}+(d\varphi)_{x+e_0,
12}=:R ,
\]
and the three faces on the right are owned by $y+e_2$, $y+e_1$, $y+e_0
\notin\hat X$ and contain no link of $\mathcal V_X$, so $R=R(o)$ is a linear
function of $o$.

\emph{The field $\varphi_1$.} For $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^3\times\{0\}$ and
$\varepsilon_\mu=0$ the edge $(x+\varepsilon,\mu)$ of the cube has offset one
in the direction $\mu$, so it is a private link of the pair $(y+\varepsilon,
\mu)$, and distinct edges lie in distinct pairs. Let $\varphi_1$ take the
values
\[
-\tfrac12,\ \tfrac12,\ \tfrac12,\ -\tfrac12,\ -\tfrac12,\ \tfrac12
\]
on the edges $(x+e_1,0)$, $(x+e_2,0)$, $(x+e_0,1)$, $(x+e_2,1)$, $(x+e_0,2)$,
$(x+e_1,2)$, minus one seventh of that value on the other seven private links
of the pair of each of these edges, and zero elsewhere. Private links are
active, the sum over the private links of every pair is zero and no inside
link is used, so $V(\varphi_1)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:blocktree}(iii). The six
pairs are those of the blocks $y+e_0$, $y+e_1$, $y+e_2$, none of which lies
in $\hat X$, so $\varphi_1$ vanishes on $\mathcal V_X$. A pair contains one
edge of the cube, so $\varphi_1$ vanishes on the other six edges, and
\begin{gather*}
F_1=\varphi_1(x+e_0,1)-\varphi_1(x+e_1,0)=1,\\
F_2=\varphi_1(x+e_0,2)-\varphi_1(x+e_2,0)=-1,\\
F_3=\varphi_1(x+e_1,2)-\varphi_1(x+e_2,1)=1,
\end{gather*}
and the outer faces take the values $\varphi_1(x+e_2,0)-\varphi_1(x+e_2,1)
=1$, $\varphi_1(x+e_1,0)-\varphi_1(x+e_1,2)=-1$ and $\varphi_1(x+e_0,1)-
\varphi_1(x+e_0,2)=1$. Two edges of the cube lie in a common plaquette only
if it is a face of the cube, so every other plaquette contains at most one
link with $|\varphi_1|=\frac12$ and three with $|\varphi_1|\le\frac1{14}$,
and $|d\varphi_1|\le\frac57=1-\delta_0$, $\delta_0=\frac27$.

Let $w\in\R^{73}$ lower $(x,1)$ by one; to keep $V_{y,1}$, the path link
$(2y+e_1,1)$, also a private link of $(y,1)$, rises by one. The link $(x,1)$
lies in $F_1$ with the sign $-$ and in $F_3$ with the sign $+$, the path link
lies in none of the six faces, and the two links share no plaquette, so $w$
changes $(F_1,F_2,F_3)$ by $(1,0,-1)$ and every plaquette by at most $1$.
Lowering $(x,2)$ in the same way changes $(F_1,F_2)$ by $(0,1)$, so the map
from the free links of $\mathcal V_X$ to $(F_1,F_2)$ has rank two. Let $o_t$
be the outer part of $(1-t)\varphi_1$, $0<t\le\delta_0/4$; its inner part
$u_1$ is zero.

\emph{Upper bound on $S^{\rm lin}_X$.} If all blocks of $\hat X$ are calm,
then $F_1\le1$, $F_2\ge-1$ and $F_3=R-F_1+F_2\le1$, so $(F_1,F_2)$ lies in
the square $[R-2,1]\times[-1,2-R]$ of side $3-R$. The map $u\mapsto(F_1,F_2)$
is affine with linear part of rank two, and $Q(\varphi(o,u))=u^{\rm T}Hu+
\ell_o(u)+{\rm const}$ with $H$ positive definite, since a change of $u$ is a
field in $\{V=0\}$ to which Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap} applies.
The image of the finite measure $e^{-\lambda Q}du$ under $u\mapsto(F_1,F_2)$
is Gaussian, with mass at most $(\pi/\lambda)^{73/2}\det H^{-1/2}$ and a
nondegenerate covariance that does not depend on $o$, so its density is at
most a constant $C_\lambda$ and $S^{\rm lin}_X(o)\le C_\lambda(3-R(o))^2$.
Let $B_t$ be the ball of outer variables about $o_t$ on which $|R(o)-R(o_t)|
\le t$; there $3-R(o)\le4t$ and $S^{\rm lin}_X\le16C_\lambda t^2$.

\emph{Lower bound on $K^{\rm lin}_X$.} At $(o_t,u_1+\frac{\delta_0}2w)$,
$F_1=1-t+\frac{\delta_0}2\ge1+\frac{\delta_0}4$, so $y$ is rough, and every
plaquette owned by a block of $\hat X\setminus X$ is at most
$(1-t)(1-\delta_0)+\frac{\delta_0}2\le1-\frac{\delta_0}2$. All plaquettes are
linear in $(o,u)$, so there is $r>0$, independent of $t$, such that these
inequalities hold with $\frac{\delta_0}8$ and $\frac{\delta_0}4$ on the ball of
radius $r$ about this point, and $Q$ is bounded there by a constant $Q_0$.
Hence $K^{\rm lin}_X(o)\ge c_r e^{-\lambda Q_0}=:k_0>0$ for $o$ within $r$
of $o_t$, with $c_r$ the volume of the ball of radius $r$ in $\R^{73}$.

\emph{Positive probability.} At $(o_t,u_1)$ every plaquette other than the
six faces has modulus at most $(1-t)(1-\delta_0)$ and the six have modulus
$1-t$, so all blocks are calm with a margin. For $o$ near $o_t$ the outer
blocks stay calm, $\varPhi_X(o)>0$, and the completions near $u_1$ stay calm,
$S^{\rm lin}_X(o)>0$. So the calm law gives positive probability to every
small ball about $o_t$, and on such a ball inside $B_t$ and within $r$ of
$o_t$, $\rho^{\rm lin}_X\ge k_0/(16C_\lambda t^2)$. Let $t\to0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:sfconditioning}
The mechanism is the conditioning: $\rho_X$ compares two parts of the mass
of the completions, and its denominator is the mass of the calm ones, which
the Bianchi identity of a cube with three outer faces near their threshold
squeezes into a corner of area $(3-R)^2/2$, while the rough completions keep
a mass of order one. Weak coupling does not help, since the same holds at
every $\lambda$; and the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm} does not apply,
since at these boundary values every completion has a face at least
$1-3t$, above $\kappa'$. In $\SU(2)$ the Bianchi identity holds up to
commutators of order $\kappa^2$, so the same construction squeezes the calm
completions only to a scale of order $\kappa^2$; whether
$\rho_X\le e^{-9|X|}$ fails almost surely for $\SU(2)$ in the shell is not
decided here. The hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(ii) can
therefore hold at best in a form that excludes such boundary values, for
example in the mean under the calm law, and Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}
(ii) is not proved in such a form for $\SU(2)$. In the linear model the mean
form holds, with an explicit constant (Corollary~\ref{cor:sfglshell}).
\end{remark}

\emph{The remainder $Z_\perp$.} Let $\mu_c=Z(c)^{-1}e^{-\lambda Q}\nu_c$ be
the constrained law on $F_c$, and let $\mathbb P$ be the law of $c$ under
the Wilson measure $\mu_L$, with density $Z(c)/Z_L$ with respect to $h$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:sfperp}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $\kappa>0$ and $Z_\emptyset(c)>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The following hold:
\[
\frac{Z(c)}{Z_\emptyset(c)}=\varXi(c)+\frac{Z_\perp(c)}{Z_\emptyset(c)},
\qquad\frac{Z_\emptyset(c)}{Z(c)}=\mu_c\{R=\emptyset\},
\]
and $0\le Z_\perp(c)\le Z(c)-Z_\emptyset(c)=Z(c)\,\mu_c\{R\ne\emptyset\}$.
\item For $\beta_W\ge1$ and $\kappa\le1$, $\int Z_\perp/Z\,d\mathbb P\le
\mu_L\{R\ne\emptyset\}\le16|T|q_\kappa(\beta_W)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) The first identity is Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(i) divided by
$Z_\emptyset$, and $Z_\emptyset=\nu_c(e^{-\lambda Q}\mathbf 1\{R=\emptyset
\})$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(i), $Z=Z_\emptyset+\sum_{X\ne\emptyset}
Z_X$, and $Z_\perp$ is a sum of parts of the nonnegative $Z_X$, $X\ne
\emptyset$. (ii) $\int\mu_c\{R\ne\emptyset\}\,d\mathbb P=\mu_L\{R\ne
\emptyset\}$ since $h=\int\nu_c\,dh(c)$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:lfsuppression}
(iii) with $X=\{y\}$ bounds each $\mu_L\{y\in R\}$.
\end{proof}

The next theorem shows that $Z_\perp$ is not zero: there are boundary values
that admit a rough completion and no calm one, with positive measure. For a
unit quaternion $g=a+b\cdot i\sigma$ write $b(g)\in\R^3$ for its vector part;
then $\delta(g,I)^2=4(1-a)$ and $|b(g)|\le\delta(g,I)/\sqrt2$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:sfquat}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_4\in\SU(2)$ with $\delta(g_i,I)\le\varDelta\le1$. Then
\begin{multline*}
\bigl\lvert b(g_1g_2g_3^{-1}g_4^{-1})-b(g_1)-b(g_2)+b(g_3)+b(g_4)\bigr\rvert\\
\le3\varDelta^2+3.54\varDelta^3 .
\end{multline*}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$b(g^{-1})=-b(g)$, and $b(gh)=a_gb(h)+a_hb(g)-b(g)\times b(h)$. Let $P_j$ be
the product of the first $j$ factors and $\varepsilon_j$ the error after $j$
factors. Then $\delta(P_j,I)\le j\varDelta$, so $|b(P_j)|\le j\varDelta/
\sqrt2$ and $1-a(P_j)\le j^2\varDelta^2/4$, and with $g$ the next factor,
\begin{align*}
\varepsilon_{j+1}&\le\varepsilon_j+(1-a_g)|b(P_j)|+(1-a(P_j))|b(g)|\\
&\quad+|b(P_j)||b(g)|\\
&\le\varepsilon_j+\frac{(j+j^2)\varDelta^3}{4\sqrt2}+\frac{j\varDelta^2}2 .
\end{align*}
Summing over $j=1,2,3$ with $\varepsilon_1=0$ gives $3\varDelta^2+
\frac{20}{4\sqrt2}\varDelta^3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sfperp}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $0<\kappa\le10^{-8}$ and $\lambda>0$. Then $Z_\perp(I)>0$:
for $X=\{y\}$ the outer variables at which $S_X=0<K_X$ and $\varPhi_X>0$ have
positive $\nu^{\rm out}_{I,X}$-measure. In the linear model the same holds
for every $\kappa>0$ and $\lambda>0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $x=2y+(1,1,1,1)$, and let the cubes $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ at $x$
be those in the directions $0,1,2$ and $0,1,3$. Each has three faces at $x$,
owned by $y$, and three opposite faces, owned by $y+e_2$, $y+e_1$, $y+e_0$
and by $y+e_3$, $y+e_1$, $y+e_0$, none in $\hat X$, which contain no link of
$\mathcal V_X$. The face $p_0$ at $x$ in the plane $\{0,1\}$ belongs to both.
\emph{The field $\varphi_2$.} Let $\sigma=\frac{11}{20}$, $\tau=\frac14$,
and let $C=x+\{0,1\}^4$. As for $\varphi_1$, the edge $(x+\varepsilon,\mu)$
of $C$ is a private link of the pair $(y+\varepsilon,\mu)$, and distinct
edges lie in distinct pairs. Let $\varphi_2$ take the value $\sigma$ on
$(x+e_2,0)$, $(x+e_1,2)$, $(x+e_3,1)$, $(x+e_0,3)$; $-\sigma$ on $(x+e_2,1)$,
$(x+e_0,2)$, $(x+e_3,0)$, $(x+e_1,3)$; $\mp\frac23\sigma$ on $(x+e_0+e_2,1)$,
$(x+e_0+e_3,1)$; $\mp\frac13\sigma$ on $(x+e_0+e_1,2)$, $(x+e_0+e_1,3)$;
$\tau$ on $(x+e_1+e_3,2)$, $(x+e_0+e_2,3)$; $-\tau$ on $(x+e_1+e_2,3)$,
$(x+e_0+e_3,2)$; minus one seventh of that value on the other seven private
links of the pair of each of these sixteen edges; and zero elsewhere. The
exchange of the coordinates $2$ and $3$ about $x$ maps $\varphi_2$ to
$-\varphi_2$. As for $\varphi_1$, $V(\varphi_2)=0$, $\varphi_2$ vanishes on
$\mathcal V_X$, since its pairs are those of blocks $y+\varepsilon$ with
$\varepsilon\ne0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, and on a $2$-face of $C$ it is given
by the sixteen values, the other edges of $C$ carrying zero. Write $[a;
\mu\nu]$ for the plaquette at $x+a$ in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$. The $2$-faces
of $C$ not at $x$ are the eighteen $[e_a;\mu\nu]$ with $a\notin\{\mu,\nu\}$
and $[e_a+e_b;\mu\nu]$ with $\{a,b,\mu,\nu\}=\{0,1,2,3\}$, owned by $y+e_a$
and $y+e_a+e_b$. Adding the values on their edges gives
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{llllll}
\hline
$[e_2;01]$ & $\frac43\sigma$ & $[e_3;01]$ & $-\frac43\sigma$ &
$[e_1;23]$ & $2\sigma-2\tau$\\
$[e_1;02]$ & $-\frac43\sigma$ & $[e_1;03]$ & $\frac43\sigma$ &
$[e_0;23]$ & $2\tau-2\sigma$\\
$[e_0;12]$ & $\frac43\sigma$ & $[e_0;13]$ & $-\frac43\sigma$ &
$[e_0+e_1;23]$ & $-\frac23\sigma$\\
$[e_2;03]$ & $\sigma+\tau$ & $[e_3;02]$ & $-\sigma-\tau$ &
$[e_0+e_3;12]$ & $\frac23\sigma+\tau$\\
$[e_2;13]$ & $-\sigma-\tau$ & $[e_3;12]$ & $\sigma+\tau$ &
$[e_0+e_2;13]$ & $-\frac23\sigma-\tau$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
and the faces $[e_1+e_2;03]$, $[e_1+e_3;02]$, $[e_2+e_3;01]$ contain one of
the sixteen edges or none. A plaquette that is not a $2$-face of $C$
contains at most one edge of $C$, so at most one link with $|\varphi_2|>
\frac\sigma7$, and has $|d\varphi_2|\le\frac{10}7\sigma=\frac{11}{14}$. Every
entry of the table has modulus at most $\sigma+\tau$, so every plaquette not
owned by $y$ has $|d\varphi_2|\le m=\sigma+\tau=\frac45$. The first three
rows of the first two columns are the outer faces of $\mathcal A$ and
$\mathcal B$, so, with the signs of the Bianchi identity as in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfshelllin}, $R_{\mathcal A}=4\sigma=\frac{11}5$ and
$R_{\mathcal B}=-\frac{11}5$.

\emph{Linear model.} As in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfshelllin}, with
$\kappa=1$, a calm completion would give, from $\mathcal A$, $(d\varphi)_{
p_0}\ge R_{\mathcal A}-2=\frac15$ and, from $\mathcal B$,
$(d\varphi)_{p_0}\le2+R_{\mathcal B}=-\frac15$. These strict inequalities,
and $|d\varphi|<1$ off $\Pi(y)$, hold on a neighbourhood of $\varphi_2$, on
which therefore the blocks off $y$ are calm, $S^{\rm lin}_X=0$, and every
completion near the inner part of $\varphi_2$ has $y$ rough, so
$K^{\rm lin}_X>0$.

\emph{$\SU(2)$.} Let $U=\exp(\kappa\varphi_2\tau_3)$ on every active link.
It is abelian, its plaquettes are $\exp(\kappa(d\varphi_2)_p\tau_3)$ with
$\delta\le\kappa|(d\varphi_2)_p|$, and its sites, products of three links
with $|\varphi_2|\le\sigma$, lie within $3\sigma\kappa<2\kappa$ of $I$, so
$U$ is regular, the cut-offs equal one, and $V^\sharp(U)=\exp(\kappa V(
\varphi_2)\tau_3)=I$. The construction in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}(ii), with $\rho=\kappa/10^4$ in place of the
$\rho$ chosen there, gives a set
$\varGamma\subset F_I$ with $\nu_I(\varGamma)>0$ on which every plaquette
satisfies $\delta(U'_p,U_p)\le90\rho$, by bi-invariance and $\delta\le d$. On $\varGamma$ every plaquette not owned
by $y$ is at most $(m+0.009)\kappa<\kappa$.

Fix $U'\in\varGamma$ and suppose that its outer variables admit a calm
completion $U''$. Then every plaquette of $U''$ is at most $\kappa$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(i) and~(iv), with $c=I$, every inside link is
within $3\kappa$ of $I$, every path link $v$ satisfies $v=\exp(-\frac1{16}
\sum_x\log(v^{-1}P_x))$ with $\delta(v^{-1}P_x,I)\le24\kappa$, so
$\delta(v,I)\le8\pi\kappa$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, and every other
link leaving a block is within $(21+8\pi)\kappa=:\varDelta$ of $I$. The
linear parts of the six faces of a cube cancel as in the linear model, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sfquat}, for the third coordinates $b_3$ of the vector parts,
\[
\bigl|b_3(U''_{p_0})-b_3(U''_{p_1})+b_3(U''_{p_2})-R^b_{\mathcal A}\bigr|
\le6\varepsilon_4,
\]
where $\varepsilon_4=3\varDelta^2+3.54\varDelta^3$,
with $p_1$, $p_2$ the other faces of $\mathcal A$ at $x$ and $R^b_{\mathcal
A}$ the signed sum of $b_3$ over its outer faces, which are those of $U'$;
likewise for $\mathcal B$. Since $|b_3|\le\kappa/\sqrt2$ on calm faces,
\[
R^b_{\mathcal A}-\sqrt2\kappa-6\varepsilon_4\le b_3(U''_{p_0})\le
R^b_{\mathcal B}+\sqrt2\kappa+6\varepsilon_4 .
\]
At $U$ the outer faces have $b_3=\sin(\kappa F/\sqrt2)$ with $F=\pm\frac43
\sigma=\pm\frac{11}{15}$ as in the table, so $R^b_{\mathcal A}=-R^b_{\mathcal
B}=3\sin\frac{11\kappa}{15\sqrt2}$, and as $\sin\theta\ge\theta(1-\theta^2/6)$,
\[
R^b_{\mathcal A}-R^b_{\mathcal B}\ge\frac{22}5\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\Bigl(1-
\frac{\kappa^2}6\Bigr)>3.1111\,\kappa .
\]
On $\varGamma$ each $b_3$ moves by at most $90\rho/\sqrt2$, since $\lVert g-g'
\rVert\ge\sqrt2|b(g)-b(g')|$, so $R^b_{\mathcal A}-R^b_{\mathcal B}$ moves by
at most $540\rho/\sqrt2<0.0382\,\kappa$. As $\pi<3.1416$, $\varDelta<46.14\,
\kappa$, so $\varDelta^2<2128.9\,\kappa^2$, $\varDelta^3<98228\,\kappa^3$ and,
for $\kappa\le10^{-8}$, $\varepsilon_4<6386.7\,\kappa^2+0.0035\,\kappa^2<
6387\,\kappa^2$ and $12\varepsilon_4<76644\,\kappa^2<0.00077\,\kappa$. With
$2\sqrt2<2.8285$,
\begin{align*}
R^b_{\mathcal A}-R^b_{\mathcal B}-2\sqrt2\kappa-12\varepsilon_4&>(3.1111-
0.0382)\kappa\\
&\quad-(2.8285+0.00077)\kappa>0.24\,\kappa
\end{align*}
at the outer variables of $U'$, which contradicts the previous display. So $S_X=0$ at the outer
variables of every $U'\in\varGamma$; since $U'$ is a completion of them
whose blocks off $y$ are calm, $y$ is rough at $U'$. By the factorisation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(i) and Fubini, the part of $Z_\perp(I)$ from
$X=\{y\}$ is at least $\int_\varGamma e^{-\lambda Q}\,d\nu_I>0$.
\end{proof}

So $Z_\perp$ is a genuine part of the weight, made of boundary values that
force a rough block, and it is not a function of the calm law. It is
suppressed like a rough block, in the mean by
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfperp}(ii) and pointwise in the outer variables by
the bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(ii) on $K_X$; a bound on $Z_\perp(c)
/Z_\emptyset(c)$ uniform in $c$ is not proved.

The small-field part therefore stands as follows. The representation of the
calm weight as $e^{-\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\log c)}$ times local factors and a
polymer sum fails at every $\lambda>0.5472$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgaugeobst}),
and, if $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$, as a product of local factors at large $\lambda$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}); the leading term must be gauge invariant and,
under the same condition, nonlocal, and its linear propagator decays at
the explicit rate of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfprop}. In the linear model the relative activities are
unbounded under the calm law at every $\lambda$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfshelllin}),
so the almost sure hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(ii)
fails there, while their mean is at most $e^{-9.2|X|}$ for $\lambda\kappa^2
\ge16$, and the Gaussian layer of the step reproduces itself at every scale
with the same constants (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfglstep},
Corollaries~\ref{cor:sfglscales} and~\ref{cor:sfglshell} below); and
$Z_\perp(I)>0$ for $\SU(2)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfperp}). Not
proved are a local expansion around a gauge-invariant leading term, any
bound on the relative activities in the shell for $\SU(2)$, and a bound on
$Z_\perp/Z_\emptyset$ uniform in $c$.

\paragraph*{The Gaussian layer of the step.}
The linear model of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfshelllin} is the Gaussian layer of
the step. This paragraph expands it around its Gaussian form at every scale.
The thresholds are placed on the fluctuation about the minimiser of the form
at given averages, the background, and not on the field. With this choice
the large-field remainder does not depend on the coarse field, its relative
weights are bounded by $e^{-9.2}$ per block for $\lambda\kappa_{\rm f}^2\ge
16$, uniformly in the coarse field, the volume and the scale, and the only
hypothesis on the form, that it dominates the plaquette form, is reproduced
