$4s(y-e_1)=-4s(y)$ when $o_0=1$, $o_1=0$. So $(d^{\mathsf T}d\varphi^*)_{
(x,0)}=4s(y)$ when $o_0=1$ and zero otherwise. The link $(x,1)$ is the
same with the roles of the directions exchanged and the sign of the
orientation reversed, which gives $-4s(y)$ when $o_1=1$. Links in the
directions $2,3$ lie in no curved plaquette. For the second equality, a
link $(x,\mu)$ with $o_\mu=1$ enters only $V_{y,\mu}$, with coefficient
$\frac18$, and a link with $o_\mu=0$ enters $V_{y,\mu}$ and $V_{y-e_\mu,
\mu}$ with $\frac1{16}$ each, and $\gamma_{B,(y-e_\mu,\mu)}=-\gamma_{B,(
y,\mu)}$. Now for every real $\varphi$ with $V(\varphi)=\gamma$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kktbound}
\sum_p(d\varphi)_p^2\ge2\ip{d\varphi}{d\varphi^*}-\sum_p(d\varphi^*)_p^2=
64\ip{\gamma}{\gamma_B}-64|T|,
\end{equation}
which for $\gamma=\gamma_B$, $\lvert\gamma_B\rvert^2=2|T|$, is $64|T|$, with
equality at $\varphi^*$. For $\gamma_A$, $T$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:whitney}
multiplies $\gamma_A$ by $t_L$, since $\gamma_A$ depends on $y_0$ alone and
$\tau_0\cos(2\pi y_0/n)=(\frac34+\frac14\cos\frac{2\pi}n)\cos(2\pi y_0/n)$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:whitney} with $k=1$ on the coarse torus of side $n$, whose
proof uses only the local structure, gives $V(\Pi(\gamma_A/t_L))=\gamma_A$
and $\sum_p(d\Pi(\gamma_A/t_L))_p^2\le Q_1(\gamma_A)/t_L^2$.

(ii) The curvature of $c^\varepsilon$ is $e^{4\varepsilon s(y)\tau}$ in
the plane $\{0,1\}$ and $I$ elsewhere, so $Q_1(c^\varepsilon)=|T|f(4
\varepsilon)$. Let $U\in F_{c^\varepsilon}$; we may assume $Q(U)\le64
\varepsilon^2|T|$. Then every plaquette has $\delta(U_p,I)\le8\varepsilon
|T|^{1/2}$, and for $\varepsilon$ small Lemma~\ref{lem:smallframes}(i)
and (iv) with $W=T$ put every link within $C\varepsilon$ of $I$, as in the
proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}(ii), using $\delta(c^\varepsilon_k,I)
\le\varepsilon$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:logbound}, $U=e^X$ with $|X|=\max_e\lVert
X_e\rVert\le C\varepsilon$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:bch}, $\lVert\log U_p-(dX)_
p\rVert\le C\varepsilon^2$, and $\delta(e^Y,I)^2\ge\lVert Y\rVert^2(1-
\lVert Y\rVert^2/24)$, so $Q(U)\ge\sum_p\lVert(dX)_p\rVert^2-C\varepsilon^3
|T|$. As in that proof, $\log V^\sharp_k(e^X)=V_k(X)+O(|X|^2)$, so the
component $X^\tau=\ip X\tau$ has $V(X^\tau)=\varepsilon\gamma_B+r$ with
$\lvert r_k\rvert\le C\varepsilon^2$. Apply~\eqref{eq:kktbound} to
$X^\tau/\varepsilon$:
\begin{align*}
\sum_p\lVert(dX)_p\rVert^2&\ge\sum_p(dX^\tau)_p^2\ge64\varepsilon^2|T|-64
\varepsilon\ip r{\gamma_B}\\
&\ge(64-C\varepsilon)\varepsilon^2|T| .
\end{align*}

(iii) By Lemma~\ref{lem:straightpaths}(iii), whose proof is local, $\Pi(\gamma_A/
t_L)$ plus a gradient that vanishes under $V$ is a field $\varphi_A$ in the
tree gauge with $V(\varphi_A)=\gamma_A$ and $\sum_p(d\varphi_A)_p^2\le
Q_1(\gamma_A)/t_L^2$. Let $U_\varepsilon=e^{\varepsilon\tau\varphi_A}$.
All its links lie in the one-parameter group $e^{\R\tau}$, so the path
product $P_x$ of a coarse link is $e^{\varepsilon\tau\sigma_x}$, $\sigma_x$
the sum of $\varphi_A$ along the path of length two from $x$. For
$\varepsilon$ small, $\delta(P_x,P_{2y})\le\varepsilon\lvert\sigma_x-
\sigma_{2y}\rvert$ is below $\frac14$, so $U_\varepsilon$ is regular, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:cutoff}(i) gives $V^\sharp_{y,\mu}(U_\varepsilon)=e^{
\varepsilon\tau V_{y,\mu}(\varphi_A)}$, that is $V^\sharp(U_\varepsilon)=
c_\varepsilon$. Then $Q(U_\varepsilon)=\sum_pf(\varepsilon(d\varphi_A)_p)
\le\varepsilon^2Q_1(\gamma_A)/t_L^2$ and $Q_1(c_\varepsilon)=\sum_Pf(
\varepsilon(d\gamma_A)_P)\ge\varepsilon^2Q_1(\gamma_A)(1-\varepsilon^2/6)$,
as $\lvert(d\gamma_A)_P\rvert\le2$.

(iv) By Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}(i), $\lambda S_1(c)-4|T|\log M\le
A_1(c)\le b\lambda Q_1(c)+e(\lambda)$; divide by $\lambda$ and let $\lambda
\to\infty$: $S_1(c)\le bQ_1(c)$. At $c^\varepsilon$, (ii) gives $b\ge4-
C\varepsilon/16$ for every small $\varepsilon$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}(ii) with any $\eta>0$ and the regular field
$U_\varepsilon$, $a\lambda Q_1(c_\varepsilon)-e(\lambda)\le(1+\eta)\lambda
Q(U_\varepsilon)+c_1(\lambda,\eta)|T|$, and $c_1(\lambda,\eta)$ grows like
$\log\lambda$; so $aQ_1(c_\varepsilon)\le Q(U_\varepsilon)$, and (iii)
gives $a\le t_L^{-2}(1+C\varepsilon^2)$. The value $4t_{32}^2=3.8491\ldots$
and $t_L\to1$ give the last statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:stepconstants}
Part (i) makes exact the right end of the Bloch spectrum stated after
Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}: $\gamma_B$ is the mode of momentum
$(\pi,\pi,0,0)$ in the plane $\{0,1\}$, and~\eqref{eq:kktidentity} is the
Lagrange condition of $q_1$ at it, with multiplier $64\gamma_B$. The field
$\gamma_A$ is the long-wavelength end. So $C_*$ is a constant of the
witness argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:lfcoarseenergy} and not of the step:
the best lower constant lies between $\theta(\kappa_0)$ on the small coarse
fields and $t_L^{-2}$, the best upper constant is $4$, and a comparison
with $\lambda Q_1$ with constants $1+o(1)$ on both sides does not exist.
Constants close to one on both sides hold for the fibre infimum itself:
by Theorem~\ref{thm:lfaction}, $\lambda S_1(c)-4|T|\log M\le A_1(c)\le(1+
\eta)\lambda Q(U)+c_1(\lambda,\eta)|T|$ for every regular $U\in F_c$. At
the linear level $S_1$ is the block-spin form $q_1$, which is not a sum of
local terms if $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss}). The reference
forms $R_k$ below
are built from the block-spin form for this reason.
\end{remark}

\emph{The conditional iteration.} Let $K\ge1$ and $\lambda_0>\lambda_1>
\dots>\lambda_K>0$. For $0\le k\le K$ let $\mathcal X_k$ be a finite
dimensional real inner product space, for $k<K$ let $B_k:\mathcal X_k\to
\mathcal X_{k+1}$ be linear and onto, and let $H_k$ be a positive
semidefinite quadratic form on $\mathcal X_k$. For a form $H$ on $\mathcal
X_k$ put $\mathcal M_kH(w)=\inf\{H(x):B_kx=w\}$, and define the reference
forms by
\[
R_0=H_0,\qquad R_{k+1}=\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\,\mathcal M_kR_k .
\]
In the application $H_k$ is the gauge-invariant Hessian $\mathcal HA_k$ of
the effective action of scale $k$ at a chain of backgrounds, in
exponential coordinates, and $B_k$ the derivative of the cut-off average.
At the trivial background, with $\mathcal X_k$ the $\g$-valued fields on
the active links of spacing $2^k$, $B_k=V$ and $H_0=2\lambda_0\sum_p\lVert
(dX)_p\rVert^2$, the Hessian of $\lambda_0Q$ at $I$, the identity $V^{(k+1)
}=V\circ V^{(k)}$ gives $R_k=2\lambda_kS_k$, where $S_k(w)=\inf\{\sum_p
\lVert(d\varphi)_p\rVert^2:V^{(k)}(\varphi)=w\}$ on the torus; by Lemma~\ref{lem:straightpaths}(iii), whose proof is local,
$R_1$ is $2\lambda_1q_1$ on each component. The hypotheses at step $k<K$ are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{relative error:} for some $0\le\varepsilon_k<1$,
\[
(1-\varepsilon_k)\tfrac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k\le
H_{k+1}\le(1+\varepsilon_k)\tfrac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k ;
\]
\item \emph{locality:} on a subspace $\mathcal Y_{k+1}\subset\mathcal X_{k+1}$
on which $R_{k+1}$ and $H_{k+1}$ are positive definite, a slice of the
coarse gauge orbits, with a metric on its coordinates and $\alpha_{k+1}\ge
0$, for every $W=e^{\alpha_{k+1}\phi}$ with $\phi$ $1$-Lipschitz,
\[
\lVert WR_{k+1}^{-1}W^{-1}\rVert\le G_{k+1},\qquad\lVert W(H_{k+1}-
R_{k+1})W^{-1}\rVert\le\frac{\ell_{k+1}}{G_{k+1}},
\]
with $\ell_{k+1}<1$;
\item \emph{large-field cost:} the weight of a coarse field of scale $k+1$
is $Z_{k,\emptyset}(c)\,\varXi_k(c)$, where $\varXi_k(c)$ is the mean,
under a probability law, of the sum over families of pairwise compatible
nonempty $\ell^\infty$-connected sets $X_i$ of blocks of scale $k+1$ of
products $\prod_i\rho_{X_i}$, with $0\le\rho_X\le e^{-9|X|}$ almost
surely and compatibility as in Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}.
\end{enumerate}
For $k=0$, the hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(ii) gives
(H3) only when $Z_\perp=0$. For $\SU(2)$, $Z_\perp(I)>0$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:sfperp}), so (H3) at $k=0$ has to keep $Z_\perp$ as part
of the weight, and is not available in the form stated.

\begin{theorem}[conditional iteration]\label{thm:iterate}
Suppose that (H1)--(H3) hold at every step $k<K$, and let $\sigma=\sum_{k<K}
\varepsilon_k$, $|T_k|=|T|/16^{k-1}$ the number of blocks of scale $k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $k\le K$, $\prod_{j<k}(1-\varepsilon_j)R_k\le H_k\le\prod_{j<k}
(1+\varepsilon_j)R_k$; in particular $(1-\sigma)R_K\le H_K\le e^\sigma R_K$.
\item Let $\lambda_k=\lambda_0-tk$, $t=2b_0\log2$, the one-loop running of
Remark~\ref{rem:constrainedopen}(c), with $t=0.0643779\ldots$ and $1/t<
15.534$ for $\SU(2)$. If $\varepsilon_k\le c_\varepsilon\lambda_{k+1}^{-2}$
for every $k<K$, then
\[
\sigma\le c_\varepsilon\Bigl(\frac1{\lambda_K^2}+\frac1{t\lambda_K}\Bigr),
\]
uniformly in $\lambda_0$ and $K$; so $\sigma\le\frac12$ once $\lambda_K\ge
32,311,3107$ for $c_\varepsilon=1,10,100$, that is $\beta_K\ge128,1244,
12428$. If instead $\varepsilon_k\ge c\,\lambda_{k+1}^{-1}$ for every $k$,
then $\sigma\ge(c/t)\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_K)$, which is unbounded as
$\lambda_0\to\infty$ at fixed $\lambda_K$.
\item For $1\le k\le K$, $\lVert WH_k^{-1}W^{-1}\rVert\le G_k/(1-\ell_k)$
on $\mathcal Y_k$ for every $W$ as in (H2), and $\lvert(H_k^{-1})_{ij}
\rvert\le G_k(1-\ell_k)^{-1}e^{-\alpha_k\dist(i,j)}$.
\item For $k<K$, $\varXi_k=\E[e^{\varLambda_k}]$, where $\varLambda_k$ is
the absolutely convergent sum of the connected clusters, those
incompatible with a given block add up to at most $\frac1{10}$, and $0\le
\log\varXi_k\le|T_{k+1}|/10$; the sum over the steps is at most $\frac8
{75}|T|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) If $H\le H'$ then $\mathcal M_kH\le\mathcal M_kH'$, and $\mathcal M_k(sH)
=s\mathcal M_kH$ for $s\ge0$; this is the argument of
Proposition~\ref{prop:formstability}, which takes infima over the same
affine subspaces and does not use definiteness. Induction on $k$ with (H1)
gives the products, and $\prod(1-\varepsilon_j)\ge1-\sigma$, $\prod(1+
\varepsilon_j)\le e^\sigma$.
(b) $\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_K+t(K-k-1)$, so $\sum_{k<K}\lambda_{k+1}^{-2}\le
\lambda_K^{-2}+\int_0^\infty(\lambda_K+tx)^{-2}dx$. For the lower bound,
$t\lambda_{k+1}^{-1}\ge\int_{\lambda_{k+1}}^{\lambda_k}d\lambda/\lambda$.
With $1/t<15.534$ the bound is at most $0.4865$, $0.4997$ and
$0.49999$ at $\lambda_K=32$, $311$, $3107$ for $c_\varepsilon=1,10,100$,
and it decreases in $\lambda_K$.
(c) The last statement of Proposition~\ref{prop:formstability} with $H_0=
R_k$ and $\varepsilon=\ell_k$; for the entries take $\phi=\dist(\cdot,j)$
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}.
(d) Theorem~\ref{thm:lfkp}(i), whose proof uses only the activity bound
and the count of connected sets of blocks, applied on the torus of scale
$k+1$ to each realisation of the activities, as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}(ii); and $\sum_{k\ge0}16^{-k}/10=
\frac8{75}$.
\end{proof}

The theorem composes hypotheses; it does not supply them. The relative
form (H1) is the one that survives composition with factor one, while an
absolute error grows by at least $4/(1+2724\kappa)$ per step
(Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth}), and order-$g^2$ errors are not
summable along the running, by (b). The locality (H2) is posed at each
scale: Lemma~\ref{lem:schur} carries a bound on $H_k-R_k$ to the Schur
complement only with the factor $(1+b_kg_k)^2$, and a relative bound
(H1) carries no locality (Proposition~\ref{prop:formstability}).

\begin{proposition}[what is proved of $(\mathrm H_k)$]\label{prop:iteratestatus}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item (H1) is not proved at any step. At $k=0$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} gives it on a box from the absolute
hypothesis (H) there, with $\varepsilon'$ containing $\delta_GC_n/(2c_*
\lambda)$, of order $g^2n^2$, and Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep} under a
loop representation of the remainder that is not proved.
\item (H2): at the trivial background the reference $R_k=2\lambda_kS_k$ is
local as a form uniformly in $k$ on $\Z^4$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:effectivelocal}),
and Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} gives decay of covariances at one scale.
The bound on $H_{k+1}-R_{k+1}$ is not proved for any $k$.
\item (H3) at $k=0$: the activities satisfy $\rho_X\le e^{-9|X|}$ where the
boundary values admit a completion calm at $\kappa/30$, for $\lambda\ge
\lambda^{**}(\kappa)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm},
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}); the shell $(\kappa/30,\kappa]$ and
$Z_\perp$, which is positive for $\SU(2)$, are not bounded, so (H3) is not
proved at $k=0$, and nothing is proved for $k\ge1$.
\item The rates of Theorems~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(iii) and~\ref{thm:sfcalm}
are increasing in $\kappa$, and $\kappa<\kappa_c$ is required, where
$0.0837613\le\kappa_c\le0.0837617$ (Sec.~\ref{ssec:witnessradius}). For
every $\kappa<\kappa_c$, $a(\lambda,\kappa)<9$ when $100\le\lambda\le245000$
and $a_2(\lambda,\kappa)<9$ when $100\le\lambda\le809300$, whatever $M\ge1$;
with $M<2.3621\cdot10^4$, $a(\lambda,\kappa_c)\ge9$ for $\lambda\ge257000$
and $a_2(\lambda,\kappa_c)\ge9$ for $\lambda\ge833000$. So, with $\beta^*$
and $\beta^{**}$ at $\kappa_c$ defined by these rates,
\begin{gather*}
9.800\cdot10^5<\beta^*(\kappa_c)\le1.028\cdot10^6,\\
3.2372\cdot10^6<\beta^{**}(\kappa_c)\le3.332\cdot10^6,
\end{gather*}
and along the one-loop running more than $1.257\cdot10^7$ steps lie between
$\lambda=809300$ and $\lambda=1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i)--(iii) restate the cited results. (iv) Both rates contain $\kappa$
only through $\lambda\kappa^2$ with a positive coefficient, and $\log M\ge
0$, so for $\kappa<\kappa_c$, $a(\lambda,\kappa)<h(\lambda)=\lambda
\kappa_c^2-c_1(\lambda,1)$ and $a_2(\lambda,\kappa)<h_2(\lambda)=0.52\lambda
\kappa_c^2-c_2(\lambda,1)$. Since $c_1(\lambda,1)$ and $c_2(\lambda,1)$ are
affine in $\log\lambda$ with positive coefficients $67.5$ and $109.5$, $h$
and $h_2$ are convex, so on an interval they are below the larger of their
values at its ends. The logarithms of $1.957$, $14$, $23040\lambda$,
$31958\lambda$ and $23621$ at the values of $\lambda$ used follow from
$x=2^ky$ with $1\le y<2$ and $\log y=2\operatorname{artanh}\frac{y-1}
{y+1}$, the series with its tail bounded geometrically. They give $c_1(100,
1)>1183$ and $c_2(100,1)>1958$, so $h(100)<0$ and $h_2(100)<0$, and, with
$\kappa_c\le0.0837617$, $h(245000)\le8.966$ and $h_2(809300)\le8.947$. With
$\kappa_c\ge0.0837613$ and $\log M<\log23621$, $a(\lambda,\kappa_c)\ge
\lambda\kappa_c^2-8\log23621-c_1(\lambda,1)$, which increases for $\lambda>
67.5/\kappa_c^2$, where $67.5/\kappa_c^2<9621$, and is at least $9.35$ at
$\lambda=257000$; and $a_2(\lambda,\kappa_c)\ge0.52\lambda\kappa_c^2-8\log
23621-c_2(\lambda,1)$, which increases for $\lambda>109.5/(0.52\kappa_c^2)$,
where $109.5/(0.52\kappa_c^2)<30015$, and is at least $11.66$ at $\lambda=
833000$. With $\beta=4\lambda$ this gives the display. The count is
$(809300-1)/t$ with $t=11\log2/(12\pi^2)$, and $\pi\ge3.14159265$ gives
$1/t\ge15.53326$, so $(809300-1)/t>1.2571\cdot10^7$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:iteratelinear}
Theorem~\ref{thm:stepconstants}(ii) is not a substitute for (H1), because
its loss is linear in the field size. Suppose it is used at a step whose
coarse fields are calm at a threshold $\kappa'$ satisfying the rate
condition $\lambda'\kappa'^2\ge9+c_1(\lambda',1)$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:lfmarkov}(iii) at the next coupling $\lambda'\ge100$, so
that $\kappa'\ge34.4\,\lambda'^{-1/2}$, and suppose $\kappa_1\ge\kappa'$.
Then $\log\theta(\kappa_0)\le-2\log(1+6031\kappa_0)\le-1716\,\kappa_0$,
and either $\theta\le\frac12$ or $\kappa_0\ge\sqrt{14}\,\kappa'$, so
$-\log\theta(\kappa_0)\ge\min\{\log2,2.2\cdot10^5\lambda'^{-1/2}\}$, which
is $\log2$ for $\lambda'\le10^{11}$. The product of these factors along
the running tends to zero as $\lambda_0\to\infty$. The loss comes from
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallstep}, whose bound is linear in $\eta$; at the linear
level there is no loss, since $q_1\ge Q_1$, and the long-wavelength fields
of Theorem~\ref{thm:stepsharp}(iii) show that no lower constant above
$t_L^{-2}$ holds.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The induction over scales}\label{ssec:allscales}

This subsection asks which hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate} follow
from the conclusions of the previous step, at the trivial background. The
relative error (H1) and the large-field cost (H3) are inputs of one step
each; they are not implied by the earlier steps. The locality hypothesis
(H2) is different: it bounds the inverse of the whole Hessian, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:h2volume} shows that it cannot hold with constants
independent of the volume, since the inverse carries the long-wavelength
modes. It is replaced below by a bound on the form $H_k$ itself. The
induction step is then proved: the relative comparison, the fibre gap and
the locality of the fibre covariance pass from step $k$ to step $k+1$ under
one condition (C) on the error of the step $k$ alone, relative and local
(Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}, Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}), the
locality with constants that grow with $k$. Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}
states the induction, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:scalecount} counts the scales.

\emph{Setting.} Throughout, $H_0=2\lambda_0\sum_p\lVert(dX)_p\rVert^2$ on
$\mathcal X_0$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_0-tk$ with $t=11\log2/(12\pi^2)$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(b), and $R_k=2\lambda_kS_k$. The torus of scale
$k$ has side $n_k=L/2^k$ in units of its spacing. Let $\hat{\mathcal X}_k$
be the $\g$-valued fields on all links of that torus, so that $\mathcal X_k
\subset\hat{\mathcal X}_k$, and let $\hat R_k=2\lambda_kS_k$ on $\hat
{\mathcal X}_k$; $R_k$ is its restriction to $\mathcal X_k$. The map $B_k=V$
sends $\mathcal X_k$ onto $\hat{\mathcal X}_{k+1}$ (Proposition~\ref
{prop:effective}(ii)), $\mathcal M_kH$ is a form on $\hat{\mathcal X}_{k+1}
$, and (H1) compares its restriction to $\mathcal X_{k+1}$ with $H_{k+1}$.
All forms are written as symmetric matrices with blocks $H_{ab}\in
\operatorname{End}(\g)$ indexed by links, and $\lVert H_{ab}\rVert$ is the
operator norm. A link of scale $k$ sits at its midpoint, measured in units
of the spacing $2^k$, and $d_k$ is the $\ell^\infty$ distance on the torus
between midpoints. For a matrix $M$ indexed by a set with a pseudometric
$d$ and $\alpha\ge0$ put
\[
\lVert M\rVert_{(\alpha)}=\sup_a\sum_b\lVert M_{ab}\rVert e^{\alpha d(a,b)}.
\]
For symmetric $M$ the Schur test gives $\lVert M\rVert\le\lVert M\rVert_{(0)}
\le\lVert M\rVert_{(\alpha)}$, and $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{(\alpha)}$ does not
increase under restriction to a subset of the indices.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:weightedcount}
For $0<u\le1$ and every link $a$ of a torus of any scale, or of $\Z^4$,
$\sum_be^{-u\,d(a,b)}\le2532\,u^{-4}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The midpoints of the links of one direction form a translate of a lattice
$\Z^4$, or of a discrete torus, and the number of its points at
$\ell^\infty$ distance at most $r$ from a given point is at most $(2r+1)^4$.
Writing $e^{-ud}=\int_d^\infty ue^{-ur}\,dr$ and exchanging sum and integral,
the sum over one direction is at most $\int_0^\infty ue^{-ur}(2r+1)^4\,dr=
384u^{-4}+192u^{-3}+48u^{-2}+8u^{-1}+1$, since $\int_0^\infty ue^{-ur}r^j
\,dr=j!\,u^{-j}$. For $u\le1$ this is at most $633u^{-4}$, and there are
four directions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[(H2) depends on the volume]\label{prop:h2volume}
Let $k\ge1$ with $n_k\ge4$, and let $\mathcal Y\subset\mathcal X_k$ be a
subspace on which $R_k$ is positive definite and with $\mathcal Y+(\mathcal
X_k\cap\ker R_k)=\mathcal X_k$. Every slice of the coarse gauge orbits on
which $R_k$ is positive definite has this property, since the gauge
directions lie in $\ker R_k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item There is $\tilde w\in\hat{\mathcal X}_k$, orthogonal to $\ker\hat
R_k$, with $\hat R_k(\tilde w)\le10\pi^2\lambda_k|\tilde w|^2/n_k^2$, and
\[
\lVert(R_k|_{\mathcal Y})^{-1}\rVert\ge\frac{n_k^2}{10\pi^2\lambda_k}.
\]
\item If the bounds of (H2) hold on $\mathcal Y$ at scale $k$ with
constants $G_k$, $\ell_k$, then $G_k\ge n_k^2/(10\pi^2\lambda_k)$ and
$\lVert(H_k-R_k)|_{\mathcal Y}\rVert\le10\pi^2\ell_k\lambda_k/n_k^2$; and
the norm of $H_k^{-1}$ on $\mathcal Y$, bounded by $G_k/(1-\ell_k)$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(c), is at least $n_k^2/(10\pi^2\lambda_k)(1+
\ell_k)^{-1}$.
\item If $\mathcal Y$ is the orthogonal complement of $\mathcal X_k\cap
\ker R_k$ in $\mathcal X_k$, then $H_k=cR_k$ with $c>0$ satisfies the
bounds of (H2) at scale $k$ only if $|c-1|<5\pi^2/(6n_k^2)$.
\item On the same $\mathcal Y$, the form $E=\varepsilon\lambda_k|x|^2$
satisfies $|E|\le\varepsilon'R_k$ on $\mathcal Y$ only if $\varepsilon'\ge
\varepsilon n_k^2/(10\pi^2)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Write $n=n_k$, $N=2^kn$, $q=2\pi/N$, and fix $Z\in\g$ with $\lVert Z
\rVert=1$. Let $\varphi$ be the fine field with $\varphi_{(x,0)}=\cos(qx_1)
Z$ and $\varphi=0$ on the links of the other directions.\footnote{This is
the lowest nonconstant Fourier mode of the torus. Its energy is of order
$N^{-2}$ times its norm, the gap of the discrete Laplacian, and this is why
the bound depends on the volume.} Its only nonzero
curvatures are on the plaquettes of the plane $\{0,1\}$, where $(d\varphi)_p
=(\cos qx_1-\cos q(x_1+1))Z=2\sin\frac q2\sin q(x_1+\frac12)Z$, so
\[
Q(\varphi)=N^3\cdot4\sin^2\frac\pi N\sum_{x_1=0}^{N-1}\sin^2q\Bigl(x_1+
\frac12\Bigr)=2N^4\sin^2\frac\pi N .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:straightpaths}(i), an identity of linear maps that holds
on the torus as well, $V^{(k)}(\varphi)$ vanishes off the direction $0$
and
\[
V^{(k)}_{y,0}(\varphi)=\sum_{j=0}^{2^k-1}\cos q(2^ky_1+j)=\rho\,\tilde
w_{y,0},
\]
with $\tilde w_{y,0}=\cos(2\pi y_1/n+c_0)Z$, $c_0=q(2^k-1)/2$, $\tilde w=0$
on the other directions, and $\rho=\sin(\pi/n)/\sin(\pi/N)$. Since $n\ge3$,
$|\tilde w|^2=n^4/2$. Hence
\begin{align*}
\frac{S_k(\tilde w)}{|\tilde w|^2}&\le\frac{Q(\varphi)}{\rho^2|\tilde w|^2}
=\frac{4\cdot16^k\sin^4(\pi/N)}{\sin^2(\pi/n)}\\
&\le\frac{4\pi^4}{n^4\sin^2(\pi/n)}\le\frac{4\pi^2}{0.8049\,n^2}<\frac{5
\pi^2}{n^2},
\end{align*}
using $\sin x\le x$, and $\sin x\ge x(1-x^2/6)$ at $x=\pi/n\le\pi/4$ with
$(1-\pi^2/96)^2>0.8049$. So $\hat R_k(\tilde w)\le10\pi^2\lambda_k|\tilde
w|^2/n^2$.

$\tilde w$ is orthogonal to $\ker\hat R_k$. Indeed $S_k\ge Q_k$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(i), whose proof applies on every lattice,
so a field $w$ in $\ker\hat R_k$ has zero curvature. The curvature of a
plaquette in the plane $\{0,1\}$ at $y$ is $w_{y,0}+w_{y+e_0,1}-w_{y+e_1,0}
-w_{y,1}$; summed over $y_0$ around the torus, the terms in the direction $1$
cancel, so $f(y_1,y_2,y_3)=\sum_{y_0}w_{y,0}$ does not depend on $y_1$. Then
$\langle\tilde w,w\rangle=\sum_{y_2,y_3}\langle Z,f(\cdot,y_2,y_3)\rangle
\sum_{y_1}\cos(2\pi y_1/n+c_0)=0$.

The form $S_k$ is invariant under the coarse gauge directions: for $h$ on
the sites of scale $k$, let $h_f$ be the fine function equal to $h(y)$ on
$B_k(y)$; then $V^{(k)}(dh_f)=-d_kh$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:straightpaths}(ii),
so $\varphi\mapsto\varphi-dh_f$ maps the fields with $V^{(k)}(\varphi)=w$
onto those with $V^{(k)}(\varphi)=w+d_kh$ and preserves $Q$. As in the
proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:straightpaths}(iii), applied to the blocks of side
two of the lattice of scale $k$, there is $h$ with $t=\tilde w+d_kh\in
\mathcal X_k$, and $t-\tilde w\in\ker\hat R_k$. By hypothesis $t=y+z$ with
$y\in\mathcal Y$ and $z\in\mathcal X_k\cap\ker R_k\subset\ker\hat R_k$. A
positive semidefinite form is constant on the cosets of its kernel, so
$R_k(y)=\hat R_k(\tilde w)$; and $y\in\tilde w+\ker\hat R_k$ with $\tilde
w\perp\ker\hat R_k$, so $|y|\ge|\tilde w|$. Therefore $\lVert(R_k|_{\mathcal
Y})^{-1}\rVert\ge|y|^2/R_k(y)\ge n^2/(10\pi^2\lambda_k)$.

(ii) The function $\phi=0$ is $1$-Lipschitz, so (H2) contains $\lVert(R_k|_
{\mathcal Y})^{-1}\rVert\le G_k$ and $\lVert(H_k-R_k)|_{\mathcal Y}\rVert
\le\ell_k/G_k$; apply (i). At the vector $y$ of (i), $H_k(y)\le R_k(y)+
\lVert(H_k-R_k)|_{\mathcal Y}\rVert|y|^2\le(1+\ell_k)\,10\pi^2\lambda_k
|y|^2/n^2$, which gives the last bound.

(iii) $R_k$ is block diagonal for $\mathcal X_k=\mathcal Y\oplus(\mathcal X
_k\cap\ker R_k)$, so its norm on $\mathcal Y$ is its largest eigenvalue on
$\mathcal X_k$, which is at least $R_k(\delta_eZ)$ for the field $\delta_e
Z$ equal to $Z$ on one active link $e$ and zero elsewhere. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(iii), $R_k(\delta_eZ)\ge2\lambda_kQ_k(
\delta_eZ)=12\lambda_k$, since a link lies in six plaquettes. If $H_k=cR_k$,
then $\lVert(H_k-R_k)|_{\mathcal Y}\rVert=|c-1|\lVert R_k|_{\mathcal Y}
\rVert\ge12|c-1|\lambda_k$, and (ii) with $\ell_k<1$ gives $12|c-1|<10\pi^2
/n^2$.

(iv) At the vector $y$ of (i), $\varepsilon\lambda_k|y|^2$ is at most
$\varepsilon'R_k(y)$, which is at most $10\pi^2\varepsilon'\lambda_k|y|^2/
n^2$.
\end{proof}

The norm of $H_k^{-1}$ on a slice is therefore of order $n_k^2/\lambda_k$
for every $H_k$ with $\lVert H_k-R_k\rVert<\lambda_k$ on it, and the entry
bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(c) is at least $n_k^2/(10\pi^2\lambda_k)
(1+\ell_k)^{-1}$ at distance zero: the covariance of the massless modes
does not decay exponentially, uniformly in the volume. By (iii), (H2)
excludes a change of the coupling by any factor independent of $L$, even
one that (H1) allows with $\varepsilon_k$ fixed. Part (iv) is the torus
form of the conversion cost $C_n$ of Remark~\ref{rem:relscales}. The
exponential decay that holds uniformly is that of the fibre covariance,
where Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(iv) gives a gap, and it follows
from a bound on the form $H_k$ rather than on its inverse:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H2$^*$)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{local form:} $\lVert H_k\rVert_{(\alpha_k)}\le\Lambda_k
\lambda_k$ on $\mathcal X_k$ with the distance $d_k$, for some $0<\alpha_k
\le1$ and $\Lambda_k\ge1$;
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{local one-step error:} the difference $D_k=H_{k+1}-
\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k|_{\mathcal X_{k+1}}$ has
$\lVert D_k\rVert_{(\alpha_{k+1})}\le\delta_k\lambda_{k+1}$ with the
distance $d_{k+1}$.
\end{enumerate}
At $k=0$, $H_0=2\lambda_0Q$ has diagonal blocks $12\lambda_0$ and, in each
row, eighteen further blocks of norm $2\lambda_0$, at the other links of
the six plaquettes of the link, all at distance at most one; so
(H2$^*$) holds at $k=0$ for every $\alpha_0\in(0,1]$ with $\Lambda_0=12+
36e^{\alpha_0}$. Hypothesis (D) concerns one integration only, while (H2)
concerns the composition of all earlier ones.

For $k<K$ let $\mathcal C_k$ be the inverse of $H_k$ on $\ker B_k\cap
\mathcal X_k$, extended by zero on its orthogonal complement in $\mathcal
X_k$ (the covariance of the fibre, up to the factor of the Gaussian
normalisation), and $\mathcal T_k:\hat{\mathcal X}_{k+1}\to\mathcal X_k$
the map that sends $w$ to the minimiser of $H_k$ on $\{B_kx=w\}$. A coarse
link $(y,\mu)$ is placed, in the units of scale $k$, at the centre $2y+e_
\mu+\frac12(1,1,1,1)$ of $B(y)\cup B(y+e_\mu)$; on the union of the links
of scale $k$ and these points $d$ denotes the $\ell^\infty$ distance in
units of scale $k$, so that $d=2d_{k+1}$ between two coarse links.

\begin{proposition}[what passes from step $k$ to step $k+1$]
\label{prop:fibreinherit}
Let $k<K$ with $n_k\ge4$, and let $H_k$ be positive semidefinite on
$\mathcal X_k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $k=0$, or if (H1) holds at the steps $j<k$ with $\sigma_k=\sum_{j<
k}\varepsilon_j\le\frac12$, then $H_k(x)\ge\lambda_k|x|^2/52$ for $x\in
\ker B_k\cap\mathcal X_k$.
\item Suppose the bound of (i) and (H2$^*$) at scale $k$, and put
$\alpha_*=\alpha_k/(11900\Lambda_k)$. Then for all links $a,b$ of scale $k$
and $i,j$ of scale $k+1$,
\begin{gather*}
\lVert(\mathcal C_k)_{ab}\rVert\le\frac{2186}{\lambda_k}e^{-\alpha_*d(a,b)},
\\
\lVert(\mathcal T_k)_{ai}\rVert\le2186\,\Lambda_ke^{-\alpha_*d(a,i)},\\
\lVert(\mathcal M_kH_k)_{ij}\rVert\le2186\,\Lambda_k^2\lambda_k\,e^{-2
\alpha_*d_{k+1}(i,j)} .
\end{gather*}
\item Under the same hypotheses, with $C_*=2186\cdot2532\cdot11900^4$,
which is less than $1.11\cdot10^{23}$,
\[
\Bigl\lVert\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k|_{\mathcal X_{k+
1}}\Bigr\rVert_{(\alpha_*)}\le C_*\frac{\Lambda_k^6}{\alpha_k^4}\lambda_{k+
1};
\]
so if (D) holds with $\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_*$, then (H2$^*$) holds at scale
$k+1$ with $\Lambda_{k+1}=C_*\Lambda_k^6\alpha_k^{-4}+\delta_k$.
\item For every positive semidefinite $H$ on $\mathcal X_k$ and $\varepsilon
\ge0$, the form $E=\varepsilon\lambda_k|x|^2$ has $\lVert E\rVert_{(\alpha)}
=\varepsilon\lambda_k$ for every $\alpha$, while $\mathcal M_k(H+E)-\mathcal
M_kH\ge4\varepsilon\lambda_k|w|^2$ on $\hat{\mathcal X}_{k+1}$. So no bound
$\lVert\mathcal M_k(H+E)-\mathcal M_kH\rVert\le C\lVert E\rVert_{(\alpha)}$
holds for all $H$ and $E$ with $C<4$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{The averages.} By the formula of the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap}, $V_{y,\mu}$ has the coefficient $\frac18$ on the
eight links $(x,\mu)$, $x\in B(y)$, $o_\mu=1$, which are never tree links,
and $\frac1{16}$ on the links of direction $\mu$ with $o_\mu=0$ in $B(y)$
and in $B(y+e_\mu)$. So a row of $B=B_k$ has absolute sum at most $2$, a
link has total weight at most $\frac18$ in the rows, and every link in the
support of a row lies within distance $1$ of the point of its coarse link:
the transverse coordinates of the midpoints differ from those of the centre
by $\frac12$, and the coordinate $\mu$ by at most $1$. The diagonal entries
of $BB^\top$ are at least $8/64$, and the row $(y,\mu)$ meets only the rows
$(y\pm e_\mu,\mu)$, in at most eight links with coefficients $\frac1{16}$,
so its off-diagonal entries add up to at most $2\cdot\frac8{256}$. By
Gershgorin, $BB^\top\ge\frac1{16}$, and likewise $BB^\top\le\frac8{64}+
\frac{16}{256}+\frac2{32}=\frac14$. These bounds act on each component in
an orthonormal basis of $\g$.

(i) At $k=0$, $H_0=R_0$. Otherwise Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(a), whose
proof uses only (H1), gives $H_k\ge(1-\sigma_k)R_k\ge\lambda_kS_k$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(iv), whose proof uses only
Theorem~\ref{thm:blockgap} and $S_k\ge Q_k$ and so applies on the torus,
gives $S_k(x)\ge|x|^2/52$ on $\ker B_k\cap\mathcal X_k$, the space $\Phi_W$
of the lattice of scale $k$ with $W$ all its blocks.

(ii) Let $\lambda=\lambda_k$, $\Lambda=\Lambda_k$, $s=\Lambda\lambda$, and
$K=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}H_k&sB^\top\\sB&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on
$\mathcal X_k\oplus\hat{\mathcal X}_{k+1}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:saddle} applies
with $h=\lVert H_k\rVert\le\Lambda\lambda$, $\beta=\frac1{16}$ and $a=
\lambda/52$: with $\Lambda\ge1$, $|x_1|\le4|g|/(\Lambda\lambda)$,
\begin{gather*}
|x|\le\frac{52(|f|+4|g|)+4|g|}{\lambda}=\frac{52|f|+212|g|}\lambda,\\
|y|\le\frac{4|f|}{\Lambda\lambda}+4|x|\le\frac{212|f|+848|g|}\lambda,
\end{gather*}
so $|x|+|y|\le(264|f|+1060|g|)/\lambda$, and $\lVert K^{-1}\rVert\le1093/
\lambda$ since $264^2+1060^2<1093^2$. With weights $e^{\alpha_kd}$, a row
of $H_k$ in $K$ has sum at most $\Lambda\lambda+\frac18se^{\alpha_k}$, and a
row of $sB$ at most $2se^{\alpha_k}$; with $\alpha_k\le1$ both are at most
$2e\Lambda\lambda\le5.44\Lambda\lambda$. Lemma~\ref{lem:combes} needs a
finite range, and is replaced as follows. For $1$-Lipschitz $\phi$ and
$0\le\alpha\le\alpha_k$, $e^{\alpha\phi}Ke^{-\alpha\phi}=K+E$ with
$\lVert E_{ab}\rVert\le(e^{\alpha d(a,b)}-1)\lVert K_{ab}\rVert$, and
$e^{\alpha r}-1\le(\alpha/\alpha_k)(e^{\alpha_kr}-1)$ by convexity in
$\alpha$; by the Schur test $\lVert E\rVert\le(\alpha/\alpha_k)\,5.44
\Lambda\lambda$. For $\alpha=\alpha_*$, $\lVert K^{-1}E\rVert\le5.44\cdot
1093/11900<\frac12$, and as in Lemma~\ref{lem:combes}
$\lVert e^{\alpha_*\phi}K^{-1}e^{-\alpha_*\phi}\rVert\le2186/\lambda$. With
$\phi=d(\cdot,b)$ every block of $K^{-1}$ satisfies $\lVert(K^{-1})_{ab}
\rVert\le(2186/\lambda)e^{-\alpha_*d(a,b)}$. If $K(x,y)=(f,0)$, then $x\in
\ker B$ and $H_kx-f\perp\ker B$, so $\mathcal C_k$ is the upper left block
of $K^{-1}$. If $K(x,y)=(0,sw)$, then $Bx=w$ and $H_kx+sB^\top y=0$, the
Lagrange condition of the minimum, which is unique by (i); so $\mathcal T_k=
s(K^{-1})_{12}$, and $H_k(x)=-s\langle Bx,y\rangle=-s^2\langle w,(K^{-1})_
{22}w\rangle$, that is, $\mathcal M_kH_k=-s^2(K^{-1})_{22}$. The three
bounds follow, with $d=2d_{k+1}$ between coarse links.

(iii) By (ii) and Lemma~\ref{lem:weightedcount} with $u=\alpha_*\le1$,
\begin{align*}
\Bigl\lVert\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k\Bigr\rVert_{(
\alpha_*)}&\le2186\Lambda_k^2\lambda_{k+1}\sup_i\sum_je^{-\alpha_*d_{k+1}(
i,j)}\\
&\le2186\cdot2532\,\Lambda_k^2\alpha_*^{-4}\lambda_{k+1},
\end{align*}
which is the bound, and restriction to $\mathcal X_{k+1}$ does not increase
it. Adding $D_k$ gives (H2$^*$) at scale $k+1$.

(iv) The infimum of a sum is at least the sum of the infima, and
$\inf\{|x|^2:Bx=w\}=\langle w,(BB^\top)^{-1}w\rangle\ge4|w|^2$ because
$BB^\top\le\frac14$. This is Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth} at
$\kappa=0$.
\end{proof}

For $k<K$ write $D_k=H_{k+1}-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_k
H_k|_{\mathcal X_{k+1}}$ for the error of the step $k$, and consider the
single condition on these errors
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{one-step error, relative and local:} for every $k<K$,
\[
-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k^{\vphantom1}}\frac{\mathcal M_kH_k}{
\lambda_{k+1}^2}\le D_k\le\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\frac{\mathcal M_k
H_k}{\lambda_{k+1}^2}\quad\text{on }\mathcal X_{k+1},
\]
and $\lVert D_k\rVert_{(\alpha_{k+1})}\le\delta_k\lambda_{k+1}$ for some
$\delta_k\ge0$.
\end{enumerate}
It is (H1) with $\varepsilon_k=\lambda_{k+1}^{-2}$ together with (D); both
concern one integration only.

\begin{theorem}[the induction over scales under one condition]
\label{thm:allscales}
Let $L/2^K\ge4$, $\lambda_K\ge32$, $0<\alpha_0\le1$, $\Lambda_0=12+36e^{
\alpha_0}$, and define recursively $\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k/(11900\Lambda_k)$
and $\Lambda_{k+1}=C_*\Lambda_k^6\alpha_k^{-4}+\delta_k$, with $C_*$ as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(iii). For $k\le K$ let $P_k$ be the
conjunction of
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $(1-\sigma_k)R_k\le H_k\le e^{\sigma_k}R_k$, where $\sigma_k=\sum_{j<
k}\lambda_{j+1}^{-2}$;
\item if $k<K$, $H_k(x)\ge\lambda_k|x|^2/52$ on $\ker B_k\cap\mathcal X_k$;
\item (H2$^*$) at scale $k$ with $(\alpha_k,\Lambda_k)$, and, if $k<K$, the
bounds of Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(ii) for the fibre covariance,
the minimiser map and the block infimum.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $P_0$ holds, and for every $k<K$, $P_k$ and (C) at the step $k$
imply $P_{k+1}$. No other hypothesis enters.
\item Hence under (C), $P_k$ holds for every $k\le K$, with $\sigma_k\le
0.4865$, so $\frac12R_k\le H_k\le1.65\,R_k$; the bounds of (a) and (b) are
uniform in $\lambda_0$, $K$ and $L$, and those of (c) are uniform in $L$.
\item The reference chain $H_k=R_k$ satisfies (C) with $D_k=0$, so $P_k$
holds for it for every $k$, unconditionally.
\item The constants of (c) are not bounded in $k$: $\Lambda_k\ge48^{6^k}$
and $\alpha_{k+1}\le\alpha_k/(5.7\cdot10^5)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) $P_0$: $H_0=R_0$, Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(i) at $k=0$, and
the computation after (D). Let $P_k$ and (C) at the step $k$ hold. By the
first half of (C), (H1) holds at the step $k$ with $\varepsilon_k=\lambda_{
k+1}^{-2}<1$; as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(a), $\mathcal
M_k$ is monotone and positively homogeneous, so (a) at $k$ gives $(1-\sigma
_k)(1-\varepsilon_k)R_{k+1}\le H_{k+1}\le e^{\sigma_k}(1+\varepsilon_k)R_{
k+1}$, which is (a) at $k+1$ since $(1-\sigma_k)(1-\varepsilon_k)\ge1-
\sigma_{k+1}$. The bound $\sigma_{k+1}\le\sigma_K\le0.4865$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(b) with $c_\varepsilon=1$ and $\lambda_K\ge32$,
and Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(i), give (b) at $k+1$. The bounds of
(c) at $k$ are Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(ii), from (b) and (H2$^*
$) at $k$, and (H2$^*$) at $k+1$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(iii)
with the second half of (C). (ii) Induction with (i); $1-0.4865\ge\frac12$
and $e^{0.4865}\le1.65$. (iii) $R_{k+1}=\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}
\mathcal M_kR_k$ by definition. (iv) $\Lambda_0\ge48$, $C_*\ge1$ and
$\alpha_k\le1$ give $\Lambda_{k+1}\ge\Lambda_k^6$, and $11900\cdot48>5.7
\cdot10^5$.
\end{proof}

Hypothesis (H2) is not used, and by Proposition~\ref{prop:h2volume} it does
not hold with $G_k$ and $\ell_k$ independent of $L$. The large-field cost
(H3) is independent of (C): it concerns the values of the action far from
the background, which no bound on Hessians at the background controls, and
the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(d) uses (H3) alone, so that part
holds at every step at which (H3) holds. The theorem is the induction that
the present estimates support: the relative comparison and the fibre gap
pass from step $k$ to step $k+1$ with constants independent of $k$, and the
locality of the fibre passes with constants that grow faster than any
exponential. The decay length of the fibre covariance at scale $k$,
$\alpha_k^{-1}$ in units of $2^k$, is more than $(5.7\cdot10^5)^k$ in those
units, so the bound of (c) says nothing beyond the first steps at any
volume. A bound uniform in $k$ cannot come from
Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(ii), (iii) alone, which use only the
size of $H_k$ and its gap, and by part (iv) of that proposition a
comparison of $H_k$ with the uniformly local reference $R_k$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:effectivelocal}) in an absolute weighted norm loses a
factor of at least four per step. Condition (C) is not proved for any $k$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:iteratestatus}(i), Remark~\ref{rem:relstepinputs}).

\begin{proposition}[the count of scales]\label{prop:scalecount}
Along the one-loop running $\lambda_k=\lambda_0-tk$, with $\beta=4\lambda$
and $b=11/(3\pi^2)$, so that $4t=b\log2$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The hypothesis $\lambda_K\ge32$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}
allows $K=\lfloor(\lambda_0-32)/t\rfloor$ steps, which is unbounded as
$\lambda_0\to\infty$; under (C) the bounds (a) and (b) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales} hold uniformly over all of them.
\item The large-field estimates of Sec.~\ref{ssec:lfstep}, in the form
proved at the first step (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm},
Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}), give no activity bound at a coupling
$\lambda\le809300$, so at most the steps with $\lambda_k>809300$ can
receive (H3) from them. At least $(809300-\lambda_K)/t-1$ steps $k<K$ have
$\lambda_k\le809300$, more than $1.257\cdot10^7$ when $\lambda_K\le1$,
whatever $\lambda_0$. The lattice spacing at the last scale with
$\lambda_k>809300$ is less than $e^{-8.713\cdot10^6}$ times the spacing of
the scale at which $\lambda_k$ reaches one.
\item The islands of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandscales} at the Wilson coupling
$\beta_W=4\lambda_0$ are controlled at the scales $j\le j_{\max}$, and if
$j_{\max}\ge1$ then $j_{\max}\le1+\log_{16}(\beta_W/(2.895\cdot10^{23}))$,
while the running from $\beta_W$ to $\beta=4$ has $(\beta_W-4)/(b\log2)$
steps.
\item Under (H1) with $\varepsilon_k\le\lambda_{k+1}^{-2}$ and $\lambda_K
\ge32$, the ratio of the upper to the lower comparison constant of $H_k$
with $R_k$ is at most $3.3$ for every $k$, and on $\Z^4$, $2\lambda_kQ_k\le
R_k\le512\lambda_kQ_k$ for every $k$. The factor four of
Theorem~\ref{thm:stepsharp} enters $R_k$ once and does not compound.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) $\lambda_K=\lambda_0-tK\ge32$ if and only if $K\le(\lambda_0-32)/t$.
(ii) By Proposition~\ref{prop:iteratestatus}(iv), for every $\kappa<
\kappa_c$ the rates satisfy $a(\lambda,\kappa)<9$ and $a_2(\lambda,\kappa)<
9$ for $100\le\lambda\le809300$, and the estimates require $\lambda\ge100$.
The steps $k<K$ with $\lambda_k\le809300$ are those with $(\lambda_0-809300)
/t\le k\le K-1$, and $K=(\lambda_0-\lambda_K)/t$; the bound $(809300-1)/t>
1.257\cdot10^7$ is in Proposition~\ref{prop:iteratestatus}(iv). With the
same count for the coupling $\lambda_{k+1}$ of the step, the conclusion is
unchanged. One step doubles the spacing, and $k$ steps lower $\beta$ by
$bk\log2$; so between $\beta=4\cdot809300=3237200$ and $\beta=4$ the spacing
grows by $2^{(3237200-4)/(b\log2)}=e^{(3237200-4)/b}$, and $b\le0.371512$
gives $(3237200-4)/b>8.713\cdot10^6$.
(iii) $\beta^*_{j+1}>16\beta^*_j$ and $\beta^*_1\ge2.895\cdot10^{23}$ give
$\beta^*_j\ge16^{j-1}\cdot2.895\cdot10^{23}$, and $\beta_W\ge\beta^*_{j_{\max}}
$. The count of steps is (i) with $\lambda_K=1$ and $t=b\log2/4$.
(iv) Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}(ii) gives the constants $\frac12$ and
$1.65$, whose ratio is $3.3$. The second statement is
Theorem~\ref{thm:effectiveupper} and $R_k=2\lambda_kS_k$. The reference is
built from infima, $R_{k+1}=\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kR_k$,
and not from a comparison with $\lambda_kQ_k$ at each step.
\end{proof}

Fig.~\ref{fig:induction} draws the induction and the growth of its constants.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig_induction.png}
\caption{The induction over scales of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}, schematic in
(a). (a)~The tori of the scales $k=0,\dots,4$, the statement $P_k$ on each
and the condition~(C) on each step; the couplings $\lambda_k$ are at least
$809300$ on the blue tori and below it on the red ones, and along the
one-loop running more than $1.257\cdot10^7$ steps lie between $809300$ and
$1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:iteratestatus}). (b)~The lower bound
$\Lambda_k\ge48^{6^k}$ on the constants of the induction, as
$\log_{10}\log_{10}$, against the bound $\sigma_k\le0.4865$, which holds
for every $k$.}
\label{fig:induction}
\end{figure*}

\begin{remark}[how the constants evolve]\label{rem:allscalesconstants}
Along the induction of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item the coupling decreases by $t$ per step; the number of steps is
unbounded as $\lambda_0\to\infty$, and nothing in $P_k$ requires it to
be bounded;
\item the summed relative error $\sigma$ is at most $\lambda_K^{-2}+1/(t
\lambda_K)$ for errors $\varepsilon_k\le\lambda_{k+1}^{-2}$, uniformly in
$\lambda_0$; errors $\varepsilon_k\ge c\lambda_{k+1}^{-1}$ give $\sigma\ge
(c/t)\log(\lambda_0/\lambda_K)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(b)), so
one-step errors of order $g^2$ do not close;
\item the comparison constants of $H_k$ with $R_k$ stay in $[\frac12,1.65]$
and the fibre gap stays $\lambda_k/52$; the lower constant $1/2956$ and the
factors $\theta(\kappa_0)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:stepconstants} concern the
coarse action $A_1$, not $H_k$, and their products over the steps tend to
zero (Remark~\ref{rem:iteratelinear});
\item the locality constants obey $\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k/(11900\Lambda_k)$
and $\Lambda_{k+1}=C_*\Lambda_k^6\alpha_k^{-4}+\delta_k$ and are unbounded;
an absolute weighted bound on $H_k-R_k$ grows by a factor of at least four
per step (Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(iv)), as in
Remark~\ref{rem:relscales};
\item the large-field input fails first: with the first-step estimates it
stops at $\lambda=809300$, more than $1.257\cdot10^7$ steps above coupling
one (Proposition~\ref{prop:scalecount}(ii));
\item the island thresholds grow by a factor of more than $16$ per scale, so
the islands are controlled on $O(\log\beta_W)$ of the
$(\beta_W-4)/(b\log2)$ scales;
\item at a curved background, outside the setting of this subsection, the
one-step factor of a plaquette remainder is $1+130\lVert\kappa^{(j)}
\rVert_2$ at scale $j$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}(iii)), and the
product over the scales is bounded exactly when $\sum_j\lVert\kappa^{(j)}
\rVert_2<\infty$ (Remark~\ref{rem:actioniteration}); on calm windows at the
levels $K_j$ this holds if $\sum_jK_j<\infty$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:actioncalm}).
Levels $K_j\le c\lambda_{j+1}^{-2}$ have $\sum_jK_j\le c(\lambda_K^{-2}+1/(t
\lambda_K))$, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate}(b). Levels $K_j\ge c\lambda_
{j+1}^{-1/2}$, the order of the calm thresholds that the large-field rate
condition requires (Remark~\ref{rem:iteratelinear}), have $\sum_{j<K}K_j\ge
(2c/t)(\lambda_0^{1/2}-\lambda_K^{1/2})$, since $t\lambda_{j+1}^{-1/2}\ge
\int_{\lambda_{j+1}}^{\lambda_j}\lambda^{-1/2}d\lambda$; then the
sufficient condition of Remark~\ref{rem:actioniteration} fails as $\lambda_0
\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
So the induction step is proved, and the induction closes over all scales
under the one condition (C): uniformly in $\lambda_0$ for the relative
comparison and the fibre gap, and with constants growing in $k$ for
locality. The first open input on the way is (C) at $k=0$. The large-field
cost is a separate input, and the estimates proved for it at the first
step give nothing at $\lambda_k\le809300$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Gauge-invariant local remainders}\label{ssec:localrem}

The factor $C_n$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} and the loss $\kappa
n^2$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops} come from the gap of the whole
window off its gauge directions. The inverse of the gauge-fixed form of
the window does not decay uniformly in $n$: by
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iv) its norm is at least $C_n^-$, so by the
Schur test and Lemma~\ref{lem:weightedcount} no bound $Ce^{-\alpha d(a,b)}$
on its blocks holds with $C$ and $\alpha$ independent of $n$, and on the
torus Proposition~\ref{prop:h2volume} gives the same. What decays
uniformly is the covariance of the fibre
(Proposition~\ref{prop:fibreinherit}(ii)), and it makes the terms of an
induced action local. This subsection shows that locality removes $C_n$
when each local term is gauge invariant on a box of its own: the gap of
that box replaces the gap of the window. It also shows that the hypothesis
(H), stated for the chart density, is incompatible with a local invariant
density on large windows, that at curved backgrounds the loss is of order
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ for every local remainder and not of order
$\kappa$ uniformly in $n$, and that condition (C) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales} follows from such a representation of the
one-step error. Gauge-invariant localised effective actions of this kind
are what the cluster expansions of Ba{\l}aban~\cite{Bal87,Bal88} produce
for his averaging operations; for the cut-off averages they are a
hypothesis here.

\emph{Setting.} Let $G\subset\U(N)$ be compact and connected, with a Lie
algebra $\g$ of trivial centre, such as $\SU(N)$, with $\ip XY=-\Tr(XY)$
on $\g$ and operator norms for matrices in $\U(N)$, as in the curved part
of Sec.~\ref{ssec:relstep}. A \emph{box} $X$ of side $r\ge1$ is the set of
sites $\prod_\nu[b_\nu,b_\nu+r]$ of the coarse lattice, which is $\Z^4$ or
a torus of side at least $r+2$. Let $L_X$ be its links, those with both
ends in $X$, $P_X$ its plaquettes, those with all four corners in $X$, and
$\ell_X=\lvert L_X\rvert=4r(r+1)^3$. A \emph{local term} on $X$ is a $C^2$
function $f$ of the links of $X$ with $f(gV)=f(V)$ for every $g\in G^X$,
where $(gV)_{y,\mu}=g_yV_{y,\mu}g_{y+e_\mu}^{-1}$. A \emph{local
remainder} is a sum $R=\sum_{X\in\mathcal X}f_X$ over a family of boxes,
repetitions allowed, with $f_X$ a local term on $X$, whose series
converges with its first two derivatives near the background. For $V\in
G^{L_X}$, $\Hess f(V)$ is the Hessian at $0$ of $\omega\mapsto f(Ve^\omega)$
on $\g^{L_X}$, and $h_X=\lVert\Hess f_X(I)\rVert$ is its norm at the
trivial field, which depends on $f_X$ alone. For a background $V_0$ and
$w\in\g^K$, extended by zero off $K$, put $Q_X^{V_0}(w)=\sum_{p\in
P_X}\lVert Z_p(w)\rVert^2$, so that $\sum_XQ_X^{V_0}$ counts each
plaquette of $Q^{V_0}$ once for every box that contains it. Put
\[
\rho_r=\frac1{4\sin^2(\pi/(2r+2))}\le\frac{(r+1)^2}4 .
\]

\begin{lemma}[a box with every site gauged]\label{lem:boxgap}
Let $X$ be a box of side $r$ and $(d_X\eta)_{y,\mu}=\eta_y-\eta_{y+e_\mu}$
for $\eta\in\g^X$. If $u\in\g^{L_X}$ is orthogonal to $d_X(\g^X)$, then
\[
\lvert u\rvert^2\le\rho_r\sum_{p\in P_X}\lVert(du)_p\rVert^2 ,
\]
where $(du)_p=u_{k_1}+u_{k_2}-u_{k_3}-u_{k_4}$ for $p$ with links
$k_1,\dots,k_4$ in the order of Sec.~\ref{ssec:relstep}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Componentwise in an orthonormal basis of $\g$ it suffices to treat real
fields. The cochain complex of $X$ in degrees $0,1,2$, with the sites,
links and plaquettes of $X$ as cells and the coboundaries $d_X$ and $d$,
is the fourfold tensor product of the complex of the path $[0,r]$, in
which $C^0=\R^{r+1}$, $C^1=\R^r$ and $d$ is the difference operator; the
orientations of the cells change only signs, which do not change norms.
With the product inner products the Laplacian $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ of the
product is the sum of the Laplacians of the factors, as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(ii). On $C^0$, $d^*d$ is the Laplacian of the
path with $r+1$ vertices, with eigenvalues $4\sin^2(\pi j/(2r+2))$ for
$0\le j\le r$. Since $d$ maps $C^0$ onto $C^1$, $dd^*$ is invertible on
$C^1$, with the nonzero eigenvalues of $d^*d$, the least being $\rho_r^{-1}$.
A $1$-cochain of the product is a sum of tensors with exactly one factor of
degree one, so $\Delta_1\ge\rho_r^{-1}$. If $u\perp d_X(C^0)$, then
$d_X^*u=0$ and $\sum_p(du)_p^2=\ip u{\Delta_1u}\ge\rho_r^{-1}\lvert u
\rvert^2$. Finally $\sin x\ge2x/\pi$ on $[0,\pi/2]$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[a local term at a flat background]\label{lem:flatterm}
Let $f$ be a local term on a box $X$ of side $r$, and let $V_0\in G^{L_X}$
have $V_{0,p}=I$ for every $p\in P_X$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item the gradient of $\omega\mapsto f(V_0e^\omega)$ vanishes at $0$;
\item $\Hess f(V_0)[w,d^X_{V_0}\eta]=0$ for every $w\in\g^{L_X}$ and
$\eta\in\g^X$, where $(d^X_{V_0}\eta)_{y,\mu}=\operatorname{Ad}(V_{0,y,
\mu}^{-1})\eta_y-\eta_{y+e_\mu}$;
\item $\lVert\Hess f(V_0)\rVert=\lVert\Hess f(I)\rVert$, and for every
$w\in\g^{L_X}$
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess f(V_0)[w,w]\bigr\rvert\le\lVert\Hess f(I)\rVert\,\rho_r\,
Q_X^{V_0}(w).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv}, the links $(x,\mu)$ of $X$
with $x_\nu=b_\nu$ for every $\nu<\mu$ form a spanning tree, and some
$g\in G^X$ has $gV_0=I$ on it. For another link $(x,\mu)$ let $\nu<\mu$ be
the least direction with $x_\nu>b_\nu$; the plaquette in the plane
$\{\nu,\mu\}$ at $x-e_\nu$ lies in $P_X$ and its two links of direction
$\nu$ lie in the tree, so its holonomy $I$ gives $(gV_0)_{x,\mu}=(gV_0)_{
x-e_\nu,\mu}$, and induction gives $gV_0=I$ on $L_X$. With $(Tw)_{y,\mu}=
\operatorname{Ad}(g_{y+e_\mu})w_{y,\mu}$, an isometry, $(gV_0)e^{Tw}=g(V_0
e^w)$, so $f(gV_0e^{T\omega})=f(V_0e^\omega)$, $Q^{gV_0}_X(Tw)=Q^{V_0}_X
(w)$ and $Td^X_{V_0}\eta=d^X_{gV_0}(\operatorname{Ad}(g)\eta)$, as in that
proof. So it suffices to take $V_0=I$, where $d^X_I=d_X$.

(i) A constant $h\in G$ acts by $e^\omega\mapsto e^{\operatorname{Ad}(h)
\omega}$, so the gradient $(\nabla_kf(0))_k$ is fixed by every
$\operatorname{Ad}(h)$, hence commutes with $\g$ and lies in the centre of
$\g$, which is $0$. (ii) The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(i),
with $\Gamma_W$ replaced by $G^X$ and $K$ by $L_X$, gives $\Hess f(0)[w,
d_X\eta]=-Df(0)[D\zeta(0)w]$, which vanishes by (i). (iii) The first
statement is the transport above. By (ii) the symmetric form $\Hess f(0)$
vanishes on $d_X(\g^X)$ in each argument, so $\Hess f(0)[w,w]=\Hess f(0)
[u,u]$ for the orthogonal projection $u$ of $w$ off $d_X(\g^X)$, which is
at most $\lVert\Hess f(0)\rVert\lvert u\rvert^2$. Lemma~\ref{lem:boxgap}
and $du=dw$, since the curvature of $d_X\eta$ vanishes, bound
$\lvert u\rvert^2$ by $\rho_r\sum_{p\in P_X}\lVert(dw)_p\rVert^2$, and at
$V_0=I$, $Z_p(w)=(dw)_p$ by~\eqref{eq:pathexp}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[local remainders at flat backgrounds]\label{thm:localflat}
Let $R=\sum_{X\in\mathcal X}f_X$ be a local remainder, let $V_0$ be flat on
every plaquette of every box of $\mathcal X$, the links off $K$ included,
and put
\[
\mathcal L_0=\sup_p\sum_{X:\,p\in P_X}h_X\rho_{r_X}.
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\lvert\Hess R(V_0)[w,w]\rvert\le\mathcal L_0\,Q^{V_0}(w)$ for every
$w\in\g^K$, on the window and, with all links variable, on $\Z^4$ or on a
torus.
\item On the window, $R$ is $\Gamma_W$-invariant and $\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)
\rvert\le\mathcal L_0\,Q^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}w)$. At $V_0=I$ this is at most
$\mathcal L_0Q_1(w)\le(\mathcal L_0/c_*)\,S_W(w)$, for every $n$.
\item If each box carries at most one term and $h_X\le\eta e^{-\alpha r_X}$
with $\eta,\alpha>0$, then $\mathcal L_0\le180\,e^\alpha\eta\,(1-e^{-\alpha}
)^{-7}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) The Hessian of the series is the series of the Hessians. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:flatterm}(iii), applied to the restriction of $w$ to $L_X$,
\begin{align*}
\lvert\Hess R(V_0)[w,w]\rvert&\le\sum_Xh_X\rho_{r_X}\sum_{p\in P_X}\lVert
Z_p(w)\rVert^2\\
&=\sum_p\lVert Z_p(w)\rVert^2\sum_{X:\,p\in P_X}h_X\rho_{r_X},
\end{align*}
which is at most $\mathcal L_0Q^{V_0}(w)$.

(ii) An element of $\Gamma_W$ fixes the links off $K$ and acts on the links
of $X$ through its restriction to the sites of $X$, an element of $G^X$; so
every $f_X$, and $R$, is $\Gamma_W$-invariant.
Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii) gives $\mathcal HR(w,w)=\Hess R(V_0)
[\Pi_{V_0}w,\Pi_{V_0}w]$, and (i) applies. At $V_0=I$, $Q^I=Q_1$ vanishes
on $\mathcal O$ and is positive semidefinite, so $Q_1(\Pi w)=Q_1(w)$, and
$Q_1\le S_W/c_*$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iii).

(iii) A plaquette in the plane $\{\mu,\nu\}$ at $x$ lies in the box of side
$r$ with corner $b$ only if $b_\mu\in[x_\mu-r+1,x_\mu]$, $b_\nu\in[x_\nu-r
+1,x_\nu]$ and $b_\lambda\in[x_\lambda-r,x_\lambda]$ for the two other
directions, so in at most $r^2(r+1)^2$ boxes of side $r$. Hence
$\mathcal L_0\le\frac\eta4\sum_{r\ge1}(r+1)^6e^{-\alpha r}$. Since $m^6\le
720\binom{m+6}6$ and $\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{m+6}6x^m=(1-x)^{-7}$,
$\sum_{r\ge1}(r+1)^6e^{-\alpha r}\le e^\alpha\sum_{m\ge0}m^6e^{-\alpha m}\le
720\,e^\alpha(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-7}$.
\end{proof}

The bound holds for every local term; for the filled loops of
Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops} the factor $\rho_r$ is not needed, since
their Hessian at a flat background is already a form in the curvatures.
At the trivial background it gives the one-step bound of
Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} without $C_n$, once the hypothesis is put on
the gauge-invariant density.

\begin{corollary}[one step with a local invariant remainder]
\label{cor:localstep}
Let $U=I$, so that $V_0=I$, and let $A^{\rm gi}=A_0+R$ near $I$, where $A_0$
is $\Gamma_W$-invariant with $\mathcal HA_0=2\lambda S_W$ and $R$ is a
local remainder with $\mathcal L_0\le\lambda\varepsilon$. Then the error
$E=\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}-2\lambda S_W$ vanishes on $\g^K\times\mathcal O$ and
\[
\lvert E(w,w)\rvert\le\lambda\varepsilon\,Q_1(w)\le\frac\varepsilon{2c_*}
\cdot2\lambda S_W(w)\qquad(w\in\g^K),
\]
so that $(1-\frac\varepsilon{2c_*})2\lambda S_W\le\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}\le
(1+\frac\varepsilon{2c_*})2\lambda S_W$ for every $n$, with $\frac1{2c_*}<
3.433$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii) the covariant Hessian is linear in
the function, so $E=\mathcal HR$. It vanishes on $\g^K\times\mathcal O$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:invariantslice}(ii), and Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}(ii)
bounds it. The constant follows from $2c_*>0.29131$, as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep}.
\end{proof}

The factor $C_n$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} and of
Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep} therefore comes from the form of the
hypothesis. Hypothesis (H) bounds the Hessian of the chart density $A$,
which differs from the invariant density $A^{\rm gi}$, the density with
respect to Haar measure, by the Haar term. The two cannot both be local on
a large window unless the error in (H) is of order $g^2$.

\begin{proposition}[the chart hypothesis against locality]
\label{prop:chartlocal}
Let $G=\SU(2)$ and $U=I$. Suppose that $A^{\rm gi}=A_0+R$ as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:localstep}, with constant $\mathcal L_0$, and that the
chart density $A$ satisfies the upper half of (H): $\Hess A(0)[\sigma,
\sigma]\le2\lambda S_W(\sigma)+\lambda\varepsilon\lvert\sigma\rvert^2$ for
$\sigma\in\mathcal O^\perp$. Then
\[
\lambda\varepsilon\ge\frac13-\frac{\mathcal L_0}{C_n^-}\ge\frac13-\frac{3
\pi^2\mathcal L_0}{(n+1)^2}.
\]
In particular $\lambda\varepsilon\ge\frac16$ on every window with
$(n+1)^2\ge18\pi^2\mathcal L_0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On the slice $A^{\rm gi}(\Upsilon(s,\eta))=A(s)+\sum_k\log j(s_k)$, so, as
in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep}(ii),
\[
\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}(w,w)=\Hess A(0)[\Pi w,\Pi w]+\frac1{12}\sum_k\Tr
\bigl(\operatorname{ad}_{(\Pi w)_k}^2\bigr),
\]
and the last sum is $-\frac13\lvert\Pi w\rvert^2$ for $\SU(2)$.
Let $w\ne0$ be the field of Lemma~\ref{lem:windowgap}(iv), with $w\in
\mathcal O^\perp$, so $\Pi w=w$, and $\lvert w\rvert^2=C_n^-Q_1(w)$. The
hypothesis gives $\mathcal HA^{\rm gi}(w,w)-2\lambda S_W(w)\le(\lambda
\varepsilon-\frac13)\lvert w\rvert^2$, and Corollary~\ref{cor:localstep}
gives that this difference is at least $-\mathcal L_0Q_1(w)=-\mathcal L_0
\lvert w\rvert^2/C_n^-$. Divide by $\lvert w\rvert^2$ and use $C_n^-\ge
(n+1)^2/(3\pi^2)$.
\end{proof}

An error of order $g^2=1/\lambda$ in each step is not summable over the
scales (Remark~\ref{rem:relscales}). The measure defines the invariant
density, and the localised actions of Ba{\l}aban are invariant; so the
hypothesis belongs on $A^{\rm gi}$, and in that form the Haar term does not
appear.

\emph{Curved backgrounds.} At a background that is not flat on a box, a
local term has a gradient there, and Lemma~\ref{lem:flatterm} fails. The
term is compared with its value at the trivial field after a gauge
transformation of the box, which costs a Euclidean term proportional to the
curvature in the box, and the Euclidean term is paid with the $\ell^4$
bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:windowlfour}. The following lemma gives the
constants from bounds on complex neighbourhoods, the form in which
cluster expansions bound their terms.

\begin{lemma}[derivatives from analytic bounds]\label{lem:cauchy}
Let $f$ be a function of the links of a finite set $L$, $a\ge0$ and
$\rho>0$; $\g\otimes\C$ carries the Hermitian extension of the norm, and
$e^\xi e^\omega$ is the product link by link.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $\omega\mapsto f(e^\omega)$ extends holomorphically to
$\{\omega\in(\g\otimes\C)^L:\lVert\omega_k\rVert<\rho\ \forall k\}$ with
modulus at most $a$, then $\lVert\Hess f(I)\rVert\le2a/\rho^2$.
\item If the function $(\xi,\omega)\mapsto f(e^\xi e^\omega)$ extends
holomorphically to the set where $\lVert\xi_k\rVert<\rho$ and $\lVert
\omega_k\rVert<\rho$ for every $k$, with modulus at most $a$, then for
every $v\in\g^L$ and $V=e^\xi$ with $\xi\in\g^L$ and $\delta=\max_k\lVert
\xi_k\rVert\le\rho/2$,
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess f(V)[v,v]-\Hess f(I)[v,v]\bigr\rvert\le\frac{4a\delta}
{\rho^3}\lvert v\rvert^2 .
\]
\item If $G=\SU(N)$ and $\lVert I-V\rVert\le\min(1,3/N)$, then $V=e^\xi$
with $\xi\in\g$ and $\lVert\xi\rVert\le\frac\pi3\sqrt N\,\lVert I-V
\rVert$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) For $v\in\g^L$, $v\ne0$, let $m=\max_k\lVert v_k\rVert$. The function
$z\mapsto f(e^{zv})$ is holomorphic for $\lvert z\rvert<\rho/m$ and bounded
by $a$, and its second derivative at $0$ is $\Hess f(I)[v,v]$, since
$\omega=zv$ is a line. Cauchy's inequality gives $\lvert\Hess f(I)[v,v]
\rvert\le2am^2/\rho^2\le2a\lvert v\rvert^2/\rho^2$.
(ii) Let $G(s,z)=f(e^{s\xi}e^{zv})$, holomorphic for $\lvert s\rvert<\rho/
\delta$ and $\lvert z\rvert<\rho/m$, with $\lvert G\rvert\le a$. Then
$\Hess f(V)[v,v]=\partial_z^2G(1,0)$ and $\Hess f(I)[v,v]=\partial_z^2G
(0,0)$. For $0\le s\le1$ the bidisc about $(s,0)$ with radii $\rho/(2
\delta)\le\rho/\delta-1$ and $\rho/m$ lies in the domain, so Cauchy's
inequality gives $\lvert\partial_s\partial_z^2G(s,0)\rvert\le2a\cdot2\delta
m^2/\rho^3$; integrate over $s\in[0,1]$.
(iii) Let $e^{i\theta_j}$, $\lvert\theta_j\rvert\le\pi$, be the
eigenvalues of $V$. Then $2\lvert\sin(\theta_j/2)\rvert\le\lVert I-V\rVert
\le1$, so $\lvert\theta_j\rvert\le\pi/3$, and $\sin x\ge3x/\pi$ on $[0,
\pi/6]$ gives $\lvert\theta_j\rvert\le\frac\pi3\lVert I-V\rVert$. The
skew-Hermitian $\xi$ with the eigenvalues $i\theta_j$ on the eigenspaces of
$V$ has $e^\xi=V$, and $\sum_j\theta_j\in2\pi\Z$ with $\lvert\sum_j\theta_j
\rvert\le\frac{N\pi}3\lVert I-V\rVert\le\pi$, so $\Tr\xi=0$ and $\xi\in
\g$. Finally $\lVert\xi\rVert^2=\sum_j\theta_j^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[local remainders at curved backgrounds]\label{thm:localcurved}
Let $R=\sum_{X\in\mathcal X}f_X$ be a local remainder near $V_0\in G^K$,
the links off $K$ given, every box of $\mathcal X$ containing a link of
$K$. Let $\kappa_p=\lVert I-V_{0,p}\rVert$, $\kappa_X=\max_{p\in P_X}
\kappa_p$ and $\delta_X=3r_X\kappa_X$, and suppose:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le\frac19$, with $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:windowlfour};
\item for every $X$ there is $t_X\ge0$ with
\[
\bigl\lvert\Hess f_X(V)[v,v]-\Hess f_X(I)[v,v]\bigr\rvert\le t_X\max_{k\in
L_X}\lVert I-V_k\rVert\,\lvert v\rvert^2
\]
whenever $\max_{k\in L_X}\lVert I-V_k\rVert\le\delta_X$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\rho_X=\rho_{r_X}$, $b_X=3r_X\bigl(h_X\rho_X(\sqrt{432}+432\delta_X)
+t_X\bigr)$,
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathcal L_\kappa=\sup_p\sum_{X:\,p\in P_X}h_X\rho_X\bigl(1+\sqrt{432}\,
\delta_X\bigr),\\
B_1=\sup_{k\in K}\sum_{X:\,k\in L_X}b_X,\qquad B_2=\sup_p\sum_{X:\,p\in
P_X}b_X\ell_X,
\end{gathered}
\]
and $\kappa_*=(\sum_p\kappa_p^2)^{1/2}$, the sum over the plaquettes of the
boxes of $\mathcal X$. Then for every $w\in\g^K$
\[
\lvert\mathcal HR(w,w)\rvert\le\bigl(\mathcal L_\kappa+c_4(B_1B_2)^{1/2}
\kappa_*\bigr)\,Q^{V_0}(\Pi_{V_0}w).
\]
None of the constants depends on $n$. If $V_0$ is flat on the boxes, the
factor is $\mathcal L_0$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}. Under the
hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:cauchy}\textup{(ii)}, \textup{(iii)} for $f_X$,
with constants $a_X,\rho$, hypothesis~\textup{(b)} holds with $t_X=\frac{4
\pi\sqrt N}3a_X\rho^{-3}$ when $\delta_X\le\min(1,\frac3N,\frac{3\rho}{2\pi
\sqrt N})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $u=\Pi_{V_0}w$ and $\lvert u_X\rvert^2=\sum_{k\in L_X}\lVert u_k
\rVert^2$, with $u=0$ off $K$. As in Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}(ii), $R$
is $\Gamma_W$-invariant and $\mathcal HR(w,w)=\sum_X\Hess f_X(V_0)[u,u]$.

Fix $X$. The tree argument in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv},
carried out in $X$, where $\sum_{\nu<\mu}(x_\nu-b_\nu)\le3r_X$ for every
link $(x,\mu)$ of $X$ and every plaquette used lies in $P_X$, gives
$g\in G^X$ with $\lVert I-(gV_0)_k\rVert\le\delta_X$ for every $k\in L_X$.
With $V'=gV_0$ and $v=Tu$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:flatterm},
$\Hess f_X(V_0)[u,u]=\Hess f_X(V')[v,v]$, $\lvert v\rvert=\lvert u_X
\rvert$ and $Q_X^{V'}(v)=Q_X^{V_0}(u)$. By (b),
\[
\lvert\Hess f_X(V')[v,v]-\Hess f_X(I)[v,v]\rvert\le t_X\delta_X\lvert u_X
\rvert^2,
\]
and Lemma~\ref{lem:flatterm}(iii) at $I$ gives
\[
\lvert\Hess f_X(I)[v,v]\rvert\le h_X\rho_X\sum_{p\in P_X}\lVert(dv)_p
\rVert^2 .
\]
As in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:smallcurv}, $\lVert Z_p(v)-(dv)_p\rVert\le2\delta_X(3b_1+
2b_2+2b_3+b_4)$ at $V'$, with $b_i$ the norms of $v$ on the links of $p$,
and a link lies in at most six plaquettes, so
\[
\Bigl(\sum_{p\in P_X}\lVert(dv)_p\rVert^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\le Q_X^{V_0}(u)^{1/2}
+\sqrt{432}\,\delta_X\lvert u_X\rvert .
\]
With $(s+t)^2\le(1+\theta)s^2+(1+\theta^{-1})t^2$ at $\theta=\sqrt{432}
\,\delta_X$, and directly if $\delta_X=0$,
\begin{align*}
\lvert\Hess f_X(V_0)[u,u]\rvert&\le h_X\rho_X\bigl(1+\sqrt{432}\,\delta_X
\bigr)Q_X^{V_0}(u)\\
&\quad+b_X\kappa_X\lvert u_X\rvert^2 ,
\end{align*}
since $\delta_X(h_X\rho_X(\sqrt{432}+432\delta_X)+t_X)=b_X\kappa_X$.

Summing over $X$ and exchanging the sums, the first terms give at most
$\mathcal L_\kappa Q^{V_0}(u)$, and the second terms give $\sum_{k\in K}
\beta_k\lVert u_k\rVert^2$ with $\beta_k=\sum_{X:\,k\in L_X}b_X\kappa_X$.
By Cauchy--Schwarz, $\beta_k^2\le B_1\sum_{X:\,k\in L_X}b_X\kappa_X^2$ and
$\kappa_X^2\le\sum_{p\in P_X}\kappa_p^2$, so
\[
\sum_k\beta_k^2\le B_1\sum_Xb_X\ell_X\sum_{p\in P_X}\kappa_p^2\le B_1B_2
\kappa_*^2,
\]
and $\sum_k\beta_k\lVert u_k\rVert^2\le(\sum_k\beta_k^2)^{1/2}\lvert u
\rvert_4^2$. Since $u\in\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$, Lemma~\ref{lem:windowlfour}
and (a) give $\lvert u\rvert_4^2\le c_4Q^{V_0}(u)$. The last statement
follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:cauchy}(ii), (iii): for $\max_k\lVert I-V_k
\rVert=\delta\le\delta_X$, $V=e^\xi$ with $\max_k\lVert\xi_k\rVert\le\frac
\pi3\sqrt N\delta\le\rho/2$.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:localcurved} extends Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}
from loop sums, whose existence for the induced action is open
(Remark~\ref{rem:loopsopen}), to every local remainder, with the same order
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ of the loss. For the plaquette sum that order is
attained (Corollary~\ref{cor:actionsharp}). Measured by the supremum of the
curvature the loss is not of order $\kappa$ uniformly in $n$, even for the
plaquette sum, a local remainder whose terms do not depend on $n$.

\begin{proposition}[no loss of order $\kappa$ uniformly in $n$]
\label{prop:supform}
Let $G=\SU(2)$, $0<\kappa\le0.02$, $n\ge(31/\kappa)^{1/2}$, and let $P$ be
the sum of $s(V_p)$ over the plaquettes with their corners in $\Lambda'$.
There are a background $V_0$ with $\lVert I-V_{0,p}\rVert\le\kappa$ for
every such plaquette and $u\in\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$ with $\mathcal HP
(u,u)<0\le\frac12Q^{V_0}(u)$. Hence a bound
\[
(1-\phi)\,\tfrac12Q^{V_0}\circ\Pi_{V_0}\le\mathcal HP\le(1+\phi)\,\tfrac12
Q^{V_0}\circ\Pi_{V_0},
\]
valid at every background with plaquettes within $\kappa$ of $I$ on windows
of side $n$, requires $\phi>1$; for every $C\le1/\kappa$ none holds with
$\phi=C\kappa$ for all $n$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take $\sin^2\alpha=\kappa/2\le10^{-2}$ and $\varsigma=-1$ in
Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}: the plaquettes in the plane $\{0,1\}$
have $\lVert I-V_{0,p}\rVert=2\sin^2\alpha=\kappa$, the others are flat,
$n\ge(31/0.02)^{1/2}>39$ and $\kappa(n+1)^2>31$, so part (ii) gives $u\in
\mathcal O_{V_0}^\perp$ with $\mathcal HP(u,u)<0$, and $\Pi_{V_0}u=u$. A
lower bound with $\phi\le1$ would give $\mathcal HP(u,u)\ge0$.
\end{proof}

Within $\kappa(n+1)^2\le2$, Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}(i) gives the
lower bound $\phi\ge0.037\,\kappa(n+1)^2$. Since $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2\le
\sqrt6(n+1)(n+2)\kappa_\infty$, the order $\kappa n^2$ in the supremum and
the order $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ in the action are the same estimate; the
action is the measure of the background that does not depend on $n$, and
on the calm windows of Corollary~\ref{cor:actioncalm} it is at most
$39.5K$.

\emph{Condition (C).} At the trivial background on the torus of the next
scale, Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}(i) gives both halves of condition (C)
of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales} from a local representation of the one-step
error.

\begin{corollary}[condition (C) from local terms]\label{cor:localC}
In the setting of Sec.~\ref{ssec:allscales}, let $k<K$ and assume $P_k$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}. Suppose that $D_k$ is the restriction to
$\mathcal X_{k+1}$ of $\Hess R(I)$ for a local remainder $R$ on the torus
of scale $k+1$, all of whose boxes have side at most $n_{k+1}-2$, with
\[
\mathcal L_0\le\frac{1.027}{\lambda_{k+1}},\qquad\Delta=\sup_a\sum_{X:\,a
\in L_X}h_X\ell_Xe^{\alpha_{k+1}r_X}<\infty .
\]
Then condition (C) holds at the step $k$ with $\delta_k=\Delta/
\lambda_{k+1}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}(i) at $V_0=I$, $\lvert D_k(x,x)\rvert\le
\mathcal L_0Q_{k+1}(x)$ for $x\in\mathcal X_{k+1}$. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:effective}(iii), whose bound $S_k\ge Q_k$ holds on
every lattice, $Q_{k+1}\le R_{k+1}/(2\lambda_{k+1})$. By $P_k$(a),
$H_k\ge(1-\sigma_k)R_k$, and $\mathcal M_k$ is monotone and positively
homogeneous, so $(1-\sigma_k)R_{k+1}=(1-\sigma_k)\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}
{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kR_k\le\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k$
on $\mathcal X_{k+1}$. With $\sigma_k\le\sigma_K\le0.4865$, as in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales},
\begin{align*}
\lvert D_k(x,x)\rvert&\le\frac{\mathcal L_0}{2\lambda_{k+1}(1-\sigma_k)}
\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k(x)\\
&\le\frac1{\lambda_{k+1}^2}\frac{\lambda_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\mathcal M_kH_k(x),
\end{align*}
because $2(1-0.4865)=1.027$; this is the first half of (C). The blocks of
$D_k$ are $(D_k)_{ab}=\sum_{X:\,a,b\in L_X}(\Hess f_X(I))_{ab}$, each of
norm at most $h_X$; two links of a box of side $r$ have midpoints at
$\ell^\infty$ distance at most $r$, and a box has $\ell_X$ links, so
$\sum_b\lVert(D_k)_{ab}\rVert e^{\alpha_{k+1}d_{k+1}(a,b)}\le\Delta$, and
restriction to $\mathcal X_{k+1}$ does not increase it.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[what the local form leaves open]\label{rem:localrem}
Four points are not settled by the results above.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item The induced action of the cut-off averages is not shown to be of the
form $A_0+R$ with $R$ a local remainder. By Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss} its
leading term is nonlocal when $(M_W)_{AB}\ne0$, and the theorems above
concern only the remainder; the bound $\mathcal L_0\le1.027/\lambda_{k+1}$
of Corollary~\ref{cor:localC} asks for terms of order $g^4$ relative to the
action, after the order $g^2$ is absorbed into $\lambda_{k+1}$.
\item The large-field estimates of Sec.~\ref{ssec:lfstep} bound the values
of polymer activities on real fields. Lemma~\ref{lem:cauchy} needs bounds
on complex neighbourhoods, and by Remark~\ref{rem:valueshessians}(b) real
bounds on values give no bound on Hessians.
\item Each term of side $r$ costs $\rho_r\le(r+1)^2/4$, the gap of its own
box, so the theorems need $\sum_rr^2(r+1)^4\sup_{r_X=r}h_X<\infty$, which
exponential decay of the terms in their size provides
(Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}(iii)).
\item The locality constants $\Lambda_k$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}
grow with $k$ whatever $\delta_k$ is; Corollary~\ref{cor:localC} does not
change that.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\subsection{What remains}\label{ssec:remains}

The results of this section leave the following statements, which together
with Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} and Sec.~\ref{ssec:coarse} are what the
cube condition (D) needs for $\SU(2)$ past the Dobrushin ceiling.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{The bad side.} For a pair whose non-path links are bad, a bound
on the Kantorovich response of the law of its eight private links, given
the inside links of its two blocks, uniform in the exterior.
Proposition~\ref{prop:fold} shows that the response of the path-link law
alone to its non-path links is infinite, so the non-path links must be
integrated over the bad set; Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly} bounds the response
of that law to every link that enters only the action, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:goodside} settles the good side to radius $1/32$.
The inside links move the fibre $\{V^\sharp_k=c_k\}$ while the bad set
does not; Proposition~\ref{prop:insidefold} shows that the path-link law also jumps
in an inside link. For $\mu=3$ the inside $\mu$-links are tree links and
Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsononly} settles the law of the eight private links;
for $\mu\le2$, Theorem~\ref{thm:eightlinkuniform} shows that its response
to an inside link is not bounded uniformly in the set over which the
non-path links are restricted. In the relative chart of
Lemma~\ref{lem:relchart} the fibre is one graph over the coordinates
$g^{-1}\ell_a$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:relresponse} bounds the response for
the two sets that the labels produce (Proposition~\ref{prop:eightlabels})
under one condition, the continuity in the mean~(J) of the Jacobian of
that chart. Theorem~\ref{thm:jholds} proves (J) when the inside
$\mu$-links of both blocks lie within $\frac1{32}$ of $I$, which includes
every configuration of $B^{\mathrm{bad}}_r$ that the labels produce, with a
constant uniform in the configuration. The constant contains the largest
normalised area of the hypersurfaces where the two paths of one index tie
at the top, which is finite by o-minimality (Proposition~\ref{prop:tiearea})
and not computed; a bound of order $t$ on the Haar measure of the set where
these paths tie at the top within $t$ is false
(Proposition~\ref{prop:thickties}). Condition (J) also holds, and the
response to the inside
$\mu$-links of one block is bounded, when those of the other block equal
$I$. For the first set the chart exists unless both blocks contain an
inside $\mu$-link $u$ with $\lVert\operatorname{Ad}(u)-1\rVert\ge1/\kappa$,
$\kappa<2.2670$, and nothing is proved in that case. The chains of Definition~\ref{def:linechain} carry the inside
links among their variables, partition the bad side, and respond to every
other link with the constants of Theorem~\ref{thm:site} in which $24$ is
replaced by their size $n\le23n_b+1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:linechain});
they cost no collar for $s\ge2$, and for $s=1$ the collar $s=2$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:linechain}). For the projected average $\widehat V$ of
Sec.~\ref{ssec:projected}, a different coarse map whose derivatives of
order at most two agree with those of $V^\sharp$ at every field whose
sixteen paths agree (Proposition~\ref{prop:projavg}), item (i) holds: the
path-link equation has exactly one solution at every field, with Jacobian
in $[\frac1{512},\frac{3375}{512}]$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:projinverse}); the
path-link law responds to the non-path and inside links with the constants
$1$ and $\frac12$, independent of $\beta_W$ and of the size of the links
(Corollary~\ref{cor:projpathlaw}); and the law of the eight private links
restricted to any fixed set of positive Haar measure of the non-path links
responds to an inside link with the constant $24\beta_W+180.5$, with no
hypothesis on the inside links, no lower bound on the measure of the set,
and no condition (J) (Theorem~\ref{thm:projresponse}). The chart decay of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chartdecay} holds for $\widehat V$ with the same
constants (Proposition~\ref{prop:projtransfer}); the route to (D) with
$\widehat V$ is Remark~\ref{rem:projroute}, and the labels, the islands
and the results off the chart are proved for $V^\sharp$ only
(Remark~\ref{rem:projscope}). For $V^\sharp$ item (i) stays as stated
above.
\item \emph{The island comparison.} For two islands in a good region,
Theorem~\ref{thm:factorisation} factorises their weight through one
kernel on the good layer between them, Theorem~\ref{thm:layerbound}
proves the covariance bound~\eqref{eq:layerbound} for the law of that
layer in the coordinates of the labels, and Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}
bounds the cross-ratio by $\varDelta$, exponentially small in the width.
Lemma~\ref{lem:lambdatwo} evaluates the prefactor, $\Lambda_2\le99.0001
\beta_W+4.65\cdot10^6$, so that $\varDelta\le1$ at the threshold needs a good
layer of width at least $99072$. Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands} performs the induction over all the
islands of a window given their labels. Theorem~\ref{thm:islandwindow} gives the smallness of its island sums
and its Dobrushin condition in every window of at most $10^{28000}$
blocks, outside probability $10^{-166}$. With the clusters of Definition~\ref{def:clusters}
as units, Theorem~\ref{thm:clustercomparison} gives these conditions in
every configuration of the labels and every window, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:clustersizes} bounds the size of the clusters block by
block, uniformly in the torus up to $M_1=10^{10^{1700}}$ blocks. No bound on
the size of the clusters of the torus is uniform in the torus: every block
is bad with conditional probability at least $\frac12e^{-12\beta_W}$,
and for every separation rule that bounds the island sums the clusters
percolate on large tori (Corollary~\ref{cor:clusterpercolation},
Proposition~\ref{prop:separationneed}). The clusters of the bad blocks of
a window replace them: the comparison holds with them as units, and in a
window of at most $10^{M_1/2}$ blocks their size is bounded uniformly in
the torus (Lemma~\ref{lem:windowclusters}). Sec.~\ref{ssec:labelcov} bounds the
covariance of the labels with the others averaged, and the covariance of
two local observables under $\mu^c$, in the mean over the coarse field and
on the whole torus: Theorem~\ref{thm:labelcov} improves the trivial bound
$2\epsilon\lvert N_A\rvert\lvert N_B\rvert$ by a factor decaying at the
rate $2\alpha_G$ down to $10^{-7011}$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:fibrecov}
gives decay at the same rate down to $10^{-14062}$, or as $e^{-\sqrt d/2}$.
For a fixed coarse field, Proposition~\ref{prop:fixedgood} gives the same
bounds for every $c$ outside a set of probability at most
$2\lvert\Lambda\rvert\epsilon^{1/2}$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:labelstretched} gives decay as $e^{-\sqrt d/20}$ in
the mean and for these $c$. What is not done is a bound for every coarse field, uniform in the
exterior, and decay at the rate $2\alpha_G$ without a floor. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction} neither follows from rarity and the
group cross-ratios: for laws with only these properties the decay is at
best stretched exponential, and across a component that is bad for every
labelling they bound nothing. In the $\SU(2)$ model,
Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} bounds the constrained law inside such a
component by the chart, at the rate $\alpha_G$ and with no cost in its
length beyond the mass $p$ of that law off the chart, whenever the fibre
has a background with plaquettes below $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$; by
Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart} this holds for coarse plaquettes up to
that size when the exterior agrees with $R(c)$, by
Proposition~\ref{prop:uniformflux} it holds for some exteriors up to
$2.39\cdot10^{-12}$, and no background exists once a coarse plaquette
exceeds $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass} shows that
$p$ tends to one as the component grows at fixed $\beta_W$, so that the
bound improves on the trivial one only for $\beta_W>10^{24}(4.40+\ln
\lvert W\rvert)$. Proposition~\ref{prop:badpassage} identifies the
constrained law, with the links that bind the entering averages moved to
the exterior, as the conditional law under $\mu^c$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:badcrossratio} bounds the cross-ratio of the weight of
the interior for ends that enter the action only, at the rate $\alpha_G$
up to a term $432\beta_W^2\bar p$. Charts local in the component do not
remove the dependence on the length: by Theorem~\ref{thm:localcharts} a
window lies on a chart fixed by its exterior with conditional probability
below $0.033^{\lvert W\rvert}$ for $\beta_W\le10^{24}$, whatever the
exterior and the coarse field. For the coarse fields $c^\theta$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:spread} the exterior $R(c)$ carries a background up
to $2.39\cdot10^{-12}$, and the reduced fibre up to $2.09\cdot10^{-12}$; for
opposite fluxes at adjacent coarse plaquettes no background with values in a
torus exists above $1.8\cdot10^{-12}$, and a general coarse field between
$6.0\cdot10^{-13}$ and $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ with exterior $R(c)$ is not
decided. An end that enters an average enters one pair factor of the fibre
measure (Lemma~\ref{lem:endpairs}), and that factor jumps under arbitrarily
small moves of the end at every value of the coarse link
(Proposition~\ref{prop:endfold}); the bound in the mean over the non-path
links that the labels need is not proved (Remark~\ref{rem:badendsopen}).
Lemma~\ref{lem:mobius} gives the mixed differences of every order in
terms of the diameter; the rate $2\alpha_G$ needs them in terms of the
length of the shortest joining tree (Remark~\ref{rem:fixedcopen}). That
