form is not proved, and it follows neither from the second differences in
every environment (Proposition~\ref{prop:pairsonly}) nor from the layer
bound~\eqref{eq:layerbound} (Proposition~\ref{prop:layerthird});
Remark~\ref{rem:treeform} names the two inputs it needs.
Proposition~\ref{prop:hiddenbit} shows that no rarity bound replaces this
comparison.
\item \emph{The island threshold.} Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold}
gives the explicit coupling $\beta^*(\rho,s)$ past which the islands of
bad blocks at one scale are rare enough to beat their entropy, at the
exponent $1/H$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:coverageopt} and the collar of
Proposition~\ref{prop:graphlaw}. It is of order $10^{13}$ at the witness
radius $10^{-4}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide}, and of order $10^{37}$
under the calmness of Corollary~\ref{cor:twoislands}; the tree count of
Proposition~\ref{prop:treethreshold} lowers it by a factor $1.7$ to $1.8$,
and the union bound over connected sets by at most a further factor $1.39$.
The same statement at the scale of the cube is not given, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:chessceiling} shows that no bound of this kind gives it: at
scale $j$ every witness of a coarse label of radius $\eta<\eta_c$ has
radius at most $1.00015\cdot4^{-j-1}\eta$, by the constant curvature of
Proposition~\ref{prop:constantcurvature}; the normalisation of the
chessboard estimate charges at least $\frac92(\log\beta_W-c_I)$ per fine
site (Lemma~\ref{lem:Zabove}); and so every bound obtained from
Theorem~\ref{thm:defects} or Proposition~\ref{prop:coarsechess} is below one
only at scales whose blocks are smaller than the cube of $D(n,\alpha)$ by a
factor at least $4.08(1-\alpha)^{1/4}$, at every coupling, with the
normalisation of Lemma~\ref{lem:wilsonZ} or, for $\beta_W\ge10^3$, the exact
one. For $\alpha\le\frac12$ and the labels of Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide}
the cube lies at least three dyadic scales higher, and for the calm labels
at least twenty
(Corollary~\ref{cor:chessceiling}). What is missing is a bound on the weight
of the coarse defects relative to $Z_L$ that does not charge the
fluctuation volume of the cube (Remark~\ref{rem:chessceiling}), and (iv)
is needed before any threshold bears on the gap.
\item \emph{The scales.} An effective action at every scale whose
one-step errors are summable in the sense of
Proposition~\ref{prop:formstability} and whose locality norms obey
Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}, down to the last $O(1)$ scales where the running
coupling is of order one; this is the large-field expansion of
Ba{\l}aban, and it is not carried out here. Theorem~\ref{thm:islandscales}
and Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide} settle the entropy count of the islands
at every scale up to $a_{k_*}/8$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:constantcurvature} shows that
fine witnesses carry it no further; the law of the iterates given their
labels, which the effective action is for, is untouched.
Proposition~\ref{prop:massgrowth} shows that the one-step errors must be
relative bounds by a gauge-invariant form: an error bounded by a multiple
of the Euclidean form grows by a factor at least $4/(1+2724\kappa)$ at each
step. Proposition~\ref{prop:relstep} gives such a relative bound
for one step at the trivial background on a box of side $n$, from an
absolute bound on the Hessian of the induced action off the gauge
directions; its factor $C_n$, of order $n^2$, is necessary for an
absolute bound (Remark~\ref{rem:relscales}). For a remainder made of filled Wilson loops the bound is relative at every
flat background (Proposition~\ref{prop:flatloops}), and $C_n$ falls on the
Haar term alone (Corollary~\ref{cor:loopstep}). At a background whose
plaquettes lie within $\kappa$ of $I$ the covariant Hessian of such a
remainder is bounded by the covariant plaquette form with a loss of order
$\kappa n^2$, at critical and non-critical points alike
(Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedloops}); the loss is attained, and for
$\kappa(n+1)^2\ge31$ the plaquette action itself has a negative direction
off the gauge directions (Proposition~\ref{prop:curvedsharp}). In terms of
the $\ell^2$ norm $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ of the curvature, the square root
of the Wilson action of the background on the window, the loss is of order
$\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ for every $n$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:actionloops}),
the unstable mode appears at a background with $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2<31.8$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:actionsharp}), and on calm windows both forms of the
loss are of order $K$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:actioncalm}). That the
induced action is a loop sum with summable coefficients is not proved: for
$\SU(2)$ loop sums are dense among invariant functions
(Proposition~\ref{prop:loopsums}), which controls neither values nor
Hessians, and a relative bound on values gives no Hessian bound at curved
backgrounds (Remark~\ref{rem:valueshessians}). Sec.~\ref{ssec:lfstep} carries out the large-field
part of one step for $\SU(2)$: each rough block costs $e^{-\lambda\kappa^2}$,
the weight of a coarse field is an exact sum over large-field regions, and
the large-field sum is the calm weight times the mean of a polymer sum
under the calm law (Proposition~\ref{prop:sfrelative}), whose activities are
at most $e^{-9}$ per block wherever the boundary values admit a completion
calm at $\kappa/30$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfcalm}). Not proved are that bound
at calm fields with plaquettes in the shell $(\kappa/30,\kappa]$, a bound
on the term $Z_\perp$, and the locality of the calm weight in $c$; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgauss} the calm weight is not a product of local factors
times a polymer sum if the rational number $(M_W)_{AB}$ of that theorem is
nonzero, as an exact computation finds (Remark~\ref{rem:sfgaussvalue}), and
then a local form has to expand around the Gaussian block-spin form. Nor can the leading term be $\lambda q^{\rm lin}(\log c)$ for $\lambda>0.5472$, by gauge invariance (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfgaugeobst}); the linear propagator of such an expansion decays at an explicit rate (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfprop}); in the linear model the relative activities in the shell are unbounded under the calm law at every $\lambda$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfshelllin}); and $Z_\perp(I)>0$ for $\SU(2)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:sfperp}). The coarse action is comparable to $\lambda$ times the
coarse curvature only up to a constant factor. Sec.~\ref{ssec:iterate} replaces the factor $C_*$ of the
comparison by $2956$ for every coarse field and by $1+O(\kappa_0)$ on the
coarse plaquettes below $\kappa_1\approx0.19\,\kappa_0$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:stepconstants}), and shows that no such comparison has
a ratio of constants below $4t_L^2>3.849$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:stepsharp}),
so that a next step has to be compared with the block-spin form.
Theorem~\ref{thm:iterate} composes the steps under three hypotheses at
every scale, a relative error, a locality bound and a large-field cost;
none is proved beyond the first step in the required form
(Proposition~\ref{prop:iteratestatus}), and the large-field estimates
of Sec.~\ref{ssec:lfstep} give no activity bound for
$\beta_W<3.2372\cdot10^6$, more than $1.257\cdot10^7$ one-loop steps
above coupling one. The locality hypothesis cannot hold uniformly in the
volume (Proposition~\ref{prop:h2volume}). Theorem~\ref{thm:allscales}
proves the step from one scale to the next under a single condition on the
error of that step, relative and local; under it the relative comparison
and the fibre gap pass to every scale uniformly in $\lambda_0$, and the
locality of the fibre with constants that are not bounded in the scale.
Sec.~\ref{ssec:localrem} proves the relative one-step bound without the
factor $C_n$ when the remainder of the action is a sum of gauge-invariant
local terms, exactly at flat backgrounds (Theorem~\ref{thm:localflat}) and
with a loss of order $\lVert\kappa\rVert_2$ at curved ones
(Theorem~\ref{thm:localcurved}); a loss of order $\kappa$ uniformly in $n$
is false (Proposition~\ref{prop:supform}). Condition (C) follows from such
a representation of the one-step error (Corollary~\ref{cor:localC}); that
the induced action has one is not proved (Remark~\ref{rem:localrem}).
\end{enumerate}
The covariance of item (ii) for a fixed coarse field and uniform in the
exterior, with decay at the rate $2\alpha_G$ without a floor, is the
single-scale part of (D) that remains open; its mean over the coarse
field, and its value for the coarse fields of
Proposition~\ref{prop:fixedgood}, are bounded by
Theorems~\ref{thm:labelcov}, \ref{thm:fibrecov} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:labelstretched}, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:fixedobstruction} the rest needs the mixed
differences of $\log Z^c$ in tree form and the response of the law across
a bad component, which Theorem~\ref{thm:badcross} gives on the chart up
to the mass of the law off the chart, which tends to one as the component
grows, for coarse plaquettes below $6.0\cdot10^{-13}$, for the coarse
fields of Proposition~\ref{prop:spread} up to $2.39\cdot10^{-12}$, and for
none above $2.418\cdot10^{-12}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:badchart},
Proposition~\ref{prop:spread}, Theorem~\ref{thm:localcharts},
Theorem~\ref{thm:offchartmass}, Remark~\ref{rem:badmassopen}); item (i) being settled for the
chains of the bad blocks by Proposition~\ref{prop:linechain} and item (ii) given the labels
of all islands by Theorem~\ref{thm:manyislands};
item (iii) is settled by Theorem~\ref{thm:islandthreshold} at one scale
and by Theorem~\ref{thm:islandswide} at every scale up to $a_{k_*}/8$;
item (iv) is the multiscale part. Sec.~\ref{ssec:groups13} carries the single-scale results of this section to every compact simple group, with explicit constants, except the parts listed in Remark~\ref{rem:groups13}. On the continuum side, Lemmas~\ref{lem:positivetime}
and~\ref{lem:nonvanishing} reduce the nontriviality of the limit to a
lower bound on one ratio of lattice two-point functions at a fixed
physical time, uniform along the tuning, which is the open input of
Theorem~\ref{thm:flowlimit}; Sec.~\ref{ssec:ratiocube} states it exactly as the
condition $(\mathrm N_u)$, shows that neither the strong-coupling range nor
the cube estimate in the form of Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} supplies it,
and reduces it to the trial states of Corollary~\ref{cor:trial}. Sec.~\ref{ssec:slabenergy} bounds the slab energy of every Lipschitz slice
function by the plaquette energy, which is at most $(3.7148+0.149/\beta_W)
/\beta_W$ for $\SU(2)$, and shows that this route gives the trial condition
only where $a_k\beta_k$ stays bounded below, not along the one-loop tuning
(Proposition~\ref{prop:lipobstruction}). The same subsection shows that no
set of upper bounds on correlations at physical separations, with constants
not exponentially small in $1/a_k$, implies $(\mathrm N_u)$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:upperbounds}); that trial states smeared in time over
a physical interval, flowed Wilson loops among them, meet the first trial
condition exactly when, up to the choice of the times, a ratio of their
correlations at physical times is bounded below
(Corollary~\ref{cor:smearedtrial}), which removes the lattice
scale from the condition but leaves a lower bound at physical separations;
and that a comparison with the Gaussian theory gives $(\mathrm N_u)$ from
relative bounds at two physical separations, which a scale-by-scale argument
along the one-loop tuning supplies only if its losses summed over the scales
stay bounded, and not with a loss of first order in the running coupling at
each scale (Proposition~\ref{prop:scalelosses}).
This is the summability required in item~(iv), now for the ratio, and $(\mathrm N_u)$ is not proved here in infinite volume; in a box of fixed size it holds for packets odd under the centre of $\SU(2)$, with degenerate limits (Corollary~\ref{cor:centreodd}). Choosing the couplings by the ratio (Sec.~\ref{ssec:ratiotuning}) makes $(\mathrm N_u)$ and the normalisation of Proposition~\ref{prop:uniquelimit}(iii) hold by construction; such a choice exists if and only if $(\mathrm N_u)$ holds along some sequence of couplings (Theorem~\ref{thm:ratiotuning}), and it leaves (D), (M), the family $\mathfrak F$ and $\beta_k\to\infty$ open. Sec.~\ref{ssec:osaxioms} shows that, given (D) along the tuning, the
Osterwalder--Schrader axioms for the spatially flowed fields, with the
symmetry $\mathrm O(3)\times\mathrm O(1)$, follow from three statements, a
moment bound (M), one spatial rotation (W) and one limit (U), each of
them necessary and none of them proved. Full $\mathrm O(4)$ invariance is not among these conclusions: at positive flow time the spatial flow breaks it even for the free field (Proposition~\ref{prop:osobstruction}(c)), so it has to be posed for $\mathrm O(4)$-covariant observables, such as fields of the four-dimensional flow, and the four-dimensional flow loses reflection positivity already for the free field (Proposition~\ref{prop:fourflow}). Of the three statements, (M) is a local moment bound together with the bound $\sup_k\Upsilon_k<\infty$, which contains $(\mathrm N_0)$ for product packets and fails in the strong-coupling range (Proposition~\ref{prop:msplit}), and the flow alone cannot give it (Proposition~\ref{prop:stationary}); its spatial comparison (M$_{\mathrm{sp}}$) follows from spatial reflection positivity (SR$_0$) of the slice field (Theorem~\ref{thm:spatialrp}), which cannot hold for a field and its Laplacian together in a state that clusters in space (Corollary~\ref{cor:srladder}) and is destroyed by the linear heat flow (Proposition~\ref{prop:heatrp}); (W) is the Ward identity for one spatial generator (Proposition~\ref{prop:wardform}); and under the renormalisation condition (RC), (U) is the vanishing of the moment differences between consecutive scales together with a totally disconnected set of limits, and a first-order bound in the running coupling for those differences does not give it (Proposition~\ref{prop:tuned}).

\section{The comparison lemma}\label{app:comparison}

Let $(G,\delta)$ be a compact group with a bi-invariant metric of diameter
$D$, $\Omega=G^A$, and $C_{ee'}$ the coefficients of Sec.~\ref{sec:state},
with row and column sums at most $\alpha<1$ and $C_{ee'}=0$ unless $e,e'$ share
a plaquette, so that $|e-e'|\le1$ for the distance of link midpoints. Fix
$\lambda>0$ with $\theta=\alpha e^\lambda<1$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:comparison}
Let $S\subset A$, possibly infinite, and let $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be probability
measures on $\Omega$ invariant under $\gamma^F_e$ for every $e\notin S$. Let
$T\subset A\setminus S$ be finite, $w_b=e^{-\lambda\dist(b,T)}$, and suppose
$\sum_{z\in S}w_z<\infty$. There is a coupling of $\mu_1,\mu_2$ whose link
distances $\varrho(b)=\E\,\delta(\sigma_b,\sigma'_b)$ satisfy
\[
\sum_{b\notin S}w_b\varrho(b)\le\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}\sum_{z\in S}w_z .
\]
If $S=\emptyset$ then $\mu_1=\mu_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The couplings form a weakly compact set and $\Psi(\pi)=\sum_bw_b\E_\pi\delta(
\sigma_b,\sigma'_b)$ is weakly continuous because $\sum_bw_b<\infty$; let $\pi^*$ be
a minimiser. For $e\notin S$ replace the pair $(\sigma_e,\sigma'_e)$ by a sample of
an optimal coupling of $\gamma^F_e(\cdot\mid\sigma)$ and $\gamma^F_e(\cdot\mid
\sigma')$, chosen measurably~\cite[Cor.~5.22]{Vil09}. Both $\mu_i$ are
invariant, so the result is again a coupling, and changing the finitely
many links that enter $\gamma^F_e$ one at a time gives $W_1\le\sum_{e'}C_{ee'}
\delta(\sigma_{e'},\sigma'_{e'})$. Minimality gives $\varrho(e)\le\sum_{e'}C_{ee'}
\varrho(e')$. Multiply by $w_e$ and sum over $e\notin S$; where $C_{ee'}\ne0$,
$w_e\le e^\lambda w_{e'}$, so
\[
\sum_{e\notin S}w_e\varrho(e)\le\theta\Bigl[\sum_{e'\notin S}w_{e'}\varrho(e')
+\sum_{z\in S}w_z\varrho(z)\Bigr],
\]
all sums are finite, and $\varrho\le D$ on $S$. If $S=\emptyset$, $\varrho\equiv0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:decay}
Let $\mu$ be the Gibbs measure of $\gamma^F$, $F$ a local function with
support $S_F$, $L_F$-Lipschitz in each link, and $H$ bounded with finite
support $S_H$ disjoint from $S_F$. Then
\[
|\Cov_\mu(F,H)|\le\|H\|_\infty L_F\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}|S_H|\,
e^{-\lambda\dist(S_F,S_H)}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Condition on the links of $S_H$~\cite[Ch.~3]{Kal21}; the conditional
measures $\mu^\sigma=\mu(\cdot\mid\sigma_{S_H})$ are invariant under
$\gamma^F_e$ for $e\notin S_H$. Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison} with $S=S_H$ and
$T=S_F$, for which $w_b=1$ on $S_F$ and $w_z\le e^{-\lambda\dist(S_F,S_H)}$ on
$S_H$, gives
$|\mu^\sigma(F)-\mu^{\sigma'}(F)|\le L_F\sum_{b\in S_F}\varrho(b)\le
L_F\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}|S_H|e^{-\lambda\dist(S_F,S_H)}$ for any two
boundary values. Since $H$ depends only on $\sigma_{S_H}$,
$\Cov_\mu(F,H)=\iint H(\sigma)\bigl(\mu^\sigma(F)-\mu^{\sigma'}(F)\bigr)\,
d\mu(\sigma)\,d\mu(\sigma')$, and the bound follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:blockcomparison}
Let the blocks partition $A$, let $C_{Bj}$ be the block coefficients of
Sec.~\ref{sec:plaqblocks}, with $\sum_BC_{Bj}\le\alpha<1$ for every $j$ and
$C_{Bj}=0$ unless every link of $B$ lies within distance $2$ of $j$, and fix
$\lambda>0$ with $\theta=\alpha e^{2\lambda}<1$. Let $S\subset A$ be a union
of blocks and let $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be invariant under $\gamma^{\mathcal B}_B$ for
every block $B\not\subset S$. With $T$, $w_b$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison} and $\sum_{z\in S}w_z<\infty$, there is a coupling
with $\sum_{b\notin S}w_b\varrho(b)\le\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}\sum_{z\in S}w_z$,
and $\mu_1=\mu_2$ if $S=\emptyset$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Take a minimiser $\pi^*$ of $\Psi$ as before. For a block $B\not\subset S$
replace $(\sigma_B,\sigma'_B)$ by an optimal coupling, for the metric $d$, of
the two block laws; it is again a coupling, and changing the boundary links
one at a time bounds the expected new $d$-distance by $\sum_jC_{Bj}\varrho(j)$.
Put $\bar w_B=\max_{i\in B}w_i$. Minimality gives
\[
\sum_{i\in B}w_i\varrho(i)\le\bar w_B\sum_jC_{Bj}\varrho(j),
\]
and $\bar w_B\le e^{2\lambda}w_j$ whenever $C_{Bj}\ne0$. Summing over the
blocks outside $S$ and using the column sums,
\[
\sum_{b\notin S}w_b\varrho(b)\le\theta\Bigl[\sum_{j\notin S}w_j\varrho(j)+
\sum_{z\in S}w_z\varrho(z)\Bigr],
\]
which gives the claim as in Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:dscomparison}
Let $n\ge2$ be even, let $V_x$, $x\in2\Z^4$, be the translates of
Sec.~\ref{sec:bypass}, and suppose that $D(n,\alpha)$ holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If a probability measure $\mu$ on $G^A$ is invariant under
$\gamma^F_e$ for every $e$ in a finite set $V$, it is invariant under
$\gamma_V$.
\item Fix $\lambda>0$ with $\theta=\alpha e^{\lambda\rho_n}<1$. Let $S\subset
A$, and let $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be invariant under $\gamma_{V_x}$ for every $x$
with $V_x\cap S=\emptyset$. With $T$, $w_b$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison}
and $\sum_{z\in S}w_z<\infty$, there is a coupling with
\[
\sum_{b\notin S}w_b\varrho(b)\le\frac{D(1+c_ne^{\lambda\rho_n})}{1-\theta}
\sum_{z\in S}w_z ,
\]
and $\mu_1=\mu_2$ if $S=\emptyset$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) Let $\nu_\eta$ be the conditional law of $Q_V$ given the links $\eta$
outside $V$. For bounded $f$ on $G^V$ and bounded $g$ of $\eta$,
$\gamma^F_e(fg)=g\,\gamma^F_ef$ for $e\in V$, so invariance gives $\int
g(\eta)\bigl(\nu_\eta(\gamma^F_ef)-\nu_\eta(f)\bigr)\,d\mu=0$ for all $g$;
taking $f$ in a countable dense set of continuous functions, $\nu_\eta$ is
invariant under every $\gamma^F_e(\cdot\mid\cdot,\eta)$, $e\in V$, for
$\mu$-almost every $\eta$. So is $\gamma_V(\cdot\mid\eta)$, whose
conditional laws of single links are the $\gamma^F_e$. The composition $P_\eta$
of the kernels $\gamma^F_e$, $e\in V$, in a fixed order has a density with
respect to Haar measure on $G^V$ bounded below by a positive constant,
because each single-link density is at least $e^{-12N^2\beta}$ times its
maximum over the group. A Markov kernel with such a lower bound has at most
one invariant probability measure (Doeblin's condition), so
$\nu_\eta=\gamma_V(\cdot\mid\eta)$.

(b) Let $\pi^*$ minimise $\Psi$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison} and call $x$
admissible if $V_x\cap S=\emptyset$. For admissible $x$ replace
$(\sigma_{V_x},\sigma'_{V_x})$ by an optimal coupling, for $d_{V_x}$, of the
two block laws; both $\mu_i$ are invariant, so the result is a coupling, and
changing the boundary links one at a time bounds the new expected
$d_{V_x}$-distance by $\sum_jC_{V_x,j}\varrho(j)$. With $\bar w_x=\max_{i\in
V_x}w_i$, minimality gives
\[
\sum_{i\in V_x}w_i\varrho(i)\le\bar w_x\sum_{j\notin V_x}C_{V_x,j}\varrho(j),
\]
and $\bar w_x\le e^{\lambda\rho_n}w_j$ whenever $C_{V_x,j}\ne0$. Let $S'$ be
the set of links outside $S$ that lie in a translate meeting $S$; each is
within distance $\rho_n$ of a link of $S$, so $\sum_{i\in S'}w_i\le
c_ne^{\lambda\rho_n}\sum_{z\in S}w_z$. A link outside $S\cup S'$ lies in
$N_n$ translates, all admissible. Summing over admissible $x$ and using
$\sum_{x:\,j\notin V_x}C_{V_x,j}=K_{c(j)}\le\alpha N_n$,
\[
N_n\sum_{i\notin S\cup S'}w_i\varrho(i)\le\theta N_n\Bigl[\sum_{i\notin
S\cup S'}w_i\varrho(i)+\sum_{i\in S\cup S'}w_i\varrho(i)\Bigr].
\]
All sums are finite and $\varrho\le D$, so $\sum_{i\notin S\cup S'}w_i
\varrho(i)\le\frac{\theta D}{1-\theta}(1+c_ne^{\lambda\rho_n})\sum_{z\in S}
w_z$; adding $\sum_{i\in S'}w_i\varrho(i)\le Dc_ne^{\lambda\rho_n}\sum_{z\in
S}w_z$ gives the bound. If $S=\emptyset$ then $S'=\emptyset$ and
$\varrho\equiv0$.
\end{proof}

The covariance bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:decay} follows from part (b) in
the same way, with $\theta D/(1-\theta)$ replaced by
$D(1+c_ne^{\lambda\rho_n})/(1-\theta)$, since the conditional measures
$\mu^\sigma$ there are invariant under $\gamma_{V_x}$ for $V_x\cap
S_H=\emptyset$ by part (a).
